notes.aatrox-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is Q1 → E to reposition → basic attack → W → Q2 → Q3. Use E immediately after pressing Q to move during the cast and land the blade’s sweet spot.
notes.aatrox-combo-w: The W combo is Q1 → W → Q2 before the pull → Q3 immediately after it. W reaches any target close enough to be knocked up by Q1, so hold W if Q1 misses; when Q1 lands, use W immediately to give the opponent less time to walk out of the chain area.
notes.aatrox-combo-ult: The teamfight combo is R → Q1 → E → W → Q2 → Q3. R increases attack damage and self-healing, so activate it just before engaging, once you are sure you can force a fight; its short duration extends only through takedowns.
notes.aatrox-skill-q-tip: Q must hit with the blade’s sweet spot to deal full damage and knock up the target. Prioritize Q1, which has the longest range, since the visible windups of Q2 and Q3 make them easier to dodge. Aim for the sweet spot on every cast to reduce your passive cooldown as much as possible and keep empowered autos cycling.
notes.aatrox-skill-passive: The passive’s empowered auto deals damage based on the target’s maximum health and restores health, while each ability hit reduces its cooldown. Its increased range lets you pressure melee opponents, so avoid wasting it on minions.
notes.aatrox-skill-e: E can move Aatrox while other abilities are in progress, letting you adjust Q’s sweet spot during its cast. Its passive restores health from damage dealt to champions, so landing abilities sustains you; using E to close in and land them also reduces the passive cooldown, bringing your next empowered auto sooner. Saving E solely for disengaging slows that entire cycle.
notes.aatrox-laning: At levels 1–2, farm safely near your turret, even if it means giving up some CS. From level 3 onward, farm with Q and take only short trades, saving Q3 and W until the opponent has used their tools to fight back. Q deals enough damage to trade without building attack damage, so in a losing matchup you can prioritize health and regeneration to stay in lane without giving up much damage.
notes.aatrox-laning-q-timing: Against melee opponents, use Q as they step forward to last-hit. If its sweet spot lands during their basic attack windup, they cannot dodge or fight back, so wait for that moment instead of using Q on cooldown.
notes.aatrox-phase: Aatrox is weak at levels 1–2 because Q has a long cooldown, but his trades become strong from level 3 onward as he invests points in Q. He peaks in the mid game as he builds ability haste and items, then struggles against duelists in late-game 1v1s.
notes.aatrox-situational-armor: If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Cloth Armor or Bramble Vest first and get Plated Steelcaps earlier. If the matchup keeps pushing you back, switch to a build that prioritizes armor and health to survive.
notes.aatrox-situational-antiheal: If the opponent’s healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item to reduce it.
notes.aatrox-teamfight: In teamfights, use W to group opponents and hit multiple targets with Q’s sweet spot. Avoid 1v1 duels and engage with your allies once you have a numbers advantage; following up their immobilizing crowd control with Q is the easiest way to land its sweet spot reliably.
notes.vs-aatrox-q: Aatrox relies on Q for most of his damage, so avoiding its sweet spot greatly reduces the damage you take. When you see him cast Q, move outside the blade’s tip area or step inside it; his pronounced windups give you time to react.
notes.vs-aatrox-passive: Aatrox’s empowered auto deals heavy damage early, so trade right after he uses it on a minion.
notes.vs-aatrox-r: R increases Aatrox’s attack damage and self-healing, which can reverse the outcome of a duel even at the same health. Its duration extends only through takedowns, so when he activates it, avoid the 1v1, create distance, and fight again after it expires.
notes.vs-aatrox-early: Aatrox can turn an early advantage into a much larger lead. Secure CS without giving up early kills, and the matchup will improve as the game goes on.
notes.vs-aatrox-w: If W hits you, leave its area before the allotted time runs out or it will pull you to the center. The area is a circle centered where the chain hit you, so the distance to escape is the same in any direction: walk out immediately instead of hesitating, and save your mobility ability for this moment.
notes.ahri-combo-basic: The basic combo is E Charm → W Fox-Fire → Q Orb of Deception. Land Charm first: Fox-Fire prioritizes charmed champions, so all three flames will hit the same target, and the follow-up abilities are guaranteed to connect.
notes.ahri-combo-q: Q Orb of Deception hits on its outward and return paths. Throw it past the enemy, then immediately move toward them so the orb hits both ways as it returns to Ahri. The return hit deals true damage, so magic resistance does not reduce it.
notes.ahri-combo-ult: R (Spirit Rush) is a mobility ability that links Ahri’s combo, and she can cast other abilities while dashing.
notes.ahri-skill-e: E Charm affects only the first target it hits, so it cannot reach an enemy behind minions. Move around the side or use R Spirit Rush to cross the minion line before casting it. Ahri can do little for a while after E is spent, so do not throw it carelessly.
notes.ahri-skill-w: W (Fox-Fire) deals greatly increased damage to low-health minions, making it useful for last-hitting and clearing waves. It also grants movement speed to help Ahri chase or disengage.
notes.ahri-skill-r: R Spirit Rush allows multiple dashes, and participating in a champion takedown while it is active increases the remaining dash count and extends its duration. Save at least one dash to get out instead of committing them all on the initial engage. If you can secure a kill, use the extra dash from the takedown to pursue the next enemy.
notes.ahri-skill-passive: P Essence Theft restores health each time you kill a set number of minions. Ahri’s lane sustain depends heavily on this healing, so keeping up your CS helps support your trades. Participating in a champion takedown heals you for more and restores R Spirit Rush dashes.
notes.ahri-phase: Ahri is weakest without R Spirit Rush because she has no mobility ability available. Her first power spike comes at level 6; after that, avoid overextending in lane while R is on cooldown. From the mid game onward, as she builds ability power, landing E Charm gives her the potential to take out a single target.
notes.ahri-laning: Use Q Orb of Deception as your main poke tool in lane, throwing it so it clips the enemy backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time. Save E Charm for a kill opportunity or a gank follow-up. When you run out of mana, stop poking and focus on farming.
notes.ahri-laning-roam: After unlocking R Spirit Rush, push the lane before roaming. Enter another lane only when both E Charm and R are available; if either is down, farm instead. Ahri’s roams depend on landing Charm.
notes.ahri-teamfight: Ahri is classified as an assassin, but she is also strong in teamfights. Grouped enemies have a harder time dodging Q Orb of Deception, and E Charm can pull one of them toward your allies for a follow-up. Poke with Q from outside the enemy’s range, then cast E when you have an angle instead of engaging head-on first.
notes.ahri-teamfight-cleanup: As the fight winds down, use R Spirit Rush to chase fleeing enemies and W Fox-Fire for movement speed. Account for the R dashes restored by each takedown when deciding how far you can chase without overcommitting.
notes.ahri-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets a full combo’s damage, buy Morellonomicon to reduce that healing after completing one core item.
notes.vs-ahri-e: Stand behind minions to block Ahri’s E Charm. Her damage potential drops sharply without it, so keep the minion wave between you and Ahri throughout laning.
notes.vs-ahri-ult: Ahri has no mobility ability when R Spirit Rush is down. Track its cooldown and time your ganks or engages for the window before it becomes available again.
notes.vs-ahri-q: Ahri’s Q Orb of Deception hits on both its outward and return paths. After dodging the first hit, keep moving out of the orb’s path back to Ahri. The return hit deals true damage, so magic resistance cannot reduce it.
notes.vs-ahri-fight: Ahri has some of the lowest defensive stats among champions and is most vulnerable right after using E Charm. Close in and attack as soon as you dodge it; her remaining ways to create distance are an R Spirit Rush dash and W Fox-Fire’s movement speed boost.
notes.akali-combo-passive-ring: Akali’s combos revolve around her passive ring: hitting an ability creates one around the target, and crossing its edge before returning prepares an empowered basic attack with twice the range. Practice moving quickly back and forth across the ring to keep your damage flowing.
notes.akali-combo-basic: For a basic trade, land Q to create the ring, step back across its edge, then return with an empowered basic attack. Its extra range lets you strike from outside the enemy’s retaliation range, and this back-and-forth poke costs no energy.
notes.akali-combo-e-double: Land the first E, cross the ring, and hit an empowered auto. Then close in with the second E and hit another empowered auto.
notes.akali-combo-allin: For a full engage, use the first R to dash past the target and close in, wear them down with Q and an empowered basic attack, then finish with the second R. Its damage increases with the health the target has lost, so save it for last; casting Q during the second dash lands both hits at once.
notes.akali-combo-r-flash: Flash can extend the range of either R dash. Combine them against a fleeing target to catch them from much farther away than expected.
notes.akali-skill-q: Q spreads in a cone, slowing targets hit at its maximum range and readying the passive ring immediately. Aim for that edge instead of casting at close range for more effective poke. Because Q costs a lot of energy, use a basic attack when you’ve already created the ring.
notes.akali-skill-w: W’s smoke grants stealth and a movement speed boost that helps Akali move through her combo faster. She briefly appears just after entering it and can be hit by skillshots in that window. Using W only to escape across open ground can get you caught, so cast it just before engaging or to interrupt a targeted enemy ability.
notes.akali-skill-e: The second E dash follows its marked target no matter how far they go. Check their position before recasting, or they may pull Akali under a turret or into the middle of the enemy team. You can also leave an E mark on W’s smoke as a way to retreat.
notes.akali-phase: At levels 1–2, Akali has some of the lowest armor and too little energy to trade well. Poke becomes viable as Q gains levels, and kill opportunities appear when she gets R at level 6. Once she completes one core ability power item, she can kill a backline target in one combo, but failing to finish the kill can still get her killed throughout the game.
notes.akali-laning: Akali ranks near the bottom in CS statistically, so giving up some farm to build a health advantage with max-range Q hits and empowered basic attacks is a normal way to play. Once you have that advantage, push the wave and move to another lane to turn it into a lead elsewhere.
notes.akali-teamfight: Let your allies start teamfights, then enter the backline after the enemy’s attention and crowd control have been spent to kill a squishy target. Before going in, check that the enemy has used their targeted crowd control.
notes.akali-situational-antiheal: If an enemy survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon to apply Grievous Wounds. Akali needs to secure the kill during her brief engage, so going in while the enemy still has healing available puts her at a disadvantage.
notes.akali-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has crowd control that can lock Akali down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items for a way to cleanse it. Getting caught immediately after engaging can kill her before she uses the second R, making that escape tool critical to survival.
notes.vs-akali-shroud-entry: Akali briefly appears when she enters her smoke. Throw a skillshot during that window to hit her inside it.
notes.vs-akali-shroud-reveal: Turrets and true sight reveal Akali inside her smoke. Place a Control Ward in the smoke or draw the fight near a turret to remove her stealth advantage.
notes.vs-akali-e-mark: If Akali marks you with E, her second dash follows you wherever you run. Dodging the first E takes away one way she can close the gap, so make avoiding that skillshot shuriken your top priority.
notes.vs-akali-early: Akali has some of the lowest armor, making her weak in close-range trades before level 6. Wait for her to leave the smoke and attack, then fight back; build a health and CS lead while her ultimate is unavailable.
notes.akali-skill-r: R can also get you out of a bad position by dashing over an enemy. Save its first cast unless you’re sure you can secure the kill.
notes.vs-akali-r: Akali’s first R is a targeted dash over an enemy champion, so you cannot dodge it by walking. Save your mobility or disengage tool while she is on you, then use it to interrupt her R engage.
notes.akshan-combo-q: To poke, hit with Q (Avengerang) on both its outgoing and returning paths. The boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy, so throwing it through a minion wave can reach an opponent much farther back than expected. Move sideways after the throw to shift its return path toward the direction they dodged the first hit.
notes.akshan-combo-passive-cancel: You can cancel the automatic second shot after a basic attack by moving, which grants movement speed. Fire both shots when you need full damage; when you need to close or create distance, move immediately after the first to cancel the second. This movement is Akshan's main way to kite.
notes.akshan-combo-passive-third: Dirty Fighting (P) deals bonus damage on every third hit from basic attacks and abilities combined, and grants a shield if that hit lands on a champion. Landing Q (Avengerang) on both its outgoing and returning paths sets up the third hit with one basic attack, so start a trade only when you can land it.
notes.akshan-combo-e: E (Heroic Swing) hooks onto terrain and swings around it, automatically firing at the nearest enemy during the swing. Swing in a wide arc around your opponent to close in, then use the third input to land where you want and fire the final shot. Colliding with a champion or terrain ends the swing immediately, so keep your arc clear of the path your opponent is walking toward.
notes.akshan-skill-e-reset: A takedown resets E (Heroic Swing), so use it to engage when the kill is certain, then use the reset to reach another target or escape. If the kill is uncertain, engaging with E leaves you without a way out.
notes.akshan-skill-w-revive: An enemy who kills an ally is marked as a Scoundrel; killing that Scoundrel revives the allies they killed and grants bonus gold. An ally falling can therefore create Akshan's biggest opportunity: in a teamfight, look for a chance to finish off the Scoundrel instead of retreating immediately. Akshan must survive for the revive to happen, so dying alongside the Scoundrel is the worst outcome.
notes.akshan-skill-w-camo: W (Going Rogue) camouflage lasts longer near terrain or brush but ends quickly in the open, so plan roams and escapes along river and jungle walls. Entering an enemy champion's detection range reveals you even while camouflaged, making a camouflaged approach against a grouped team unworkable. When a Scoundrel is present, a trail toward them and bonus movement speed help you chase.
notes.akshan-skill-r-target: Comeuppance (R) shots hit the first enemy or structure in their path. Minions are executed instantly, so a wave won't block the shots, but an enemy frontliner or turret in the way will absorb them all. Because the damage increases with the target's missing health, use R to finish off fleeing enemies from long range.
notes.akshan-skill-r-channel: Akshan is rooted while aiming R (Comeuppance), and the target sees an aiming indicator. Charge it for a long time only if the target's escape route has no wall: moving behind terrain can waste every stored bullet. You can fire before reaching full charge, so release the shots before the target reaches a wall.
notes.akshan-laning: Akshan's level 1 attack damage is among the lowest of all champions, so he cannot win a straight basic attack fight. His lane advantage comes from hitting with Avengerang (Q) on both passes and using the Dirty Fighting (P) shield. Trade only at a range where Q can hit on the way out and back, avoid forcing trades outside that range, and check that the shield is ready before going in.
notes.akshan-laning-roam: After pushing the wave, use E (Heroic Swing) to cross terrain and roam to another lane. Follow river and jungle walls with W (Going Rogue) camouflage to approach out of sight, then check E's cooldown before choosing your route back.
notes.akshan-phase: Akshan is weak at levels 1–2. Even if you learn E (Heroic Swing) first, early trade damage comes from Q (Avengerang), so those trades depend on finding a Q angle. Kill opportunities rise sharply when level 6 R (Comeuppance) and the first core item come together; because critical strike affects R's damage, building critical strike items through the mid and late game improves both its finishing power and basic attack damage.
notes.akshan-teamfight: Akshan should not start a fight from the front. Once the fight has begun and the enemy has used their immobilizing abilities, enter from the side with Heroic Swing (E) and finish off targets whose health has been reduced. If an ally falls first, Going Rogue (W) can turn the entire fight around, so ignore other targets and focus on the Scoundrel.
notes.akshan-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing targets, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. R (Comeuppance) deals more damage based on missing health, so an enemy who heals can move out of your finishing range entirely.
notes.vs-akshan-w: Killing one of Akshan's allies marks you as a Scoundrel. If Akshan kills you while you are marked, the allies of his whom you killed are revived. Until the mark is gone, avoid facing him alone and fight outside his finishing range in teamfights.
notes.vs-akshan-camo: W (Going Rogue) camouflage lasts longer only near terrain and brush. Place vision around river and jungle walls to reveal Akshan's roaming route; his camouflage ends on its own in open areas. Entering an enemy champion's detection range also reveals him, so staying grouped can prevent a camouflaged approach.
notes.vs-akshan-e: Akshan needs terrain to hook onto for E (Heroic Swing). Push him into an open area without walls to deny both his engage and escape, or walk into his swing path to end it immediately. A takedown resets E's cooldown, so denying him a kill also prevents that reset.
notes.vs-akshan-r: Akshan is rooted while aiming R (Comeuppance), and an indicator appears on its target. If you are low on health, move behind terrain to block all the bullets, or stay grouped so someone in front can take them for you. Fleeing alone through an open area is the most dangerous option.
notes.vs-akshan-q: Akshan's Q (Avengerang) travels farther each time it hits an enemy, making it dangerous to stand behind a minion wave. Dodge both its outgoing and returning paths, and account for the return path shifting if Akshan moves sideways after throwing it.
notes.vs-akshan-early: Akshan's level 1 attack damage is among the lowest of all champions, leaving him weak in early basic attack fights. If your champion can pressure him at close range, push for an advantage at levels 1–2, then farm outside his Q (Avengerang) poke range.
notes.alistar-combo-wq: Alistar’s standard combo is W Headbutt immediately into Q Pulverize, knocking up the displaced target where they land to keep the crowd control chain going. To send an enemy toward your allies, get behind them before using W; positioning comes before the combo.
notes.alistar-combo-qw: Q → W knocks the target up first, then pushes them in your chosen direction. Use it to peel enemies off your backline or drive them outward instead of toward your allies.
notes.alistar-combo-flash: Use Flash during Q’s cast to move Pulverize’s area toward the target. Landing Q from an unexpected distance and immediately using W to push the target toward your allies is Alistar’s main kill setup.
notes.alistar-skill-e: While E Trample is active, Alistar can move through units, so use it to pass through minions or escape along a narrow path. Once E has dealt enough damage to a champion, his next basic attack stuns them; build it up during a trade to gain another crowd control effect.
notes.alistar-skill-r: R Unbreakable Will immediately removes all impairing effects already on Alistar and greatly reduces incoming damage. Use it just after enemy crowd control catches you or as focused fire begins, rather than before engaging, to benefit from both effects. Account for the fact that it does not prevent crowd control applied afterward.
notes.alistar-skill-passive: P Triumphant Roar gains a stack whenever Alistar stuns, knocks up, or pushes back an enemy; at full stacks, it heals him and nearby allies. Landing abilities on enemies gives him sustain in lane, so when the stacks are nearly full, engage once more after a trade to trigger the heal, then back off.
notes.alistar-phase: Alistar’s level 1 health and armor are among the highest in the game, making him strong in early trades. His kill pressure peaks at levels 2–3, once his crowd control is available; later, when he deals very little damage, focus on starting fights and protecting allies.
notes.alistar-laning: Alistar is a lane pressure support. Look for a Q Pulverize opportunity when an enemy steps forward to last-hit, but engage only when your allied marksman can reliably follow up: if you use both Q and W Headbutt and the engage fails, both abilities will be down at once, leaving you open to a counterattack.
notes.alistar-laning-mana: Alistar’s abilities cost a lot of mana, so he cannot repeat his combo early on. A failed engage costs both mana and lane control; if the opening is uncertain, trade with E and wait for a better chance.
notes.alistar-teamfight: In teamfights, push an enemy damage dealer toward your allies or peel enemies off your backline. With R active, Alistar can charge through the enemy team, absorb most of its damage, and break its formation, so focus on disrupting enemy positions rather than dealing damage.
notes.alistar-dive: When an enemy is under their turret, Alistar can make a strong dive by using W to push them deeper beneath it. Check first that your allies have enough damage to finish the target, then take turret aggro yourself and activate R as you go in.
notes.alistar-situational-boots: For Alistar, movement speed increases engage range, making Boots of Swiftness generally valuable. If the enemy team deals mostly physical damage, choose Plated Steelcaps instead to survive lane and teamfights.
notes.vs-alistar-r: Alistar takes much less damage while R is active. When he uses it, avoid wasting abilities on him; back off, let it expire, then fight again.
notes.vs-alistar-r-cc: Alistar's R only removes impairing effects already on him when he activates it.
notes.vs-alistar-turret: When defending by your turret, do not give Alistar room to get behind you.
notes.vs-alistar-cooldown: Alistar’s threat comes from his close-range Q and W. Counterattack immediately after he uses both; while they are on cooldown, he can do little, so use that time to push the lane or reposition.
notes.ambessa-combo-dash: Every Ambessa combo relies on her passive dash: issue a move or attack command during an ability’s cast, and she dashes in that direction when it ends. Without a command, she uses the ability in place. Command toward an opponent to engage or backward to retreat while casting; the same ability can take you in or out.
notes.ambessa-combo-basic: For a basic trade, dash in with E, let its extra strike land as the dash ends, then use a basic attack, hit with Q (Cunning Sweep) at the blade’s edge, follow with Sundering Slam, and finish with another basic attack. Weaving attacks between abilities consumes passive stacks and restores enough resources to complete the combo.
notes.ambessa-combo-q-recast: Q (Cunning Sweep) must hit an enemy to ready Sundering Slam, and the second cast is available only briefly. Minions count, so if a champion is out of range, hit a minion with Cunning Sweep and aim Sundering Slam at the champion. A complete miss removes the second strike; set up a hit before trading.
notes.ambessa-combo-ult: R (Public Execution) sends Ambessa to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line, letting her reach the backline past a tank but also pulling her toward an unintended target farther along that line. Check who is last before casting. After landing, use the suppression and stun to follow with E, a basic attack, Q (Cunning Sweep), and Sundering Slam.
notes.ambessa-skill-passive: Passive stacks build whenever Ambessa starts a dash and expire after a short time. They increase her basic attack range and attack speed, so weave attacks between abilities for more total damage instead of letting stacks expire unused. Use the extra range to land a hit from a distance the opponent thinks is safe.
notes.ambessa-skill-q: Both Q (Cunning Sweep) and Sundering Slam deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes but only half damage closer in. If you are too close, dash behind or to the side of the opponent to create space and connect with the blade’s edge. Q also deals damage based on maximum health, so use it to trade against opponents who build health instead of saving it only for farming.
notes.ambessa-skill-w: W (Repudiation) grants a shield, then slams the area around Ambessa after a brief windup. Taking damage from an enemy champion, large monster, or structure during the windup greatly increases the slam’s damage; minion damage does not. Cast W just before an opponent uses an ability or during a tower dive, since casting it safely in advance gives you only the shield and a weaker slam.
notes.ambessa-skill-e: E (Lacerate) hits a short area around Ambessa and applies a slow that nearly stops its target but wears off quickly. Follow immediately with Q to land the blade’s edge during that brief window. Starting a dash with E adds another strike when the dash ends, so pair it with a move command; because E is also her most reliable way to close the gap, save it from farming unless a kill is possible.
notes.ambessa-skill-r: Once learned, R (Public Execution) provides armor penetration and healing based on ability damage even while unused, giving Ambessa a substantial boost to dueling and sustain at levels 6, 11, and 16. Those effects remain after casting, so use R for a sure kill or access to the backline. Ambessa is unstoppable during the cast, and crowd control cannot interrupt it.
notes.ambessa-laning: As a melee mid laner, Ambessa takes early poke from ranged opponents, so avoid forcing an engage. Use the blade’s edge of Q (Cunning Sweep) to last-hit and poke while keeping up in levels. When the opponent steps forward to last-hit, dash in with E (Lacerate), land Q at the blade’s edge and follow with Sundering Slam, then leave immediately; staying close lets them hit you with all their abilities. After pushing the wave, use Ambessa’s repeated dashes to gain more by getting vision at an entrance to the enemy jungle or moving to a side lane.
notes.ambessa-phase: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2, when one or two abilities give her too few dashes to chain. Trades become viable at level 3 with both Q and E, and R’s passive gives her a major boost at level 6. Almost all her damage ratios scale with bonus attack damage, making the mid game her peak as core items come together. Late in the game, dashes are her only way out after engaging, so avoid going in alone against grouped opponents and look for an isolated target from the flank.
notes.ambessa-teamfight: Ambessa should not engage head-on. Once your allies draw the opponents’ attention, flank with R (Public Execution) to reach the backline and take down one target with its suppression and stun. Go in after the opponents have used their key crowd control and defensive abilities. If burst damage is about to hit just before you engage, use W (Repudiation) first to gain a shield and empower its slam with the damage taken. Plan your escape route before engaging so you can dash out immediately with E (Lacerate) after taking down the target.
notes.ambessa-situational-antiheal: If the opponent sustains through their own healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early so you can finish them after your combo.
notes.ambessa-situational-cleanse: If the opponent has crowd control that restricts movement, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar so you can dash and line up Q after R lands.
notes.vs-ambessa-w: A shield followed by a brief windup signals Ambessa’s W (Repudiation). Abilities or basic attacks that damage her during that windup greatly empower its slam, so stop attacking and walk out of range.
notes.vs-ambessa-q: Both strikes of Ambessa’s Q deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes and half damage closer in. If you cannot easily get out of range, move toward Ambessa to take less damage. Dodging the first strike, Cunning Sweep, completely prevents Sundering Slam from being readied.
notes.vs-ambessa-passive: Ambessa can follow each ability with a short dash, and her remaining passive stacks increase basic attack range and attack speed. An ability can close a gap that looks safe, so step forward only while her abilities are on cooldown; counterattack right after she has used them all and spent her stacks.
notes.vs-ambessa-r: Ambessa’s R teleports her to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. She is unstoppable during the cast, so crowd control cannot interrupt it; even if a tank stands in front, R will catch a backline champion farther along that line. During a standoff, avoid lining up your backline with Ambessa, and have backline champions use walls or allies to break her angle.
notes.vs-ambessa-e: Ambessa’s E applies a slow that nearly stops you but wears off quickly. Use a mobility ability or cleanse immediately after it hits to avoid the Q strike at the blade’s edge; waiting for the slow to end gives her time to finish the combo.
notes.vs-ambessa-phase: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has only one or two abilities, and immediately after using them all; she peaks in the mid game as core items come together. Avoid giving up early kills and keep up in levels to improve the matchup. Once she learns R, its armor penetration and healing remain active even while it is unused, so do not assume a one-on-one fight is safe just because she has cast it.
notes.amumu-combo-engage: The basic engage is Q in, then R, E, turn on W, and auto attack. Q leaves the target stunned as Amumu arrives, so R will land; E and W then add area damage and reduce defensive stats. Use R before E so your allies can make full use of the stun.
notes.amumu-combo-flash-r: If enemies are grouped but you have no Q angle, Flash in and use R immediately: it erupts around Amumu, leaving both Q charges available to disengage or chase afterward. Opening with Q instead can pull you toward one target and away from the others, reducing the number hit by R.
notes.amumu-combo-double-q: Q stores up to two charges, so space them out: close in with the first, then use the second if the target escapes with a mobility ability. When ganking for an ally, the most reliable play is to hold the first charge until just after the target Flashes.
notes.amumu-skill-passive: Cursed Touch makes targets hit by Amumu's auto attacks take more magic damage; W continually reapplies the curse, and R applies it too. Staying close also increases your allies' magic damage, so weave in an auto attack after engaging to boost your team's damage.
notes.amumu-skill-q: Q, Bandage Toss, is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Minions and jungle monsters can block it, so approach a target behind a wave from the side; casting from brush or behind a wall gives them less time to react. If the angle is uncertain, hold Q, since a miss leaves Amumu without a way to close in.
notes.amumu-skill-w: While active, W, Despair, continually damages nearby enemies based on their maximum health and reapplies the curse. It drains mana, so turn it off while moving and use it during fights and jungle clears. W is more effective against targets with high maximum health, making a spot beside the enemy frontline valuable in teamfights.
notes.amumu-skill-r: R, Curse of the Sad Mummy, is an instant area stun around Amumu, so you must get close to land it. Aim for multiple grouped enemies as a rule, but stunning even one enemy diving your allied damage dealer is more valuable if it turns the fight around. The worst outcome is waiting for several targets and missing everyone.
notes.amumu-jungle: Clear mainly with E and use W in short bursts to manage mana. Amumu loses a lot of health on his first clear, so avoid risky early invades and let monsters hit you to shorten E's cooldown and keep the clear moving. Turn W off while traveling; running out of mana leaves you unable to gank or contest objectives.
notes.amumu-gank: Before level 6, ganks depend entirely on Q. When a lane is pushed out and the target stands behind minions, Q gets blocked, so gank when the wave is pushed toward your side and approach from the river or brush for a side angle. After level 6, Flash and R can finish a gank even if Q misses.
notes.amumu-objective: The narrow terrain around Dragon and Baron naturally groups enemies, making both Q and R easier to land. Amumu is more effective in these fights than in a head-on fight on open ground, so establish objective vision early and strike as enemies enter a narrow passage.
notes.amumu-teamfight: Amumu can start teamfights, but engaging alone without R leaves him little to do. Wait on a flank outside enemy vision, engage as their formation narrows, and use R only when your allies are ready to follow. Once in, keep W on and stay among the enemy frontliners to maintain both damage and the curse.
notes.amumu-phase: Amumu is weak before level 3 and loses a lot of health while clearing. Getting R at level 6 makes him much stronger in ganks and objective fights; he peaks in mid to late game teamfights after building magic penetration and damage over time items. His solo fighting remains weak throughout the game, so avoid fighting alone in a side lane.
notes.amumu-situational-antiheal: If enemies rely on healing to sustain, build Morellonomicon between core items. W's continuous magic damage makes it easy to maintain Grievous Wounds on several enemies at once.
notes.vs-amumu-r: Amumu's R, Curse of the Sad Mummy, stuns an area around him. While he has it available, spread out from your allies and take fights in open terrain instead of narrow passages. Its short range means keeping your distance before Amumu gets close will largely neutralize it.
notes.vs-amumu-q: Amumu's Q, Bandage Toss, is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Keep a minion wave or jungle monsters between you and him to block his way in; in lane, moving unpredictably and staying behind minions greatly reduces his chance of a successful gank.
notes.vs-amumu-w: Amumu's W, Despair, continually deals nearby enemies magic damage based on their maximum health. Health alone is less effective against him, so include magic resistance in your defensive build. Even as a frontliner, keep adjusting your distance so you do not remain beside Amumu for long.
notes.vs-amumu-e: Amumu's E, Tantrum, passively reduces physical damage taken, and basic attacks against him shorten its cooldown. Trying to bring him down with physical damage alone takes time and lets him cast E repeatedly, so build armor penetration or attack alongside allies who deal magic damage.
notes.vs-amumu-cleanse: Amumu poses little threat once R is down, so draw it out before committing to a full fight. Even one source of crowd control removal on your team can turn the teamfight, and a key damage dealer with Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar can negate an entire R.
notes.vs-amumu-early: Before level 6, Amumu is weak because his jungle clear is slow and costs a lot of health. Invade his jungle early or push lanes that offer gank opportunities in advance to delay his level 6. Exploit this window before he gets R, or he will keep dictating when fights begin afterward.
notes.amumu-skill-e: E, Tantrum, passively reduces physical damage taken, and each basic attack that hits Amumu shortens its cooldown. Taking hits on the frontline therefore lets him cast E more often; its active deals area magic damage around him and is his main source of jungle clear damage.
notes.anivia-combo-basic: The basic trade is Q → early Q detonation → E. Q chills enemies it hits, and E deals double damage only to a chilled target. If Q misses, hold E rather than waste its cooldown and mana.
notes.anivia-combo-r: In teamfights, cast R first, wait for Glacial Storm to reach full size, then use Q → E. Once fully grown, it chills enemies, so Frostbite (E) deals double damage even without Q; casting R early sets up that bonus.
notes.anivia-combo-wall: Block the enemy’s retreat with W, then detonate Q in front of the wall. An enemy trapped there cannot avoid Q’s explosion stun, giving you time to land both E and R. Wall → Q detonation → E is Anivia’s only guaranteed solo combo.
notes.anivia-skill-q: While Q travels, it passes through enemies, dealing damage and slowing them; it stuns in an area only when reactivated or when it reaches the end of its range. Against opponents who read its path and sidestep, predict where they will dodge and detonate it a little early. When farming without needing the stun, you can simply let Q pass through.
notes.anivia-skill-w: W’s wall grows longer with each rank: at low ranks it blocks a jungle passage, while at high ranks it can divide an entire teamfight area. The wall stands in the cursor’s direction when cast, so place it perpendicular to an enemy’s path to stop them. It blocks allies too; putting it in front of an enemy while your team is engaging can trap your allies instead.
notes.anivia-skill-e: E is Anivia’s main damage ability and her only source of instant damage. Its short cooldown lets you use it repeatedly as long as the target is chilled, making Q and R the setup for E. Using E to clear minions without chilling them can leave you short of mana when it is time to trade.
notes.anivia-skill-passive: Rebirth (P) turns Anivia into an egg when she takes lethal damage, then revives her at full health if the egg survives for a set time with altered defensive stats. An egg left to take hits alone usually breaks, while nearby allies or a turret can help it survive. You can position more aggressively while Rebirth is available, but after it triggers, position as a fragile champion until its cooldown ends.
notes.anivia-skill-r: Glacial Storm (R) continually drains mana while active and ends on its own if Anivia moves too far away. Turn it off as soon as you have pushed the wave or blocked the intended area. Anivia depends heavily on mana, and forgetting to turn R off once can cost you two E casts in the next fight.
notes.anivia-laning: Anivia’s health, armor, and movement speed are all among the lowest, so focus on surviving lane rather than winning it. Save Q for stopping ganks and setting up guaranteed attacks instead of poking, and last-hit with basic attacks and E to keep up in levels. Statistically, Anivia builds her lead through CS rather than kills.
notes.anivia-laning-gank: With no mobility ability and very low movement speed, Anivia has to rely on W to survive a gank. Keep it available whenever you have pushed the lane, then place the wall behind you along your escape route rather than across the enemy’s approach.
notes.anivia-laning-wave: Learning R greatly speeds up wave clear, but turning it on and off costs considerable mana. Use it on waves when you intend to push before roaming or establishing vision. Pushing without a purpose spends mana you will need for the opponent’s next engage.
notes.anivia-phase: Anivia is weakest at levels 1–5, when she lacks both mana and damage. Learning R at level 6 sharply improves her wave clear and sustained damage; she comes into her own in the mid game as items ease her mana problems, then takes on a greater role controlling terrain with W and R in the late game.
notes.anivia-teamfight: In teamfights, stay well behind your frontline and place R where the fight will begin so the storm can grow. When the enemy engages, use W to cut off their follow-up and create a numbers advantage, then clear the enemies trapped in front with Q and E. Draw fights toward narrow passages, where a single wall has more impact.
notes.anivia-situational-antiheal: If an enemy’s self-healing keeps offsetting R’s sustained damage, use Morellonomicon to reduce their healing. Anivia deals damage over time rather than in a short burst, so once healing reduction applies, every moment the enemy stays in R works in your favor.
notes.vs-anivia-egg: When Anivia takes lethal damage, she turns into an egg and revives at full health. It is hard to destroy the egg alone, so attack with your jungler or another ally to make sure it breaks. Once she has revived, she is among the most fragile champions until Rebirth comes off cooldown; that is your chance to kill her.
notes.vs-anivia-q: Flash Frost (Q) travels in a straight line, then explodes and stuns where it is when Anivia reactivates it. Simply sidestepping its path can leave you caught by a predicted detonation. As a ranged champion, stay outside Q’s range; as a melee champion, move toward Anivia and past the explosion radius.
notes.vs-anivia-e: A Q hit or a fully grown Glacial Storm (R) chills you, causing the next Frostbite (E) to deal double damage. Anivia’s burst window comes immediately after Q lands, so stop fighting in place and immediately leave the storm or use a mobility ability to avoid the next E.
notes.vs-anivia-wall: Crystallize (W) can block an entire jungle passage even at a low level. In narrow jungle or river paths, a single wall can cut off your escape from Anivia, so fight her in a wide part of the lane when possible. When engaging, save Flash in case the wall separates you from your allies.
notes.vs-anivia-early: Anivia has some of the lowest movement speed and health in the game and no mobility ability. Pressure her with your jungler before level 6 to force Rebirth or kill her outright; a lead built then weakens her ability to control terrain later.
notes.annie-skill-passive: Annie’s Pyromania (P) stacks as she uses abilities a set number of times, then adds a stun to her next damaging ability. Whether that stun is ready shapes every decision: opponents keep their distance when it is, giving her control of the lane, but without it she is fragile and has no mobility, so do not move forward.
notes.annie-skill-passive-e: Using E does not consume a ready stun. Learn E early to stack the stun safely during a standoff.
notes.annie-combo-ult-engage: With the stun ready, engage with R (Summon: Tibbers) for an area stun, then follow with W (Incinerate) and Q (Disintegrate). Before going in, check that the stacks are full and that another ability has not consumed the stun.
notes.annie-combo-solo: Against one target, open with a stunning Disintegrate (Q), Annie’s longest-range ability, then land Incinerate (W) and a basic attack during the stun. Starting with the shorter-range W gives the target time to escape as Annie closes in, so choose the order based on whether the remaining abilities will land before the stun ends.
notes.annie-skill-q: Killing a target with Q (Disintegrate) refunds its mana cost and halves its cooldown. Last hit minions with Q to build stun stacks for almost no mana, keeping up Annie’s early farming and lane pressure.
notes.annie-skill-w: Incinerate (W) hits a cone in front of Annie, making it useful for pushing a wave at once or hitting several enemies in a teamfight. Its high mana cost and short range make it a poor choice for single-target poke; early on, save it for pushing the wave or a clear kill opportunity.
notes.annie-skill-e: E (Molten Shield) grants a shield and movement speed. Use it just before engaging to reach W (Incinerate) and R (Summon: Tibbers) range, or to absorb enemy poke. You can also cast it on an ally; summoned Tibbers always receives its effects, so use E right after summoning him if you want him to survive longer.
notes.annie-skill-r-tibbers: Learning R (Summon: Tibbers) passively grants magic penetration, increasing the damage of Annie’s other abilities. Cast R again to direct Tibbers toward fleeing enemies or check vision in a bush. He becomes enraged and moves much faster when Annie stuns an enemy or dies, so her death does not necessarily end the fight.
notes.annie-laning: While the stun is unavailable, stay behind the middle of the lane and last hit with Q (Disintegrate). Once the stacks are full, start a combo as the opponent steps forward to last hit a minion; if those two conditions do not coincide, wait.
notes.annie-laning-roam: Annie’s roam is especially threatening with her stun ready because she can use it as soon as she arrives. Push the wave before moving to a side lane, but do not spend all your stacks clearing it and arrive without the stun.
notes.annie-phase: Annie can stun from level 1, giving her early kill opportunities. Her level 6 R (Summon: Tibbers) and stun combo is her first major power spike, and her burst is strongest in the mid game with two or three ability power items. Her short range and lack of mobility make engaging harder later, so use earlier leads to close out the game.
notes.annie-teamfight: Annie’s teamfight often hinges on a single R (Summon: Tibbers) engage. Wait until the stun is ready and two or three opponents group together, then engage only from a position where your allies can follow up immediately; Annie has no way to escape afterward.
notes.annie-teamfight-peel: If there is no opening to engage in a teamfight, stay back and guard your allied carry. Stun enemies who reach that ally and cast Molten Shield (E) on the ally rather than yourself; summoning Tibbers (R) early and placing him in front of your team keeps incoming enemies burning and makes them hesitate to engage.
notes.annie-situational-tenacity: After engaging with R (Summon: Tibbers), Annie has no mobility ability to escape. If the opposing team has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, fit Quicksilver Sash between your core items to cleanse one crowd control effect after going in.
notes.vs-annie-passive: A white swirl around Annie means her stun is ready, so stay outside her ability range while it is visible. Once she uses the stun, pressure her before she can rebuild the stacks.
notes.vs-annie-no-mobility: Annie has no mobility ability, and her health and defenses are among the lowest. Close in when her stun is unavailable, leaving her few ways to respond; if you have forced her to use Flash, a jungle gank can secure the kill.
notes.vs-annie-tibbers: Summoned Tibbers continuously burns nearby enemies, so keep your distance even after killing Annie. Her death enrages him and makes him faster, and he can be dealt with using Smite.
notes.vs-annie-teamfight: Most of Annie’s teamfight impact rests on a single area stun from Summon: Tibbers (R). If she is out of sight or her stun is ready, avoid standing together in groups of two or three. R has short range, so she must move forward to use it; decide in advance who will take her down immediately when she does.
notes.vs-annie-range: Annie’s abilities have relatively short range for a mage, so poke her from a distance. Against a longer range opponent, she must spend health and mana to move forward; look for that moment.
notes.vs-annie-mr: All of Annie’s damage is magic, and learning R (Summon: Tibbers) grants her magic penetration. Build enough magic resistance to survive her burst, then counterattack after her combo.
notes.aphelios-skill-weapon-cycle: Aphelios carries a main weapon and an off-hand weapon, and his basic attacks and abilities consume ammo. When the main weapon runs out, it moves to the back of the rotation and the next weapon takes its place. Your weapon combination depends on where you spend ammo, so even using it on minions can change what you carry into the next fight.
notes.aphelios-skill-e-preview: The E slot shows which weapon is coming next. Check the E slot to anticipate your weapon combination for the next wave, gank, or objective.
notes.aphelios-skill-w: W Phase swaps your main and off-hand weapons, while Q always uses the main weapon’s ability. Bring the weapon you want forward with W, use Q, then swap back with W. Its cooldown is short enough to swap twice during a combo, but swapping does not restore ammo.
notes.aphelios-skill-calibrum: Calibrum is a poke weapon: its Q marks a target, and consuming the mark lets you attack once more from beyond your normal range. This is the one weapon phase in which you can win a trade without closing the distance, but its immediate damage is low, so avoid starting a direct fight.
notes.aphelios-skill-gravitum: Gravitum Q roots every enemy slowed by Gravitum, so apply the slow with basic attacks before using Q. With Gravitum in your off-hand, slow multiple enemies, then bring it forward with W and use Q for an area root. Time your team’s engage around this rotation.
notes.aphelios-skill-infernum: Infernum is an area-damage weapon: its Q attacks in a cone, followed by one attack with the off-hand weapon. Its wave clear and teamfight area damage make this the phase to push the lane and prepare for a roam or objective.
notes.aphelios-skill-crescendum: Crescendum Q places a turret that uses the same weapon as your off-hand. Choose that weapon with W before placing the turret; pressing Q without considering the pairing can produce a much weaker turret for the same ammo.
notes.aphelios-skill-severum: Severum’s Q lets Aphelios move quickly while attacking nearby enemies with both his main and off-hand weapons. It is effectively his only way to reposition during a fight, so you can play farther forward while it is available, but if you use Q solely for damage, account for having no way out afterward.
notes.aphelios-combo-ult: R Moonlight Vigil attacks every champion it hits once more with your main weapon and applies that weapon’s on-hit effects. Choosing your main weapon with W before casting R is therefore a key part of the combo: Gravitum leads from an area slow into a root, while Infernum greatly increases area damage.
notes.aphelios-phase: Aphelios gains permanent stats instead of leveling abilities with skill points, so he has few of the level spikes other marksmen have. Q unlocking at level 2 and R at level 6 are the two clear exceptions; his power rises gradually otherwise. His item spikes are substantial, so focus on farming without taking losses early and look for fights after completing a core item.
notes.aphelios-laning: Adjust your laning to your weapon phase: poke enemies down with Calibrum, clear the wave to gain control with Infernum, and add Gravitum’s root to your support’s or jungler’s engage. When your weapon combination is unfavorable, avoid forcing a fight and manage your ammo.
notes.aphelios-teamfight: Aphelios has low movement speed and can only move quickly with Severum, so poor positioning in a teamfight can get you killed. Attack from behind your frontline using your range, rooting multiple enemies with Gravitum or damaging grouped enemies with Infernum as your current weapons allow. Do not force a role in the fight when your combination is poor.
notes.aphelios-situational-cc: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. Outside the Severum phase, you have no way to escape on your own.
notes.aphelios-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, add Mortal Reminder. Weapons apply different on-hit effects, but its healing reduction applies whichever weapon you attack with.
notes.vs-aphelios-weapon-read: Aphelios’s strength depends on the weapons he is holding. His E slot reveals the next weapon, so watch what is coming and trade when his current weapons have low immediate damage; you can win decisively even at the same level.
notes.vs-aphelios-gravitum: Gravitum Q roots anyone slowed by that weapon. If a Gravitum basic attack slows you, immediately move out of range, and do not stand close to allies while the slow is active.
notes.vs-aphelios-mobility: Aphelios has very little mobility and, without Severum, has no escape other than Flash. Catch him during that window and you can take him out before a teamfight begins.
notes.vs-aphelios-ult: R Moonlight Vigil must hit a champion to trigger, and every champion it hits takes one additional attack from Aphelios’s main weapon. The more tightly you group, the greater the damage, so spread out before engaging when he can use R.
notes.vs-aphelios-calibrum: A Calibrum mark lets Aphelios hit you once more from beyond his normal range. Retreat as soon as you are marked and preserve your health; if you keep taking damage during the Calibrum phase, you may lack the health to withstand an all-in during the Infernum and Gravitum phase.
notes.ashe-combo-q-prestack: Q Ranger's Focus requires stacks from basic attacks. Build them on minions before a fight so you can unleash empowered attacks as soon as it starts; although each attack fires multiple arrows, on-hit effects count it as a single basic attack.
notes.ashe-combo-engage: To engage, stun with R Enchanted Crystal Arrow, follow with W Volley for damage and a slow, then activate Q Ranger's Focus and keep attacking. R stuns longer the farther it travels, so try to land it from as far away as possible before closing in.
notes.ashe-skill-e: E Hawkshot stores charges and offers a safer way to scout than placing wards. Use it early to check unwarded objective areas and the enemy jungler's path, and don't let it sit at full charges. It reveals its flight path as well as its destination, so aim it along routes where enemies may gather.
notes.ashe-skill-r: R Enchanted Crystal Arrow can stun targets across virtually the entire map. Aim where an enemy is going, rather than where they are standing; a close-range hit has a shorter stun, so create distance before firing unless the situation is urgent. It is also valuable for plays in other lanes, so don't waste it on lane poke.
notes.ashe-skill-w-poke: W Volley is virtually Ashe's only lane poke. At low ranks, its long cooldown and high mana cost can cost you last hits if you use it carelessly, so fire only when you are confident it will hit, such as when the enemy support steps forward. Its cooldown drops significantly as it gains ranks, letting you poke more often.
notes.ashe-phase: Ashe can create kill opportunities with a single R Enchanted Crystal Arrow from early on, so her lane pressure rises noticeably after level 6. She has no way to escape on her own, however, and poor positioning can get her killed. With midgame items, her slow and range let her control teamfights, though she has less late-game burst damage than other marksmen.
notes.ashe-laning-wave: Ashe has no mobility ability, so avoid pushing the lane too far. Keep it pulled back and use P Frost Shot's slow to discourage enemies from approaching. Always consider the enemy jungler's possible approach routes, and check inside bushes with E Hawkshot before moving forward.
notes.ashe-laning-trade: In small bot-lane fights, let your support engage first, then follow with W Volley and basic attacks to keep the enemy slowed. Stepping forward to start the fight yourself leaves Ashe vulnerable to a counter-engage.
notes.ashe-laning-tower: Activate Q Ranger's Focus when taking a turret. Nearby minions let you build stacks quickly and use Q repeatedly, greatly increasing your damage to the turret. Push the lane, then look for a chance to attack it to secure your lane advantage.
notes.ashe-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and keep enemies who engage slowed, giving your team time to close in. Ashe has virtually no way to protect herself, so remain behind your frontline and move with your allies as soon as they start grouping.
notes.ashe-teamfight-r: Before a fight, decide whether R Enchanted Crystal Arrow will start the teamfight or stop an enemy engage. If your team has no other way to engage, it is your only way to start the fight, so don't spend it on poke or an escape.
notes.vs-ashe-mobility: Ashe has virtually no mobility or defensive tools, making her vulnerable once an enemy gets close. In lane and teamfights, commit your resources to creating a way to reach her.
notes.vs-ashe-r: Ashe’s R, Enchanted Crystal Arrow, travels in a straight line, so running straight away will get you hit. Keep changing direction to make your movement harder to predict, and avoid starting small skirmishes from outside vision while her R is available.
notes.vs-ashe-w: Ashe’s lane poke relies entirely on W Volley. Its fan-shaped spread can usually be dodged by stepping sideways, and the moment after she uses W is your chance to trade damage.
notes.vs-ashe-q-window: Once Ashe builds stacks with basic attacks and activates Q Ranger's Focus, her damage rises sharply for a short time. Keep your distance while it is active, then move in after it ends.
notes.ashe-combo-w-reset: W applies Frost Shot's slow to multiple enemies at once in a cone.
notes.ashe-skill-passive: P Frost Shot slows with both basic attacks and abilities. Ashe's critical strikes strengthen that slow instead of dealing bonus damage, making critical strike chance a way to keep enemies from escaping rather than a source of burst damage.
notes.vs-ashe-slow: P Frost Shot's slow refreshes with every basic attack, making it hard to escape by walking. Avoid staying within Ashe's basic attack range for long; when you approach, use a mobility ability to close the gap in one move.
notes.asol-skill-passive-stardust: Aurelion Sol’s growth depends on Stardust rather than levels or items. It stacks permanently when his abilities damage champions and is never lost on death: Q earns it by staying on the same enemy for a while, E earns it while champions remain inside, and R earns it for each champion hit. Minions and monsters that die inside E also grant Stardust, so farming drives his growth. Collect it from every wave, even in a lane you cannot win.
notes.asol-skill-q: Q (Breath of Light) deals full damage only to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Keep it on the same target long enough to trigger bonus damage and Stardust; repeatedly switching targets wastes that opportunity. Canceling immediately after casting briefly locks the ability, so avoid tapping it for short bursts of poke.
notes.asol-skill-w: Treat W (Astral Flight) as a way to strengthen Q (Breath of Light): during flight, Q’s cooldown and maximum channel duration are removed, and its base damage rises. Helping secure a takedown soon after damaging a champion refunds almost all of W’s cooldown, so use it when a takedown is within reach. Without one, W stays on cooldown for a long time; because channeling Q also halves flight speed, leave it off when flying to escape.
notes.asol-skill-e: E Singularity controls terrain rather than dealing damage. Lane minions and jungle monsters inside it have their movement speed reduced to zero, while champions are slowly pulled toward the center and executed if their health falls below the threshold there. As Aurelion Sol gains Stardust, both its area and execute threshold grow, making even a path covered by E dangerous to cross later in the game. Epic monsters cannot be executed.
notes.asol-skill-r: Once enough Stardust has accumulated, R changes from Falling Star, which stuns, into The Skies Descend, which knocks enemies up and adds a wide shockwave and a slow. Check which version is ready: use Falling Star to follow up on ganks or cut off escapes, and The Skies Descend to start teamfights.
notes.asol-combo-poke: When trading, place E (Singularity) first and layer Q (Breath of Light) over it. As E pulls the enemy toward its center, hold Q on one target long enough to trigger bonus damage and Stardust. Starting with Q lets the enemy sidestep and break contact.
notes.asol-combo-fight: In a full fight, use R to restrict movement, place E (Singularity), then fly in with W (Astral Flight) while continuously channeling Q (Breath of Light). Q has no channel duration limit during W, concentrating Aurelion Sol’s damage in that window. If the enemy remains inside E when the flight ends, they may fall below its execute threshold.
notes.asol-laning-early: Aurelion Sol’s health and armor are among the lowest, so at levels 1–5, catching waves takes priority over trading. Q (Breath of Light) hits the first target in its path, and a minion in front prevents full damage to the champion behind it. Poke only when your opponent steps beside the minion wave; otherwise, leave Q off.
notes.asol-laning-wave: To clear a wave, hold the minions in E (Singularity), then layer Q (Breath of Light) over it. Minions inside E have zero movement speed and cannot spread out, while each unit that dies there grants Stardust. Because farming provides permanent growth, giving up a wave to roam costs Aurelion Sol more than it does other mid laners.
notes.asol-phase: Aurelion Sol is weakest at levels 1–8, when he has little Stardust; focus on staying alive and farming waves. He grows much stronger in mid game once R is empowered and he has one core item. Later, Stardust keeps increasing E’s area and execute threshold as well as R’s impact area, turning him into a late-game carry. Buying time is part of his win condition.
notes.asol-teamfight: In teamfights, hold the frontline in place and keep applying Q (Breath of Light), whose maximum-health damage is effective against durable enemies. There is no need to overextend toward the backline. Channeling Q slows Aurelion Sol’s movement, so turn it on only after allies draw the enemy’s attention or R restricts their movement.
notes.asol-teamfight-objective: In the narrow terrain around an objective, E Singularity can block an approach. Champions can pass through it, but stepping into the center risks execution, so low-health enemies cannot cross. Before the teamfight begins, place E in a passage the enemy must take and position your allies on the opposite side.
notes.asol-situational-zhonya: If the enemy can dive onto you, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. Channeling Q (Breath of Light) keeps you in place, and W (Astral Flight) stays on cooldown for a long time without a takedown; you need a way to survive the initial engage long enough to deal damage.
notes.asol-situational-antiheal: Buy Morellonomicon when enemy healing becomes a problem. The sustained damage from Q (Breath of Light) and E (Singularity) keeps healing reduction applied for an extended period.
notes.vs-asol-stardust: Aurelion Sol’s strength scales with Stardust, which stacks permanently when his abilities damage champions and remains even if he dies. Taking unnecessary Q (Breath of Light) poke helps him grow, so step out of range to avoid it.
notes.vs-asol-q: Q (Breath of Light) deals full damage only to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies, so stand behind minions or an ally when he tries to poke. It must stay on the same target for a while to trigger bonus damage and Stardust; move out of its line of fire quickly to deny both.
notes.vs-asol-e: E (Singularity) executes enemies at its center when their health is below the threshold. If you are low, avoid even its edge. The pull is slow enough to walk out immediately after entering, so keep moving outward if you get caught.
notes.vs-asol-w: If Aurelion Sol helps secure a takedown after entering with W, he recovers almost all of its cooldown. Fight back when he enters with W and deny the takedown. Counterattack right after he uses W.
notes.vs-asol-r: Once Aurelion Sol has enough Stardust, R changes from a stun into a knockup with an area shockwave and slow. If your team groups up late in the game, a single empowered R can knock everyone up and decide the fight. Spread out before he engages, especially in narrow passages.
notes.vs-asol-early: Aurelion Sol’s early health and armor are among the lowest, and his only mobility tool is W (Astral Flight), which has a long cooldown. If your champion can close the gap, engage hard when W is down to stop him from scaling before he stacks Stardust.
notes.aurora-combo-q-recall: Q (Twofold Hex) hits twice: the first hit applies a curse, and recasting retrieves it, damaging enemies along its return path. Because the return damage scales with the target’s missing health, land an auto attack or E before retrieving it. The curse returns automatically when its duration ends, so line up the return path before then to avoid losing damage.
notes.aurora-combo-allin: For an all-in, land Q’s first hit, approach with W (Across the Veil), auto attack, use E (The Weirding), then retrieve Q. W’s stealth and movement speed give the opponent less time to react, while the auto attack builds passive stacks. E provides the final hit and hops Aurora backward to disengage; Q can still damage enemies along its return path from that distance.
notes.aurora-combo-teamfight: In teamfights, enter with R to slow enemies, use E inside the area, then retrieve Q. Enemies entering or leaving R's area are slowed. Aurora can travel between opposite sides of R's area.
notes.aurora-skill-passive: P (Spirit Abjuration) triggers after Aurora damages the same target multiple times, dealing damage based on their maximum health; when that target is a champion, a spirit follows Aurora and restores her health. Abilities alone may leave the stacks incomplete, so weave in auto attacks. This healing is her source of lane sustain: take short trades to build stacks, then back off, instead of relying only on ranged poke.
notes.aurora-skill-q: Use Q (Twofold Hex) differently for wave clear and champion poke: its return damage is greatly reduced against minions and monsters, so judge wave clear by the first hit, while the return is the main source of damage against champions. When chasing a fleeing opponent, delay the return as long as possible so it lands after they have lost more health.
notes.aurora-skill-w: W Across the Veil gives Aurora a hop, stealth, and a movement speed boost, and its cooldown resets when she takes part in an enemy champion takedown. In a dive where you can secure a kill, that reset lets you use W to engage and still have an escape. If a takedown is uncertain, remember that Aurora is a fragile ranged champion: engage with W only when you can count on the reset.
notes.aurora-skill-e: E (The Weirding) deals area damage and applies a strong slow before hopping Aurora backward. Use it as an opponent engages to counterattack and create distance at once. The hop goes opposite the cast direction, so check where you will land before casting; because the slow fades over time, use any follow-up ability immediately.
notes.aurora-skill-r: R (Between Worlds) can initiate a fight and control an area, trapping opponents or blocking their engage. You can recast it to end the zone early: keep it active when enemy reinforcements are outside, but end it and retreat with your team if your allies need to leave. Choose your entry point with Aurora’s ability to cross from one side of the zone to the other in mind.
notes.aurora-laning-trade: Land Q as your opponent steps forward for a last hit, then add an auto attack to build passive stacks before retrieving the curse. A cursed opponent may move off the straight return path between them and Aurora, disrupting their farming. Repeat these short trades and back off; the passive’s healing helps Aurora maintain her health.
notes.aurora-laning-roam: Push the wave, then use W Across the Veil to cross terrain and roam. Its hop, stealth, and movement speed boost can hide the final part of your approach even if the enemy has vision of you. Aurora’s damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks among the highest while her deaths are relatively low, which fits a pattern of poking safely in lane and spending the time you gain in other lanes.
notes.aurora-phase: Play carefully at levels 1–2, when Aurora has only Q and low armor. At level 3, W opens up trading and roaming; from level 6, R enables dives and teamfight initiation. Her laning statistics are stable, but her win rate rises after three core items, so aim to reach that point through safe poke and farming instead of forcing early kills.
notes.aurora-teamfight: Do not jump in first with R while opponents still have their engage abilities: Aurora’s low durability can leave her trapped inside her own zone. Wait until they have used their initiation abilities or an ally has applied crowd control, then use R to trap them, follow with E’s slow, and retrieve Q for area damage. You can move much more aggressively once W’s cooldown resets.
notes.aurora-situational-zhonya: If the opposing team has a lot of immobilizing crowd control aimed at Aurora, fit Zhonya’s Hourglass between core items. Her escapes depend on the hops from W and E, both of which are ineffective when she is immobilized; the item can also help her survive being trapped inside R’s zone after engaging.
notes.aurora-situational-antiheal: If opponents have a lot of healing, buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-aurora-q: Q (Twofold Hex) curses you on hit, then deals damage again when Aurora recasts it or its duration ends. That return damage follows the path between you and Aurora, so move off the straight line or change your angle to her substantially after being cursed to reduce the second hit.
notes.vs-aurora-missing-hp: Q Twofold Hex deals more damage on its return based on the target’s missing health, so trades against Aurora become sharply worse as your health falls. Below half health, staying nearby while cursed can quickly put you within kill range. If your health is in doubt, back off before Q returns.
notes.vs-aurora-w: If Aurora suddenly disappears, she has used the brief stealth from W (Across the Veil). Targeted abilities cannot hit her during it, so place an area ability where she may land instead of wasting a cast. Wait a moment and she will reappear.
notes.vs-aurora-w-reset: When retreating from a teamfight, don't leave a low-health ally behind where Aurora can chain another engage.
notes.vs-aurora-r: R (Between Worlds) slows enemies entering or leaving its zone. Retreat before the zone appears if you want to get out without taking that slow; if you stay inside, commit to fighting Aurora. She can cross from one side to the other, so chasing her directly may let her escape.
notes.vs-aurora-dive: Aurora has low armor growth, ordinary movement speed, and only E’s backward hop to create distance from an opponent who gets close. Engage once to draw out E, then catch her with a second engage. After level 6, account for R as well; when both E and W are down, she has few ways to escape.
notes.azir-skill-w-projection: Azir’s own attack range is short; his effective reach depends on where he places his W soldiers. When an enemy is near a soldier, that soldier attacks in a straight line, so judge damage angles from its position rather than Azir’s. One attack can hit multiple enemies lined up along that path, but if several soldiers hit the same target, damage drops sharply after the first and on-hit effects apply at half strength. Spread two soldiers apart to cover different angles instead of overlapping them.
notes.azir-skill-w-charges: W holds up to two charges, but place two soldiers at once only when you are certain of a kill; always keep one charge available. Placing a soldier beyond a wall and dashing to it with E is Azir’s only escape route, and E also grants a shield, so using it early while being chased has no downside. If you place a soldier poorly and run out of charges, you lose both your escape route and your means of dealing damage.
notes.azir-skill-q: Q sends soldiers to a targeted location, damaging and slowing enemies along their path. An enemy takes damage only once even if multiple soldiers pass through them, so use Q to reposition soldiers rather than to stack damage. Its cooldown is long early on, and a careless cast can cost you the entire next trade; use it only when you have a reason to place your soldiers at the destination.
notes.azir-skill-e: E dashes Azir to a soldier and grants a shield. Colliding with an enemy champion stops the dash and restores one soldier charge, so E can either create distance for an escape or carry Azir into an enemy to recover that charge. Decide where you want E to take you when you place the soldier.
notes.azir-skill-r-defense: Think of R as a defensive tool first: cast it as enemies engage your allies to push them away, then use the lingering soldier wall to block their path briefly. Allies can pass through it, giving them a route that diving melee enemies cannot use. In a narrow passage, the wall can trap the enemies trying to follow up.
notes.azir-skill-passive: Azir’s passive can raise a Sun Disc where a turret has fallen. It is especially valuable for defending an area after an allied turret is destroyed or holding ground after taking an enemy turret. The Disc has armor and magic resistance and lasts for a short time, so remember which destroyed turret sites lie near likely objective fights.
notes.azir-combo-poke: To poke, place a soldier in front of the enemy with W, attack through it, then move it toward the enemy with Q. Keep the attack command active as the soldier moves so it attacks again as soon as it arrives. If you cast Q first, the soldier ends up near the enemy while Azir remains farther away, so attack before repositioning it.
notes.azir-combo-shuffle: To push an enemy toward your allies, place a soldier behind them with W (Arise!), dash to it with E (Shifting Sands), then immediately cast R (Emperor's Divide) toward your team. R pushes the enemy away from Azir and into your team. E stops when it hits an enemy champion, so position the soldier at an angle that lets you get past them without colliding. If the combo fails, Azir is left alone among the enemy team; attempt it only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
notes.azir-laning-soldier-position: During laning, place a soldier between the enemy minions and champion. From there, it can secure last hits while threatening the champion if they approach. Placing soldiers only behind the minions lets you farm but gives up poke; placing them right next to the champion gives you poke but costs you last hits.
notes.azir-laning-mana: Each soldier costs mana to place and disappears when its duration ends. Replacing soldiers when nothing is happening drains your mana, leaving you without soldiers or mana when the enemy jungler arrives. Place them only when an opponent enters range or you need to last-hit; otherwise, it is better to stand without one. In patch 26.17 mid-lane statistics, Azir’s CS at 14 minutes ranks in the upper-middle range while his kill statistic ranks near the bottom, so aim to farm safely during lane.
notes.azir-phase: Azir is weakest early: his health and defensive stats are among the lowest, Q’s long cooldown leaves gaps between trades, and E is his only way to survive an enemy jungle gank. He takes shape in the mid game as Q’s cooldown shortens and soldiers become available more often, then becomes a hypercarry late as he builds both attack speed and ability power. Minimize losses early instead of seeking an advantage, and do not stand forward in lane when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.
notes.azir-teamfight: In teamfights, keep Azir back and send soldiers forward to deal sustained damage to the enemy frontline; Azir himself should never move to the front. Focus on when to cast R rather than looking for an opening to engage: the safest use is to push enemies away as they dive your backline. Push an enemy toward your allies only when your team is clearly winning the fight. Azir deals strong sustained damage but lacks burst, so avoid facing an enemy alone.
notes.azir-situational-antiheal: If the enemy frontline sustains through healing, buy Morellonomicon between core items so your soldiers' sustained attacks can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.azir-situational-banshee: If the enemy's main damage is magic and they have a targeted ability that starts an engage on Azir, buy Banshee's Veil to block that first ability and buy time to place soldiers.
notes.vs-azir-soldier-window: All of Azir’s damage comes from his sand soldiers, and Q has a cooldown after moving them. Approach while a soldier is stationary, avoiding the line it stands on; move around behind or beside it to close in on Azir himself.
notes.vs-azir-burst: Azir grows stronger as time goes on but lacks burst damage. Avoid extended trades and overwhelm him in a short burst. He is fairly fragile, so finish him as soon as you catch him; if you let him go, he will keep wearing you down with his soldiers.
notes.vs-azir-e: Azir escapes by using E to dash to a soldier placed beyond a wall. If he places one near a wall, block that route or engage before he can use it. E stops when it collides with an enemy champion, so standing in his intended path can interrupt the dash.
notes.vs-azir-r: R (Emperor's Divide) pushes enemies away and leaves a soldier wall briefly in place, which Azir’s allies can pass through. If you dive his team in a narrow passage, one R can push back everyone who went in and trap those following behind. Engage in an open area, approaching from multiple directions.
notes.vs-azir-early: Azir aims to farm safely behind his soldiers during laning. Close in when they expire or he runs low on mana, when he has few ways to fight back. He also lacks R before level 6, so pressure him early with your jungler to slow his growth.
notes.bard-combo-q-wall: Q (Cosmic Binding) stuns only if it hits a wall or a second enemy after passing through its first target. Fire it at an enemy with a wall behind them or when they line up with a minion; an isolated enemy in open space will only be slowed.
notes.bard-combo-r-setup: R (Tempered Fate) also affects allies, so aim it to avoid catching your allied damage dealer.
notes.bard-combo-r-defense: Use R to save an ally just as a finishing ability is about to hit them, breaking its target lock. You can also put a diving enemy in stasis to separate them from your allies.
notes.bard-skill-chime: Collecting chimes strengthens Bard’s meep attacks and increases his movement speed, but chasing them at the cost of leaving your lane partner alone is a poor trade. Pick up chimes when the wave is pushed out and the lane is safe, or along your recall route.
notes.bard-skill-meep: Meep empowered basic attacks are Bard’s way to harass: approach and hit the enemy when you have meeps, and don’t waste them on minions. With enough chimes, the attacks spread to nearby targets and slow them, making trades much more valuable.
