notes.bard-skill-w-charge: W (Caretaker’s Shrine) heals more as it charges over time, so place a shrine in advance and step on it later if healing isn’t urgent. Enemy champions destroy shrines by walking over them; put yours behind your allies, away from the enemy and the middle of the lane.
notes.bard-skill-e-both: Enemies can use E (Magical Journey) portals too. Before opening one to escape, check whether an enemy can follow; allies travel through them faster than enemies, but the route is open to both.
notes.bard-skill-e-entry: Travel through an E portal with your jungler or mid laner to start a fight from an unexpected angle.
notes.bard-phase: Bard is ordinary at levels 1–2 while he collects chimes, but stronger meep attacks and increased movement speed make his roams faster as they build up. From level 6, R can turn an objective fight around; later, his main roles are catching enemies out and intervening in teamfights.
notes.bard-laning-absence: Bard’s long absences leave his marksman holding the lane alone. Before roaming, check that the enemy has used their engage ability, choose a moment when the wave is moving toward your turret, and place W shrines for your partner.
notes.bard-laning-trade: In lane, slow the enemy with Q before trading with a meep attack. Choose fights near brush by a wall or at the river tri-brush, where the terrain also gives you a chance to stun with Q.
notes.bard-teamfight: In teamfights, Bard’s role is to catch enemies out and cut them off. Pin an engaging enemy against a wall with Q, or use R to briefly remove the enemy’s main damage dealer from the fight or stop someone arriving late. Bard should not stand at the front absorbing damage.
notes.bard-teamfight-objective: R affects Dragon and Baron too. As the enemy jungler prepares to Smite, put both the objective and the enemy in stasis to delay the Smite contest, and coordinate the timing with your jungler beforehand.
notes.vs-bard-shrine: Bard’s W shrines disappear when an enemy steps on them. If you see one in lane, adjust your path to remove it rather than letting Bard or his allies use it for free.
notes.vs-bard-portal: The opposing team can use Bard’s E portals too. If he opens one to escape, follow and chase when it’s safe; also keep your flank covered, since Bard can enter through a portal.
notes.vs-bard-ult: Bard's R affects allies, enemies, monsters, and turrets alike.
notes.vs-bard-q: Bard’s Q needs a wall or a second target to stun. Don’t stand with your back to a wall or line up with an ally or minion, and you’ll only be slowed.
notes.vs-bard-roam: Bard often leaves lane to collect chimes. When he disappears from view, you have a chance to create a 2v1 in bot lane; signal on the minimap at the same time, since he may appear in another lane.
notes.vs-bard-mobility: Bard’s E portal is his only escape tool. Make him use it, then look for another opening to close in and catch him.
notes.bard-combo-q-angle: If there’s no wall or another enemy behind your target, Q won’t stun. Before firing, take a few steps sideways to line up yourself, the target, and the wall; those two or three steps can turn the hit into a stun.
notes.belveth-combo-basic: In a standard fight, close in with Q and an auto attack, knock the enemy up with W, then re-engage with the reset Q. Hitting a champion with W resets Q’s cooldown in the direction W was cast, letting you dash that way once more immediately; without the reset, Bel’Veth’s engage ends after one Q.
notes.belveth-combo-e-timing: Activate E as the enemy starts their burst combo, rather than immediately after engaging: Bel'Veth takes much less damage and gains lifesteal while casting it. Using another ability or pressing E again ends it immediately, so avoid Q and W while relying on E to survive. When you only need to hold out briefly before escaping with Q, cancel E deliberately.
notes.belveth-skill-q-direction: Q has a separate cooldown for each direction, so you cannot dash the same way twice in a row but can immediately dash in another direction. Use that to move and dodge in a zigzag, changing directions with Q as you escape instead of fleeing in a straight line.
notes.belveth-skill-q-onhit: Q (Void Surge) applies on-hit effects to the first target it hits, making it both a dash and the equivalent of one basic attack. Because it becomes a major source of damage when Bel'Veth builds on-hit items, line it up to pass through enemies in fights instead of using it only to move. Its cooldown also shortens as attack speed rises, so building attack speed improves her mobility.
notes.belveth-skill-w: W (Above and Below) is Bel'Veth's only guaranteed crowd control and resets Q. Using it too early in a gank lets the enemy escape with a mobility ability after being knocked up, leaving her without a way to close the gap. Draw out their mobility ability or Flash first, or use W to cut off their direction of travel when they are on the opposite side of their escape route.
notes.belveth-skill-passive: Lavender stacks from Death in Lavender grant permanent attack speed: a takedown on a large minion or monster grants one, while a takedown on a champion or epic monster grants two. Bel’Veth’s late-game strength depends on those stacks, so secure takedowns on large jungle monsters and join team fights to keep scaling. After using an ability, she briefly gains bonus attack speed and ghosting; use Q once when you need to pass through minions.
notes.belveth-skill-r-coral: Bel’Veth can use R to transform into her true form only by consuming Void Coral, which drops after she takes part in a champion or epic monster takedown. Check where the coral lands immediately after a kill in a fight. The transformation increases maximum health, attack range, and attack speed, so once you have coral, use it just before the next fight or objective contest rather than saving it.
notes.belveth-skill-r-voidling: Coral left by a Void epic monster differs from ordinary coral: transforming with it turns nearby minions that die into Void Remora, which push the lane for you. After taking a Void objective, choose the lane you want to pressure and transform near it.
notes.belveth-jungle-clear: Keep your jungle clear moving by using Q (Void Surge) between camps and maintaining your rotation. It deals bonus damage to monsters, and its cooldown is tracked by direction, so you can use it within a camp as well. In camps that cost you health, activate E (Royal Maelstrom) to heal through lifesteal while clearing and save blue essence or potions.
notes.belveth-jungle-gank: Bel’Veth cannot make a gank work with W alone. Look for lanes where an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed up and has a long way to escape. If a gank looks uncertain before level 6, clear large monsters for stacks and establish vision around objectives instead.
notes.belveth-phase: Bel'Veth is weakest at levels 1–3, when both her health and attack damage are low, so avoid encounters with the enemy jungler then. Duels become viable in the mid game after maxing Q, completing your first core item, and beginning to build stacks; she peaks in the late game once she has enough stacks. Because her early game stats are generally among the lowest, getting through that phase without falling behind is itself a successful start.
notes.belveth-teamfight: Bel’Veth should not lead the front line in team fights. Once your tank absorbs the enemy engage, flank into the backline with Q, kill one enemy, and use Q to get out. If targeted abilities focus you right after you engage, activate E; after a takedown, consume the dropped coral to transform and gain an advantage in the next fight. E needs no target and automatically attacks the lowest-health enemy, making it especially useful for finishing opponents in chaotic fights.
notes.belveth-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents your sustained damage from securing kills, buy Executioner’s Calling first and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Auto attacks and Q’s on-hit effects let Bel’Veth keep reapplying Grievous Wounds.
notes.belveth-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities that can lock Bel’Veth down, fit Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar between core items. She survives by keeping Q available to move, so removing the time she spends immobilized is more valuable than building armor.
notes.vs-belveth-early: Bel’Veth has low health and attack damage at levels 1–3, making jungle invades and early encounters strong opportunities to pressure her. Take large monsters and camps before she builds stacks to slow her growth.
notes.vs-belveth-w: W (Above and Below) is Bel'Veth's only guaranteed crowd control. Dodging it denies her Q reset and greatly slows her pursuit, leaving her only Q to stay close. When she reaches you, turn sideways to avoid W instead of running straight back.
notes.vs-belveth-e: Bel’Veth takes much less damage while standing still and casting E, so using burst abilities into it wastes their damage. Wait until E ends before using them, or interrupt the cast with immobilizing crowd control.
notes.vs-belveth-q: Bel’Veth’s Q has a separate cooldown for each direction, so she cannot immediately dash again in the direction she just used. When escaping or aiming a skillshot, use the line she just dashed along as your reference.
notes.vs-belveth-coral: Bel’Veth needs a champion or epic monster takedown to obtain Void Coral and transform, so giving her even one kill makes the next fight much harder. If an ally dies in a fight, retreat before she collects the coral rather than re-engaging there, and delay team fights while she is transformed.
notes.blitz-combo-basic: The basic combo is Q to pull a target in, E to knock them up, then R to finish. Chained without gaps, these abilities leave a squishy target no time to fight back; landing the combo within your turret’s range makes it much deadlier by adding turret attacks.
notes.blitz-combo-e-prefire: Activate E just before Q hits so you knock the target up as soon as they are pulled in. Waiting until after the pull gives them time to escape with a mobility ability, so anticipate the hit and activate E early.
notes.blitz-combo-w-e-first: If you are unsure you can land Q, reverse the order: approach with W, knock the target up with E, then land Q while they are airborne or as they start to flee. Your approach will be visible, so check that the enemy has used their crowd control and start from brush.
notes.blitz-combo-e-reset: E resets your basic attack timer, so when harassing, use it immediately after a basic attack to land two attacks in quick succession.
notes.blitz-skill-q: Q pulls only the first enemy it hits along its path, so wait until your target moves away from minions or hide in brush to conceal your range. Its high mana cost and long cooldown mean spamming it early can cost you the entire laning phase. Simply holding Q also creates pressure, and keeping it to make the enemy back off is often better than throwing it at an uncertain angle.
notes.blitz-skill-w: W helps Blitzcrank approach or escape, though its self-slow when it ends makes it less useful for getting away. Its large attack speed boost is also valuable against objectives, so activate a saved W when you start attacking Dragon or Rift Herald.
notes.blitz-skill-r: R has a short cooldown for an ultimate, so you can use it to push waves, disrupt a siege, or clear minions to open a Q angle. Its passive lightning triggers automatically when you enter combat and may hit an enemy unintentionally, so account for that when sneaking up.
notes.blitz-skill-r-hold: In an extended one-on-one fight without minions, it is better to hold R: after several hits, its passive lightning deals more damage than the active cast. Use R when you need immediate burst damage or a silence, or when you need to remove an enemy shield.
notes.blitz-phase: At level 1, Q’s high mana cost and long cooldown leave Blitzcrank with little threat for a while after he uses it. His grab pressure takes hold at levels 2–3 and stays strong through the early and mid game. Later, he cannot kill a target alone, so a grab without allied follow-up can work against you.
notes.blitz-laning: Laning as Blitzcrank revolves around brush vision: controlling brush conceals your grab range, while enemy vision leaves few openings. When Q is on cooldown, fall back instead of stepping forward and protect your ally as they farm.
notes.blitz-laning-invade: Q is especially strong in narrow jungle chokepoints. Join early invades to catch the enemy jungler there or create a chance to steal a camp; if your lane is stable, pressure jungle routes with your allies.
notes.blitz-teamfight: Blitzcrank cannot kill a healthy target alone, so throw Q only when allies can follow up immediately. After engaging, stay on the target with E and W to maintain pressure and give your allies the confidence to follow in.
notes.blitz-situational-thornmail: If the enemy's main damage is physical and they also have healing, choose Thornmail for both armor and healing reduction.
notes.vs-blitz-minion: Q pulls only the first target it hits along its path. Keep minions between you and Blitzcrank in lane by standing behind them, rather than beside them, to block the grab.
notes.vs-blitz-cooldown: At level 1, Q costs a lot of mana and has a long cooldown. Immediately after Blitzcrank misses it, he poses no threat for a while, so use that window to push the lane or trade.
notes.vs-blitz-mana: Q costs a lot of mana, so watch Blitzcrank’s mana bar: when he is out of mana and cannot grab, you have a safe window.
notes.vs-blitz-peel: Blitzcrank lacks the damage to finish a target with crowd control alone. Bypass him and engage on his allies behind him; he can protect only one of them, giving your team the advantage.
notes.vs-blitz-shield: When Blitzcrank gets low on health, Mana Barrier (P) gives him a shield that scales with mana, making him harder to kill than he looks. Secure a way to finish him before committing to a kill in one burst.
notes.vs-blitz-vision: Without brush vision, you cannot see Blitzcrank’s grab range. Clear the brush with Control Wards, and keep well away from it when moving through areas without vision.
notes.blitz-skill-passive: Mana Barrier activates when Blitzcrank falls below 30% health, and its shield scales with maximum mana rather than decreasing as he spends mana. Items that increase maximum mana strengthen it; after it triggers, account for the time without a shield during its cooldown when looking for an engage.
notes.brand-skill-passive-blaze: Blaze is central to Brand’s damage. Abilities apply stacks, and reaching maximum stacks on a champion or large jungle monster triggers an explosion shortly afterward that deals area damage based on maximum health. Build combos around applying stacks in the right order. When farming, apply Blaze before last-hitting a burning unit to restore mana.
notes.brand-skill-q: Q Sear stops at the first enemy it hits and stuns only a target that is already burning. Opening with Q will not stun, and a minion can block it, so use it when the target is burning and the projectile’s path is clear of minions.
notes.brand-skill-w: W Pillar of Flame erupts after a warning, giving enemies time to walk out. Place it ahead of their movement or layer it over an ally’s immobilizing effect or your Q stun. It deals more damage to burning targets, so apply Blaze first; its long range also makes it Brand’s only poke that minions cannot block.
notes.brand-skill-e: E Conflagration spreads around its target, with twice the spread range if that target is burning. Set a minion on fire, then use E to reach an enemy champion standing beside it. Even the threat of that spread makes it hard for enemies to stand near their minions.
notes.brand-skill-r: R Pyroclasm prioritizes champions with fewer Blaze stacks when it bounces. Among many clustered enemies, it is harder to hit the same target repeatedly; with fewer targets, it bounces back to one target more often. Count the available targets before casting: use R to spread stacks in larger fights and to concentrate damage on one target in smaller fights.
notes.brand-combo-stun: The key to a stun combo is to avoid opening with Q. At range, apply Blaze with W, then stun with Q; when the enemy is already close, E into Q is faster. Either way, Blaze must be on the target before Q arrives.
notes.brand-combo-burst: For single-target burst, use W → Q stun → E → W. The Q stun lets you land the delayed second W, while Blaze reaches maximum stacks and adds an explosion. W deals more damage to a burning target, and E spreads twice as far from one, so changing the order greatly reduces what you get from the same abilities.
notes.brand-combo-aoe: When several enemies are grouped, set them on fire with W, then spread Blaze with E. For an area combo, build stacks with W and E, then use R.
notes.brand-laning: In lane, focus on poking with W. Its long range and ability to pass through minions let you place it where the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit. It costs a lot of mana, though, and Brand’s health is among the lowest in the game; linger within enemy range after a poke and you can die on the spot. Brand’s 14-minute death count is statistically among the highest for supports, reflecting that risk.
notes.brand-laning-allin: Go all in when the enemy has Blaze and Q is available. Check that they are burning before engaging: landing Q then guarantees a long stun, giving your marksman time to land basic attacks while you use W and E. An all-in opened without Blaze will not work.
notes.brand-phase: Brand’s damage comes mainly from Blaze explosions rather than individual abilities, so his trades grow stronger around levels 3–6, when he can chain at least two abilities. He peaks in the mid game as he builds ability power. Late in the game, his health remains among the lowest and he has no mobility ability, so getting picked off first leaves him unable to contribute to a teamfight. His late-game value depends on positioning rather than damage.
notes.brand-teamfight: Stay in the back during teamfights and deal area damage without diving in. Wait for enemies to group, apply Blaze with W, spread it with E, then cast R. Blaze’s maximum-health-based explosion also damages the frontline, so there is no need to move forward to target the backline.
notes.brand-teamfight-choke: R needs nearby targets to keep bouncing and stops early when enemies spread out. Cast it in narrow passages near objectives or when the enemy formation tightens. If they have already spread out, save R and use E and W to keep Blaze on the frontline.
notes.brand-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to keep Grievous Wounds active longer through damage over time.
notes.vs-brand-blaze: Brand’s threat comes from Blaze stacks rather than individual abilities: consecutive hits build toward an explosion. Dodging his first Q or W breaks the combo, so focus on avoiding that opening hit.
notes.vs-brand-q: Brand's Q stuns only burning enemies. If you are on fire, move out of Q's path or hide behind a minion. Move after Blaze wears off.
notes.vs-brand-cluster: Brand’s E spreads twice as far from a burning target, while R bounces between enemies. If you cluster together, a hit on one player can spread to everyone, so space out before engaging and stay away from any ally who is burning.
notes.vs-brand-r: Brand’s R starts with a slow projectile, giving you time to spread out after you see the cast. Move away from allies immediately; if you are burning, move even earlier because R will also slow you.
notes.vs-brand-minions: Brand can poke indirectly by applying Blaze to a minion wave and spreading it with E. Avoid last-hitting beside a burning minion, and step to the side before moving in where the waves meet.
notes.vs-brand-punish: Brand has very low health and no mobility abilities, so engage as soon as he uses W if he remains in range. Once you get close, his only response is a Q stun, and he cannot land that stun unless you already have Blaze.
notes.braum-skill-passive: Concussive Blows begins when Braum applies the first mark; allied basic attacks can then add stacks. The final stack stuns the target and deals magic damage, so Braum needs his marksman to attack the same target to complete the crowd control. Agree on a target with your ally before starting a trade.
notes.braum-skill-passive-window: For a short time after the stun, stacks cannot build again, but Braum's basic attacks deal bonus damage, so staying close and attacking is still worthwhile. The mark does not last long: if allies fail to follow up on the first stack, it expires.
notes.braum-skill-w: Braum can use W (Stand Behind Me) to leap to allied minions as well as champions, making minions useful for repositioning. On arrival, both Braum and his target gain armor and magic resistance, with Braum receiving the larger bonus. W protects an ally while making Braum tougher, so use it to jump toward an ally just before Braum takes a beating.
notes.braum-skill-e: E (Unbreakable) intercepts and destroys projectiles from the direction Braum faces, negating damage from the first and reducing damage from those that follow. It cannot block attacks from the side or behind, so stand in front of your ally and put yourself between them and the enemy marksman. Because the shield lasts only a short time, raise it when you see a key enemy skillshot being cast.
notes.braum-skill-r: R (Glacial Fissure) has a noticeably long cast animation before sending a fissure straight ahead. Its first target is knocked up longer the farther they are from Braum, so aim that first hit at a distant key target rather than an enemy nearby. The lingering fissure creates a strong slowing zone that acts as a barrier.
notes.braum-combo-engage: Start an engage by landing Q (Winter's Bite) to slow the target and apply the first Concussive Blows stack, then close the gap with W (Stand Behind Me) to a forward minion or ally and use basic attacks to add the remaining stacks for a stun. Allied basic attacks stack Concussive Blows much faster, so signal which target to attack as soon as Q hits.
notes.braum-combo-ult-chain: After knocking an enemy up with R, land Q just before they touch down to add a slow and a stack. They cannot use movement abilities while airborne, so following R with Q and basic attacks can carry the crowd control straight into a stun.
notes.braum-combo-peel: Hit a nearby enemy with Q, leap to the ally you need to protect with W, then raise E toward the threat.
notes.braum-phase: Braum is fairly strong in lane: from level 1, Q can start a trade, and he has high defensive stats. At level 6, R gives him a way to force an engage and control terrain, while defensive items keep him strong through the mid game. His own damage is very low late, though, so his impact drops sharply if his allies have fallen behind.
notes.braum-laning: Throw Q when a gap opens between minions or an enemy steps up to last-hit. When Q hits, move in with your allies to build Concussive Blows stacks. If Q misses, back off and wait for it to come off cooldown. Use your positioning to limit the enemy marksman's space and keep them from stepping forward.
notes.braum-laning-vision: Braum gains little from roaming: his movement speed is ordinary, and W needs an ally or minion, so he cannot move quickly alone. Stay in lane to protect your marksman, maintain vision around the river and bushes, and use Q and E to delay an incoming enemy jungler.
notes.braum-teamfight: In teamfights, stand between your backline and the enemy damage dealers. Stay beside your marksman and use R lengthwise against enemies diving in to split their formation, placing the lingering fissure across the path of their follow-up so the fight is divided in two.
notes.braum-situational-cleanse: If the enemy can immobilize and burst down your marksman, buy Mikael's Blessing earlier. Braum can block attacks with his body, but he cannot remove crowd control already applied to an ally.
notes.vs-braum-stacks: Braum's stun requires several stacks. Once marked, move out of range before the remaining stacks build to avoid the stun entirely; standing still and taking more hits is the worst choice.
notes.vs-braum-q: Braum needs to land Q or a basic attack to apply the first Concussive Blows mark. Q stops at the first enemy it hits, so stand behind minions to block it and avoid lining up with Braum when a gap opens between them.
notes.vs-braum-e: Projectiles cannot get through E from the direction Braum faces. Wait for the shield to drop, or move around his side to attack from outside that direction. If your marksman keeps attacking from the front, Braum can shield his team from your team's damage.
notes.vs-braum-r: Braum's R has a long enough cast animation to react: dodge sideways out of its straight path and position early to avoid the slowing zone it leaves behind. The farther its first target is from Braum, the longer the knockup, so backline champions should be especially careful to stay off that line.
notes.vs-braum-damage: Braum deals very little damage himself. Instead of trying to kill him, target the ally he is protecting or find another route past him to the backline. If you pour damage into Braum, he has already done his job.
notes.braum-skill-q: Q (Winter's Bite) hits only the first enemy in its path, heavily slowing them and applying a Concussive Blows stack. Minions block it, so look for gaps between them in lane; as Braum's main way to start a trade from range, a missed Q makes that trade hard to begin.
notes.briar-combo-gank: For a gank, stun the target with Q (Head Rush), activate W (Blood Frenzy), land a basic attack, then recast W (Snack Attack). Use Q first because Blood Frenzy takes away Briar’s ability to choose her target; locking onto the intended enemy before activating W keeps her from attacking someone else.
notes.briar-combo-r: In teamfights, land R's bloodstone to trigger an area fear on arrival, then stun with Q, land a basic attack, recast W for the bite, and finish with E. The bloodstone also interrupts an enemy's channel on hit, so use it to stop channeled ultimates. If the enemy is escaping toward a wall, fully charge the finishing E to stun them against it.
notes.briar-skill-passive: Briar has no base health regeneration and spends current health whenever she uses an ability, so standing still will not heal her; she must keep attacking and maintain bleed stacks. The more health she is missing, the more she recovers, so low health alone is not a warning sign, but casting abilities in quick succession while low costs her even more health.
notes.briar-skill-w-control: Activating W taunts Briar toward the nearest enemy and takes away your control, so treat it as a damage boost after choosing a target, not as an engage tool. Use Q to reach that target first; if the enemy frontline is in front of you, opening with W can pull you toward the wrong opponent.
notes.briar-skill-w-recast: Recasting W (Snack Attack) empowers Briar’s next basic attack to deal damage based on the target’s missing health and heal her for that amount. Wait until the enemy has lost health to get more value from it, but if Briar is in danger and needs the healing, use it immediately instead of waiting for a finishing blow.
notes.briar-skill-w-jungle: Using Q on a minion or monster during Blood Frenzy removes Briar’s priority for attacking champions. This can keep a passing champion from drawing her away while she clears a camp, but avoid using Q on a monster when you need to chase a champion.
notes.briar-skill-e: E (Chilling Scream) is Briar’s only way to end Blood Frenzy herself and regain control. Charging it reduces incoming damage and heals her based on her maximum health, making it useful for survival in fights and recovery while hunting. A fully charged scream knocks enemies back and stuns them if they hit a wall, so charge it all the way against an enemy with a wall behind them; in open space, release it early for damage and a slow.
notes.briar-skill-r: The first champion hit by R’s (Certain Death) bloodstone becomes Briar’s prey, so your aim determines the target. Fire from an angle where the frontline cannot block the shot if you want to reach a particular enemy. On landing, Briar fears nearby enemies other than her prey, allowing her to engage and split up a grouped team at once.
notes.briar-jungle-clear: At jungle camps, use Blood Frenzy's area basic attacks, then charge E to heal when your health drops.
notes.briar-jungle-gank: Briar ranks among the highest champions for kill participation at 14 minutes, but her death statistics are also near the bottom. Her ganks are strong, yet a failed engage can quickly get her killed. Gank lanes where an ally has guaranteed crowd control or the enemy has pushed up; if there is no opening, leave W off because its taunt prevents you from turning back.
notes.briar-phase: Once Briar has Q, W, and E and unlocks R at level 6, she can find solo kills. She peaks in the mid game when she has both attack damage and health, but her level 18 health ranks among the lowest of all champions, so engaging first in a late game teamfight can get her killed before she heals. Later on, let an ally start the fight, then go in to finish it.
notes.briar-teamfight: Briar chases one target relentlessly, so choose an R target your allies can attack alongside you right away. Landing alone in the enemy backline leaves her surrounded when the fear ends; enter after an ally lands the first crowd control, and if the fight turns bad during Blood Frenzy, use E to end it and regain control—her only way to retreat.
notes.briar-situational-antiheal: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Briar’s bleed and area basic attacks spread damage in small hits, making healing reduction easy to maintain; in a fight where both sides rely on healing, the side that applies it first wins.
notes.briar-situational-qss: Consider Mercurial Scimitar against a long root. Briar heals only while she is close enough to land basic attacks, so time spent rooted and unable to attack costs her health.
notes.vs-briar-w: Put your frontline in Briar's path when she dives with W to protect your backline carry. When Briar engages with W, the backline carry should not stand in front.
notes.vs-briar-e: Crowd control during E’s (Chilling Scream) charge can stop both Briar’s healing and her wall stun. As soon as she begins charging the scream, use a stun or knockup, and avoid fighting with your back to a wall because a fully charged E can stun anyone it knocks into one.
notes.vs-briar-passive: If you encounter Briar in the jungle, damage her to delay her next move.
notes.vs-briar-r: R’s (Certain Death) bloodstone makes the first champion it hits Briar’s prey, so keep your frontline ahead of your backline carry to block the shot. Once marked, you are hard to escape by running alone: Briar gains resistances and movement speed as she chases you to the end. Move toward your allies as soon as you become the prey and fight back together.
notes.vs-briar-early: Push the lane and secure vision to prepare for Briar's ganks. Without vision, don't stand in the middle of the lane for long.
notes.caitlyn-combo-trap-q: Place W under the enemy or where they will retreat; when the trap triggers, follow with a Headshot and then Q. A trapped target is within Headshot range from much farther away and takes full Q damage, making the moment just after the trap triggers your best chance to deal maximum damage.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-headshot: Landing E increases Headshot range against that target. Follow up with a Headshot, place W where they will retreat, then use Q; treat E as a way to set up Headshot, not as a way to hold the enemy in place.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-reposition: Fire E away from the enemy to propel Caitlyn backward. Use that recoil to create distance or escape over a wall.
notes.caitlyn-skill-passive: Headshot activates after a set number of basic attacks and charges faster when you attack from brush. Move in and out of lane brush to charge it, then use it on a champion; avoid hitting minions once it is ready.
notes.caitlyn-skill-w: W can store multiple charges, so place traps before a fight to have its cooldown ready when the fight starts. Put them where enemies must pass, such as brush entrances, jungle approaches, or behind you.
notes.caitlyn-skill-e-keep: E is Caitlyn's only escape. Using it to poke leaves you unable to respond to an enemy engage, so save it until you have confirmed that the enemy has used their engage ability.
notes.caitlyn-skill-r: Another enemy champion can intercept R, so avoid using it in chaotic fights. Use it to finish a fleeing target, a duel opponent, or an enemy in another lane only when no one can block its path; Caitlyn remains stationary while casting.
notes.caitlyn-phase-early: Caitlyn's long range lets her pressure opponents from level 1, even without items. Laning is her strongest phase, so build an early lead through CS and turret pressure.
notes.caitlyn-phase-late: In the mid to late game, Caitlyn's raw damage falls behind that of other marksmen with strong sustained damage. Her power peaks when she converts a lane lead into turrets and objectives; afterward, use her range advantage to deal damage from a safe position.
notes.caitlyn-laning-push: Caitlyn ranks among the best in CS and turret plating. Use her range advantage to push the wave first, pin the enemy under their turret, and break its plates. While the wave is pushed, place W at river approaches to guard against ganks.
notes.caitlyn-laning-trade: Trade only when Headshot is ready. Poking with basic attacks without it wastes your range advantage and gives the enemy an opening to close in; after a trade, immediately back out of their range to deny an engage.
notes.caitlyn-teamfight: In teamfights, attack from the edge of Caitlyn's maximum range and place W along enemy approach routes and around your feet to stop opponents from closing in. With no mobility ability, secure your position before the fight starts and save E solely to interrupt an engage.
notes.caitlyn-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Caitlyn's range lets her keep attacking throughout teamfights and maintain its healing reduction.
notes.vs-caitlyn-r: Caitlyn’s R, Ace in the Hole, hits another enemy champion instead if they stand in the bullet’s path. If an ally is targeted, step into its path to block the shot for them.
notes.vs-caitlyn-rooted-cast: Caitlyn stands still while casting Q or R. When you see either cast animation, close in or find an angle to attack; the best time to engage is just after she uses Q to clear the wave.
notes.vs-caitlyn-trap: Stepping on a W trap roots you, extends Caitlyn's Headshot range against you, and exposes you to heavy damage. Assume traps are placed in brush and narrow passages; change your approach or send minions ahead.
notes.vs-caitlyn-e: Caitlyn's E, 90 Caliber Net, is her only escape and moves her through recoil. Engage after she uses it, when she has no way to create distance.
notes.vs-caitlyn-phase: Caitlyn is strongest in lane and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid taking unnecessary risks and giving her kills early; even farming CS under your turret will improve the matchup.
notes.caitlyn-skill-q: Q deals reduced damage to targets beyond the first and leaves Caitlyn stationary while she aims. Firing it at a champion behind minions wastes damage, so use it only when the enemy steps clear of the minions or is caught in a trap.
notes.vs-caitlyn-q: Caitlyn's Q, Piltover Peacemaker, passes through targets but deals reduced damage after the first. When she uses it to poke, stand behind allied minions so they take the first hit.
notes.camille-combo-trade: In lane, trade with an auto attack → first Q → wait → second Q. Delaying the recast greatly increases Q’s bonus damage and converts part of it to true damage, so weave in another auto attack between casts when you have time. Catch the enemy with W’s outer edge as well to slow them and heal yourself.
notes.camille-combo-engage: Engage by using E to reach a wall → cast W while traveling on the hook → recast E for the collision stun → auto attack → first Q → second Q. Camille can cast W during the hook’s travel, so time its windup to finish as the leap ends and slow enemies even far from the wall. Open the fight with an auto attack on an enemy champion to activate your passive shield.
notes.camille-combo-ult: For a guaranteed kill, slow the enemy with W’s outer edge → trap them with R → auto attack → first Q → auto attack → second Q. R has a short cast range, so first hold the enemy in place with E’s stun or W’s slow. Camille is untargetable during R’s cast, letting her ignore enemy crowd control and close in.
notes.camille-skill-q: Q is an on-hit ability that empowers Camille’s next basic attack, allowing both casts to trigger Spellblade effects such as Trinity Force. Its second hit converts part of the damage to true damage, bypassing armor. To land both hits, hold the enemy in place with E’s stun, W’s slow, or allied crowd control; because Q rides on basic attacks, wait until any attack negation, blind, or dodge has been used before committing it.
notes.camille-skill-w: W gets its value from the outer edge of its cone: only that portion deals bonus damage, slows the enemy, and heals Camille, providing her lane sustain and engage opportunities. Its windup can leave a nearby enemy inside the cone’s inner area, so step back before casting to catch them with the outer edge.
notes.camille-skill-e: E needs a wall for its hook to latch onto, though firing the hook does not count as movement and remains available while Camille is rooted. When she reaches the wall, E reveals the direction of nearby enemies, helping her spot a brush ambush. The leap gains range toward a visible enemy champion but stops at the first enemy it hits, so change your angle if someone stands in front of your target. Since Camille relies on E to engage, choose whom to catch before using it.
notes.camille-skill-passive: Camille’s passive shield activates only when she lands a basic attack on an enemy champion, granting either a physical or magic shield based on that enemy’s damage type. Hitting a minion will not trigger it, so open a fight with an auto attack to gain the shield before using abilities and committing. Because Camille gains little health as she levels, the shield effectively serves as a defensive stat.
notes.camille-item-vs-physical: If the opponent’s main damage is physical, Camille’s passive shield will be physical, complementing armor items. Buy Plated Steelcaps early, then build Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen to gain a substantial advantage in side-lane 1v1s.
notes.camille-item-vs-magic: If the opponent’s main damage is magic, Camille’s shield will be magic, making it efficient to build magic resistance alongside it. Choose Ionian Boots of Lucidity for ability haste; if burst is the problem, use Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team with long crowd control chains, buy Quicksilver Sash first.
notes.camille-phase: Camille’s low base stats and slow wave clear make her weakest at levels one and two. Start trading once Q and your passive shield are available; after learning R, you can take control of jungle skirmishes and follow up on ganks. Her strongest point is midgame with two core items. Late game, avoid a head-on fight with ranged carries and force 1v1s in the side lane instead.
notes.camille-laning: Start lane by chipping away with W’s outer edge while saving E. Lure the enemy toward a wall for an engage, but farm if they stand behind minions and far from walls. E and your passive shield have long cooldowns, so avoid trades while they are unavailable and preserve your health. Camille farms slowly; focus on CS and wait for a chance to join your jungler instead of forcing an early engage.
notes.camille-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to isolate one target. Trap the enemy’s main damage dealer to keep them from escaping while your team finishes them off; when R’s area appears, it knocks other enemies back and effectively forces a 1v1. Enter with your allies, since going in alone can leave you dead after catching just one target. If the teamfight setup is poor, push a side-lane turret to draw enemies out.
notes.vs-camille-e: Camille’s engage depends on E latching onto a wall. Against her in lane, stay away from walls, position among minions, and avoid being pushed toward a wall. She can cast W while traveling on the hook, so even positions a considerable distance from a wall can be within her threat range.
notes.vs-camille-e-interrupt: A knockback or pull can interrupt Camille’s E leap after her hook latches onto a wall. If interrupted, she loses both the collision stun and the attack speed increase, leaving her in melee range without her engage tool. Save your knockback or pull for the moment the hook catches the wall.
notes.vs-camille-r: Once trapped inside The Hextech Ultimatum (R), you have virtually no way out. Camille is untargetable as she enters, so crowd control used at that moment will not stop her; save your counter ability, survive until the area expires, then fight back. R has a very short cast range, so Camille must first hold you in place with Tactical Sweep (W)’s slow or Hookshot (E)’s stun. Dodge that setup or Flash away before she gets close, and R will not reach you.
notes.vs-camille-passive: Camille’s passive creates either a physical or magic shield based on the enemy’s damage type. Since it blocks only one type, attack with an ally who deals the other type to bring her down faster. Avoid trading immediately after the shield activates and approach once it wears off.
notes.vs-camille-q: Camille’s damage is concentrated in her Q-empowered auto attacks, and armor cannot reduce the true damage portion of her second Q. Attack negation, a blind, or stealth can deny that empowered attack. You can also create distance while she waits for the second Q, causing the attack to miss.
notes.vs-camille-early: Camille’s low early stats and slow wave clear leave her weakest before her first core item. Take lane control and deny farm before she completes it to keep delaying her items. From midgame onward, defend the side lane: left alone, she takes down turrets quickly.
notes.cass-combo-poke: The basic poke combo is Q → E. Hitting a champion with Q gives Cassiopeia a large movement speed boost, letting her follow while staying in E range. Q is both her damage ability and her only way to gain mobility, so walking forward to trade after missing it does not work.
notes.cass-combo-allin: The guaranteed combo is R → Q → repeated E: stun the target with R, place Q's poison where they stand so it takes full effect while they cannot move, then use E on the poisoned target whenever it comes off cooldown for maximum damage. You can get the same result by placing Q's poison first and casting R as the opponent rushes onto it.
notes.cass-skill-q: Q detonates at the targeted spot after a short delay, so aim ahead of where the opponent is walking rather than where they stand. The goal is to apply poison, not deal immediate damage; if a hit is uncertain, place Q early on a path they must cross or where they will step up to last-hit.
notes.cass-skill-e: E deals bonus damage and heals Cassiopeia only against a poisoned target, so poison first instead of spending mana on an unpoisoned one. Its cooldown is very short: keep casting it while Q’s poison lasts, and last-hit with E to refund mana and manage your resources as you farm.
notes.cass-skill-e-stationary: E is most valuable when you can use it repeatedly on a target that cannot move. While killing a monster or immediately after stunning an opponent with R, save your other abilities and keep using E until the target can leave.
notes.cass-skill-w: Use W to control space, not for its damage. Enemies inside its poison cloud cannot use movement abilities, so placing it beneath an opponent who has dashed in stops them from advancing or escaping. Its long cooldown leaves you open to the next engage if you misuse it, so do not waste it on poke.
notes.cass-skill-r: R stuns enemies facing Cassiopeia but only slows those facing away. Cast it into an opponent charging straight at you; using it on a fleeing opponent’s back spends its long cooldown on a slow, and moving behind an opponent to cast it is disadvantageous for the same reason.
notes.cass-laning-farm: In lane, apply poison with Q and last-hit with E. E refunds mana when it kills a target, so following this sequence keeps your mana up; otherwise, you will run out before level 6. Cassiopeia has some of the lowest early armor among champions and is especially vulnerable to basic attack poke, so stand behind minions and avoid giving your opponent an angle to attack.
notes.cass-laning-wave: Using Q to push an entire wave can leave you without enough mana for W when a gank comes. Unless you need lane priority, keep the wave in the middle and clear it with E last-hits; do not push forward while the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.
notes.cass-phase: Cassiopeia is weakest at levels 1–2: her armor is among the lowest in the game, and one ability is not enough to trade damage. Her sustained damage rises sharply from mid game once E has been leveled and she has mana items; late game, she has some of the highest teamfight damage as long as she is not caught. Her 14-minute CS ranks highly while her damage ranks low, so focus on scaling early and look to deal damage later.
notes.cass-teamfight: Cassiopeia does not initiate fights. Stay behind your frontline, apply poison with Q, and keep casting E on poisoned targets for sustained damage. Use W on the route enemies take toward your backline or under an enemy who has already dived in, and save R for the moment several enemies charge at you head-on.
notes.cass-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, move Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your build, between core items. Cassiopeia has no mobility ability and can die once caught, but surviving briefly lets her sustained E damage turn the fight around.
notes.cass-situational-mercurial: If the enemy’s finishing blow comes from a magic damage composition that opens with a long stun, buy Quicksilver Sash to remove that stun. Every moment Cassiopeia spends under crowd control costs her damage time, so the cleanse itself is the goal rather than the magic resistance.
notes.vs-cass-r: Cassiopeia’s R stuns only enemies facing her. Turn away when you see its cast animation: taking the slow instead of the stun lets you escape rather than die on the spot. When close to her, the biggest mistake is continuing to deal damage while facing her head-on.
notes.vs-cass-e: Cassiopeia's E deals more damage to poisoned targets and heals her.
notes.vs-cass-w: You cannot use movement abilities inside Cassiopeia’s W poison cloud. If your champion engages with a dash, close the distance before W is placed; if it is already down, take a route that avoids the cloud. Cassiopeia is looking for the moment you try to dash while standing in it and nothing happens.
notes.vs-cass-early: Cassiopeia has some of the lowest armor among champions and no mobility ability. Pressure her with basic attacks and short trades throughout levels 1–5 to win lane decisively; ganks are also more likely to succeed for the same reasons. If you fail to build a lead then, the mid to late game favors her.
notes.vs-cass-teamfight: Late game, Cassiopeia can win teamfights through sustained damage if she is not caught. Instead of pushing straight at her, establish vision to cut off her route or engage just after she uses W elsewhere. Once you have an opening, apply guaranteed crowd control first and finish the fight before she gains movement speed.
notes.chogath-combo-basic: For a basic trade, activate E before closing in with a basic attack, knock the target up with Q, silence them with W while they are airborne, then land the remaining E empowered attacks. E has no cast time, so turn it on before engaging; if Q misses, back off.
notes.chogath-combo-q-timing: Q warns enemies at the target location before it activates, so they can walk out of a careless cast. Place it as an opponent steps forward to last hit with a basic attack, immediately after an ally lands crowd control, or after W silences them and locks out their mobility ability.
notes.chogath-combo-wq: If the opponent looks likely to dodge Q with a mobility ability, lock it out with W before placing Q. W's silence does not stop opponents from walking.
notes.chogath-skill-r-stacks: Killing a target with R grants a Feast stack, increasing Cho'Gath's maximum health, size, attack range, and Feast range. Stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters have a cap; reach it during the laning phase. Beyond that cap, only champion and epic monster kills grant stacks.
notes.chogath-skill-r-execute: R deals true damage, ignoring armor and magic resistance. Even a tanky opponent is a guaranteed kill once their health is low enough, making R especially valuable against tanks that are hard to finish. If the kill is uncertain, save it: its long cooldown costs you both a chance to grow and a way to finish the target.
notes.chogath-skill-e: E adds spikes to the next three basic attacks, piercing every enemy in a straight line ahead and slowing them. Its damage scales with the target's maximum health, making it especially strong against frontliners who build health, and that damage grows with Feast stacks. Against monsters, a fixed damage value applies instead, so E also helps clear jungle camps.
notes.chogath-skill-w: W silences enemies in a cone, briefly shutting down assassins and mages who rely on abilities. Save it for just before they cast a key ability instead of using it automatically during a trade. It costs more mana than Cho'Gath's other abilities, so using it too often early can leave you unable to stay in lane.
notes.chogath-skill-passive: Carnivore restores health and mana whenever you kill a unit, with the amount increasing as you level up. Cho'Gath struggles with mana early, so securing each last hit helps sustain you in lane. When your health is low enough to make a trade uncertain, secure minion kills to heal instead of forcing one.
notes.chogath-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, Q is your only way to start a trade, so do not force one. Clear minions with E's piercing spikes to stay in lane, and call for a jungle gank when the opponent pushes the wave. After level 6, watch for a chance to execute them when they forget that Feast stacks have extended your R range.
notes.chogath-laning-antigank: Cho'Gath has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks, but Q and W can turn one around. When a gank comes, do not place Q ahead of time in your escape direction; wait until the enemies close in and commit to a direction, then place Q and use W to lock out their pursuit ability. Pulling the wave toward you and drawing in the enemy jungler suits this approach especially well.
notes.chogath-phase: Cho'Gath is vulnerable at levels 1–2 because he lacks mana and abilities. Trades become viable at level 3 once he has Q and W, while R at level 6 creates opportunities for kills and Feast stacks. His base stat growth is low enough that his maximum health at level 18 ranks among the lowest, and Feast stacks make up the difference; without them, he remains an ordinary melee champion even late in the game.
notes.chogath-teamfight: Cho'Gath should stand in front of his allies rather than dive into the backline. Place Q along the enemy's approach to delay their engage, then silence their initiator with W just as they are about to use an ability. With no mobility ability to get back after moving forward, stay no more than a step ahead of your frontline.
notes.chogath-teamfight-ult: In teamfights, use R on a low health enemy carry. A kill immediately grants a Feast stack and increases Cho'Gath's maximum health, making him tougher as the fight continues. When the kill is certain, finish the target yourself instead of leaving it to an ally and saving R; the stack also benefits you in later fights.
notes.chogath-situational-antiheal: If an opponent survives through healing, build Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Cho'Gath can keep dealing damage with Q and E, maintaining the effect throughout a fight once it is applied.
notes.vs-chogath-q: Q activates after a warning appears beneath your feet, giving you time to react. Step sideways as soon as you see the indicator, and save your mobility ability for that moment. Cho'Gath needs Q to land to continue his combo, so dodging it makes his remaining abilities far less threatening.
notes.vs-chogath-w: W silences enemies in a cone in front of Cho'Gath. If it hits you, you cannot use a mobility ability to escape and may take the follow-up Q. Avoid starting a trade directly in front of him; move to his side, and if silenced, walk out before trying to use an ability.
notes.vs-chogath-r: Defensive items cannot block R's true damage. Do not stay near Cho'Gath when your health falls to half or less. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's R range.
notes.vs-chogath-stacks: Cho'Gath's late-game durability comes from Feast stacks rather than stat growth. Stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters have a cap, so beyond it his growth stops unless he gets champion kills. When your health is uncertain, simply avoiding death near him helps keep the enemy frontline smaller.
notes.vs-chogath-e: E's spikes scale with the target's maximum health and pierce everything in a straight line in front of Cho'Gath, so building only health makes them hurt even more. Standing in line behind minions lets him poke you while clearing the wave; move out of the line of his basic attacks.
notes.vs-chogath-mobility: Cho'Gath has no mobility abilities: keep your distance and he cannot close the gap, while a jungle gank leaves him with no way to escape. In lane, poke from outside Q's range and look for a gank just after he uses Q on the wave.
notes.corki-combo-poke: For poke, fire Q before R: Q briefly reveals the area and champions it hits, making the follow-up R much easier to land. Repeating this from maximum range steadily wears down the enemy’s health.
notes.corki-combo-allin: For an all-in, jump in with W to leave a trail of fire, activate E and keep auto attacking, then finish with R. Corki can move and auto attack while E fires, and its armor and magic resistance reduction makes the following attacks and R hit harder.
notes.corki-combo-bigone: Every third R shot deals heavy damage, so count your shots and time the big missile to finish your target. If you spend the first two clearing a wave, the big one may not be ready when you need it.
notes.corki-skill-r: R stops gaining charges when full, so leaving it capped wastes potential charges; emptying it completely leaves you without missiles for a fight. Auto attacking a champion reduces its charge time, so weave attacks into your poke to get missiles back sooner.
notes.corki-skill-e: E reduces armor and magic resistance in a cone, increasing your allies’ damage as well as your own. In teamfights, aim it at the target your allies are attacking rather than the tank directly in front of you, and keep your position while moving and auto attacking as it fires.
notes.corki-skill-w: W is Corki’s only mobility ability and his only way to cross terrain. His movement speed is very low, so once W is down, he has virtually no way to escape. Don’t spend it to engage early; use it only after the enemy has used all its engage abilities, or save it for an escape.
notes.corki-skill-q: Q is especially valuable for the vision it provides: throw it into bushes or unwarded paths to check for ambushes, or hit a fleeing enemy to reveal their position so your allies can catch up. Use it to locate the enemy jungler before an objective, too.
notes.corki-skill-passive: Corki’s passive converts part of his auto attack damage to true damage, including damage from Spellblade effects. Weave in auto attacks even against heavily armored enemies instead of relying only on abilities. As of the 26.17 tooltip, the passive provides only this conversion, so do not plan an engage around the Package (Special Delivery) described in older guides.
notes.corki-laning: In lane, build small advantages with your range and Q and R poke. Corki’s very low movement speed makes him especially vulnerable to ganks, so avoid pushing toward the enemy turret without vision and keep W available to escape.
notes.corki-laning-farm: When the enemy pokes you, farm the wave safely instead of trading back.
notes.corki-phase: Corki’s low base stats make him very weak at levels 1–5. His level 6 R and first core item give him strong poke, and he peaks in the mid to late game with two or three items. Focus on getting through the early levels without falling behind.
notes.corki-teamfight: In teamfights, stay back and fire R while using E to reduce the defenses of the target your allies are attacking. Enter with W only after all enemy engage abilities and targeted crowd control have been used; Corki’s low movement speed makes escape difficult once he is caught.
notes.corki-objective: In objective fights, R lets Corki deal damage safely from beyond a wall or outside enemy vision. There’s no need to move into vision to find a position: reveal the enemy team with Q, then fire R to cut down the time they can spend attacking the objective.
notes.corki-situational-antiheal: If the enemy sustains through your poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to keep that damage from being healed.
notes.vs-corki-r: Corki’s R damages enemies around the first target it hits, so hiding behind minions will not protect you. Move out of missile range and reposition to avoid consecutive hits, especially from the much stronger third missile.
notes.vs-corki-w: Engage Corki right after he uses W, when his mobility is down. If you try to close in while it’s available, he can escape over terrain.
notes.vs-corki-mobility: Corki has one of the lowest movement speeds, making it easy to stick to him with slows or targeted dashes and leaving him especially vulnerable to ganks. His base stats are also low for the first five levels, so pressuring him then to slow his growth is most effective.
notes.vs-corki-e: Corki’s E reduces both armor and magic resistance when it hits, increasing all damage that follows. It covers a cone, so move sideways instead of standing in front of it; that alone will get you out of most of its area.
notes.vs-corki-q: Corki’s Q reveals your position for a while when it hits. If it catches you during an escape, use a mobility ability immediately to create distance rather than assuming you are safe once you leave normal vision.
notes.vs-corki-scaling: Corki grows stronger as he gets more items. If early lane pressure and ganks don’t disrupt his farm, he can safely fire missiles from the back in the mid to late game and lock in a win. The key is to deny him time to farm comfortably.
notes.darius-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is E Apprehend → auto attack → W Crippling Strike → Q Decimate. Pulling an enemy into melee range guarantees the auto attack and W; W resets the auto attack timer, letting you build three Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Finish with Q, taking half a step back to land the blade.
notes.darius-combo-execute: The execution combo is E Apprehend → auto attack → auto attack → W Crippling Strike → Q Decimate → auto attack → R Noxian Guillotine. The extra auto attack matters because R’s damage scales with the target’s Hemorrhage stacks; using R before reaching maximum stacks can let a kill escape. E’s slow keeps the enemy in range while you add those attacks.
notes.darius-skill-passive: Hemorrhage stacks up to five times, and reaching maximum stacks greatly increases Darius’s attack damage. His damage is ordinary before then, so alternate auto attacks and abilities to build stacks as quickly as possible. He grows stronger the longer a fight lasts, making survival a way to deal more damage; back off from a fight you started with no Hemorrhage stacks.
notes.darius-skill-q: Q Decimate deals full damage only with the blade, and its healing depends on how many enemy champions and large monsters the blade hits. Casting Q while pressed against a target hits with the handle, costing you both damage and healing. In lane, step back as you cast to catch the enemy champion with the blade; you can also use Flash during the cast to move the blade’s hitbox.
notes.darius-skill-w: W Crippling Strike resets the auto attack timer and applies a strong slow. Use it immediately after an auto attack to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly, or slow a fleeing enemy to keep them in Q and R range. With no mobility ability, Darius also relies on this slow to escape a bad fight. Using W on a minion costs you a stack you could have applied to a champion.
notes.darius-skill-e: If the enemy has a mobility ability, use E Apprehend right after they spend it: a dash can easily dodge an early E, while pulling them back as they try to escape lets you land the full combo. Flash does not work during E’s cast, so use Flash before E for a surprise engage. E’s passive already grants armor penetration, lowering the priority of penetration focused items with overlapping effects.
notes.darius-phase: Darius is weak at levels 1–2 while he has few abilities, but gains strength at level 3 with both W and Q available and again at level 6 when he gets R. He depends little on items and stays strong through the mid game, though his lack of mobility and sustain leaves him vulnerable to prolonged attrition against ranged poke. Engaging becomes difficult in standard late game teamfights, so turn your lane advantage into gains during his strong periods.
notes.darius-situational-armor: If the enemy deals mostly physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps early, then add Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen. Both provide armor and slow enemies while you stay close, helping Darius keep up despite his lack of mobility.
notes.darius-situational-magic: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Mercury’s Treads to shorten immobilization, then build Force of Nature. A single root or stun can ruin Darius’s entire combo because he has no mobility ability, so prioritize tenacity over magic resistance.
notes.darius-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing can turn a fight around, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Darius wins through extended brawls, where sustained enemy healing can reverse the outcome.
notes.darius-laning: Laning is about keeping the enemy within E Apprehend range. Freeze the wave on your side so they must step forward for minions, then land E from brush or narrow terrain to secure your combo. Darius has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks, so establish vision before moving forward after pushing the wave.
notes.darius-teamfight: Darius is at a disadvantage in head on teamfights: he struggles to reach backline damage dealers and can be focused down before he gets there. In narrow terrain, pull multiple enemies with E Apprehend and hit them together with Q Decimate’s blade to build up healing. A kill with R Noxian Guillotine resets its cooldown, so start the chain with a target you can reliably finish. Without that terrain, pressure a side lane through 1v1s instead.
notes.vs-darius-e: All of Darius’s combos start with E Apprehend: if he pulls you in, his basic attack, W Crippling Strike, and Q Decimate are guaranteed to land. Poke only from outside E range, and save mobility abilities and Flash to respond to E rather than using them to escape. The only window to trade is when E misses or is on cooldown.
notes.vs-darius-passive: Darius’s attack damage rises sharply at maximum Hemorrhage stacks, so create distance whenever stacks are building; a fight you were winning can turn against you. Hemorrhage expires over time, so disengage briefly to let the stacks fall off, then reengage.
notes.vs-darius-q: Darius’s Q Decimate heals him according to how many enemies its blade hits. When he starts casting, move beyond the blade’s range or get right next to him so the handle hits instead, reducing both damage and healing. Poke him right after he uses Q to clear minions.
notes.vs-darius-r: Darius’s R Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that increases with the target’s Hemorrhage stacks, and a kill resets its cooldown. If you have several stacks and low enough health to be at risk, leave R range completely rather than trying to survive with armor; your death could start a chain of kills against your team.
notes.vs-darius-phase: Darius lacks mobility and sustain, but Q healing and maximum Hemorrhage stacks make extended fights dangerous. Repeat short hit and run trades instead, forcing him to recall to recover health. W’s slow is his only way to escape, so keep pressing once you have a favorable position. He is exceptionally strong in early skirmishes and dives, though, so watch for the enemy jungler joining him.
notes.diana-combo-basic: For a basic trade, land Q Crescent Strike, close in with E Lunar Rush, auto attack, then activate W Pale Cascade. Using E on a target marked by Moonlight immediately resets its cooldown, so save the second E as a way out instead of using it right away.
notes.diana-combo-allin: After level 6, the all-in sequence is Q, E, W, an auto attack, R Moonfall, then the remaining E. Activate W immediately after closing in with E, since its orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. R pulls enemies in before dealing damage a short time later, so to overlap that damage with Q and an auto attack, use R first and land both before it hits.
notes.diana-combo-r-engage: When several enemies are grouped, reverse the order: enter with E, pull them together with R, then use Q and W. R deals more damage for each champion it pulls in, so its timing differs when targeting one opponent versus several; opening with R against a lone opponent wastes it.
notes.diana-skill-q: Q Crescent Strike travels in a curve, making it effective against opponents who dodge in a straight line. Diana's entire combo starts with landing Q, but its short cooldown and low mana cost mean you should keep throwing it even if you miss. A target it hits is briefly revealed.
notes.diana-skill-w: W Pale Cascade's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy and last briefly, so activating W from too far away lets them disappear. Bursting the last orb grants another shield and extends its duration; stay close enough to use every orb for both damage and survivability.
notes.diana-skill-e: E Lunar Rush resets its cooldown only when used on a target marked by Moonlight. Entering with E without a mark lets you dive in aggressively but leaves you no way back out. If you are unsure you can land Q, or the opponent still has crowd control available, land Q before using E.
notes.diana-skill-passive: P Moonsilver Blade deals area damage to nearby enemies every set number of attacks and briefly grants a large attack speed boost right after you use an ability. Leaving after casting abilities alone gives up much of that damage, so weave auto attacks between them.
notes.diana-skill-r: R Moonfall deals damage and pulls opponents toward Diana, disrupting their movement. Use it to catch fleeing enemies or stop a champion diving onto your allies, but avoid it when you cannot withstand the opponents it pulls in.
notes.diana-phase: Diana is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has melee range and no combo. With Q, W, and E available at level 3, she can trade damage, and learning R at level 6 creates her first kill opportunity. She peaks in the mid game with at least two ability power items; in the late game, her value depends on whether she can eliminate one target and escape alive.
notes.diana-laning: In mid lane, respect Diana's melee range and farm with Q while waiting for level 6. Use W to clear caster minions and push the wave, then look for gank opportunities with your jungler. After level 6, an opponent who stays after being hit by Q presents a kill opportunity.
notes.diana-jungle: In the jungle, clear camps quickly with W's orbs and P Moonsilver Blade's area damage. For ganks, approach through unwarded brush or from behind to line up Q, since landing it resets E; entering with E after missing Q leaves you unable to get back out.
notes.diana-teamfight: In teamfights, approach from the side toward the enemy damage dealers instead of entering head-on. Go in once the enemy's key crowd control has been used or an ally has engaged and drawn their attention. R is most valuable when it pulls several enemies together; if that opportunity is unavailable, save the reset E, eliminate one damage dealer, and get out.
notes.diana-situational-cc: If the enemy has a root that lands without aiming, Diana will be locked down the moment she goes in, unable to do anything before she dies. Buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to break the root immediately after engaging.
notes.diana-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents a kill in one combo, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon.
notes.vs-diana-q: Diana's combos start with Q Crescent Strike. Because it curves, sidestep instead of retreating straight back. If it hits and applies Moonlight, move away: E can hit you twice.
notes.vs-diana-w: Diana’s W Pale Cascade orbs last only a few seconds. Fighting her up close right after she activates W means taking every orb and the full shield, so wait until the orbs disappear and the shield wears off before engaging.
notes.vs-diana-e: If Diana dives in with E without first landing Q, she has no way back out; catch her with a slow or stun. If Q has already hit you, E will reset, so give up on trapping her and create distance.
notes.vs-diana-r: Diana's R Moonfall deals more damage for each champion it pulls in, so standing together in a teamfight lets it catch several of you at once. Use vision to deny her an entry angle from the side, and spread out with her possible angle of entry in mind.
notes.vs-diana-early: Diana is weakest before level 6, when her melee range and lack of a finishing tool limit her. Build a CS lead during that window, then push the lane ahead of her level 6 timing or stay near your turret to weather her first all-in.
notes.drmundo-combo-basic: For a basic trade, slow the enemy with Q, close in, activate W, then land an E-enhanced basic attack. W stores the most damage taken in the brief window immediately after activation, so use it just before the enemy’s combo hits.
notes.drmundo-combo-w-recast: W fully restores its stored gray health only if an enemy champion is nearby when it explodes. Reactivate it yourself while the enemy is in the explosion range instead of letting it expire; if they are retreating, delay reactivation slightly to catch them in the blast.
notes.drmundo-combo-e: E empowers your next basic attack, so you must get within attack range. Its damage increases as your health falls, making a counterattack after taking damage especially strong. A minion killed with E is knocked back and damages enemies in its path; angle the attack toward your opponent when you want to clear the wave and harass them at the same time.
notes.drmundo-skill-q: Q (Infected Bonesaw) deals damage based on the target’s current health, making it strong against full-health enemies but weak as a finishing blow. It hits only the first target, so minions can block it, though hitting a minion or monster can still provide healing. Decide whether you want a kill opportunity or healing before throwing it.
notes.drmundo-skill-passive-bag: Dr. Mundo’s passive ignores the first immobilizing effect at the cost of health and drops a canister nearby. Picking it up restores health and reduces the passive’s cooldown, while an enemy champion can destroy it by stepping on it. When a canister drops, picking it up before continuing the trade is often worthwhile.
notes.drmundo-skill-passive-timing: Whether Dr. Mundo can take a fight depends on his passive. When it is available, he can ignore the enemy’s first immobilizing effect and close in; when it is down, that effect will stop him. If the enemy jungler is missing and your passive is down, do not push the lane forward.
notes.drmundo-skill-r: R (Maximum Dosage) heals immediately based on missing health, making it more effective when Dr. Mundo is low. At higher ranks, it heals more for each nearby enemy champion, so activating it while surrounded by several enemies restores more health than using it while fleeing. Account for the healing over time as well; waiting for the immediate heal alone can get you killed.
notes.drmundo-skill-r-engage: R’s movement speed boost helps Dr. Mundo engage: after joining a teamfight with Teleport, activate it and walk into the enemy backline. Because he has no dash, choose fights with the understanding that he cannot reach the backline while R is unavailable.
notes.drmundo-phase: Dr. Mundo has virtually no early kill pressure, ranking among the lowest champions by early kill statistics. His low deaths and strong CS make surviving and farming the right approach in lane. His one-on-one sustain rises sharply from the mid game once he has level 6 R and his first core item, while health items in the late game also increase the attack damage E grants.
notes.drmundo-laning-sustain: Healing from Q hits, passive regeneration, and canister pickups lets Dr. Mundo stay in lane without leaving. Use canister and Q healing before spending potions, and recall after the wave has pushed toward the enemy turret. The time he spends holding his lane is itself part of his scaling.
notes.drmundo-laning-ranged: Against a ranged opponent, even entering Q range is a losing trade. Farm from behind minions and use Q only for healing, then look to close in when your jungler ganks or just after the opponent uses an ability on the wave.
notes.drmundo-teamfight: Dr. Mundo does not start teamfights. Once enemies engage your allies, activate R and walk in, slow an enemy damage dealer with Q, then hit them with E. If the enemies ignore Dr. Mundo, their damage dealer dies; if they attack him, his healing wastes their time. Either way, your team benefits.
notes.drmundo-situational-mr: Dr. Mundo has very low magic resistance early, leaving him vulnerable to magic damage compositions. Buy Spirit Visage earlier in those matchups: it raises both magic resistance and healing received, directly supporting the healing from Q, W, and R.
notes.drmundo-situational-attackspeed: If the enemy marksman relies on attack speed, buy Frozen Heart. Its armor and reduction to nearby enemies’ attack speed buy Dr. Mundo time to walk into the backline.
notes.vs-drmundo-passive-bait: Dr. Mundo’s passive ignores the first immobilizing effect. Trigger it with weaker crowd control before using your key engage ability; reversing that order lets his passive negate your crucial crowd control.
notes.vs-drmundo-bag: An enemy champion can destroy a canister Dr. Mundo drops by stepping on it. After a trade, retreat through the canister to deny both its healing and the reduction to his passive cooldown.
notes.vs-drmundo-q: Dr. Mundo’s Q (Infected Bonesaw) hits only the first target and deals damage based on current health. Keep minions between you and him to block most casts, and remember that it hurts most when your health is full.
notes.vs-drmundo-r-window: Treat Dr. Mundo as unkillable while his R is active. Look for a dive or force an objective while it is down; when it is available, spend your time gaining an advantage in another lane or at an objective instead of trying to kill him.
notes.vs-drmundo-early-mr: Dr. Mundo’s early magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions, so you can pressure him hard in lane if magic damage is your main source of damage. Secure an advantage early, because his magic resistance rises substantially with levels and that advantage disappears.
notes.draven-combo-juggle: Draven’s basic rotation is to activate Q, auto-attack, move to the bouncing axe’s landing marker, catch it, and attack again. He can hold two axes at once, so aim to have one in the air while catching the other; maintaining that rhythm empowers every auto-attack.
notes.draven-combo-w: Use W just before catching an axe. The catch resets W’s cooldown, letting you refresh its movement speed boost immediately and keep it active without a gap; waiting until after the catch wastes that reset.
notes.draven-skill-q-uptime: Draven drops every axe he is holding if he goes too long without auto-attacking. If you will not fight within the next few seconds, leave Q off: it costs mana, and the axes will disappear anyway. When a fight is likely, activate Q before your first auto-attack so the opening hit is empowered.
notes.draven-skill-q-give-up: Give up an axe if its landing spot is dangerous.
notes.draven-skill-w-collision: W's movement speed boost lets Draven pass through units. Getting blocked by minions on the way to an axe is the most common reason to drop one, so use W when you need to move through them. Early on, though, its mana cost is high; using it repeatedly just to move can leave you without W when a fight starts.
notes.draven-skill-e: It's hard to control the direction E knocks an opponent. Save E to interrupt an opponent's dash or a skill they're casting. Use E when you urgently need space to catch an axe.
notes.draven-skill-r: R travels out and returns. Its damage falls each time it passes through a unit, but that reduction resets on the return trip. If you think an opponent will dodge it, recast just before the axe reaches them so it turns back over them with its damage reset. The execute threshold scales with League of Draven stacks, making a heavily stacked Draven's R lethal to low-health opponents within range.
notes.draven-skill-passive: Catching an axe, killing a minion or monster, and destroying a turret build passive stacks; a champion kill converts those stacks into bonus gold proportional to their number. Death removes half your stacks, so when you have plenty, look for a reliable way to participate in a kill and cash them in instead of forcing a solo fight. Dying before cashing them in is the most common way Draven loses games.
notes.draven-laning: With axes in hand, Draven almost never loses a damage trade in lane. Move alongside the enemy marksman and auto-attack while they hit a minion, then catch the bouncing axe to gain an advantage without taking a return hit. This pressure is why his laning CS and turret plate numbers rank among the best. His movement speed is low, though, so always account for an enemy jungler's gank as you step forward to catch an axe.
notes.draven-laning-vision: Chasing an axe landing marker can easily narrow your awareness of your surroundings. Check the minimap every few seconds. Keep wards in the brush and river along the path you take to catch axes.
notes.draven-phase: Draven peaks in lane: his laning kills, CS, and turret plate numbers are all among the best, and he relies on the gold earned early to close out the game. As the game goes on, safe places to catch axes disappear and enemies have more ways to engage, making him relatively weaker. How quickly you turn an early lead into turrets and objectives determines the outcome.
notes.draven-teamfight: Never enter a teamfight first as Draven. Let your allies initiate and the enemy use their engage abilities before moving in, so you have room to catch axes.
