If space is tight, maintain just one axe and auto-attack from safety instead of trying to juggle two. Save E to interrupt enemies diving your allied damage dealers.
notes.draven-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has several forms of immobilizing crowd control, take Cleanse instead of Barrier. Draven must keep moving to catch axes; getting locked down once can make him drop an axe and lose his damage. If a summoner spell cannot cover the matchup, fit Mercurial Scimitar between your core items.
notes.vs-draven-axe-spot: Aim skillshots at Draven’s axe landing spot rather than at Draven. He has to walk there to catch it, forcing him to take the hit or lose the axe; either choice costs him.
notes.vs-draven-disrupt: Draven's strength comes from keeping his axes going. Knockbacks, slows, and immobilizing crowd control that keep him from reaching an axe's landing spot sharply reduce his damage. Make him drop an axe before trying to kill him.
notes.vs-draven-two-axes: Avoid early damage trades with Draven when he has two axes; his auto-attack damage in that state wins any lane trade. Engage when he has only one axe or none.
notes.vs-draven-safe-farm: If you cannot trade with Draven, farm safely and deny him a chance to kill you. That alone lets the wave push toward you, drawing him forward into a position your jungler can attack.
notes.vs-draven-snowball: Draven uses the gold he earns early to build momentum, but a death costs him half his accumulated stacks. Shutting him down as a team early can erase his late-game damage; keep looking for chances to catch him alone even after the laning phase.
notes.vs-draven-r: Draven’s R comes back after passing you, with its damage reduction reset. Dodging it once is not enough if you stay in its path: move completely clear of both the outbound and return routes, or get out of range if you are low on health.
notes.draven-skill-q-control: Throwing an axe at a target who is too close makes its landing spot hard to control. Axes land in the direction Draven is moving, so your movement as you attack determines where you will need to stand for the next catch. Axes do not bounce back from turrets, so account for the interruption to your axe rotation while taking one down.
notes.ekko-combo-fast: For the fastest damage combo, throw Q, then close in with E as Q returns. The outgoing and returning Q hits overlap with E’s empowered basic attack, immediately triggering the third P hit.
notes.ekko-combo-full: For a full combo, place W ahead of the enemy’s path first, slow them with Q, then use E to enter the sphere and stun them. Follow with a basic attack and use R if needed. W takes time to set up, so casting it after you close in gives the enemy time to escape.
notes.ekko-combo-e-cast: You can cast other abilities during E’s dash: throw Q as you move, or use E to reach a placed W sphere quickly and set up a stun. This lets E extend the reach of your other abilities.
notes.ekko-combo-r: R returns you to where you were a few seconds ago and deals area damage there. Set up your return position deliberately before going in; using R from the middle of a group of enemies lets you deal damage and escape at the same time.
notes.ekko-skill-passive: P triggers on the third hit against the same target and grants movement speed if that target is a champion. Two Q hits, one on the way out and one on the way back, plus a basic attack will trigger it; so will one ability hit and two basic attacks. Build combos around that third hit, then use the movement speed to get out, making the risk of going in worthwhile.
notes.ekko-skill-q: Q deals more damage on its return than on its way out. Pushing an enemy toward a wall improves your chances of landing both hits. Q also clears minion waves and jungle monsters, but overusing it can leave you without enough mana for a combo when a fight starts.
notes.ekko-skill-w: Casting W leaves a signal the enemy can see, and the sphere takes time to set up and triggers only when Ekko enters it. Place it ahead of the enemy’s escape route or approach path instead of using it after you have already closed in. Its long cooldown means a missed W can seriously hurt your chances in a fight.
notes.ekko-skill-w-passive: W’s passive makes basic attacks against low-health enemies deal bonus damage based on their missing health. Even after using all your abilities, one or two basic attacks may finish the kill, so do not waste R if those attacks will do it.
notes.ekko-skill-r: R can deal damage or get you out of danger, and it heals more when you have lost more health during the few seconds it rewinds. For healing alone, waiting as long as possible is best in theory, but in a teamfight, crowd control or burst damage may stop you before you can cast it.
notes.ekko-phase: Jungle Ekko’s early clear is not especially fast, but W’s stun gives him a high chance of successful ganks. He can start fights often from level 6, when he learns R, and again later as his ability cooldowns become much shorter. As he builds ability power, his damage, W shield, and R healing all grow, making him strongest in the mid to late game.
notes.ekko-laning-gank: When ganking, place W behind the enemy along their escape route, slow them with Q, then go in with E. Time W to coincide with an ally’s crowd control so the enemy cannot dodge it even after seeing the signal; placing it in plain sight too early lets them back away from the lane.
notes.ekko-laning-split: Q’s wave clear and E’s damage to structures make Ekko a strong split pusher, while his mobility lets him escape enemies sent to catch him. If a teamfight is not an option, pressure a side lane to draw enemies out.
notes.ekko-teamfight: Do not go in first in a teamfight. Wait until the enemy has used their engage abilities and crowd control and your allies have started the fight, then jump into the backline. Set up a safe return point for R before entering so you can survive even if the attempt fails; decide where you will return before choosing where to go in.
notes.ekko-situational-tenacity: Choose Mercury’s Treads if the enemy has a lot of hard crowd control. Ekko needs to keep moving, and being locked down once can kill him before he uses R.
notes.vs-ekko-ult-ready: Ekko is weakest while R is on cooldown. A trailing afterimage means R is ready, so do not overcommit to chasing him even if he looks low on health.
notes.vs-ekko-w: Ekko’s W leaves a visible signal when cast and takes time to set up. Remember where the signal appeared and stay out of that area to deny both the stun and the shield.
notes.vs-ekko-q: Ekko’s Q deals more damage on its second hit as it returns. Watch the direction he throws it and step out of its return path to cut the damage you take in half.
notes.vs-ekko-cc: Ekko is vulnerable to crowd control, especially just after he closes in with E and his dash is unavailable. Stun or root him then to force out R or stop him outright.
notes.vs-ekko-chase: If you chase a low-health Ekko whose R is ready, aim a skillshot ahead of time at his trailing afterimage rather than at Ekko himself. That is where he will return, and he often chooses to use R to turn the fight around instead of running away.
notes.vs-ekko-bait: With both W and R on cooldown, Ekko is an ordinary melee champion. Bait out those abilities with a decoy fight, then start the main fight.
notes.elise-skill-form: Elise has R, Spider Form, from level 1. It changes her weapon rather than serving as a burst button, and its short cooldown lets her switch forms within a fight. Each human form ability that hits an enemy stores a dormant spiderling; transforming summons them all at once. Land your human form abilities before transforming, or you lose the spiderlings they would have provided.
notes.elise-skill-q-threshold: Human form Q, Neurotoxin, deals more damage when the target has more current health, while Spider Form Q, Venomous Bite, is strongest after the target has lost health. Open with Neurotoxin and finish with Venomous Bite; biting a healthy enemy uses its reach without getting much damage from it.
notes.elise-skill-e-cocoon: Human form E, Cocoon, is Elise’s only hard crowd control, and landing it often decides whether a gank succeeds. It affects only the first unit hit, so throw it from behind or beside the lane once you have an angle clear of minions and jungle monsters. Cocoon also reveals stealthed enemies and can check bushes, but do not waste it when a gank depends on it.
notes.elise-skill-e-rappel: Spider Form E, Rappel, is both a movement and dodge tool: Elise cannot be targeted while airborne, allowing her to avoid targeted abilities and turret attacks. She can cross a wall by landing on a nearby enemy unit, but drops back where she rose if none is available. Before using it to escape over a wall, check for a minion or jungle monster on the other side; its long cooldown leaves her without an escape once it is used.
notes.elise-skill-w-spiderlings: Human form W, Volatile Spiderling, walks to a chosen location before exploding, so place it after the enemy is caught or their escape direction is clear. Spider Form W, Skittering Frenzy, increases the attack speed of Elise and her spiderlings, making it most valuable when they are already attacking. Spiderlings attack the target Elise bites with Spider Form Q, Venomous Bite, so bite the enemy you want them to focus.
notes.elise-skill-mana: Spider Form abilities cost no mana, so when mana runs low, save your human form abilities and keep clearing camps in Spider Form. Its basic attacks deal bonus magic damage and heal Elise.
notes.elise-combo-gank: For a gank, land human form E, Cocoon, place W under the target, use human form Q, transform with R, then close in with Spider Form Q and basic attacks. Confirm that Cocoon hits before continuing: transforming first gives up the hard crowd control the gank needs. Landing all your human form abilities before transforming also summons the maximum number of spiderlings for the follow-up.
notes.elise-combo-escape: During a turret dive or countergank, Spider Form E, Rappel, lets Elise dodge targeted abilities and turret attacks as she rises. Land on a unit across a wall, then immediately use R to return to human form and get into range. You can also reach a fleeing enemy with Spider Form Q and escape with Rappel, but do not make an engage that depends on that escape while Rappel is on cooldown.
notes.elise-laning-clear: Clear camps mainly in Spider Form to save mana and limit health loss through its healing basic attacks. As you enter a camp, use human form abilities to build up spiderlings, then transform immediately and send them in to clear faster. Health-based damage is capped against monsters, so spending too long fighting a large monster alone is inefficient.
notes.elise-laning-gankpath: After the first few camps, shift to ganks and invades. Start looking for ganks as soon as you learn Cocoon, prioritizing lanes pulled toward your side where the enemy has moved forward.
notes.elise-phase: Elise is strongest from learning E, Cocoon, through the mid game. Having her transformation from level 1 gives her high damage for her level, making an early gank especially valuable. Later, health-based damage accounts for less of her damage as enemy health grows, and her teamfight contribution falls because Cocoon is her only hard crowd control. Turn early leads into objectives and turrets to end the game quickly.
notes.elise-teamfight: In teamfights, look for an angle to land E, Cocoon, instead of standing on the front line. Stay back in human form before the fight to catch a key enemy, then follow an ally’s engage in Spider Form to finish a weakened target. Go in once an ally has landed area crowd control or a key enemy has already lost health, and fight near a unit you can land on with Rappel so you have a way out.
notes.elise-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item. It adds healing reduction while maintaining the magic damage Elise needs for her burst.
notes.elise-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has burst engage, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. Elise is most exposed immediately after throwing Cocoon, so use the item to avoid the counterattack.
notes.vs-elise-form: Elise’s human form Q, Neurotoxin, hits hard against targets at full health. When she transforms into Spider Form, use your mobility and defensive abilities.
notes.vs-elise-cocoon: Elise’s gank depends on landing human form Cocoon, which affects only the first unit it hits. Stand behind your minion wave in lane so minions block it, and use minions or jungle monsters as cover elsewhere. Near the jungle, keep away from walls and take routes with clear vision.
notes.vs-elise-rappel: Rappel can move Elise onto a nearby enemy unit, but without one she lands where she rose. When chasing her, clear nearby minions and jungle monsters or block her route to them to limit her escape. Targeted abilities will miss while she is airborne, so save them and aim skillshots at her landing spot in advance.
notes.vs-elise-cooldown: Rappel has a long cooldown, leaving Elise without an escape immediately after she uses it. Once both Rappel and Cocoon are on cooldown, turn and attack her; her relatively low magic resistance means she cannot withstand being caught for long.
notes.vs-elise-phase: Elise builds leads through early ganks to end games quickly, while her farming numbers are low. Avoid giving her early kills and draw out the game to improve the matchup. Keep ample vision during early laning, and do not push too far when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.
notes.evelynn-combo-gank: For a gank, apply W from outside vision, approach while the mark matures, then trigger it with Q to charm the target. Follow with empowered E to dash in, recast Q, and finish with R. Q reaches farther than E, so it can trigger the charm without getting close; waiting until the target is held in place keeps the empowered E dash from missing.
notes.evelynn-combo-execute: R deals much more damage to targets below a certain health threshold, so use Q and E to bring them into execute range before casting it to finish. Evelynn retreats backward after R, making it both a finisher and an escape.
notes.evelynn-skill-passive: Demon Shade activates after Evelynn spends a while without basic attacking or using abilities, and grants camouflage starting at level 6. Damage from an enemy champion or turret briefly disables it. While camouflaged, a yellow eye appears above an enemy champion who comes close, and Evelynn is revealed if they come closer; use the eye to judge your distance. When low on health, recover through Demon Shade’s healing each second in a brush before using a potion.
notes.evelynn-skill-q: The first Q hit marks its target, adding damage to subsequent attacks against that same target, and Q can be recast to fire several more spikes. Recast spikes target the nearest enemy, making a champion hard to aim at among minions; move beside the wave for a clear angle before firing.
notes.evelynn-skill-w: The W mark must mature for a set time to charm and reduce magic resistance. Triggering it early with a basic attack or ability applies only a slow and can ruin the gank, so listen for the sound of the heart filling before setting it off. Cast W before approaching to give the mark time to mature, rather than applying it during the fight.
notes.evelynn-skill-e: Always use E while empowered: it deals much more damage, dashes to the target, and hits every enemy along its path, whereas unempowered E has short range and no dash. Demon Shade resets E’s cooldown and empowers it again when it activates, so step out briefly between fights to regain E. If the charm wears off, use Q instead of chasing the target just to land empowered E.
notes.evelynn-skill-r: While casting R, Evelynn becomes untargetable, letting her avoid targeted abilities and basic attacks unless their effects are already incoming. That makes it both a finisher and a way to dodge attacks, but it sends her backward, so it is not an engage tool. Account for the brief delay before Demon Shade can activate again after R.
notes.evelynn-laning-clear: At jungle camps, apply W to the large monster first, wait for the mark to mature, then trigger it. Its longer charm and greater bonus damage against monsters let Evelynn clear without losing health. Use Q for damage during the clear, and angle empowered E through every monster when several line up.
notes.evelynn-laning-path: Before level 6, Evelynn has no camouflage, making ganks rarely viable, so focus on clearing both sides of the jungle to level up. After level 6, approach through an unwarded route, such as the river or behind a lane. Camouflage only ends when she enters combat; the real danger is a ward the enemy has placed beside one of their jungle camps. Clear wards along your gank path first.
notes.evelynn-laning-target: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret: the enemy has farther to retreat, giving W time to mature. Opponents with several mobility abilities can escape before then, so against them choose a lane where an ally can land crowd control first.
notes.evelynn-phase: Level 6 is Evelynn’s turning point. Before then, she lacks camouflage and struggles to give W time to mature, making her ganks weak; afterward, she can approach unseen and open with a charm, sharply increasing her kill involvement. The numbers reflect this: at 14 minutes, her CS is among the lowest while her kills are among the highest. She wins through kills after level 6 rather than farming.
notes.evelynn-teamfight: Stay off the front line in teamfights. Activate Demon Shade, circle to the side or rear, and position behind the enemy backline damage dealers; go in only after the enemy’s key crowd control has been used on your frontline. Angle empowered E through grouped enemies so it hits everyone along its path. In fights around objectives, you can combine Smite with R to attempt a steal and use R’s retreat to escape.
notes.evelynn-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing repeatedly takes targets out of execute range, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.evelynn-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass sooner if an enemy assassin immediately counterattacks when you engage. Use its protection and R’s untargetability at separate times to survive twice during one engage.
notes.vs-evelynn-ward: Control Wards are a basic precaution against Evelynn. Because Demon Shade ends when she enters combat, even a regular ward beside your jungle camp will spot her if she starts a fight there. Place vision where she opens fights as well as along her gank paths.
notes.vs-evelynn-early: Before level 6, Evelynn lacks camouflage and needs time for W to mature, leaving her few ways to start a fight herself. She is especially vulnerable to early jungle invades, so if you can win the fight, take her camps early to delay level 6.
notes.vs-evelynn-w-tell: A W mark on you means Evelynn is already nearby preparing to charm you. Retreat before it matures, and immediately alert your team with a minimap ping and chat. She has not entered combat yet, so placing an area ability on her likely approach path can damage her while she is still camouflaged.
notes.vs-evelynn-e: Empowered E after the charm accounts for most of Evelynn’s damage. Once charmed, you cannot break free, so your position beforehand is crucial: avoid narrow paths along walls and move within your team’s vision with room to retreat.
notes.vs-evelynn-r: Evelynn’s R deals much more damage below a certain health threshold. After a fight, even a modest amount of health left can put you in range to be finished by one ability, so do not remain in an unwarded area while in execute range. She is untargetable as she casts R; using a targeted ability on her then wastes it.
notes.vs-evelynn-teamfight: Evelynn targets backline damage dealers in teamfights, so they should stay within areas their team has vision of and save immobilizing crowd control for her. Her health and defensive stats are low enough that catching her just once immediately after she engages can end the fight for her.
notes.ezreal-skill-q-engine: Landing Q reduces the cooldown of all abilities. Ezreal relies on landing Q to use E again quickly. Hold Q if you don't have an angle to land it.
notes.ezreal-skill-q-onhit: Q applies on-hit effects. Against enemies who are hard to approach, use Q to apply on-hit effects from outside basic attack range.
notes.ezreal-skill-w-order: W Essence Flux attaches an orb that you detonate with a follow-up attack or ability. Detonating it with an ability refunds that ability’s mana cost, so land W before using Q Mystic Shot to manage your mana; using Q first and throwing W afterward wastes mana.
notes.ezreal-skill-w-objective: W Essence Flux attaches to structures and large jungle monsters as well as champions. When taking a turret or fighting over an objective, attach W and detonate it with a basic attack or Q Mystic Shot; at an objective, save W until the fight starts.
notes.ezreal-skill-e: E is Ezreal's only escape. E has a long cooldown. Use E aggressively only after the enemy has used all their engage abilities.
notes.ezreal-skill-e-lineup: A short sideways E Arcane Shift can open a Q Mystic Shot angle that minions were blocking. Use it to shift your position rather than advance; the homing bolt fired on landing prioritizes a target marked by W Essence Flux, so attach W first to direct the bolt where you want it.
notes.ezreal-skill-r: R Trueshot Barrage travels in a straight line and pierces targets, letting it sweep through multiple waves or a jungle camp, though it deals reduced damage to minions and regular monsters. Treat wave clear as a secondary benefit: use R to finish a visible fleeing enemy from long range or hit grouped enemies before a teamfight starts.
notes.ezreal-combo-poke: For poke, use W Essence Flux → Q Mystic Shot → basic attack. Q detonates W for damage from both abilities and a mana refund, while passive stacks increase your attack speed for the follow-up basic attack. Fire W only when the enemy is away from the minion wave, or a minion will catch it first.
notes.ezreal-combo-allin: For an all-in, use W Essence Flux → basic attack → Q Mystic Shot → E Arcane Shift to change your angle and close in → basic attack, then R Trueshot Barrage if needed. Position E to cut off the enemy’s escape route, and judge beforehand whether Q’s cooldown reduction will let you fire a second Q.
notes.ezreal-phase-early: Ezreal is most vulnerable at levels 1–2, when his base health and armor are low and he lacks E Arcane Shift. Keep a safe distance and survive by last-hitting with Q Mystic Shot instead of looking for trades or a kill; even after unlocking R Trueshot Barrage at level 6, avoid stepping forward.
notes.ezreal-phase-scaling: Ezreal builds an advantage through CS and accumulated damage rather than early kills: at 14 minutes, his kill count ranks low among marksmen, while his CS and damage per minute rank near the top. His power arrives from mid game onward once he has two core items, so focus on avoiding losses until then.
notes.ezreal-laning: Last-hitting with Q Mystic Shot pushes the wave. With one of the lowest movement speeds in the game, Ezreal can struggle to escape a gank in a pushed lane even with E Arcane Shift, so use Q less for farming and let the wave come toward you with basic attacks when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown. Once the jungler appears on the other side of the map, push with Q, then recall or establish vision.
notes.ezreal-laning-mana: Ezreal’s lane endurance depends on mana. Attach W Essence Flux and detonate it with an ability to recover mana and keep poking; getting the order wrong can leave you out of mana with the wave partly pushed. Base your recall timing on your remaining mana rather than your health.
notes.ezreal-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the back and keep firing Q Mystic Shot. Ezreal is fragile and has no way to engage, so build up damage with Q and W Essence Flux from the edge of your range while your frontline holds the enemy in place. Save E Arcane Shift to escape after an enemy diver reaches you.
notes.ezreal-situational-antiheal: Against enemies who sustain through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early to apply Grievous Wounds from afar with Q Mystic Shot. Upgrade it to Mortal Reminder to keep Grievous Wounds applied throughout teamfights.
notes.vs-ezreal-fragile: Ezreal has low health and armor, so he goes down quickly once you reach him. Establish vision and find an angle to close the distance instead of trading poke with him from afar.
notes.vs-ezreal-e: Look for a chance to kill Ezreal right after he uses E. Force Ezreal to use E with a short engage, then go all-in. If Ezreal keeps landing Q, E's cooldown drops quickly.
notes.vs-ezreal-move-speed: Ezreal has one of the lowest base movement speeds in the game. If your team has a slow or movement speed boost, you can catch him after forcing out E Arcane Shift, so approach a gank from an angle that blocks his escape route first.
notes.vs-ezreal-w: When a W Essence Flux orb attaches to you, Ezreal’s next basic attack or ability that hits will detonate it for extra damage. Briefly step out of his range before re-engaging to avoid taking both hits in one trade.
notes.vs-ezreal-r: R Trueshot Barrage pierces targets along a straight line, so it can finish you if you flee at low health along a visible straight path. Turn around walls or terrain as you retreat, and avoid lining up with your allies where R could hit you together.
notes.vs-ezreal-minions: All of Ezreal’s damage comes from skillshots, and minions can block Q Mystic Shot for you. Keep the wave between you and him as you move along its inside edge; facing him in open ground without minions leaves you taking hits without being able to trade back.
notes.fiddle-skill-passive-scarecrow: A Harmless Scarecrow replaces Fiddlesticks’ trinket with effigies that serve as scouts and decoys. When spotted, an effigy briefly mimics Fiddlesticks and can make enemies think he is engaging; from level 6, it also reveals nearby wards. Just before a teamfight or objective, place one at your planned entry point to check enemy vision, then choose where to cast R. Fiddlesticks can also mimic an effigy by standing still briefly, letting him wait motionless in a brush to ambush passing enemies.
notes.fiddle-skill-q: Q Terrify works in two ways: damaging an enemy with an ability while Fiddlesticks is out of combat and unseen, or while posing as an effigy, automatically fears them; casting Q directly targets an enemy, fears them, and deals damage based on their current health. Q deals increased damage to a target recently feared by Fiddlesticks, so after engaging with an automatic fear, use it again to finish them off.
notes.fiddle-skill-w: Completing W (Bountiful Harvest) without interruption greatly reduces its remaining cooldown, so do not start the channel when it is likely to be interrupted. Its bonus damage based on missing health lands at the end of the channel; lower the enemy’s health first to increase that damage.
notes.fiddle-skill-e: E (Reap) covers a wide area, but only enemies in its center are silenced. Aim the center at an enemy to interrupt a channel or cast; if you need to stop an escape, the wider slow is enough. E is also the easiest ability to open an attack with from outside enemy vision.
notes.fiddle-skill-r: R Crowstorm shows its channel before Fiddlesticks blinks in, giving enemies time to react if they can see him. Cast it only from outside their vision, such as over a wall, from brush, or from a blind spot. Since enemies can respond by immobilizing him and moving out of range, choose narrow terrain where they cannot easily spread out.
notes.fiddle-combo-gank: For a gank, start outside enemy vision with E Reap to trigger an automatic fear, then begin channeling W Bountiful Harvest while the target is feared. An ability hit from outside vision applies fear without a direct Q cast, and E’s reach makes it the opening ability. Save Q Terrify for just after the target uses a mobility ability or to finish them off.
notes.fiddle-combo-ult: In a teamfight, enter with R, apply E’s slow and silence as you land, then channel W to completion. Fear is needed first for the full damage; if someone can counterattack immediately after you land, use Q on that target. Protecting W’s channel is the aim of the combo.
notes.fiddle-laning-clear: Build your jungle route around W: group monsters with E, then complete W to deal more damage to them, heal enough to maintain your health, and reduce W’s remaining cooldown so you can move straight to the next camp. A route where W gets interrupted hurts both clear speed and health management.
notes.fiddle-laning-gank-path: Ganks depend on approaching unseen, because an ability only triggers the automatic fear when Fiddlesticks is outside enemy vision. Circle through the brush behind the lane or a blind spot near the river. A control ward cuts that lane’s gank value by at least half, so ask an ally to clear it or gank another lane.
notes.fiddle-laning-objective: Before an objective, use an effigy to check enemy vision and positions, then take a spot in a brush.
notes.fiddle-phase: From mid game, once R and core ability power items are ready, a single engage can turn a teamfight around. In late game, Fiddlesticks still initiates fights over objectives with R. Fiddlesticks is vulnerable if enemies spread out after the engage.
notes.fiddle-teamfight: Fiddlesticks’ role in a teamfight is to initiate, but both W and R involve channels, so a single immobilizing effect can ruin the whole combo if he goes in first. Cast R after an ally’s immobilizing effect lands or the enemy uses a key counter ability, and land where several enemies are grouped with no room to retreat.
notes.fiddle-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has strong burst physical damage, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to survive the focus fire right after engaging with R.
notes.fiddle-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to keep Grievous Wounds applied through W and R's damage over time.
notes.vs-fiddle-r: Fiddlesticks’ R (Crowstorm) shows its channel before the blink. If you see him casting it, interrupt him with an immobilizing effect or a slow; if you cannot, leave its area and wait out its duration. Staying there to fight is the worst choice.
notes.vs-fiddle-ambush: If Fiddlesticks has been out of sight for a while, watch for an R ambush from a brush. The surest response is to place control wards in brushes and along entry paths near objectives, and avoid entering an unwarded narrow passage while grouped together.
notes.vs-fiddle-q: An ability hit from Fiddlesticks applies fear when enemies cannot see him, so any area without vision can become a fear threat. During jungle gank windows, keep vision in the brush behind the lane, and do not walk past a motionless effigy until you have confirmed it is not the real Fiddlesticks.
notes.vs-fiddle-w: Completing W (Bountiful Harvest) without interruption greatly reduces its remaining cooldown and heals Fiddlesticks for a lot. Even a brief immobilizing effect cuts both his ability to cast it again and his sustain, so use saved crowd control as soon as he starts channeling.
notes.vs-fiddle-cluster: Fiddlesticks’ W, E, and R all hit multiple enemies, so spread out before he engages and avoid facing him in narrow terrain where one entry can catch everyone. E silences only targets in the center of its area, so avoid standing in the middle of your team.
notes.vs-fiddle-punish: Fiddlesticks is fragile and has no mobility ability, making the moment he lands with R your chance to counterattack. Save an instant immobilizing ability or a spell defense tool for R, then focus your damage on his landing spot so he cannot complete a channel.
notes.fiora-combo-basic: For a short trade, Q toward a vital, auto attack, then use E. E empowers the next two basic attacks, with the second guaranteed to crit; if a new vital appears while E is active, hit it with that critical strike.
notes.fiora-combo-vital-angle: The vital’s position determines the combo: if it appears on the opponent’s back or side, use Q to reach and hit it; if it appears in front, hit it with an auto attack and E, saving Q to chase or disengage. Each vital hit grants movement speed, making the next one easier to reach, so look for an angle to hit two vitals in one fight.
notes.fiora-skill-vital: Hitting a passive vital deals true damage based on the opponent’s maximum health, restores health, and grants movement speed. Vitals reappear elsewhere after a set time or when hit, so if the current one is hard to reach, wait for the next rather than forcing an engage. Because armor does not reduce this true damage, Fiora can take down tanks even when they stack armor.
notes.fiora-skill-q: Q Lunge dashes in the chosen direction and strikes the nearest enemy, prioritizing a vital within its hit area. Hitting an enemy greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, letting Fiora use it again quickly while she stays close and keeps landing hits. A miss leaves the full cooldown in place and takes away both an engage and an escape option, so hit something as you move, even a minion or ward.
notes.fiora-skill-riposte: W Riposte blocks all attacks and immobilizing effects during its brief cast, then counterthrusts; blocking an immobilizing effect turns the counterthrust’s slow into a stun. Save it for a moment when the opponent must use immobilizing crowd control. Even while available, W pressures the opponent to hold their abilities.
notes.fiora-skill-e: E Bladework increases attack speed, slows with its first empowered auto attack, and guarantees a critical strike on the second. Use the slow to stay close, then aim the critical strike at a vital for much more damage in the same combo. Activate E once you can stay close enough to land both attacks, or the unused empowerment will go to waste.
notes.fiora-phase: Fiora’s 1v1 grows stronger as she gains items, so there is no need to force fights early. She is weak in large teamfights and gains advantages through split pushing.
notes.fiora-situational-antiheal: Against an opponent who relies on sustained healing, build Executioner’s Calling between core items. Fiora wears opponents down by hitting vitals one at a time; if they heal between hits, she cannot make the duel work.
notes.fiora-laning: Keep trades short and back off. After hitting one vital, use the movement speed to create distance before the opponent can retaliate. Trading to draw out their mobility ability first also gives Fiora an advantage when she can use hers while staying close.
notes.fiora-laning-vs-physical: Against an opponent with strong physical damage trades, focus on limiting early losses rather than winning lane. Give up some minions if necessary, but stay within experience range and let the wave come toward your turret. Once your items come together in the mid game, force 1v1s in a side lane; Fiora can turn an unfavorable matchup around as she scales.
notes.fiora-teamfight: Avoid large fights and apply pressure in a side lane. R Grand Challenge reveals four vitals on its target, making it most valuable in 1v1s and small skirmishes.
notes.fiora-teamfight-ult: If you have to take a teamfight, Fiora can use R (Grand Challenge) on the enemy frontline instead of the backline. Its vitals deal true damage based on the target’s maximum health, making it especially valuable against opponents who have stacked armor. Striking all four vitals or killing the target heals Fiora and nearby allies, potentially turning the fight around, so it is often better to use R to bring down a hard-to-break frontline than to avoid it.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte: When facing Fiora, first bait out W Riposte. It blocks all attacks and immobilizing effects during its brief cast, then counterthrusts; blocking an immobilizing effect makes the counterthrust stun. While W is available, avoid committing roots or stuns, and sidestep as you use key abilities to avoid the counterthrust.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte-aatrox: Fiora will try to use W Riposte to block Aatrox’s third Q cast or W pull. Bait it out with his first and second Q casts, then use the third Q cast and W. Hold Aatrox’s W while Fiora’s is available.
notes.vs-fiora-vital: The vital marked on your body shows which direction Fiora will approach from. Position on the opposite side to narrow her angle, then counterattack as she dashes toward the vital. Do not chase too far after a short trade.
notes.vs-fiora-ult: When Fiora uses R Grand Challenge, hug a wall to block access to one vital and keep her from hitting all four. If she hits all four, Fiora and nearby allies heal, which can turn the teamfight.
notes.vs-fiora-late: Fiora wins late-game 1v1s, so do not face her alone in a side lane. Send at least two players to take her down or force a teamfight. Stacking armor will not reduce the true damage from her vitals.
notes.fizz-combo-ult: The safest assassination combo is to land R Chum the Waters first, then close in with Q Urchin Strike as the shark knocks the target up. Hit them with a W Seastone Trident empowered attack while they are airborne to avoid a counterattack and keep E Playful / Trickster available for your escape. Use the time between the fish attaching and the shark appearing to close the gap.
notes.fizz-combo-e-entry: To engage with E Playful / Trickster, approach while untargetable, slow the target on landing, then follow with a W Seastone Trident empowered attack and Q Urchin Strike. This spends your escape first, so the enemy can counterattack if they still have key abilities or you have no allied support.
notes.fizz-combo-q-entry: Engage with Q Urchin Strike by dashing through the target, landing a W Seastone Trident empowered attack, and using E Playful / Trickster to dodge the counterattack. Fizz is not untargetable during the Q dash and can be hit by attacks, so choose this engage only after the enemy has used their skillshots and crowd control.
notes.fizz-skill-passive: Fizz’s passive, Nimble Fighter, lets him move through units, so in lane he can walk straight between minions to poke with W and approach from an angle his opponent may not expect. Its fixed damage reduction on every attack is especially noticeable in early, small trades.
notes.fizz-skill-q: Q Urchin Strike dashes through its target and can target enemy minions. Use a minion to dodge a skillshot or escape a gank while saving E Playful / Trickster, or dash through one to extend your approach toward an opponent. Q also applies on-hit effects, so it can trigger items.
notes.fizz-skill-w: A W Seastone Trident empowered attack deals magic damage and applies a bleed. Killing a target with it refunds mana and nearly resets W's cooldown, so last-hitting minions with W preserves mana and keeps it available. Miss the last hit, and W goes on its full cooldown, leaving you without that damage for trades.
notes.fizz-skill-e: E (Playful / Trickster) makes Fizz untargetable, letting him dodge skillshots and enemy ultimates entirely. Early in lane, its high mana cost and long cooldown mean he can use it only once or twice, so save it and play cautiously rather than treating it like invincibility. Avoid putting yourself in a position where E is your only escape.
notes.fizz-skill-e-recast: Pressing E again while untargetable makes Fizz leap forward and ends the effect early. The recast has a smaller area and no slow, but can help him create more distance or close the gap. If you need to dodge crowd control or a delayed explosion, do not recast; stay untargetable for the full duration.
notes.fizz-skill-r: R Chum the Waters can be useful even when it misses: an enemy who moves to avoid the shark loses time and may break from a clustered formation. Throw it where the enemy is going rather than where they stand, or deliberately aim into a grouped team to scatter them.
notes.fizz-phase: Fizz can threaten kills from level 2 or 3; closing in aggressively as soon as you level up before your opponent can force their Flash or secure a kill. His burst peaks when level 6 R Chum the Waters coincides with his first core item, and he remains strong at assassinating a single target late in the game. With effectively only one way to engage, though, he struggles when enemies group up.
notes.fizz-laning-trade: Fizz has no built-in healing, so even a winning trade can leave him low on health.
notes.fizz-laning-roam: Fizz is a melee mage who does not rely on attack speed, so his tower pressure is weak and he gains little from leaving a lane pushed. If you drive your opponent out of lane, use that time to join fights in a side lane or the jungle. Roaming lets your opponent push the lane, so move only after pushing the wave toward their tower.
notes.fizz-teamfight: In teamfights, approach from the flank and use R Chum the Waters to pick off one backline enemy. Wait until the enemy has used their targeted crowd control, and keep E Playful / Trickster available by avoiding its use for poke or movement before you engage. If your target is hiding behind their team, give up the engage and use R to scatter their formation.
notes.fizz-situational-antiheal: Healing can offset Fizz's burst and keep an assassination target alive. Because his damage is magic, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb early against a target with healing, then upgrade it to Morellonomicon when you can afford to delay a core item. Executioner's Calling only gives attack damage, which does not suit Fizz's scaling.
notes.vs-fizz-e-cooldown: As soon as Fizz's E Playful / Trickster goes on cooldown, he loses both an attack and an escape option. This is the clearest window to counterattack, so save crowd control and burst damage for it. Early on, his mana limits him to using E only once or twice in lane.
notes.vs-fizz-entry-read: Fizz has two ways to engage. If he comes in with E Playful / Trickster, he must land an auto attack and wait for W Seastone Trident's bleed to trigger; if he comes in with Q Urchin Strike, he must first walk into its range. Either way, counterattack right after he applies W.
notes.vs-fizz-w-lasthit: If Fizz misses a last hit with a W empowered attack, W goes on its full cooldown. Watch his last hits in lane and trade the moment he wastes W, when a substantial part of his main damage is unavailable.
notes.vs-fizz-group: Fizz relies on E for both engaging and escaping, making it difficult for him to enter a grouped formation. Stay close to your allies, bait out E, then focus him down while he has no way out. Avoid walking alone, since getting caught leaves you no way to recover, and do not chase him.
notes.vs-fizz-r: If the fish from R (Chum the Waters) attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts so they are not knocked back too. Fizz enters with Q as the shark knocks its target up; put damage or crowd control in his path to force out E. Even if you die, your allies can catch him afterward once E is gone.
notes.galio-combo-qe: For a basic trade, cast Q Winds of War, then use E Justice Punch to knock the enemy into it. The vortex forms only where the two gusts overlap, so aim at where the enemy will land rather than where they are standing.
notes.galio-combo-e-windup: Justice Punch (E) steps back before dashing forward, giving it more range than it appears to have and letting you dodge enemy skillshots during the step back. The dash stops if it hits terrain, so it gets cut short against an enemy with a wall behind them.
notes.galio-combo-w-charge: You can release W Shield of Durand at any point during its charge, and a longer charge extends the taunt. Charging reduces incoming damage but slows Galio, so start as the enemy’s combo comes in, absorb less damage, then answer with the taunt.
notes.galio-combo-full: For a full combo, knock the enemy up with Justice Punch (E), start charging Shield of Durand (W) before the knockup ends and release it quickly to follow with a taunt, then place Winds of War (Q) on that spot. If you wait until the knockup ends to start W, the enemy can walk away.
notes.galio-skill-r-shield: R Hero’s Entrance shields an ally when cast, before Galio arrives. Cast it as soon as an ally is caught to help them survive while Galio flies in, but choose the moment carefully: Galio cannot move from his position during the cast, so the decision cannot be taken back.
notes.galio-skill-r-timing: Hero's Entrance (R) knocks up all enemies around its landing point, but its cast is visible to them, giving them time to spread out. Land where an ally's crowd control is holding them in place; casting it on an ally who is already dying only leaves Galio alone in the middle of the enemy team.
notes.galio-skill-w-passive: W Shield of Durand passively grants a shield after Galio goes a while without taking damage. A single poke hit removes it in lane, so step forward only while it is up; once it breaks, back off and wait for it to recharge.
notes.galio-skill-passive: Each ability hit on a champion reduces the cooldown of P Colossal Smash, so don’t cast your abilities and retreat without landing an empowered basic attack. Its damage scales with magic resistance, letting defensive items add to your damage.
notes.galio-phase: Levels 1–2 are Galio’s weakest because his mana costs are high and he does not have E Justice Punch yet. He can start trading at level 3 when he learns E, and his value rises sharply at level 6 when R Hero’s Entrance lets him influence other lanes. Later, his role shifts from dealing damage to engaging, controlling enemies, and surviving with magic resistance.
notes.galio-laning: In lane, hit both the wave and the enemy with Q Winds of War to manage mana. As a melee champion, Galio is vulnerable to ranged poke, so save E Justice Punch to disengage against ranged opponents. Close in only just after the enemy uses their main ability on minions, then follow up with W Shield of Durand’s taunt.
notes.galio-laning-roam: Galio’s main job is to push the wave into the enemy tower and use R Hero’s Entrance to help another lane. Before going, account for the farm lost during the play and whether Teleport can make up for it.
notes.galio-teamfight: In teamfights, arrive with R Hero’s Entrance to knock enemies up, then use W Shield of Durand’s taunt to pull key threats away from your allies. Target the champion positioned to kill an ally right now.
notes.galio-teamfight-zone: Galio holds the front line and blocks off space. Place Q Winds of War’s vortex in a narrow passage to cut off the way in, and use E Justice Punch to block the enemy damage dealer’s escape route. Stagger your taunt and knockup to keep enemies controlled.
notes.galio-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, build Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. Colossal Smash (P) damage, Shield of Durand (W) damage reduction, and Hero's Entrance (R) damage all scale with magic resistance, so that defensive stat also increases Galio's damage.
notes.vs-galio-w: Galio takes much less damage while charging W Shield of Durand. When you see the charge, hold your damage and walk out of taunt range; the longer he charges, the longer the taunt lasts, so trying to stand your ground is the worst choice.
notes.vs-galio-q: Q Winds of War’s vortex forms only where its two gusts overlap. Avoid that spot to escape most of its damage over time, which scales with maximum health and therefore hits champions with more health harder.
notes.vs-galio-r: Galio’s R Hero’s Entrance has a visible cast animation and marks its landing area in advance. Walk out of the marked area immediately, and while R is ready, avoid starting a skirmish with Galio’s team in another lane.
notes.vs-galio-e: Galio’s E Justice Punch stops when it hits terrain. Standing near a wall shortens the distance he can close and makes it harder for him to continue his combo; dodge when you see the initial step back.
notes.vs-galio-lane: Galio is vulnerable to ranged poke because he is melee, and his mana costs are high. Make him spend abilities clearing the wave, then push the lane when his mana is low to deny him the chance to use R Hero’s Entrance in another lane.
notes.vs-galio-armor: Building magic resistance increases both Galio’s damage and defense, but his base armor is relatively low. Mix in physical damage instead of relying entirely on magic damage, or pressure him with physical damage early while his armor is low.
notes.gangplank-combo-barrel-chain: Powder Kegs with overlapping blast radii explode in a chain, so detonating the front keg with Q sets off those behind it and extends your reach by the length of the chain. The same target cannot take damage more than once from that chain; use it to extend your range and maintain the slow, not to increase damage.
notes.gangplank-combo-basic-trade: Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q to apply the slow, then follow up with Q or a basic attack. Wait for the slow before moving in to land a melee attack.
notes.gangplank-combo-barrel-prime: A newly placed Powder Keg has too much health to detonate with one Q. Place it where you expect to fight and let its health fall over time so one hit will set it off; spending Q on a keg that has not aged enough will ruin the trade.
notes.gangplank-skill-passive: Trial by Fire’s burn applies only to melee basic attacks, not Q. Destroying a Powder Keg resets the passive’s cooldown and grants movement speed, so you can detonate kegs in succession to chase or disengage.
notes.gangplank-skill-q: Q (Parrrley) applies on-hit effects and can critically strike, making it useful for both ranged last hits and harass. Check your remaining mana each time you decide whether to use it on your opponent or to secure a last hit.
notes.gangplank-skill-w: W (Remove Scurvy) is primarily for removing crowd control, not restoring health. Don’t use it early just because you’ve lost health; use it immediately after a key enemy crowd control effect lands to break the combo. You have no answer to crowd control that lands after W is spent.
notes.gangplank-skill-r-global: R (Cannon Barrage) can strike anywhere on the map, and its greatest value is in fights in other lanes. Watch the minimap to finish low-health enemies with it, or cast it ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path to cut off their escape.
notes.gangplank-skill-r-upgrade: Spend the Silver Serpents earned with Q to upgrade R at the shop. Depending on the upgrade, it gains more bombardments or adds true damage and a strong slow, so recall and upgrade it before an expected teamfight.
notes.gangplank-phase: Gangplank is weak at levels 1–2 because there is little time for Powder Kegs to age and a single keg deals little damage. He grows much stronger in the mid game once his full keg combo can land at once, while R gives him map-wide influence from level 6. Keg range and bombardment keep him strong late, so get through the early game without falling behind.
notes.gangplank-laning-farm: Gangplank can last-hit safely with Q without pushing the lane. In an unfavorable matchup, farm with Q in front of your turret and wait until you reach the level where your Powder Keg combo is ready before trading damage.
notes.gangplank-laning-barrel-zone: Use Powder Kegs to control space: placing them at brush entrances or along river paths can block jungle entry routes, and an opponent's attempt to destroy one reveals their position. A keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding.
notes.gangplank-laning-mana: Overusing Powder Kegs and Q together drains mana quickly. Decide in advance how many kegs to spend on a trade and save the rest for farming; if an opponent closes in while you are out of mana, you lose both your means of fighting back and escaping.
notes.gangplank-teamfight: Stay behind your team in teamfights. Place a Powder Keg in advance beside an area where the enemy team might stand, then detonate it with Q from behind to maintain an area slow. Layer R (Cannon Barrage) over it to block both their retreat path and the area around the keg, leaving them nowhere to stand.
notes.gangplank-teamfight-entry: Move in yourself only after the opponent has used their key targeted abilities. W Remove Scurvy can clear crowd control once, so overlapping effects can kill you. If the opening is uncertain, placing a Powder Keg and backing away is enough to do your part.
notes.vs-gangplank-barrel: A Powder Keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding. Destroy nearby kegs from outside their blast radius, and never step where two kegs overlap. As a keg ages, it becomes easier to detonate with one hit and more dangerous to approach.
notes.vs-gangplank-timing: Gangplank cannot execute his full Powder Keg combo before the kegs have aged. Close in and trade right after he places one, but back away if an aged keg is nearby.
notes.vs-gangplank-w: W (Remove Scurvy) clears all crowd control and heals based on missing health. Save the key crowd control you need to secure a kill until after Gangplank uses W; if the fight looks likely to last, get Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon for Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-gangplank-ult: From level 6, R (Cannon Barrage) can land anywhere on the map. Don’t cross a wide area alone when low on health, and time objective fights around whether the opposing Gangplank has used R.
notes.garen-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use Q Decisive Strike to close the gap, land its empowered auto attack to silence your opponent, then use E Judgment while they cannot retaliate with abilities.
notes.garen-combo-ult: To finish an opponent, use Q Decisive Strike, land the empowered auto attack, then use E Judgment before casting R Demacian Justice. Because R deals true damage based on missing health, let E deal its full damage first when the opponent is staying in range; if they show signs of escaping, recast E to end the spin early and use R immediately.
notes.garen-skill-q: Q Decisive Strike removes all slows affecting Garen. Since he has no mobility ability, save this chase tool until just after an opponent slows you. Its empowered auto attack remains available briefly, so you can activate Q outside attack range, close in, and still apply the silence.
notes.garen-skill-w: W Courage grants a shield and tenacity for only a very brief moment after casting, while its damage reduction lasts longer. Time it for an incoming enemy ability so the shield and tenacity can help you withstand damage and crowd control. Its passive permanently increases armor and magic resistance whenever you kill a unit, so securing last hits in lane also builds your defenses.
notes.garen-skill-e: E Judgment gains more hits per spin from attack speed and can critically strike, so mixing attack speed and critical strike chance yields more total damage than building only attack damage. Repeated hits also reduce a champion’s armor; if you have allied physical damage dealers, completing the spin helps their damage too. E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy, so during trades, position yourself with only the opposing champion inside the spin rather than catching minions alongside them.
notes.garen-skill-passive: P Perseverance restores Garen’s health after he goes some time without being hit by a champion, and minion attacks do not interrupt the healing. After a trade, briefly retreat into a brush or behind a turret to recover before returning; this sustain can keep you in lane even in unfavorable matchups.
notes.garen-phase: Garen’s base health and P Perseverance healing make him strong in early melee trades. He peaks in the mid game as Q Decisive Strike’s duration increases and R Demacian Justice reaches rank 2. Later, enemy durability makes E Judgment’s spin damage less sufficient and leaves him more reliant on R’s execute, so use lane pressure and split pushing to secure your advantage during that mid game peak.
notes.garen-situational-onhit: E Judgment’s spin damage does not apply basic attack on-hit effects, making items that derive much of their value from those effects, such as Blade of the Ruined King, less efficient for Garen’s main damage source. At a comparable value, choose items that grant attack speed and critical strike chance.
notes.garen-situational-boots-slow: If the enemy team has many slows, choose Boots of Swiftness over Berserker’s Greaves. Q Decisive Strike can remove a slow, but until it comes off cooldown, slow resistance helps reduce the time it takes to close the gap.
notes.garen-situational-mr: If enemy magic damage is a threat, switch to Mercury’s Treads for magic resistance and tenacity. Tenacity is especially valuable because being locked down by crowd control while E Judgment spins without hitting anyone is particularly costly for Garen.
notes.garen-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder earlier; if healing reduction is needed even sooner, get Executioner’s Calling first. Healing opponents can offset E Judgment’s sustained damage, making trades difficult without healing reduction.
notes.garen-laning: Let the wave push toward you. Garen has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks when he pushes the lane, so keep wards available. Trade as your opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion, and if E Judgment pushes the wave, retreat into a brush to recover with P Perseverance.
notes.garen-teamfight: Garen cannot initiate teamfights himself. Once your allies engage, time W Courage as you enter, hold the front line while E Judgment reduces enemy armor, and use R Demacian Justice on an opponent whose health has fallen. Walking straight in leaves you vulnerable to kiting, so look for a flank or an approach from outside vision toward the enemy backline. If there is no opening for a teamfight, split push instead, using P Perseverance to stay in a side lane without recalling and keep one opponent occupied.
notes.vs-garen-q-cooldown: Garen’s Q Decisive Strike empowers an auto attack that silences you and prevents retaliation with abilities. Since Q does not have a short cooldown, start a trade right after he uses it on a minion or spends the empowered attack; do not approach first while Q is active.
notes.vs-garen-silence: Garen’s Q Decisive Strike silence interrupts abilities with long cast times and channeled ultimates. Hold those abilities while his empowered auto attack is ready, then use them after he has spent the silence.
notes.vs-garen-e: Garen’s E Judgment deals continuous damage while he spins and bonus damage to the nearest enemy, so staying close for longer puts you at a disadvantage. Avoid extended fights and repeat short trades where you hit and back away. If you cannot leave the spin’s range, move among allied minions so a minion becomes the nearest enemy; also avoid approaching Garen inside a brush, where you would take the full spin damage.
notes.vs-garen-w: Immediately after Garen activates W Courage, its brief shield and tenacity help him withstand burst damage and crowd control. When you see the activation, delay your combo slightly before using it.
notes.vs-garen-r: Garen’s R Demacian Justice deals true damage based on his opponent’s missing health, so armor and magic resistance cannot reduce it. Do not count on tank items to save you: below half health, stay outside his R range. Champions that repeatedly recover from low health through life steal are especially vulnerable to its execute.
notes.vs-garen-mobility: Garen has no mobility ability and struggles to leave his lane to influence others. Push the wave hard to expose him to jungle ganks, then, once the wave is pushed in, create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
notes.garen-combo-e-first: If the enemy is already in melee range, use E Judgment before Q Decisive Strike. You can activate Q during the spin without interrupting it, then apply the silence with your first auto attack after E ends; this lets you save Q until the enemy tries to counterattack with an ability.
notes.gnar-skill-rage: Gnar’s passive, Rage Gene, builds Rage when he deals or takes damage. Once the bar is full, his next ability transforms him into Mega Gnar, so the ability use determines the timing. If you are not ready to engage, hold your abilities at full Rage and trigger the transformation when you want it.
notes.gnar-skill-rage-window: When Mega Gnar’s duration ends and he returns to Mini Gnar, he cannot build Rage for a while. This is his weakest window, so finish the fight and back off before the transformation ends. Opponents will try to engage during that window; anticipate when it will begin and position accordingly.
notes.gnar-combo-mini: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Q Boomerang Throw, then E Hop onto a minion or enemy to bounce forward, and finish with an auto attack. Catching the returning boomerang greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, so aim your E movement along its return path. Repeated hits on the same target trigger W Hyper for bonus damage and a large movement speed boost.
notes.gnar-combo-transform: For a transformation all-in, use E Hop at full Rage to close the gap and trigger the transformation. Landing on a unit makes Mini Gnar bounce farther; transform during the bounce to land as Mega Gnar, then stun with W Wallop, auto attack, and follow with Q Boulder Toss. Using another ability to transform before closing in leaves you without that way to reach the enemy.
notes.gnar-combo-wall-r: Finish Mega Gnar’s combo with R GNAR! Position Gnar, the enemy, and a wall in a straight line before casting: only enemies thrown into a wall are stunned and take bonus damage. Follow the stun with W Wallop to keep them controlled. Without a wall hit, R only knocks enemies back and slows them.
notes.gnar-combo-flash-r: If you cannot line up a wall stun, use Flash to reposition and aim R (GNAR!) toward the wall. It throws nearby enemies in the direction Gnar faces, so flashing behind an opponent can turn a poor angle into a wall angle.
notes.gnar-skill-q: Gnar’s Q works differently in each form. Mini Gnar’s Q Boomerang Throw returns after hitting an enemy, deals reduced damage to subsequent targets, and has a greatly reduced cooldown if he catches it. Mega Gnar’s Q Boulder Toss deals area damage, but the boulder stops where it hits an enemy; throw it where you can pick it up to reduce the cooldown. Catching either projectile is a key part of the damage cycle.
notes.gnar-skill-w: Mini Gnar’s W (Hyper) is a passive that triggers after repeated hits on the same target, so very short trades will not activate it. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it useful against tanks, and it grants movement speed when triggered; when poking, focus auto attacks and Q (Boomerang Throw) on one target. Mega Gnar’s W (Wallop) is a separate ability that slams the area in front of him and stuns enemies, so take care not to press W in Mini form and waste passive stacks.
notes.gnar-skill-e: Mini Gnar’s E Hop bounces much farther when he lands on a unit, while Mega Gnar’s E Crunch lands without bouncing and deals area damage, giving him a shorter escape. Use E to engage as Mega Gnar, but check its cooldown first so it will be available to escape after you return to Mini Gnar.
notes.gnar-phase: At levels 1–2, Gnar can gain an advantage by poking with ranged auto attacks and Q Boomerang Throw. His base health is among the lowest of all champions, though, so avoid extended close fights early even as Mega Gnar. Kill opportunities open up with R GNAR! at level 6, and he peaks in the mid game after completing his first core item. Late in the game, he gets the most value from terrain that offers a wall angle.
notes.gnar-laning: In lane, poke as Mini Gnar with ranged auto attacks and Q Boomerang Throw, then back away before the opponent can retaliate. Use Q to clear waves and catch the boomerang to keep reducing its cooldown without spending mana. Commit to a close-range all-in only when you transform into Mega Gnar, and finish the trade before the transformation ends.
notes.gnar-laning-rage: Taking damage also builds Rage, so drawing minion aggro or taking hits without trading back can force a transformation at the wrong time. Transforming under the enemy turret or without allied support wastes it. Plan where to transform around recalls, level-ups, and jungle involvement, then adjust how much you trade until that moment.
notes.gnar-teamfight: Gnar’s teamfight impact depends on a wall angle. Choose the fight location in advance, position so opponents have a wall behind them, then engage as Mega Gnar and open with R GNAR! If you are still Mini Gnar, stay back and poke with Q Boomerang Throw while building Rage instead of forcing an engage.
notes.gnar-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing a fight during Mega Gnar’s transformation, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce it. His Mega form has a fixed duration, so drawn-out fights put him at a disadvantage.
notes.vs-gnar-rage: Watch Gnar’s Rage bar when deciding when to fight. For a while after he returns from Mega to Mini, he cannot gain Rage or transform again. This is his weakest window: go all-in or start a teamfight with your allies.
notes.vs-gnar-wall: Gnar’s R GNAR! stuns and deals bonus damage only when it throws you into a wall. Avoid standing with your back to one or positioning yourself between Gnar and a wall. Teamfights in tight spaces favor him.
notes.vs-gnar-mini: Mini Gnar can poke from range, but his base health is among the lowest of all champions. If you can close the gap, fight him up close in Mini form; otherwise, farm near your turret and wait for his transformation cycle.
notes.vs-gnar-q: Mini Gnar’s Q Boomerang Throw can hit on both the outward and return paths, and catching it greatly reduces its cooldown. Move out of the boomerang’s path to make the catch harder; if Gnar misses it, the gap before his next Q poke is noticeably longer.
notes.vs-gnar-mega: Mega Gnar is durable and deals heavy burst damage, but he is slow, and his E Crunch does not bounce or travel as far as Mini Gnar’s E Hop. When he transforms, keep your distance instead of fighting him head-on and wait out the transformation. Watch his appearance and Rage bar for signs that a transformation is near.
notes.gragas-combo-eq: Gragas’s core combo is E into Q: while dashing with E, roll Q to the landing spot, then recast it while the target is knocked up. They cannot walk out of the barrel’s radius, so both abilities are guaranteed to hit.
notes.gragas-combo-qe: For Q into E, roll out the barrel first and wait for the opponent to come near before engaging. The longer it stays out, the more damage and slow it gains, so time the detonation to E’s impact instead of triggering it immediately. This is especially strong in lane ganks where the opponent’s retreat path is predictable.
notes.gragas-combo-full: The full combo is E hit, W, Q detonation, then R if needed. Because W takes time to drink, press it during E’s knockup so the empowered basic attack lands before the target comes down. Use R to move the opponent where you want, rather than simply to finish them off.
notes.gragas-skill-q: Q (Barrel Roll) lets you choose when to detonate the barrel. The longer it sits, the more damage and slow it gains, but enemies can see and dodge it, so in fights, detonate it when they cannot move. It deals reduced damage to minions, making it inefficient for clearing waves; save it for fights rather than farming.
notes.gragas-skill-w: W’s damage reduction starts as soon as Gragas begins drinking, so press it when you see an opponent’s burst coming, before it hits. The empowered basic attack deals maximum health based damage around its target, making it especially strong against jungle camps and high health opponents.
notes.gragas-skill-r: R pushes opponents outward from the explosion point, so land it behind a target to send them toward your team. Landing it between the target and your team pushes them away instead. It cannot push opponents over walls, so account for its limited displacement against someone standing next to one.
notes.gragas-skill-r-split: R (Explosive Cask) can also split the enemy formation: land it between the front line and back line to push only the back line away. This gives your team time to clear the front line with a numbers advantage and has a more direct impact on winning a teamfight than using R to seek a kill.
notes.gragas-skill-passive: Use abilities at each jungle camp to stay healthy and manage your mana.
notes.gragas-jungle: While jungling, wear down camps quickly with W (Drunken Rage)'s empowered basic attack and stay healthy through passive healing. E (Body Slam)'s short cooldown creates frequent gank opportunities, so watch the lanes and show up whenever an enemy is within E's reach instead of clearing every camp.
notes.gragas-jungle-gank: For the most reliable gank, circle behind the lane, roll Q onto the opponent’s retreat path, then use E to knock them up as they try to back away. Engaging with E from the front gives them a path to walk toward their turret and sharply reduces your chances.
notes.gragas-phase: Learning E at level 2 or 3 opens up ganks, while R at level 6 creates reliable kill opportunities. Gragas’s burst peaks in the mid game after one or two ability power items; in the late game, his lack of sustained damage narrows his role to burst and disrupting enemy formations.
notes.gragas-teamfight: In teamfights, activate W, engage with E to knock up the back line, follow with Q, and use R to split the enemy formation. Before going in, check that the opponent has used their targeted crowd control and that your team is close enough to follow up. If Gragas dies first, your team loses its means of initiating.
notes.gragas-situational-tenacity: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier so you can detonate Q after engaging.
notes.vs-gragas-r: Gragas’s R pushes enemies outward from the explosion point. When he has R available, do not stand with your back to an enemy turret or the enemy team: being pushed toward them can get you killed. Standing against a wall shortens the distance you are pushed and is safer.
notes.vs-gragas-e: Gragas's E (Body Slam) cooldown is greatly reduced when he collides with an enemy, letting him use it again soon after. Chase him too far and he can escape with two E casts while your team gets picked off; pursue only when you are certain you can kill him.
notes.vs-gragas-q: A Q barrel does not detonate as soon as it rolls in, so leave its radius immediately when you see one. The longer it stays out, the more damage and slow it gains; avoid standing on it. If E hits you near the barrel, you will take both E and Q’s explosion.
notes.vs-gragas-w: When Gragas starts drinking with W, hold your burst until the damage reduction ends. It applies from the moment he begins drinking, so the same abilities will deal much more damage if you wait briefly.
notes.vs-gragas-position: Gragas’s engage depends on E, so avoid narrow paths and bushes without vision, and keep your back line from standing alone within its range. If E hits you, immediately move out of the barrel’s radius; fighting back in place leaves you exposed to Q’s explosion.
notes.vs-gragas-late: Gragas wins through burst and formation disruption in the early and mid game, but his sustained damage is weak late. Hold your formation and survive early and mid game objective fights, and the matchup improves as time goes on.
notes.gragas-skill-e: Hitting an enemy with E greatly reduces its cooldown, letting you engage and then use it again to disengage. A miss leaves you waiting out the full cooldown, so decide before going in whether to use E to initiate or save it for an escape.
notes.graves-combo-engage: Close the gap with E (Quickdraw), then land basic attacks at point-blank range. Since the dash loads one shell, using E just before a reload keeps your damage going without interruption. Once you are close, block the opponent’s vision with W (Smoke Screen) and follow with Q (End of the Line), leaving them little time to react.
notes.graves-combo-q-wall: Q (End of the Line) explodes immediately on hitting terrain. Against an opponent backed up to a wall, aim at the wall so the explosion gives them no time to dodge; against an enemy on the other side, fire Q along the wall so only the explosion reaches them.
notes.graves-combo-r: R (Collateral Damage) explodes again in a cone behind the champion it hits, so line it up when other enemies are behind your target. Casting it also knocks Graves backward, letting you use it to finish a target or escape over a wall.
notes.graves-skill-passive: Basic attacks use a two-shell magazine, then Graves must reload. Each shell fires a spread of pellets, all of which are blocked by the first unit they hit. You cannot hit an enemy behind a minion or ally, so approach from an angle with no units between you and your target.
notes.graves-skill-q: Q (End of the Line)’s follow-up explosion deals far more damage than the outgoing projectile. Aim slightly ahead of or beside an opponent so they remain in the explosion area even if they dodge the projectile. At jungle camps, fire Q into a wall to cover the whole camp with the explosion.
notes.graves-skill-w: When ganking, place W on the opponent's escape route to help your allies chase.
notes.graves-skill-e: Using E (Quickdraw) toward an enemy champion grants twice as many armor stacks, and each basic attack hit reduces its cooldown. Keep landing attacks during a fight to use E twice. Spending it carelessly on an early escape costs you both an engage tool and armor.
notes.graves-phase: Graves’s level 1 attack damage and armor are among the highest, helping him clear early camps quickly and win level 2–3 fights. R (Collateral Damage) gives him a finishing tool at level 6, improving his ganks. His short range and low magic resistance leave him vulnerable if caught first late in the game, so use his early to mid game power peak to secure objectives and vision and cement your lead.
notes.graves-laning-route: Graves’s fast jungle clear makes him an efficient farmer. At camps with walls nearby, fire Q (End of the Line) into a wall to clear even faster. If a gank opportunity is uncertain, clear camps instead to build a level and gold lead.
notes.graves-teamfight: Do not initiate teamfights from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, use E (Quickdraw) to move in from the side or rear and get close to their damage dealers. Stay where no unit can get between you and your target; that positioning has the greatest effect on your damage.
notes.graves-situational-antiheal: Against opponents who survive through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Graves deals his damage in a short burst, so applying healing reduction makes a substantial difference to your chance of securing a kill.
notes.graves-situational-boots: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps to bolster your magic resistance.
notes.vs-graves-block: The first unit hit blocks every pellet of Graves’s basic attack. In a chaotic fight, keep a minion or ally between you and him to block his main source of damage.
notes.vs-graves-reload: After firing both shells, Graves must reload and briefly cannot basic attack. Counterattack or create distance immediately after his second shot.
notes.vs-graves-smoke: W (Smoke Screen) limits your vision and slows you while you are inside it, but its effects end as soon as you leave. Take the shortest route out, then reengage.
notes.vs-graves-q: Graves’s Q, End of the Line, explodes immediately when it hits terrain, leaving no room to dodge the blast if you fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow jungle passage. Take fights against Graves in open terrain whenever possible.
notes.vs-graves-armor: Almost all of Graves’s damage is physical, so armor makes a noticeable difference. Buying Plated Steelcaps earlier can change how early to mid game fights play out.
notes.graves-laning-gank: Gank when the enemy has pushed past the middle of the lane and an ally can lock them down. Use E (Quickdraw) to close the angle, then throw W (Smoke Screen) onto their escape path. The smoke blocks the vision of enemies inside it without blocking allied vision, creating an opening for your ally’s abilities to land.
notes.gwen-combo-basic: Build Q stacks with auto attacks, then close in with E, land an empowered auto attack, and cast Q. Without stacks, Q snips fewer times and deals much less damage, so hit even a minion to build stacks before trading.
notes.gwen-combo-q-center: Only enemies in the center of Q’s cone take some of its damage as true damage and have Gwen’s passive applied to them. Position the target in the center rather than merely aiming Q in their direction; landing that center hit matters especially against targets with high armor and magic resistance.
notes.gwen-combo-w-cancel: While Gwen is inside W’s mist, enemies outside it cannot target her. Activate W just as an enemy starts a targeted ability or auto attack to make it miss, but remember that W does not block turret attacks during a dive.
notes.gwen-combo-w-reposition: Recast W to draw the mist toward Gwen. If she tries to leave it with E, W recasts automatically, so move the mist yourself first to stay untargetable as you advance. When you reposition the mist determines how long W remains useful.
notes.gwen-skill-e-reset: E refunds a substantial part of its cooldown on the first hit, even against a minion. In a wave, you can use it to engage and then escape in quick succession; in open ground with nothing to hit, the full cooldown leaves you stuck.
notes.gwen-skill-e-range: E’s empowered auto attacks gain both attack speed and range. After closing in on a ranged opponent, use that extra reach to land another attack even if they start backing away.
notes.gwen-skill-passive: Gwen’s passive deals magic damage based on the target’s maximum health and heals her only when it hits a champion. Each auto attack is worth more against a high-health frontline target, but clearing minions alone gives her no healing; her sustain depends on how long she can keep attacking champions.
notes.gwen-skill-r: R can be cast up to three times, with more needles on each cast. Use the first, slowing cast to catch a fleeing enemy, then recast only if you can keep them in range long enough to land the third.
notes.gwen-skill-r-passive: When R hits an enemy champion, it applies Gwen's passive, so use the first cast from range to damage and slow them before closing in with E. It can help start an engage instead of serving only as a finisher.
notes.gwen-phase: Gwen’s trades are weak at levels 1–2, before she can build Q stacks. Once she learns W, she can avoid poke from ranged opponents, and her dueling grows stronger in midgame as she builds ability power items. Late game, her maximum health damage lets her cut down the enemy frontline directly.
notes.gwen-laning: In lane, build Q stacks with auto attacks and use W to avoid counterattacks. Gwen ranks high in damage per minute at 14 minutes but tends to have fewer kills, so her value comes from scaling: avoid forcing early engages and focus on CS and levels.
notes.gwen-laning-w-gank: W also helps Gwen survive ganks: activating it as a gank begins can avoid targeted crowd control from enemies outside the mist. Keep it available while pushing the wave.
notes.gwen-teamfight: In teamfights, Gwen’s job is to cut down the frontline directly. Engage with E, use W to avoid focused attacks, then land Q’s true damage on the frontline with a center hit. Go in when the enemy’s key crowd control is down or W is ready.
