notes.gwen-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing could turn a duel, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Gwen can stay close and keep landing auto attacks and Q to maintain the effect.
notes.vs-gwen-w: Gwen cannot be targeted from outside W’s mist while she is inside it. Move into the mist or wait for it to expire before using targeted abilities or Ignite; turrets ignore the mist, so pushing her under a turret is effective.
notes.vs-gwen-q: The center of Gwen's Q cone deals heavy true damage. Move sideways to get out of the center of Q's cone. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce Q's true damage.
notes.vs-gwen-e: Hitting something with E gives Gwen a large cooldown refund, letting her use it repeatedly around minion waves. To catch her, draw her into an area without minions or engage with immobilizing crowd control ready.
notes.vs-gwen-passive: Gwen needs to auto attack champions to sustain herself, so stay outside her auto attack range to stop the healing. Trade at early levels before she builds Q stacks, and avoid getting close when Q is fully stacked.
notes.vs-gwen-mr: Gwen’s maximum health magic damage makes stacking health alone hurt you more. Build magic resistance items such as Spectre’s Cowl, but keep your distance as well: magic resistance cannot reduce the true damage at the center of Q.
notes.hecarim-combo-gank: For a gank, activate E (Devastating Charge) early, run in from outside vision, and take a wide route to build distance. As you reach the target, use W (Spirit of Dread), then Q (Rampage), then the empowered E basic attack to knock them back. Its damage and knockback distance increase with the distance traveled after activation, so circle around once instead of attacking immediately.
notes.hecarim-combo-e-r: E (Devastating Charge) stops losing duration during R (Onslaught of Shadows), so you can activate E, run in, and charge with R, then land an empowered E basic attack after R ends with your accumulated travel distance intact. For maximum damage, use E → run → R → landing fear → empowered E basic attack → Q (Rampage).
notes.hecarim-combo-q-stack: Each Q (Rampage) hit adds a stack, increasing its damage and shortening its cooldown. Hit a jungle monster with Q just before a gank or objective fight to build stacks, then land two fully stacked Qs in quick succession as soon as you arrive.
notes.hecarim-skill-passive: P (Warpath) converts bonus movement speed into attack damage, so the speed from E, R, Ghost, and boots all contributes to Hecarim’s damage. Start fights while that bonus speed is active; standing and fighting after it wears off sharply reduces your damage even with the same items.
notes.hecarim-skill-q: Q (Rampage) damages enemies around Hecarim, so use it whenever it comes off cooldown. Its reduced damage to minions makes it inefficient for clearing waves, but during a fight, keep hitting something—even a monster or minion—to maintain its stacks and cooldown reduction.
notes.hecarim-skill-w: W (Spirit of Dread) heals Hecarim based on damage nearby enemies take, including damage dealt by allies. Activate it in the middle of a fight where allies and enemies are clustered together; it provides almost no healing when you flee alone. Healing from jungle monsters is capped, so do not rely on it solely for clearing.
notes.hecarim-skill-e: E (Devastating Charge) lets you pass through minions and monsters. Use it to cross a lane through a wave or escape between minions, and position yourself so the empowered basic attack knocks the enemy toward your allies or toward the enemy turret, whichever you intend.
notes.hecarim-skill-r: With R (Onslaught of Shadows), Hecarim travels only to the targeted location, while the spectral riders always continue to the end of its range. You can stop beside a nearby target to fear them and still damage enemies farther behind with the riders. Fear duration increases with the distance charged, so start from as far away as possible.
notes.hecarim-phase: Hecarim’s early jungle clear is ordinary until Q (Rampage) gains stacks, but once he has W (Spirit of Dread), he clears faster without losing health. Level 6 and R (Onslaught of Shadows) bring his first power spike, and he peaks in the mid game with attack damage and ability haste. Late in the game, his durability falls short of a tank’s, so a frontal entry can get him killed quickly; engage from the side instead.
notes.hecarim-jungle-path: Hecarim clears quickly, so keep cycling through camps. Before level 6, E (Devastating Charge)’s knockback is his only hard crowd control, making ganks less likely to succeed; clearing your camps and reaching level 6 is more valuable than forcing one. As soon as you hit level 6, approach a lane and look for an opening to use R (Onslaught of Shadows).
notes.hecarim-gank-angle: Before level 6, gank only when you can get behind the enemy. Activate E (Devastating Charge) outside vision, circle toward their escape route, and use the empowered basic attack to knock them toward your allies. Charging straight at them gives E too little travel distance, weakening both its damage and knockback and letting the enemy simply walk away.
notes.hecarim-teamfight: In teamfights, avoid trying to push through the enemy tank; use R (Onslaught of Shadows) from the side or behind to split the damage dealers’ formation. The moment its fear disrupts the enemy team is your allies’ cue to enter. Once you engage, stay in the thick of the fight with W (Spirit of Dread) active so it can heal you.
notes.hecarim-situational-cc: Hecarim’s damage depends on movement speed, so being rooted cuts his damage as well. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after your first core item to remove one immediately after engaging.
notes.hecarim-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps you from finishing a dive, buy Executioner’s Calling after your first core item to reduce that healing. If you no longer need it, sell it last.
notes.vs-hecarim-w: Hecarim’s W (Spirit of Dread) heals him based on damage nearby enemies take, including damage his allies deal. Having several players stay close and attack him for a long time can keep him alive instead. His durability falls short of a tank’s, so finish him with a short burst of damage or back out of W’s range before reengaging.
notes.vs-hecarim-e: Hecarim’s E (Devastating Charge) gains damage and knockback distance the farther he runs after activation. If he suddenly turns and runs the other way, he is building travel distance rather than fleeing. Break his line of sight or move toward your allies so the knockback does not leave you isolated.
notes.vs-hecarim-r: Hecarim’s R (Onslaught of Shadows) can fear several players at once when they are grouped together, so spread out your teamfight formation to limit how many it catches. Fear takes away control of your movement rather than stopping movement entirely; be ready to use a cleanse or mobility ability before it hits.
notes.vs-hecarim-ms: Slows and roots also reduce Hecarim’s damage. When the fight starts, apply movement impairments to Hecarim first.
notes.vs-hecarim-early: Hecarim’s ganks are weak before level 6 because he lacks reliable hard crowd control, but his fast camp clear lets him reach level 6 early. Avoid pushing your lane too far early on, and establish river vision once the enemy jungler reaches level 6.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-placement: Turrets have a placement limit and shut down shortly after Heimerdinger moves too far away, so place them where you intend to stand rather than throwing them ahead. As support, set them at brush entrances or river approaches instead of the middle of the lane to gain vision and poke where enemies must pass. You can store multiple placement charges; save at least one to put a turret down immediately when a fight breaks out.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-priority: Turrets prioritize enemies Heimerdinger has recently damaged or who are attacking him. Hit the target you want them to focus with an auto attack or ability first; as support, tag the enemy ADC even if a tank is standing in front. This can make a substantial difference to your turret damage.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-charge: Turrets charge slowly on their own and fire much more powerfully at full charge, so check their charge before starting a fight; a newly placed turret poses little threat. Each W rocket that hits a champion charges nearby turrets a little, while hitting an enemy champion with E fully charges them at once. Plan your engage around that charging sequence.
notes.heimerdinger-combo-basic: Set up turrets where the fight will happen, land E directly at its center to stun the target and fully charge the turrets, then fire W while they shoot and auto attack the enemy you want them to focus. E comes first for the instant turret charge, not its damage. W's rockets converge on your cursor, but only the first hit deals full damage, so aim a little behind the enemy to make the convergence point overlap them and choose an angle that minions cannot block.
notes.heimerdinger-combo-r-e: As support, usually use R to empower E: the grenade bounces several times, with larger stun and slow areas that can catch enemies the narrow direct hit would miss. After activating R, throw E along the enemy's retreat path rather than at their feet so its bounces follow them, then pour turret fire and W into the stunned target to start the teamfight. If you activate R by mistake, cast it again to cancel it.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-r-choice: The ability you empower with R changes its role. Empowered Q creates a turret that does not count toward the placement limit, applies an area slow, and is immune to crowd control; use it to hold narrow passages near objectives or defend an allied turret. Empowered W fires successive volleys for burst damage, making it useful for finishing a fleeing enemy or clearing an incoming wave. Empowered abilities cost no resources, so you can also use one in a pinch when you are out of mana.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-e: E damages and slows enemies throughout its area, but only those hit at the center are stunned. Its unempowered direct hit area is narrow, so throw it after the enemy uses their mobility ability or over an ally's crowd control; otherwise, aim ahead toward a narrow passage on their retreat path. E also fully charges turrets, so do not spend it carelessly on wave clear.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-passive: Heimerdinger gains movement speed near allied turrets and his own. With no mobility ability, he relies on that speed to escape: when holding a risky lane position, set a turret on your retreat path beforehand, and when defending under an allied turret, use the boost to walk out of enemy engage abilities.
notes.heimerdinger-laning-support: Support Heimerdinger's turrets can push the wave. If you do not want to push, place them outside minion range, in brush or behind the lane, so they attack enemy champions instead. To push the enemy ADC out of lane, deliberately place turrets in the lane and secure vision as you advance. An enemy stepping forward to destroy a turret gives you a good chance to land E directly.
notes.heimerdinger-laning-mid: In mid, turrets absorb the wave for Heimerdinger, helping him hold the lane and farm. Cluster them behind the lane and turret fire plus an E stun can punish an enemy jungler's engage, even turning a dive in your favor. His lack of mobility makes solo roams difficult, so push decisively to keep your opponent in lane and let your jungler gain an advantage elsewhere.
notes.heimerdinger-phase: Heimerdinger's health and armor are among the lowest of all champions, making levels 1–2, when he has only one turret, his most dangerous period. At level 3, multiple turrets and E give him lane control; at level 6, R greatly improves his ability to start fights. Later, his turrets cannot keep up with moving skirmishes, so draw fights to a position you have chosen in advance.
notes.heimerdinger-teamfight: In teamfights, choose the ground before the enemy engages: place and charge turrets in a narrow passage near an objective or beside an allied turret, then draw enemies into them. Avoid moving fights in open areas where the turrets cannot contribute. If the enemy engages, interrupt them with an E stun and retreat behind your turrets; while your allies hold the position, use an R-empowered turret to block the route.
notes.heimerdinger-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who can dive straight onto you, fit Zhonya’s Hourglass into your core build. Heimerdinger has no mobility skill to escape once they engage, but his deployed turrets keep firing while he buys time, turning those extra moments into damage.
notes.heimerdinger-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing lets them withstand your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon: turret shots deal damage gradually, and without reduced healing, that damage can be offset by their recovery. If gold is tight as support, delay it until after you complete one core item.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-turret: Turrets shut down shortly after Heimerdinger moves too far away, so pushing him out is faster than destroying them one by one. They prioritize targets he has recently damaged or who are attacking him; when diving, have a durable ally hit Heimerdinger first to draw turret fire before your damage dealers go in.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-e: Heimerdinger's grenade stuns only at its center; a hit outside the center merely slows. When its landing marker appears, keep moving sideways to leave the center. That stun is his only guaranteed crowd control and a direct hit instantly fully charges nearby turrets, so avoiding it also greatly reduces the burst that follows.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-r: After level 6, R empowers Heimerdinger's next ability. An empowered grenade bounces several times and has a much larger stun area, while empowered rockets can finish a low-health ally with burst damage. While his ultimate is available, avoid grouping in narrow passages, especially for a standoff at a single spot in front of an objective.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-body: Heimerdinger's health and armor are among the lowest of all champions, and he has no mobility ability. If you go around his turret position or withstand its fire, a single engage can take him down. Avoid repeated head-on trades in front of his turrets; approach from the side or through brush instead.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-timing: Turrets charge over time and fire much harder at full charge, so engage just after one is placed or immediately after it fires a powerful shot. If Heimerdinger hits a champion with E, nearby turrets instantly reach full charge; leave their range immediately if the grenade hits you.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-melee: As a melee champion, last-hitting inside turret range can expose you to both turret fire and rockets. Do not force yourself to take the wave: wait outside turret range and step forward only after Heimerdinger uses E or spends all his turret placement charges. If you cannot confidently close the gap and take him down, give up the lane and pressure a side lane instead.
notes.hwei-skill-subject-system: Hwei’s Q, W, and E select subjects rather than cast spells: press one to open its three options, then press Q, W, or E again to cast. The three spells within a subject share a cooldown. Selecting a subject costs nothing until you cast, so choose one in advance when you can and keep the cast key ready to react faster.
notes.hwei-skill-passive: Hit an enemy champion with one spell, then a different spell before the mark expires to trigger Signature of the Visionary beneath them. Follow the first hit promptly; the explosion deals area damage, so landing the second hit on grouped enemies can damage them all.
notes.hwei-skill-q: Subject: Disaster is Hwei’s main source of damage. Devastating Fire (QQ) is a fast projectile that deals damage based on maximum health, making it useful for single-target poke and against bulky enemies; Severing Bolt (QW) reaches far but takes time to land, while Molten Fissure (QE) leaves a lava pool whose damage over time and slow deny an area. All three share a cooldown, so choose the spell that fits the situation before casting.
notes.hwei-skill-q-lightning: Severing Bolt (QW) deals sharply increased damage based on missing health when its target is isolated or immobilized. Use it as a finisher immediately after you or an ally applies crowd control, or aim ahead of a fleeing enemy to catch them as they run.
notes.hwei-skill-w: Subject: Serenity is Hwei’s only way to support allies. Fleeting Current (WQ) increases allies’ movement speed along a straight path to help them engage or retreat, while Pool of Reflection (WW) shields allies within its area. Stirring Lights (WE) adds damage to the next few hits and restores mana, making it useful when mana runs low midway through lane. Serenity has the longest cooldown and highest mana cost; using one of its spells also locks out the other two until that cooldown ends, so choose deliberately.
notes.hwei-skill-e: Subject: Torment offers three forms of crowd control: Grim Visage (EQ) fears the first enemy hit to stop an engage, Gaze of the Abyss (EW) leaves an eye that grants vision and roots an enemy entering its area, and Crushing Maw (EE) pulls enemies toward a target point and slows them. Place the eye at a river entrance or bush opening ahead of time for vision and protection against ganks; under heavy jungle pressure, save Torment for that purpose instead of using it to poke.
notes.hwei-skill-r: Spiraling Despair (R) attaches to the first enemy champion hit, grows while stacking slows, then ends in a large area explosion. Land it when enemies cannot easily spread out, ideally on the front line of a grouped team, and follow with Subject: Disaster.
notes.hwei-combo-pull: Pull enemies together with Crushing Maw (EE), then land Severing Bolt (QW) there for increased damage and a Signature explosion.
notes.hwei-combo-poke: For lane poke, land Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete Signature of the Visionary with Grim Visage (EQ) or Molten Fissure (QE). Spells within Subject: Disaster share a cooldown, so two consecutive hits from that subject are impossible and the second hit must come from another subject.
notes.hwei-combo-ult: In a teamfight, land Spiraling Despair (R) on grouped enemies, pull back anyone trying to spread out with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Molten Fissure (QE) or Devastating Fire (QQ). As R’s slow stacks, enemies struggle to walk out of Molten Fissure’s pool.
notes.hwei-phase: Hwei is very weak at levels 1–2: only one subject is available, leaving him without a second spell to complete Signature of the Visionary, and mana is tight. He can start poking once two subjects are available, then gains major power spikes at level 6 when he gets R and after completing his first core item. Because he is fragile and has among the lowest defensive stats, dealing damage safely from behind is more valuable at every stage than stepping forward.
notes.hwei-laning: Clear waves with Molten Fissure (QE), then use any time left over to poke with Devastating Fire (QQ). Prioritize farming over risky poke and look for a Signature of the Visionary combo when an enemy lines up behind minions. Hwei’s mana costs are high enough that wasting a subject can cost you the next wave, so avoid casting whenever a cooldown ends.
notes.hwei-teamfight: In teamfights, play at the edge of Hwei’s range and place Molten Fissure (QE) across the enemy’s approach. If they begin an engage, turn back the leader with Grim Visage (EQ), then commit Subject: Disaster after an ally catches someone. Keep Subject: Torment available to deal with enemies who reach you instead of spending it all on poke.
notes.hwei-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against melee enemies who must get close to deal damage. Hwei has virtually no mobility and is unlikely to survive being caught; Zhonya’s stasis can run down the time they have to engage while his remaining subjects come off cooldown.
notes.vs-hwei-signature: Hwei’s Signature of the Visionary damage is completed when two different spells hit in quick succession. If the first hits you, move immediately instead of holding your ground so the second misses; taking just one hit and backing off prevents the passive explosion.
notes.vs-hwei-lightning: Severing Bolt (QW) deals much more damage when it hits you while you are immobilized or isolated. If crowd control catches you, use a cleanse or movement ability to escape as quickly as possible, and stay near allies to avoid the isolation condition.
notes.vs-hwei-eye: The eye left by Gaze of the Abyss (EW) grants vision and roots the first enemy that enters it. Before ganking, check for an eye; if one is present, take another route or let a minion or something else trigger it first.
notes.vs-hwei-dive: Hwei has no mobility and is very fragile, with Subject: Torment his only way to answer an enemy who gets close. Engage just after he uses that subject to poke or clear a wave; if it is ready, the first champion in may be feared or rooted.
notes.vs-hwei-zone: Hwei uses ground effects and his eye to limit where enemies can move.
notes.illaoi-combo-basic: For trades, pull out the spirit with E, cast Q toward a tentacle to start its slam, then use W to close in on the target and make every nearby tentacle strike with you. Cast Q first so two slams overlap when W lands.
notes.illaoi-combo-teamfight: To start a teamfight, pull out the nearest enemy’s spirit with E, immediately use R to summon as many tentacles as possible, then start attacking the spirit. With the spirit already pulled out, a hit on it counts toward R’s tentacle count, greatly increasing the number summoned.
notes.illaoi-combo-aoe: The spirit and its host can both be hit by the same area ability, and damage dealt to the spirit transfers to the host. When an ally has area damage, one cast can effectively hit the host twice, so pull the spirit into a spot their ability can reach.
notes.illaoi-skill-tentacle-terrain: Tentacles spawn near impassable terrain, a set distance apart. Illaoi’s damage drops sharply in open areas without tentacles. Draw fights toward walls and areas with tentacles.
notes.illaoi-skill-tentacle-queue: Tentacle attack commands are queued: command a tentacle that is already slamming, and it will strike again as soon as the first attack ends. Use Q and W in quick succession, overlapping the commands to produce consecutive slams without wasting either one.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-vessel: A spirit pulled out by E inherits the target’s current health. If you want to turn the enemy into a Vessel, lower their health before landing E so you can kill the spirit quickly; against a full health target, the spirit will hold out while Illaoi wears herself down.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-finish: Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host, but damage dealt to the host does not transfer to the spirit. If a fleeing enemy has less health than their spirit, you can finish them by attacking it even after they move out of reach. That is why you should land E before starting a fight.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-position: Cast E from the side with your turret and tentacles, where it is safest. An enemy who moves in to defend the spirit must fight among the tentacles; one who stays away becomes a Vessel and carries tentacles with them. Either outcome favors Illaoi.
notes.illaoi-skill-r: Use R as your allies engage or to counter an enemy’s advance, rather than to start a fight yourself. It spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages, making it more valuable when enemies are grouped. If Illaoi goes in alone and uses R first, she gets fewer tentacles and is likely to be caught.
notes.illaoi-skill-r-window: After R, tentacles briefly become untargetable and slam faster. This short period is Illaoi’s peak damage window, so you need a way to keep enemies in place throughout it. If they simply spread out and walk away, R goes to waste.
notes.illaoi-skill-passive-heal: When a tentacle hits an enemy champion, Illaoi heals in proportion to her missing health, so each slam restores more when she is low. Where tentacles can reach, fighting back at half health is better than retreating; where they cannot reach, she has virtually no way to heal.
notes.illaoi-phase: At level 1, Illaoi has only one tentacle and weak trades, but her laning grows stronger once she starts leveling E. Level 6 and R are her biggest turning point, reflected in her damage per minute ranking among the highest at 14 minutes. Later, her lack of guaranteed crowd control makes solo engages less valuable, and she shifts to a frontline role.
notes.illaoi-laning: In lane, draw the wave into an area where you have set up tentacles. Keep it near a wall and cast E as the enemy steps forward to last-hit. With both CS and damage per minute ranking among the highest at 14 minutes, maintaining pressure builds an advantage without forcing a dive.
notes.illaoi-laning-tp: Teleport can target tentacles whether they are active or inactive. Leave one near the lane or objective you plan to return to before recalling, since its location determines how quickly you can get back to lane.
notes.vs-illaoi-tentacle: Illaoi’s strength lies near her tentacles. Destroy them when you can; if you cannot spare the time, draw her into open ground away from walls. Taking a fight where tentacles are set up means losing regardless of the item difference.
notes.vs-illaoi-vessel: If you do not intend to fight, break the spirit tether, become a Vessel, and dodge the first tentacle slam. Then stand beside that tentacle until the mark expires. Leaving it intact and staying close prevents further slams from hitting you while keeping Illaoi from gaining more tentacles.
notes.vs-illaoi-heal: Illaoi heals more as her health falls, making her much tougher than she looks. Diving her at half health can let a few tentacle hits restore her health, so apply Grievous Wounds with Executioner’s Calling before committing.
notes.vs-illaoi-r: R is Illaoi’s peak damage window, but it is short. Spread out during it to leave her no targets to attack and let the ultimate expire. Since R spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages, avoid grouping up in front of her in the first place.
notes.vs-illaoi-laning: In lane, Illaoi draws the wave near a wall to set up tentacles. Keep the wave away from walls and last-hit from outside E range to deny most of her pressure. She has no guaranteed crowd control, so dodging E keeps her from holding you in place.
notes.vs-illaoi-e-fight: If your spirit has been pulled out and you can fight, fight back. If you only run, the spirit survives intact and you become a Vessel.
notes.irelia-combo-engage: For an engage, place the first E behind your opponent, stun them with the second E, then dash in with Q, land a basic attack, and use W. E marks champions it hits and resets Q’s cooldown, letting you use Q twice before the stun ends.
notes.irelia-combo-farm: Finishing a low-health minion with Q resets its cooldown, letting Irelia chain dashes through the wave. Those dashes are her way in and out, so check the wave’s position before engaging or escaping.
notes.irelia-skill-e-placement: E sends two blades toward each other, stunning enemies caught between them. Placement is everything: put the first blade behind your opponent or on their escape route to catch them whichever way they move. If you do not recast E, the second blade fires automatically from Irelia’s position after a short delay, so poor positioning can waste it.
notes.irelia-skill-w: Irelia cannot move while charging W, but takes reduced damage. Save it for the moment an enemy assassin dives in or a gank arrives instead of spending it early for damage. From mid game onward, try to bait out your opponent’s abilities before activating it.
notes.irelia-skill-passive: Ionian Fervor grants more attack speed as its stacks build, and at maximum stacks Irelia’s basic attacks deal bonus damage. Attacking a champion, structure, or large monster refreshes its duration, so build stacks by hitting minions with abilities just before a fight; going in stacked can change the outcome of a 1v1.
notes.irelia-skill-r: R traps the first champion it hits inside a blade wall. To leave, the target must cross it and take damage and a heavy slow, or use Flash. Aim it across the escape route, with the wall opening toward your allies so they can catch the trapped target.
notes.irelia-phase: Irelia is weak in level 1 trades but starts winning short trades at level 3, once she has her abilities. Her first major power spike comes with R at level 6, and she grows stronger with items after that. She also has one of the highest death rates, so repeated reckless engages can erase that growth.
notes.irelia-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, chances to trade are hard to find. Use chained Q dashes to secure CS safely and keep pace in growth; forcing an approach and wasting E leaves you open to a gank immediately afterward.
notes.irelia-laning-melee: Against melee opponents, build Ionian Fervor stacks before trading, then repeatedly go in for short trades and back off. Save E to interrupt their counterattack or escape rather than using it for damage.
notes.irelia-laning-q-reserve: Using Q carelessly on minions leaves you with no escape when an opponent closes in. Use it only to finish minions so its cooldown keeps resetting, and never open an engage by using Q on an unmarked opponent.
notes.irelia-teamfight: Start a teamfight by using R to split the enemy formation, stun a trapped target with E, then chain Q dashes into the backline. Irelia is a priority target for the enemy team, so wait for your allies’ crowd control to land before going in if you want to survive.
notes.irelia-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps negating short trades, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.irelia-situational-cc: Buy Quicksilver Sash against a team that locks you down and kills you immediately after you engage, before you can activate W. Irelia needs to keep landing basic attacks once she closes the gap, and a single root can ruin the entire fight for her.
notes.vs-irelia-r: If you are trapped in Irelia’s R blade wall, it is better to wait for the blades to disappear. Crossing the wall deals additional damage and applies a heavy slow, which can stop you from escaping.
notes.vs-irelia-teamfight: Focus Irelia first when a teamfight starts. Her R can split your formation and her E can stun several champions at once, allowing her to control the fight if left alive.
notes.vs-irelia-w: True damage ignores the damage reduction from Irelia’s W. Ignite combines true damage with healing reduction, disrupting her ability to withstand damage with W and recover with Q.
notes.vs-irelia-q-minion: Irelia can close the gap by chaining Q dashes through low-health minions. Do not leave a half-health minion between you and her, and step back to keep your distance as minions are about to die.
notes.vs-irelia-early: Irelia is weak in level 1–2 trades. Take control before she has all her abilities, then use that advantage to disrupt her farming and slow her growth.
notes.irelia-skill-mark-vision: Hitting a champion or large monster marked by E or R with Q resets Q’s cooldown. Chain Q onto a marked opponent to stay on them, and use marks on large monsters to speed up your jungle clear.
notes.ivern-combo-gank: For a gank, land Q (Rootcaller), cast E (Triggerseed) on an ally as they close in, and recast Q to follow if needed. An ally who attacks the rooted target automatically dashes into range, so Rootcaller is your ally’s way in rather than a source of damage for Ivern. Wait until your ally is ready before casting Q, or the root duration will go to waste.
notes.ivern-combo-e-timing: E explodes after a short delay, so apply it early enough for the explosion to coincide with the end of Q’s root. The slow then takes over as the root ends, leaving the enemy no opening to escape.
notes.ivern-combo-daisy: Summon Daisy!, command her to attack, then put E on her. E works on Daisy! as well as allies, turning her into an area slow when she stands in the middle of the enemy team. Keep her attacking the same target so her third hit knocks them up.
notes.ivern-skill-passive-jungle: Ivern does not fight monsters other than epic monsters. Instead, he plants a grove at a camp and harvests it once it has grown for gold and experience. Planting costs health and mana, and growing takes time, so plant at several camps ahead of time and make a circuit to harvest them. Groves grow faster as Ivern levels up.
notes.ivern-skill-passive-smite: Smite immediately frees a camp with a growing grove, speeding up Ivern’s jungle clear. Save it when Dragon or Rift Herald is coming up, though, since you also need Smite for objectives. Ivern can attack epic monsters directly, so use basic attacks and Daisy! to damage them during objective fights.
notes.ivern-skill-q: Q has long range but is a skillshot that hits only one target, and it is Ivern’s way to start a fight. Hitting a monster with it halves its cooldown, so landing Q on a nearby camp monster while moving or escaping can have it ready for the next gank. Do not spend it on a monster right before a fight.
notes.ivern-skill-w: Brush created by W blocks vision, creates ambush spots, and adds damage to the basic attacks of Ivern inside it and nearby allies. It disappears if your team loses vision inside it, so maintain vision with a ward or an ally’s position when setting an ambush. Placing brush under your allies just before a teamfight gives them stronger basic attacks and a vision advantage.
notes.ivern-skill-e: If E (Triggerseed) does not hit an enemy, its shield refreshes, so there is no downside to putting it on your allied carry before a fight when it is safe to do so. Recasting it over an existing shield is wasteful, though; look for the moment your ally is about to start taking damage.
notes.ivern-skill-r: Daisy! can block non-targeted abilities for your allies, so position her between your carry and an incoming enemy engage. Her third consecutive hit on the same target knocks them up; keep her focused on that target rather than repeatedly changing her orders.
notes.ivern-jungle-route: Monsters do not attack Ivern, so clearing the jungle does not cost him health. Plant seeds at camps, head straight to a lane to try a gank, then return to harvest once the seeds have grown. His pathing should overlap camp growth with lane visits: Ivern grows by spending more time showing up in lanes rather than lingering in the jungle.
notes.ivern-jungle-vision: Ivern is very weak in a 1v1, so avoid routes where you might meet the enemy jungler. Secure vision first and path toward your allies; rotating among all three allied lanes is more valuable than counterjungling.
notes.ivern-phase: Ivern can gank with Q as early as level 2 or 3. Daisy! gives him much more control over fights at level 6, while his role in the mid and late game is to protect his allied carry and stop enemy engages. He depends on his allies’ damage, so if they fall behind, he has little he can do.
notes.ivern-teamfight: Start teamfights from the back, catching one enemy with Q for your allies to attack and using E the moment an enemy engage reaches your carry. Keep Daisy! in front of the carry as a wall; if the enemy formation has already broken, place her in their escape path to seek a knockup. If Ivern stands in front and dies, his shield and Daisy! disappear with him.
notes.ivern-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down your allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing between core items to remove effects E cannot cleanse.
notes.vs-ivern-q: Ivern’s threat begins with Q. His allies automatically dash into range of a target it roots, so win the positioning battle before he fires rather than trying to react after it hits. Keep minions or terrain between you and Ivern to limit his Q angles.
notes.vs-ivern-brush: Ivern’s brush can appear where there was none and remain for quite a while, but it disappears if his team loses vision inside it. Deny that vision to remove the ambush spot, and do not walk carelessly past brush that suddenly appears.
notes.vs-ivern-daisy: While Daisy! is alive, Ivern’s team effectively has another frontline unit. She can absorb skillshots, so avoid firing non-targeted abilities at an enemy behind her. Her third consecutive hit on one target knocks them up; if she starts attacking you, move to break the chain.
notes.vs-ivern-solo: Ivern himself deals almost no damage, so focus on stopping the ally he shields before spending time trying to kill him. If only Ivern remains, you have already won the fight. His mobility and brush help him escape, so do not chase too far.
notes.vs-ivern-jungle: Ivern plants seeds at camps and waits for them to grow, making his harvest route predictable. Place vision in his jungle early to see which camps he will return to and when; as the enemy jungler, ambush him there, since he is weak in a 1v1.
notes.vs-ivern-e: Ivern’s E explodes shortly after it is applied and leaves a slow. Engaging on an already shielded target can leave you struggling to retreat when the slow follows, so wait for the shield to explode before going in.
notes.janna-skill-q-charge: Q Howling Gale grows where Janna casts it and launches when recast. A longer charge increases its range, damage, and knockup duration, but Janna can do nothing while it charges, and enemies who see the tornado can walk out of its path. Fire it immediately to stop an engage; charge it only when the enemy is out of vision.
notes.janna-combo-q-brush: To land a fully charged Q, hide the tornado behind a wall or in a bush while it charges, then launch it the moment an enemy enters its path. You can also follow an ally’s immobilizing crowd control with Q for a guaranteed hit. The charge makes a sound, though, so account for enemies hearing it and backing away.
notes.janna-skill-w: W Zephyr passively grants movement speed and ghosting, letting Janna pass through minions and choose her angle freely. When used, W deals more damage with additional movement speed, so poke with it while you have a movement speed bonus.
notes.janna-skill-e: E (Eye Of The Storm) grants a shield and attack damage, so cast it as damage is about to land; using it early only wastes its duration. Each time Janna hinders an enemy champion’s movement with an ability, E’s cooldown is reduced, meaning that landing Q or W on a champion helps her shield more often. Her defense depends on successful harassment.
notes.janna-skill-e-turret: E can also shield an allied turret. If enemies are diving or pushing it, the shield can let it withstand a few more hits. Remember this option when responding to a dive, alongside shielding your carry.
notes.janna-skill-r: R Monsoon immediately knocks enemies back, then heals nearby allies for its duration. Moving or using an ability ends it at once, so stand still after casting if you need the healing. If you only need the knockback to escape, move immediately and give up the healing. The knockback cannot push enemies over walls.
notes.janna-combo-r-timing: R can turn a fight by interrupting the enemy’s engage as it reaches an ally, a channeled ultimate as it begins, or an attempt to kill an ally just before it succeeds. You can Flash into the middle of the enemy formation and use R to separate their front and back lines, but Janna will be left among them.
notes.janna-skill-passive: P Tailwind speeds up allies moving toward Janna. Stay ahead of them in the direction of retreat so they can escape faster, and move ahead when chasing so they can catch up. Janna’s position itself provides this utility.
notes.janna-laning: Janna’s goal in lane is to stop enemy engages, not secure kills. When the opposing support walks in, fire Q immediately to knock them up, then slow them with W to end the trade. Because these abilities cost a lot of mana, avoid using them to clear minions or for pointless poke; save them for moments when your carry is actually at risk of being hit. The same applies to turret dives: hold Q until the enemy goes in, then fire it immediately to disrupt the entire dive.
notes.janna-roaming: W’s passive movement speed and ghosting let Janna roam quickly without getting caught on minions. Her greatest value, though, comes from stopping engages beside her ADC, so leave lane only when the wave is safely pushed or your ADC has recalled. Otherwise, spend that time placing vision near mid or jungle entrances to spot ganks early.
notes.janna-vision: After identifying the enemy's approach, decide whether to launch Q immediately or charge it. Get vision in bushes to create chances to charge Q from inside them. Do not walk alone through areas without vision.
notes.janna-teamfight: In teamfights, Janna stops the enemy’s engage. Stay beside your allied carry instead of standing in front of an enemy looking for an opening, then push the enemy back with Q or R as they go in. Against a dive focused composition, save R to stop the engage; if the enemy struggles to engage, use E and W to give your carry more time to deal damage.
notes.janna-phase: Janna has little kill pressure in early lane, but she is among the best supports at staying alive. Learning R at level 6 gives her the power to shut down an enemy engage, while support items make her shields and healing more valuable from the mid game onward. Late in the game, keeping an allied carry alive longer can change the outcome of a teamfight.
notes.janna-situational-cleanse: If the enemy is locking down and killing your allied carry, buy Mikael’s Blessing earlier. E’s shield cannot remove crowd control that has already landed, so when being locked down is what gets your carry killed, the cleanse takes priority over the shield.
notes.vs-janna-r: Janna’s R pushes nearby enemies away and can stop an engage entirely, so save an interrupt for the moment she uses it. Its knockback cannot push you through a wall; engaging with your back to one shortens how far you are pushed and makes it easier to close in again.
notes.vs-janna-q: Q’s tornado makes a sound while charging. If you hear it from a bush or outside your vision, stay out of its path. A fully charged tornado has much greater range and knockup duration, making an engage especially risky just after Janna disappears from vision.
notes.vs-janna-e: A target shielded by E absorbs damage and gains attack damage, making their counterattack stronger. Avoid wasting burst damage into the shield: engage after it expires or target someone else. Account for E returning sooner each time Janna hinders an enemy with an ability.
notes.vs-janna-target: Janna has among the lowest health, armor, and magic resistance, so getting caught can kill her outright. While she stays behind her allied carry, she can keep pushing back engages; establish vision and look for a moment when she is isolated, or set up a pick on Janna first.
notes.vs-janna-lane: Janna is strongest just after she buffs an ally with E. Keep pressuring the ally she protects to force her to spend the shield; this is more effective than poking Janna herself. Her abilities cost a lot of mana, so making her waste Q and W a few times can give you control of the lane.
notes.vs-janna-w: W (Zephyr) gives Janna ghosting, letting her pass straight through minions. Minion walls and allied bodies will not block her or narrow her escape route, so catching her requires immobilizing crowd control or an engage ability that closes the distance at once.
notes.jarvan-combo-eq: Everything starts with EQ: place E (Demacian Standard), then immediately use Q (Dragon Strike) to dash toward the flag and knock up enemies in your path. Press the abilities almost simultaneously so your target cannot walk away while the flag lands. Placing it beyond the target lets Jarvan IV dash past and block their path; placing it between the target and your allies drives them toward your team.
notes.jarvan-combo-full: For the full combo, knock the target up with EQ, auto attack as soon as you land to apply Martial Cadence’s bonus damage, trap them with R Cataclysm, then use W Golden Aegis for a shield and slow. Always weave in that auto attack between abilities, or you lose the passive damage.
notes.jarvan-combo-eq-flash: Flash after the EQ dash begins to shift its endpoint and knock up a target beyond its normal range. Because enemies may judge the distance by the flag's position, save EQ Flash for a target you must interrupt.
notes.jarvan-skill-q-unstoppable: The Q dash toward a flag still works while slowed or rooted, so you can escape as long as the flag remains. Before entering a dangerous area, leave one in the direction you may need to flee.
notes.jarvan-skill-q-wall: Throw a flag over a thin wall and dash to it with Q to cross the terrain. This gives you another way in or out, so identify walls you can cross before a fight; in the jungle, use the same move to cut between camps and save time.
notes.jarvan-skill-w: Golden Aegis absorbs more damage for each enemy champion it hits, so use W after entering a group instead of activating it early while alone. Its slow is more useful for limiting an enemy's escape route or delaying their approach than simply finishing a combo.
notes.jarvan-skill-e-aura: E grants attack speed passively even when unused, and placing its flag increases nearby allied champions' attack speed too. Put a flag beside an objective when you start attacking it; outside fights, place it beyond enemy vision so it does not reveal your angle of approach.
notes.jarvan-skill-r-cage: Cataclysm's wall blocks allies as well as enemies, so check where you will land before using R to avoid trapping your own damage dealers. Recast R to bring the wall down immediately if needed, or use it defensively to cut off an enemy chasing an ally.
notes.jarvan-skill-passive: Martial Cadence deals bonus damage based on the target's current health and can trigger on the same target only once every set period. It hits hardest when the enemy is at full health, so make your first auto attack in a trade against the champion and time later attacks around when the passive can trigger again.
notes.jarvan-phase: Jarvan IV can gank from level 2, once he has EQ. His early clear speed and damage per minute are average, so farming camps alone is not enough; look for early ganks and objective pressure to build an advantage. At level 6, R lets him catch out a target, and he is strongest through the mid game as his items come together. Later, his value comes more from engaging and trapping enemies than from damage.
notes.jarvan-laning-gank: A gank starts with getting the enemy into EQ range. If your ally's lane is pushed toward the enemy turret, wait until it comes back before entering, and check whether the target has used their mobility ability. Placing your flag ahead of time and using only Q as the enemy approaches is harder to predict and more likely to succeed.
notes.jarvan-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to isolate an enemy backline damage dealer, but trap them only where your allies can follow up immediately; fighting alone inside the wall can get you killed. If the enemy engages on your team first, use R to stop their engager instead.
notes.jarvan-teamfight-object: In objective fights, place E Demacian Standard in advance to boost your allies’ attack speed, and save EQ for the enemy’s approach. Coordinate the engage with your team: if Jarvan IV goes in first, the enemy may steal the objective.
notes.jarvan-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Trapping a target with R lets Jarvan IV stay close and fight long enough to maintain the healing reduction.
notes.vs-jarvan-eq: Jarvan IV’s main threat is EQ. When E Demacian Standard lands at your feet or nearby, a Q Dragon Strike dash can follow, so move away from the flag immediately. Without a flag, Q is only a short jab and poses little threat.
notes.vs-jarvan-flag-wall: Jarvan IV can throw a flag over a thin wall and dash to it to cross the terrain, so fleeing along a wall does not guarantee safety. When he disappears from vision, position with possible approaches over walls in mind.
notes.vs-jarvan-r: Jarvan IV can recast R to remove Cataclysm's wall himself, so do not count on waiting for an opening. If trapped, commit to escaping with a movement ability that crosses walls or to killing Jarvan IV inside the wall; circling it indecisively is the worst choice.
notes.vs-jarvan-w: Jarvan IV’s W Golden Aegis grants a stronger shield when more enemy champions are nearby. If he jumps into several enemies and uses it, a burst of damage will mostly be absorbed by the shield, so wait until it is gone before dealing finishing damage.
notes.vs-jarvan-passive: Jarvan IV's first auto attack deals bonus damage based on current health, and Martial Cadence can trigger on the same target only once every set period. It hurts most at full health, making the moment just after you take that first hit a reasonable window to trade back.
notes.vs-jarvan-early: Jarvan IV can gank as soon as he has EQ at level 2, so establish early vision in bushes that give him an EQ angle and avoid pushing the lane too far. He is most dangerous through the mid game as his items come together; late in the game, being isolated by R is a greater threat than his damage.
notes.jax-combo-engage: Engage with E → Q → recast E mid-leap → auto attack → W → auto attack. Activate E before Q to stun almost as soon as you land, before the opponent can disengage. If you need to guarantee the stun, use Flash and recast E together as soon as E can be recast.
notes.jax-skill-e-core: E Counter Strike is a defining part of Jax’s skill ceiling: while active, it dodges every basic attack except turret attacks, and its recast deals more damage for each attack dodged. Activate it as the opponent starts an attack animation to avoid both the attack and any bonus damage or crowd control carried by it. Choosing when to recast E is central to the mind game: approach with E active, click back as if retreating, then immediately close in with Q or Flash to leave little time to react. If two enemies attack you at once during a gank, activate E immediately.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-melee: Jax has the advantage in level 1 trades against melee opponents. With only one ability available to each side, basic attacks and minion aggro account for most of the damage; E Counter Strike lets him dodge those attacks while adding increased recast damage and a stun. Use the health lead from this strong window to get through the weaker laning phase that follows.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-ranged: Against ranged opponents, save E Counter Strike for an all-in you can reliably win or to respond to a gank instead of using it against a single poke. With E on cooldown, Jax has no defensive tool, so stay outside the opponent’s range until it is ready, even if that means giving up CS. Look for an angle to engage with Q Leap Strike, activating E just before the leap so the stun follows your landing.
notes.jax-skill-e-limit: E Counter Strike dodges basic attacks but reduces ability damage only slightly, and only when it comes from area-of-effect abilities. Against opponents who deal mainly magic damage through abilities, activate R Grandmaster-at-Arms as you enter combat for its armor and magic resistance instead of relying on E to survive. Save E for key basic attacks or crowd control carried by them.
notes.jax-skill-q: Use Q Leap Strike to engage or escape rather than primarily for damage. Its long range and unit targeting let you jump to minions and wards, so a ward placed in advance can create both an escape route and an approach angle. Against melee opponents, move into range to start a trade and save Q to chase or disengage. If an opponent moves forward away from their turret, Q can put Jax on their retreat path and make escape difficult.
notes.jax-skill-r: R Grandmaster-at-Arms passively adds magic damage to every third consecutive attack, so keep attacking without breaking your basic attack rhythm. Its active grants more armor and magic resistance for each champion hit; activate it where several enemies are grouped to get the most from it. Both W Empower and R have AP ratios, allowing Jax to make full use of items that grant both attack damage and ability power.
notes.jax-phase: Jax is strong in level 1 melee trades but weakest at levels 2–5, before he has his full set of abilities, because he lacks poke, a farming ability, and sustain. His fighting power rises sharply when he unlocks R at level 6 and when he completes his first core item. Late in the game, passive attack speed stacks combined with items let him dominate head-on fights against champions who rely on basic attacks, though his damage increasingly falls short against tanks building both health and armor.
notes.jax-situational-item: Choose situational items based on how you are dying. If an enemy basic attack carry is doing well, Frozen Heart reduces their attack speed and can turn the fight after E Counter Strike ends. If magic burst kills you before you can act, use Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability; against a composition that kills you as soon as you are crowd controlled, take Sterak’s Gage to survive.
notes.jax-laning: Aim to get through lane without falling behind. Start trades with P Relentless Assault stacks already built, and when E Counter Strike is on cooldown, farm only from outside the opponent’s range. Move behind the opponent so they must pass Jax to return to their turret; that position makes E and Q more likely to connect. E’s recast also deals area damage, so save it to push a wave into the enemy turret and create a safe recall window.
notes.jax-teamfight: Jax’s main contribution to a teamfight is the area stun from E Counter Strike. Activate E before using Q Leap Strike to jump into grouped enemies and stun several at once. Because he lacks sustain and defensive stats, enter second, following an ally’s crowd control or engage. When there is no reason to start a teamfight, pushing side-lane turrets can draw enemy defenders away.
notes.vs-jax-e: Do not basic attack while Jax’s E Counter Strike is active: it dodges basic attacks along with their bonus damage and crowd control, then deals more recast damage for each attack dodged. Back out of its stun range without attacking and wait for the duration to end, saving your mobility ability for that moment. E does not block ability damage itself, so plan your trades around abilities.
notes.vs-jax-bait: Jax may activate E Counter Strike, feint an approach, then retreat to bait out your mobility ability or ultimate. Do not spend an escape or defensive ability just because he activates E; trade during its cooldown after it ends. With little defensive ability while E is unavailable, Jax is especially vulnerable to pressure from you and your jungler.
notes.vs-jax-early: Jax’s laning phase is weak because he lacks poke, a farming ability, and healing, but he has the advantage in level 1 melee trades. Avoid forcing a fight while each player has only one ability, then build a CS and level lead from level 2 onward. Make use of that lead before his fighting power rises sharply when he unlocks R at level 6 and completes his first core item.
notes.vs-jax-ranged: As a ranged champion, whittle down Jax’s health with basic attack poke, but stop attacking while E Counter Strike is active. Successive basic attacks increase his attack speed and damage, so repeat short trades instead of prolonged fights to break his attack rhythm. Q Leap Strike can target units, making minions and wards ways for him to close in; avoid standing beside a minion wave, watch how many allied minions remain in front of him, and stay outside Q range.
notes.vs-jax-teamfight: When Jax jumps into a teamfight, spread out so the area stun from E Counter Strike cannot hit several of you together. If he enters with E active, wait out its duration before using abilities, then focus crowd control on him immediately after the stun ends to kill him. If he is pushing a side-lane turret, split your team to pressure his side of the map and trade objectives instead of forcing a one-on-one fight.
notes.jax-combo-trade: For short trades, use basic attack → W → basic attack. W Empower resets your basic attack timer, so press it before the attack animation finishes to fit in another hit. Stack P Relentless Assault on minions before trading, then, after activating R, time W with the bonus damage from consecutive attacks for a burst.
notes.jayce-combo-gate-poke: In cannon form, place E Acceleration Gate and fire Q Shock Blast through it. Passing through the gate increases the blast’s range, speed, and damage, letting it reach the opponent before they can react. Place the gate and fire Q with as little delay as possible, since placing it early gives the opponent time to sidestep.
notes.jayce-combo-allin: Land Q Shock Blast in cannon form, switch to hammer with R, then leap in with Q To the Skies! and follow with a basic attack, W Lightning Field, and E Thundering Blow to knock the target back, in that order. The first basic attack after switching to hammer deals bonus magic damage, so land it immediately after the switch.
notes.jayce-combo-shred: Your first basic attack after switching from hammer to cannon lowers the opponent’s armor and magic resistance. Land one as you disengage after a melee combo to strengthen your follow-up Q poke and your allies’ damage.
notes.jayce-combo-e-knockback: Hammer E Thundering Blow knocks opponents back, so aim it carefully. Pushing someone toward your allies or a wall lets you keep chasing, while a careless knockback can send them out of your range and break your combo. It is most useful for pushing an opponent out from under your turret or peeling away an enemy who engages on you.
notes.jayce-skill-passive: Each weapon swap briefly increases your movement speed. Even when you do not intend to trade, swapping while moving helps you dodge poke or close the distance; keeping the swap cooldown running also shortens the time needed to prepare a combo.
notes.jayce-skill-r-defense: Hammer form increases your armor and magic resistance. Switch to it when you are likely to take heavy damage or get caught to improve your chances of surviving.
notes.jayce-skill-e-gate: Allies also gain movement speed when they pass through Acceleration Gate, so place it along their path when following up on a gank or retreating.
notes.jayce-skill-w: Hammer W Lightning Field passively restores mana with every hammer basic attack, so clear minions in hammer form when mana is tight. Cannon W Hyper Charge speeds up your next few attacks; save it for attacking objectives or pressuring turrets.
notes.jayce-phase: Jayce can use both forms from level 1, making him strongest early; build a lead in the early to mid game through lane advantage and objectives.
notes.jayce-laning: Farm in cannon form while poking with Q from outside the opponent’s range. Keep the wave near the middle instead of pushing it all the way in, and disrupt the opponent’s last hits. If they close in, use R to switch to hammer for the added armor, then counter with a Q leap and E knockback.
notes.jayce-teamfight: Open teamfights with cannon Q from the back, entering briefly only after the enemy formation breaks up. Land a hammer combo on the backline, then immediately switch to cannon and disengage; staying where you entered leaves you vulnerable to being picked off.
notes.jayce-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the opponent sustains through your damage with healing. Jayce’s poke lands in separate hits, so an opponent who can keep healing will recover the health you chipped away.
notes.jayce-situational-mercurial: If the opponent opens with crowd control that locks you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. Jayce’s health and armor are among the lowest, so being held in place can quickly get him killed.
notes.vs-jayce-stance: Adjust your response to Jayce’s weapon form: a cannon signals ranged poke, while a hammer signals a leap in and knockback.
notes.vs-jayce-gate: When Jayce places Acceleration Gate, Shock Blast is about to follow. Sidestep out of its line as soon as you see the gate to dodge the empowered Q.
notes.vs-jayce-early: Jayce is strongest early. If you fall behind, farm defensively instead of forcing a comeback, and stall until your own power spike.
notes.vs-jayce-squishy: Jayce’s health and armor are among the lowest. Bait out his Q To the Skies! leap, then engage while it is on cooldown and he has no way to close the distance or escape.
notes.jayce-skill-q-cannon: Cannon Q Shock Blast explodes on hitting an enemy or reaching maximum range, dealing area damage. Aim its explosion at where your opponent is moving rather than relying on a direct hit. A minion causes it to explode on contact, so an opponent behind the minion takes damage only if they are within the explosion radius.
notes.vs-jayce-poke: Cannon Q is a straight-line skillshot, so move side to side while farming. If your health gets low, clear the wave and return rather than forcing yourself to stay in lane.
notes.jhin-skill-passive: Jhin’s Whisper fixes his attack speed and makes him reload after a set number of shots. His final shot always critically strikes, deals more damage based on the target’s missing health, and grants movement speed, so save it for a champion instead of spending it on a minion. Simply holding that shot can force an opponent back; there’s no need to fire it immediately.
notes.jhin-skill-q-bounce: Q, Dancing Grenade, bounces only to the nearest target it has not hit; it neither prioritizes low health targets or champions nor hits the same target twice. Plan its path around target positions and the number of targets, using kills on successive bounces to strengthen the next hit and send the final bounce into a champion.
notes.jhin-skill-q-timing: Q’s travel time between bounces depends on the distance between targets. If they are far enough apart, add a basic attack while the grenade is bouncing to lower a target’s health before a later, stronger bounce reaches them.
notes.jhin-skill-w: W, Deadly Flourish, has exceptional range and reaches its target almost as soon as it fires, so account for the cast time when aiming. Its narrow width makes an unsupported shot easy to dodge; fire after an ally immobilizes the target or your trap triggers, and scan for targets you can hit from afar before approaching a fight.
notes.jhin-skill-w-root: W roots only targets recently hit by Jhin’s basic attack, his trap, or an ally’s attack. Targets outside its range, or targets hit before Jhin learns W, receive no mark. To secure a root, mark the target first with a basic attack or trap.
notes.jhin-skill-e: E, Captive Audience, stops recharging when both charges are available. Keep one for escaping or following up, and place spare traps in bushes and along the river as they become available to block gank routes. Their vision, slow, and ability to set up a W root make them especially valuable in areas without vision.
notes.jhin-skill-e-stack: When an enemy steps on overlapping traps, the later trap usually deals reduced damage. Two placed in exactly the same spot explode together for full damage, but stacking them sacrifices their use for vision or stopping a chase. Reserve that setup for an objective where you know exactly where enemies will enter.
notes.jhin-skill-r: R, Curtain Call, deals much less damage to a full health target and grows stronger as the target loses health, making it a tool for picking off retreating enemies rather than opening a teamfight. Its final shot hits especially hard, so avoid wasting it on someone with almost no health left. Roots, slows, and blinds cannot interrupt R, but stuns and knockbacks can; open it from a safe position.
notes.jhin-skill-r-lane: From far enough away, R’s firing cone covers the entire lane, leaving an opponent no room to escape sideways. When targeting someone fleeing down a narrow lane, opening R from a distance is more accurate than firing from close range.
notes.jhin-combo-lane: For a lane trade, use basic attacks to set up caster minions for successive Q kills, angle Q so each kill strengthens the next bounce, and let the final bounce hit the enemy champion before immediately following with your empowered final shot. Together, the grenade and final shot can take a substantial portion of an opponent’s health in a single midgame trade.
notes.jhin-combo-root: For a reliable combo, catch the target with an E trap or an ally’s immobilizing effect, root them with W, then basic attack through your final shot and finish with R if needed. Casting W first on an unmarked target deals damage but does not root.
notes.jhin-phase-early: Jhin’s fixed attack speed and low movement speed make him vulnerable to enemies who close the gap quickly. Early on, hold your final shot to keep opponents back while securing CS. At 14 minutes, his damage per minute is relatively low but his deaths are the lowest, reflecting how much better he is at surviving safely early than steadily wearing opponents down.
notes.jhin-phase-power: Jhin excels at burst damage rather than sustained damage. Once he learns R at level 6, he can influence fights outside his lane, and as his items accumulate, Q and his final shot can pick off fragile targets. Enemies who build a lot of health remain difficult for him, so prioritize less durable targets.
notes.jhin-laning: Manage your reloads during lane: after firing the final shot, step out of the enemy’s range and use abilities to secure CS until the reload finishes. Q can clear caster minions at once, so use it to push the wave before recalling or leaving to place traps.
notes.jhin-teamfight: Jhin relies heavily on his team: he needs a durable frontline to stand behind and an ally’s immobilizing effect to land W reliably. In teamfights, stay as far back as possible while using your range, and fire W and R right after allied crowd control lands. With no mobility ability to escape once caught, place traps along enemy engage routes in advance.
notes.jhin-teamfight-scout: Jhin’s long range and traps provide scouting and area control. Deep vision can reveal an enemy alone in the jungle for a long range pick with W or R; while waiting for a teamfight, use vision and traps to narrow the routes enemies can take.
notes.jhin-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing kills, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Jhin relies on his final shot and R to finish targets as their missing health increases, so healing can throw off that damage calculation.
notes.vs-jhin-reload: After firing his set number of bullets, Jhin cannot basic attack while reloading. Engage during the reload or just after he has fired his first one or two shots; back off when his final bullet remains, because it can deal a sudden burst of damage. Count his remaining shots whenever you face him.
notes.vs-jhin-w-root: W, Deadly Flourish, roots only enemies recently hit by Jhin’s basic attack or trap, or attacked by one of his allies. If his basic attack has just hit you or you have stepped on a trap, move out of its straight path; W is very narrow and can be dodged once you know its angle. Jhin often fires it after an ally’s immobilizing effect, so account for his position as soon as that crowd control lands.
notes.vs-jhin-traps: Jhin places invisible E, Captive Audience, traps around the map. Stepping on one slows you, but the explosion takes time, so a champion with enough movement speed can keep moving through before it detonates. Even if you know where a trap is, Jhin may be waiting for you to step on it to remove it; avoid getting rooted by W while standing on the trap.
notes.vs-jhin-r: R deals more damage as its target loses health, and its final shot hits especially hard. If you are below full health, focus on dodging; if someone must block a shot, the ally with the highest current health percentage should take it rather than automatically sending the frontline.
notes.vs-jhin-q-bounce: Each target Q kills as it bounces strengthens the next hit. When laning against Jhin, stand a step away from the wave and avoid standing beside low-health allies or minions: Q can kill them and bounce to you with increased damage.
notes.vs-jhin-tank-lead: Jhin picks off fragile targets with burst damage and struggles against enemies who build a lot of health. When advancing on him, send the frontline in first to absorb W and R shots and trigger traps, allowing the damage dealers behind them to enter range unharmed.
notes.jhin-skill-reload: Jhin is weakest when he runs out of ammo, but he can still use abilities while reloading. Keep moving and use Q, W, and E to cover that downtime.
notes.jinx-combo-rocket-poke: Switch Q to rockets and basic attack a minion beside the enemy champion to poke without drawing minion aggro: the blast deals full damage to every enemy in its radius.
notes.jinx-combo-fight: Slow the enemy with W and deal damage from a distance with rocket basic attacks, then switch Q to the minigun for its attack speed if they close in; once a champion is too close, attack speed is more valuable than range.
notes.jinx-combo-escape: When chased, place E traps behind you along your escape route and slow the pursuer with W. The traps root enemies as soon as they step on them, so place them together in a narrow passage to force the pursuer through them.
notes.jinx-skill-q-rocket: Q rockets give Jinx more range and area damage, but each attack costs mana and her attack speed is slower. Use them to poke, clear waves, siege turrets, or hit grouped enemies; switch back to the minigun otherwise.
notes.jinx-skill-q-minigun: Consecutive minigun basic attacks build attack speed stacks, making it strongest at full stacks. If a fight looks likely, build them in advance by attacking minions if necessary so you can deal full damage from the start.
notes.jinx-skill-w: W has very long range and reveals the location of the first enemy it hits. Use it to check brush, gain vision ahead of an objective, or slow an enemy before moving in. Its cast time shortens as your attack speed rises, making it easier to land after building minigun stacks.
notes.jinx-skill-e: E has a long cooldown and is Jinx’s only way to protect herself, so spending it on poke leaves her defenseless against an engage. Placing it in a narrow passage near an objective or at a brush entrance in advance can deter enemies from moving in.
notes.jinx-skill-r: R deals more damage the farther it travels, plus bonus damage based on the target’s missing health. It is weak at close range, so use it to finish fleeing enemies or enemies in other lanes from afar, rather than firing at someone right in front of you.
notes.jinx-phase-early: Jinx’s early kill participation and damage per minute are about average for a marksman, so she is not a champion that pulls ahead in lane. Her range is also relatively short; prioritize rocket poke and safe CS over forced trades to reach her item timing sooner.
notes.jinx-phase-late: As a hypercarry, Jinx grows much stronger with each core item. Get Excited! can carry a won fight into the next one, so winning a late game teamfight can let her take control of the game.
notes.jinx-laning-mana: Every rocket basic attack costs mana. Use rockets only for poke and take routine CS with the minigun to conserve it; running out makes both wave clear and self protection difficult, so find a chance to recall before that happens.
notes.jinx-teamfight: At the start of a teamfight, poke with rockets and W from the edge, and move in with the minigun only when you are sure it is safe. Jinx has no dash and can die once caught, so her positioning determines how much damage she can deal.
notes.jinx-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Rocket basic attacks deal area damage, letting you apply Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-jinx-minigun: Jinx’s minigun takes time to build attack speed stacks. When she is poking with rockets, she has no minigun stacks; use that opening to close in and burst her down.
notes.vs-jinx-r: Jinx’s R, Super Mega Death Rocket!, deals less damage the closer you are to her. If she tries to finish you with it, either move out of its finishing range or close in on her.
notes.vs-jinx-e: Jinx's E has a long cooldown. Jinx relies almost entirely on E to protect herself. Engage after Jinx misses or uses E.
notes.vs-jinx-mobility: Jinx has no dash and is among the slowest champions. Save your engage ability until she misses her W slow or uses E; then she has no way to respond.
notes.vs-jinx-passive: Get Excited! gives Jinx large movement speed and attack speed boosts after a takedown or a structure is destroyed. She can catch you even if you run after an ally dies or a turret falls, so avoid starting a fight during that window.
notes.vs-jinx-rocket-splash: Jinx’s rocket basic attacks deal full damage to enemies near their target. When she uses them to take CS, stand away from the minions so you do not take the splash damage.
notes.jinx-skill-passive: Get Excited! activates when Jinx participates in a champion takedown, kills an epic monster, or destroys a structure. After taking a turret, use its large movement speed and attack speed boosts to move to the next objective or chase an enemy.
notes.ksante-combo-q-shockwave: Q Ntofo Strikes needs repeated casts to reach its full effect: each hit builds a stack, and at full stacks the next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. Minions also grant stacks, so hit the wave with Q just before a fight to prepare the shockwave for your opponent.
notes.ksante-combo-w-timing: While charging W Path Maker, K'Sante is unstoppable and takes reduced damage. Start charging as the enemy's combo lands to absorb the damage, then counterattack. A longer charge extends the stun but gives the enemy time to walk aside, so hold it only after they have used their mobility ability or been caught by the Q shockwave.
notes.ksante-combo-allin: For a full combo, build Q stacks and pull the enemy in with the shockwave, stun them with W, drive them into a wall with R All Out, then use E to close the gap again and follow with auto attacks and Q. Each ability leaves a passive mark, so weave an auto attack between abilities to deal the full damage.
notes.ksante-skill-r-transform: R All Out transforms K'Sante. Pushing an enemy into a wall sends them through it and deals an extra hit, making R especially valuable when they have terrain behind them. All Out also sharply reduces K'Sante's maximum health, bonus armor, and magic resistance, turning him from a tank into a melee damage dealer. Even with defensive items, he is vulnerable during it, so activate R only when the enemy's main crowd control is down and your team can follow up immediately.
notes.ksante-skill-r-upgrades: During All Out, Q and E have shorter cooldowns, E dashes faster, and W’s cooldown resets. W also gains true damage, but no longer knocks enemies back or stuns them. Use all your crowd control to hold enemies in place before activating R; afterward, focus on staying close and attacking.
notes.ksante-skill-q-scaling: Q Ntofo Strikes gains damage and a shorter cooldown from both armor and magic resistance. Building defensive items improves both, so prioritizing them over attack items ultimately makes Q hit harder.
notes.ksante-skill-e-ally: Using E Footwork on an allied champion greatly extends the dash and shields that ally too. Keep it available to reach and shield a teammate who gets caught, rather than using it only to go in yourself.
notes.ksante-skill-passive: Abilities leave passive marks that you collect by hitting the target with an auto attack. Casting an ability and backing away leaves much of that damage unused, so finish trades with an auto attack after an ability. During All Out, both auto attacks and abilities gain damage based on maximum health; keep using your abilities and stay close enough to attack.
notes.ksante-phase: Levels 1–2 are K'Sante's weakest because he has only Q to rely on. Once W and E are available at level 3, he can trade; at level 6, look for a solo kill if you can drive the enemy into terrain with R. His strongest period is the mid game, when defensive items improve both Q's damage and cooldown. Late game, contribute through engages and crowd control more than damage.
notes.ksante-laning-farm: K'Sante does not need to force the wave forward to win lane. Keep it in the middle and last-hit with Q, building stacks to catch your opponent with the shockwave only when they move among the minions. His damage output is relatively low, so surviving and keeping the enemy jungler from intervening is more valuable than repeatedly taking short trades to chip away at their health.
notes.ksante-laning-trade: Slow the enemy with Q, collect the mark with an auto attack, then retreat with E if they fight back. Save E primarily for disengaging, since using it to go in leaves you without a way out; dive in with E only immediately after the enemy uses a mobility ability or key ability.
notes.ksante-teamfight-r: In teamfights, your first priority is to use R to push an enemy backline damage dealer toward your team and isolate them. Activating it also leaves K'Sante in the middle of the enemy team and makes him less durable, so do so only when your allies are close enough to follow up immediately. If they are not ready, save R and hold the front line with the Q shockwave and W stun.
notes.ksante-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between defensive items. K'Sante spends extended periods fighting up close in All Out, making it easy to keep the healing reduction applied.
notes.ksante-situational-mr: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, buy Spectre’s Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. K’Sante has relatively low base magic resistance, and because his Q damage and cooldown scale with magic resistance, these items improve both his defense and offensive power.
notes.vs-ksante-r-window: When K'Sante activates R All Out, his maximum health, bonus armor, and magic resistance drop sharply, leaving him vulnerable for a while. Focus your damage on him as soon as he activates it instead of retreating, but do not face him alone: his damage and lifesteal also increase in this form.
notes.vs-ksante-q: After enough Q hits, K'Sante's next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. If consecutive Qs have hit you, move out of the next one's range or keep a mobility ability ready to dodge it. He can also build stacks on minions, so watch the stack indicator on K'Sante.
notes.vs-ksante-w: While charging W, K'Sante is unstoppable and takes reduced damage. When you see the charge, hold your crowd control and burst damage, watch the direction of his dash, and sidestep it. The longer he charges, the longer the knockback and stun last.
notes.vs-ksante-early: K'Sante is weakest at levels 1–2, when he has only Q, so chip away at his health then. If you do not, the lane becomes harder to turn around as defensive items increase Q's damage and shorten its cooldown.
notes.vs-ksante-omnivamp: In All Out, K'Sante heals from all damage he deals. If you expect a prolonged close-range fight, make sure at least one teammate has healing reduction, and do not let him keep attacking while surrounded by multiple allies.
