notes.vs-ksante-r-wall: K'Sante's R hurts most when you have a wall behind you: hitting the wall pushes you through the terrain and deals an extra hit. When facing him, keep terrain away from your back to greatly reduce the value of his ultimate.
notes.kaisa-skill-passive: Plasma is central to every calculation. Stack it with basic attacks and W, then detonate it at maximum stacks for magic damage based on the target’s missing health; the lower their health when it triggers, the better. An ally immobilizing the target also adds a stack, so count ahead when playing with a support who has hard CC.
notes.kaisa-skill-w: W Void Seeker has very long range, but it costs a lot of mana, and missing it puts you behind in lane. Hitting a champion refunds most of its cooldown, so fire only when you’re confident it will land; don’t force it against someone hiding behind minions. A hit also grants true sight, letting you keep track of a target who flees into brush or stealth.
notes.kaisa-skill-q-wave: Q Icathian Rain deals much more damage to low-health minions. Before recalling or roaming, lower the wave’s health evenly with basic attacks so one Q can clear it; when you need the lane to push toward you, avoid using Q to farm.
notes.kaisa-skill-q-target: Q Icathian Rain missiles automatically track and split among nearby enemies, with repeated hits on the same target dealing much less damage. It is most effective when only one enemy champion is in range; minions nearby draw missiles away and weaken your trade. Use Q when your opponent steps away from the wave.
notes.kaisa-skill-e: E Supercharge charges faster as your attack speed increases. Its slow charge early on makes it unreliable for escaping, but activating it lets you pass through units, so use it to move through minions. Each basic attack reduces its cooldown; keep attacking during a teamfight to get a second E.
notes.kaisa-skill-r: Kai'Sa's R (Killer Instinct) can dash only to an enemy with a Plasma mark, so it is not a free repositioning tool: you must first mark the target with W or a basic attack. Using it carelessly can leave you in the middle of the enemy team with only a shield, so it is safer to save R for finishing enemies or adjusting your angle rather than using it to engage.
notes.kaisa-combo-poke: For a poke combo, use W, follow with one or two basic attacks to detonate the multiple Plasma stacks it applies, and time Q to overlap with the detonation for more damage when the target’s health is low. If W misses, save Q and back off.
notes.kaisa-combo-allin: Start an all-in by closing the gap with E, using its movement speed and ability to pass through units while charging. Once in range, build Plasma with basic attacks, then use Q last so its damage overlaps with the detonation. Using Q before closing in gives the enemy time to retreat and leaves its missiles split among minions.
notes.kaisa-combo-r-entry: For a long-range engage, mark the target with W, wait until they respond to your ally’s engage with their immobilizing and counterattack abilities, then follow with R and finish with basic attacks and Q. Dashing in as soon as W lands leaves you alone against an enemy who still has every means to fight back.
notes.kaisa-phase-early: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2: her range is short even among marksmen, and her base attack damage and armor are low. Farm safely instead of starting trades, and settle for chipping away with W. Unlocking R at level 6 does not make her immediately strong.
notes.kaisa-phase-evolution: Kai'Sa’s power spikes depend on items rather than levels. Her abilities evolve when their stat thresholds are met, making each completed core item a step up in strength. Focus on avoiding losses before your first core item, then start fights proactively once you have your second.
notes.kaisa-laning: In lane, let the wave push toward you and poke with W. Kai'Sa’s low armor makes direct trades unfavorable, so if the enemy marksman pushes, stay back and collect CS instead of forcing your way forward. When you need to push, clear a damaged wave with Q, then recall or secure vision.
notes.kaisa-teamfight: Start teamfights from the back, applying marks with W. Once the enemy frontline has spent its immobilizing abilities and engage tools on your frontline, use E and R to find an angle in and detonate Plasma with basic attacks. R’s shield only covers the cost of entering once; check that E is available to get out before you commit.
notes.kaisa-teamfight-vs-stealth: Against a stealth champion, W’s true sight is valuable on its own. Land it just before a fight to keep seeing their position even if they disappear, and its mark also gives you an angle to follow with R.
notes.kaisa-situational-antiheal: If the enemy’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after your first core item and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Kai'Sa’s repeated basic attacks keep the healing reduction active for a long time.
notes.kaisa-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team can immobilize Kai'Sa and kill her, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. She needs E and R to find an engage angle, and a single immobilizing effect can stop the entire engage.
notes.vs-kaisa-r-mark: Kai'Sa’s R can dash only to a target with a Plasma mark. The moment after her W hits is the most dangerous; if it hits you, retreat toward your allies until the mark disappears to deny her an R angle.
notes.vs-kaisa-q-minions: Kai'Sa's Q (Icathian Rain) missiles split among nearby enemies, and each additional missile that hits the same target deals less damage. Stand near allied minions to spread out the missiles, and do not step away from the wave alone when Kai'Sa looks ready to use Q.
notes.vs-kaisa-early: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2 because her range is short and her armor is low. Push the lane during this window to deny her CS and chip away at her health, delaying the item gains she needs to grow stronger.
notes.vs-kaisa-plasma: Kai'Sa's passive Plasma detonation hits harder the less health you have. If you have stacks and are at about half health, the next one or two basic attacks may hurt far more than expected, so move out of range and wait for the stacks to expire.
notes.vs-kaisa-e-vision: Evolved E briefly conceals Kai'Sa. Before a fight, place Control Wards in side brush and along approach routes to guard against her appearing from the flank, and draw her near a turret to reveal her while she is stealthed.
notes.vs-kaisa-burst: Even a fed Kai'Sa is fragile because her armor and magic resistance scale poorly. Immobilize and kill her just after she dashes in with R, before her shield wears off; if you let the engage go unanswered, she can keep dealing damage with basic attacks.
notes.kalista-skill-passive-hop: Kalista’s passive, Martial Poise, lets her hop in the direction of a move command issued during an auto attack or Q windup. This keeps her moving while she attacks; more attack speed means more hops in the same time and greater effective mobility. Her mobility comes from how often she attacks, rather than her movement speed stat.
notes.kalista-skill-passive-limit: A single move command to hop keeps Kalista’s original auto attack target, letting her reposition without switching targets. She cannot hop when nothing is within attack range, and attack speed slows reduce how far she travels over time. Without something to attack, she is slow.
notes.kalista-skill-e-lasthit: When E Rend kills a target, its cooldown resets and it refunds mana, making it a reliable tool for last hits. If several speared minions remain, one E can clear the wave and reset its cooldown.
notes.kalista-skill-e-stacks: E's damage depends on how many spears are in the target. Stack spears during a trade, then use E when the enemy retreats. Use E before the spears disappear or the enemy gets completely out of range.
notes.kalista-skill-q: If Q Pierce kills the first target it hits, it passes through and leaves spear stacks on the next target. Check the front minion’s health before firing to clear the wave and stack spears on a target behind it. Martial Poise also lets Kalista hop during Q’s cast animation, so choose a direction as you fire to retreat or close in.
notes.kalista-skill-w: W Sentinel’s passive triggers only when Kalista and her Oathsworn attack the same target, so follow your support’s target during trades for the extra damage. Use its active to scout around objectives or enemy jungle entrances; there is no need to save it.
notes.kalista-skill-r: Coordinate R Fate’s Call with your Oathsworn support beforehand, since pulling them in and throwing them can go to waste without a plan. It can start a fight or rescue a support in danger of being caught. Your Oathsworn cannot act while in stasis, so use R when your team is ready.
notes.kalista-combo-trade: A basic trade starts with one spear stack from Q, followed by auto attacks that add stacks and hops after each attack to maintain distance; use E when the enemy retreats. If they close in, keep attacking while hopping backward. If they pull away, hop forward to stay within attack range.
notes.kalista-combo-wave-finish: Kill a speared minion with E to reset its cooldown, then use E again on the enemy champion.
notes.kalista-phase: Kalista is strong at early lane pressure and harass when she levels E first. Kalista is strongest in the mid game as she builds attack speed items. Kalista remains vulnerable to immobilization and heavy slows late in the game.
notes.kalista-laning: During laning, harass while hopping near minions.
notes.kalista-teamfight: In teamfights, hop to just behind the front line and deal sustained damage, then hop backward immediately when an enemy with an engage ability closes in. Stack spears on one target and use E as that target retreats. Using R to rescue an ally is often safer than using it to start a fight.
notes.kalista-situational-qss: When Kalista is rooted, her auto attacks and hops are interrupted.
notes.kalista-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the enemy team has a champion with healing. Kalista’s sustained auto attack damage lets her keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-kalista-poise: Martial Poise depends on Kalista’s basic attacks: push her out of attack range and she cannot hop, or reduce her attack speed and she covers less distance in the same amount of time. Displacement and attack speed reduction can therefore shut down her mobility.
notes.vs-kalista-windup: Kalista cannot cancel her basic attack windup, and she must start that attack to hop. Watch for that moment to land a skillshot reliably: predict when the hop will begin instead of waiting to see it.
notes.vs-kalista-vision: If Kalista loses vision of you, even an auto attack already in flight will miss and fall to the ground. Entering brush or moving behind a wall can therefore reduce the damage you take from her auto attacks.
notes.vs-kalista-r: R Fate’s Call pulls in and throws Kalista’s Oathsworn support to start a fight. If the support stays close beside her, be ready for the throw: prepare crowd control at the expected landing spot or spread out in advance.
notes.vs-kalista-catch: Kalista relies on hopping for mobility, so she has little way to escape once caught. Use forced movement or immobilization as soon as you have an opening to engage; she is among the most prone to early deaths of any marksman.
notes.vs-kalista-rend: At low health, several spears stuck in you can leave you vulnerable to execution even while standing in lane. Once stacks build up, manage your health more cautiously or leave lane until the spears disappear.
notes.karma-skill-passive: Karma’s passive, Gathering Fire, reduces Mantra’s cooldown whenever an ability damages an enemy champion. Keep landing abilities to cycle Mantra rather than saving it; playing passively stalls that cycle, so poke whenever you have the chance.
notes.karma-skill-r-early: Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point, giving Karma an empowered ability while other champions are still without their ultimates. Use that advantage whenever a level 1–2 fight is possible.
notes.karma-skill-q: Q, Inner Flame, damages and slows the first target hit and nearby enemies. Minions can block it, so aim for the moment an enemy champion steps out from behind the wave; a hit also reduces Mantra’s cooldown. Mantra Q leaves a burning zone after the explosion, so place it where the enemy has to stay.
notes.karma-skill-w: W, Focused Resolve, roots only if the tether stays connected, so an enemy can usually walk out of W on its own. Use it after slowing them with Q or when E lets you keep up. Mantra W restores missing health and extends the root, making it a way to survive when you’re caught.
notes.karma-skill-e: E Inspire grants both a shield and movement speed, making it useful for helping an ally engage or escape as well as blocking damage. Cast it just before they go in or pull back rather than after they have been hit; Mantra E also shields nearby allies.
notes.karma-combo-engage: Open by slowing with Q, holding the enemy for W’s root, then using E to help an ally move in while they deal damage. If you can’t get close enough, cast E on yourself for movement speed and enter W range.
notes.karma-combo-mantra-q: Mantra Q’s burning zone detonates shortly after the first explosion. Place it on a target rooted by W or held by an ally’s crowd control so the full damage lands; without crowd control, an enemy you’re poking can walk out and take only half.
notes.karma-phase: Mantra is available from level 1, making Karma relatively strongest in early 2v2 fights. As levels and items build up, her single-target burst becomes less effective; later, focus on keeping allies alive with area shields and movement speed.
notes.karma-laning-mana: Karma cycles Mantra through poke, but careless use of Q and E can drain her mana by the middle of the laning phase. Cast Q only when you have a chance to hit an enemy champion, rather than spending it just to clear minions.
notes.karma-laning-disengage: As support Karma, prioritize peeling over starting fights in lane. When the enemy support engages, use W Focused Resolve to hold the engaging champion and E Inspire to get your marksman out. Even one successful response can put an enemy engage composition at a disadvantage throughout the lane phase.
notes.karma-roaming: E’s movement speed makes roaming with an ally faster. When preparing for a mid gank or to join an objective fight, consider saving Mantra to accelerate nearby allies together with Mantra E.
notes.karma-teamfight: Gathering Fire can recharge Mantra multiple times in a teamfight, so use your first cast promptly. Choose Mantra W to stop an enemy engage, Mantra E against area burst, or Mantra Q to secure an already favorable position; afterward, keep landing basic abilities to bring the next Mantra up sooner.
notes.karma-situational-cc: If the enemy can lock down your carry with immobilizing crowd control, get Mikael’s Blessing early. E’s shield blocks damage but cannot remove crowd control.
notes.karma-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, reduce it with Morellonomicon.
notes.vs-karma-passive: Every ability Karma lands reduces Mantra’s cooldown, so taking free poke helps recharge it. Move behind minions or out of range to make her abilities less likely to hit.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-q: The burning zone left by Mantra Q detonates in place after a short delay. If the initial blast hits you, immediately walk out of its circle to avoid the heavy follow-up damage.
notes.vs-karma-w-disengage: Karma’s W, Focused Resolve, can stop an engage by catching the champion who goes in. Keep your distance and draw out W before engaging.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-w: Mantra W restores Karma’s missing health while its tether is connected, then roots you after a delay. If it catches you, burst Karma down or move far enough to break the tether before the root takes hold.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-e: Mantra E shields all nearby allies, making burst damage largely ineffective while the shields are active. Wait for them to expire before engaging.
notes.karthus-skill-passive-death: After dying, Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time, so if you have little health left, die among the enemies and use E and Q in spirit form. Stay close enough to make full use of that time.
notes.karthus-skill-passive-r: Karthus can use R in spirit form, so if it is available when you die and an enemy is low on health, use it to finish them off. Do not let your time in spirit form pass without casting abilities.
notes.karthus-skill-q: Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy. In trades, aim at opponents who are clear of minions; when farming, cast it where multiple targets overlap.
notes.karthus-skill-e: E can be toggled on and off, but it drains mana quickly while active. Keep it on only while an opponent is in range, then turn it off immediately. Its passive restores mana whenever Karthus kills an enemy unit, so secure the last hit yourself; this is his only source of mana.
notes.karthus-skill-w: Enemies can pass through W, but doing so heavily slows them and reduces their magic resistance. Place it where an opponent must cross it to make the following Q and R deal more damage.
notes.karthus-skill-r: R Requiem hits every enemy champion regardless of distance, but its channel must finish or the entire effect is lost. Cast it only from a safe position or when an ally can protect the channel. It is not just a finishing move: using it at the start of a teamfight lowers every enemy’s health and creates an opening for your allies to engage. It can also pressure scattered opponents at the same time to open up an objective. Ask your allies how the other lanes are doing to choose the right moment.
notes.karthus-combo-basic: For a basic trade, place W along your opponent’s escape path, then land Q beyond it. Crossing the wall reduces their magic resistance, making Q hit harder, while the heavy slow makes Q’s warning indicator harder to dodge.
notes.karthus-combo-melee: In close combat, turn on E, stay close to your opponent, and land Q at their feet when they are clear of minions. E deals damage continuously while they remain in range. Turn it off as soon as the fight ends to save mana for the next one.
notes.karthus-laning-clear: At camps, turn on E and land Q where the monsters overlap. If your mana drops below half, do not force another camp. Karthus ranks among junglers with the highest CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute, so clear camps and waves instead of repeatedly trying to gank.
notes.karthus-laning-gank: Karthus has no mobility ability or instant immobilizing effect, making it hard to gank alone. Go in when an ally has already immobilized the opponent or the opponent has pushed far up the lane; otherwise, use W to limit their escape path and help your allies engage.
notes.karthus-phase: Before level 6, Karthus has no way to escape and is easy for the enemy jungler to catch. Once he has R and core ability power items in the mid game, he can affect the entire map; in late game teamfights, he keeps dealing damage even after dying.
notes.karthus-teamfight: In teamfights, keep landing Q from the back and position yourself to die as late as possible. If the entire enemy frontline has engaged your allies, turn on E and move in to deal area damage. If you are going to die, do so among the enemies to make use of E and Q in spirit form.
notes.karthus-situational-zhonya: If an opponent can jump onto Karthus, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. He has no mobility ability and is easy to catch up close; if an engage interrupts R’s channel, the ultimate has no effect.
notes.karthus-situational-banshee: If the enemy team deals heavy magic damage and can interrupt R with a targeted immobilizing effect, buy Banshee’s Veil. Blocking the first ability often lets you finish channeling R.
notes.vs-karthus-passive: Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time after dying. Move away from his body immediately after killing him to avoid Q and E in spirit form, and do not stop there to heal or attack an objective.
notes.vs-karthus-r: Karthus’s R damages every enemy champion regardless of distance. After a fight or when returning to lane, keep enough health to survive it; if you are unsure, recall again.
notes.vs-karthus-q: Karthus’s Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy, so stand with minions or allies to reduce the damage and walk out of its warning area when it appears. If he misses Q while farming, he loses the mana spent on it.
notes.vs-karthus-w: Passing through Karthus’s W heavily slows you and reduces your magic resistance, making the following Q and R hurt more. When he places the wall, change your escape route to go around it.
notes.vs-karthus-early: Before level 6, Karthus has no mobility ability or immobilizing effect. Disrupt his growth with jungle invades or early ganks; he clears camps among the fastest and can catch up quickly if left undisturbed.
notes.vs-karthus-teamfight: Karthus keeps dealing damage in teamfights after dying, so reposition immediately if you kill him. Plan the fight around clearing the frontline before he gets within E range.
notes.kassadin-skill-passive: Kassadin’s passive reduces incoming magic damage and lets him pass through units. The damage reduction helps him withstand lane opponents who deal magic damage, while the lack of unit collision lets him chase straight through a minion wave along the shortest path—even when an opponent retreats behind it.
notes.kassadin-skill-q: Q, Null Sphere, interrupts channels and grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. In lane, treat it as a defensive tool: time it for an enemy mage’s poke or use it to stop a channeled ability. Spending it on a minion for damage leaves you exposed to that poke.
notes.kassadin-skill-w: W, Nether Blade, passively adds magic damage to basic attacks; activating it greatly empowers the next attack and restores missing mana. The restoration is much greater against a champion, so when mana runs low, landing a W attack on an opponent can be faster than recalling. In a late teamfight, that mana can fund another R after repeated casts have drained you.
notes.kassadin-skill-e: Each nearby spell cast reduces E, Force Pulse’s cooldown, so spells exchanged by both teams can bring it back faster while Kassadin stays near the lane. Farther away, it must run its full cooldown; balance a safe distance from poke against the faster E cycle.
notes.kassadin-skill-r: Casting R, Riftwalk, repeatedly within a short time doubles its mana cost and increases its damage. It is both Kassadin’s mobility tool and his main damage ability, so his remaining mana determines how much damage he can still deal. Before going in, decide how many casts you can afford and whether to save one to escape; securing the blue Smite buff greatly eases the mana burden.
notes.kassadin-combo-burst: For a basic burst combo, enter with R, Riftwalk, then use E, Force Pulse, a W, Nether Blade, empowered basic attack, and Q, Null Sphere, in that order. R’s entry damage and E’s slow help keep the target close, while the W attack restores some mana for your next R. Hold Q until the end to interrupt an enemy movement ability or channel.
notes.kassadin-combo-chase: Chase with repeated R, Riftwalk, casts. From the second cast onward, each costs twice as much mana but also deals more damage, so use them freely when they will secure the finish. Before chasing, count how many casts your remaining mana allows: running out removes your escape tool and leaves you open to a counterattack.
notes.kassadin-laning-early: As a melee mage, Kassadin takes one sided poke at levels 1–5. Use Q, Null Sphere’s, shield to absorb magic poke, focus on CS, and keep the wave near your turret without pushing it. His 14 minute kills and CS rank near the bottom among mid laners, while his deaths are among the lowest; surviving and buying time is the normal path.
notes.kassadin-laning-wave: Once E, Force Pulse, is leveled, nearby spell casts reduce its cooldown and speed up waveclear. Staying near the lane despite enemy poke can therefore be worthwhile, but pushing the wave leaves Kassadin especially vulnerable to the enemy jungler. After pushing, retreat into an area where you have vision.
notes.kassadin-phase-six: Level 6 is a turning point for Kassadin: gaining R, Riftwalk, lets him slip past poke and reach opponents, shifting control of the lane. Its cooldown falls sharply with each rank, however, so his strongest period comes after maxing R. Overextending right at level 6 as though he has already peaked will delay his growth.
notes.kassadin-phase-late: Kassadin is a late game hypercarry, so even after an early setback, play to extend the game. Dying while trying to force a lane win delays the growth he depends on. In a bad matchup, give up a few CS if necessary and keep leveling safely.
notes.kassadin-teamfight: Never start a teamfight from the front. Once the enemy has spent immobilizing abilities on your frontline and their formation has broken, use R, Riftwalk, to reach the backline, deal burst damage, and use it again to leave. Decide beforehand how many casts to spend entering and how many to reserve for escape.
notes.kassadin-teamfight-side: R, Riftwalk, lets Kassadin join and leave fights quickly, making side lane play effective. When no teamfight is starting, collect waves in a side lane, then join once a fight begins to maximize your growth. Standing in the middle of a quiet standoff instead leaves you vulnerable to being picked off.
notes.kassadin-situational-banshee: Against a composition built around magic damage and targeted immobilization that stops your entry, buy Banshee’s Veil. Blocking the first spell creates an opening to engage with R, Riftwalk, and, together with the passive’s magic damage reduction, greatly improves your survival.
notes.vs-kassadin-early: Before level 6, Kassadin is a melee mage with no way to close the gap. Win the lane during this window: push waves to keep him under his turret and pressure him with your jungler to build a level and CS lead. If you fail to do so, he becomes increasingly hard to handle as the game goes on.
notes.vs-kassadin-r: Kassadin’s R, Riftwalk, costs twice as much mana with repeated casts. When chasing him, watch his mana bar and count how many more times he can use it. Once he runs out, he loses that mobility entirely; that is your moment to counterattack.
notes.vs-kassadin-q: Kassadin’s Q, Null Sphere, interrupts channels and grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. Use magic poke while Q is on cooldown so the shield cannot absorb it, and wait until he has used Q before starting a channeled ability.
notes.vs-kassadin-e: Each spell cast near Kassadin reduces E, Force Pulse’s, cooldown, so casting freely in lane helps him get it back sooner. Avoid unnecessary spells near him, and clear waves from outside his range when possible.
notes.vs-kassadin-passive: Kassadin takes less magic damage and ignores unit collision, so a wall of minions will not stop his chase and magic damage alone is unlikely to bring him down. If your team relies heavily on magic damage, have an ally with physical damage and an immobilizing ability lock him down first.
notes.vs-kassadin-late: Late in the game, Kassadin uses R, Riftwalk, to reach and eliminate the backline, then casts it again to escape. Backline champions need magic resistance and an instantly available immobilizing ability; Banshee’s Veil or Quicksilver Sash is the most reliable way to neutralize the first step of his entry combo. Above all, do not stand alone within his R range.
notes.kata-combo-qe: For Katarina’s basic combo, use Q, watch for its dagger to land behind the enemy, then E to the dagger. Picking it up deals passive damage to all nearby enemies and nearly resets E’s cooldown. If you E directly to the enemy after Q, you lose that entire sequence, so check where the dagger lands first.
notes.kata-combo-we: W throws a dagger above Katarina that lands on the ground shortly afterward. Use it while standing on top of an enemy, then pick up the dagger for guaranteed damage; from a distance, use W → E to leap to your own dagger and immediately recover E’s cooldown. Think of W as a way to make E available again, rather than a movement speed boost.
notes.kata-combo-allin: For the full combo, use W to set up a dagger, Q to place another behind the enemy, then E to the Q dagger to engage. Pick up the remaining W dagger and use R. Placing the daggers in different spots gives you the option to reposition and pick one up during R.
notes.kata-combo-w-during-r: Press W just before R to add damage without interrupting R. You can move while channeling, so walk over a nearby dagger during R to pick it up and add passive damage.
notes.kata-skill-passive: When a champion Katarina recently damaged dies, Voracity greatly reduces all her skill cooldowns, restoring the combo she needs to move on to the next target. In teamfights, aim to finish off the lowest-health enemy first and chain those resets.
notes.kata-skill-passive-radius: The damage area when Katarina picks up a dagger is much larger than its pickup area, and the damage is centered on her rather than the dagger. Pick it up as you move into the middle of a group of enemies to hit more of them.
notes.kata-skill-q: Q targets an enemy, bounces to nearby targets, and drops a dagger behind the first target hit. In lane, target a front minion to hit your opponent with a bounce and poke safely from farther away. The dagger will also land behind that minion, so decide beforehand whether its position allows an engage or makes this a poke only.
notes.kata-skill-e: E can target an enemy, ally, or dagger and move Katarina to any chosen spot near it. Using E on a dagger restores its cooldown almost immediately, while using it on another target leaves the full cooldown. Learn its maximum range, and before leaping in, check for a dagger or ally you can use to escape. E can also leap to jungle plants and interactive objects, opening unexpected ways to engage or get out.
notes.kata-skill-r: R channels rapid attacks against the three nearest enemy champions, applies healing reduction to those it hits, and partially applies on-hit effects, including item effects. Check that the enemy’s immobilizing skills have been used before casting, since crowd control can interrupt the channel. Depending on the situation, canceling R early to escape is a valid choice.
notes.kata-phase: Katarina is weak at levels 1–2 because Q has a long cooldown and she cannot reliably cycle through daggers. Short trades become possible at level 3 once she has both Q and E; kill opportunities rise sharply at level 6 when she learns R and again when she finishes her first core item. She has no resource cost, so she can keep using skills, but E leaps are her only defensive tool, making it difficult to engage against teams with crowd control even late in the game.
notes.kata-laning: In lane, focus on last-hitting and poking with Q bounced through minions without forcing the wave to push. Katarina tends to have a low CS count, so look for an opponent’s mistake rather than focusing on farming. The best moment to engage with Q → E to its dagger is right after the opponent uses a skill on the wave.
notes.kata-laning-reset: Katarina builds a lead by refreshing her skills through takedowns. After clearing the wave, use dagger rotations to reach a side lane or objective fight quickly; each kill speeds up your next move. Staying in lane solely to farm leaves her strengths unused.
notes.kata-teamfight: Do not engage first in a teamfight. Wait until the enemy uses its immobilizing skills on your frontline, then use a dagger placed in advance to reach the backline and cast R. Before going in, leave yourself a dagger or an ally you can E to for an escape.
notes.kata-teamfight-antiheal: R applies healing reduction to targets it hits. Against an enemy with strong healing, do not save it only to finish a kill; as their healing begins, position so R includes them.
notes.vs-kata-dagger: Katarina needs to pick up daggers for both damage and movement. Watch where they land and stand clear of those areas to take away her path in and her attack angles. In a teamfight, keeping your whole team away from dagger locations can effectively shut her out.
notes.vs-kata-q: If Q hits you, its dagger lands behind you. Move toward Katarina to put distance between yourself and the dagger and delay her next engage; retreating instead may put you directly on it.
notes.vs-kata-r: Save an immobilizing crowd control skill for R, a channel that deals heavy damage quickly. Interrupting it after it starts can prevent most of that damage. Account for its healing reduction when judging whether healing will keep you alive through it.
notes.vs-kata-e-cd: When Katarina uses E on something other than a dagger, it goes on its full cooldown. That is your window to punish her, but picking up a dagger during it will still reduce the cooldown. Occupy or block the remaining dagger locations as you pressure her.
notes.vs-kata-mr: Most of Katarina’s damage is magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance even if she builds attack damage items. R also includes physical damage, however, so magic resistance alone will not negate all of it.
notes.vs-kata-reset: A kill reduces Katarina’s skill cooldowns and lets her engage again immediately. Pull back or protect low-health allies to deny her the first kill and break the chain.
notes.kayle-phase-early: Levels 1–5 are Kayle’s weakest point in the game: she has melee range, the lowest magic resistance of any champion, and no mobility or defensive skill, so an enemy laner and jungler who commit to killing her can do so. Focus on staying alive and collecting experience and CS rather than winning the lane; giving up a few CS is a normal decision, not a mistake.
notes.kayle-phase-6: Level 6 is Kayle’s first major power spike. P (Divine Ascent) gives her ranged basic attacks, letting her harass melee opponents and take trades she could not take before. Manage the wave from late level 5 to reach level 6 before your opponent, then look for your first trades.
notes.kayle-phase-11: At level 11, basic attacks at maximum P (Divine Ascent) stacks send out fire waves, and E (Starfire Spellblade) begins exploding around its target on hit. The added area damage improves both wave clear and teamfight damage. Before then, slow rotations are acceptable; afterward, push the lane quickly and join objective fights.
notes.kayle-phase-16: Level 16 completes Kayle’s transformation: P (Divine Ascent) keeps her Exalted state active permanently and raises her range to its maximum. She can start fights with maximum range, attack speed, and fire waves without building stacks first. Aim to reach this point; trying to force a decisive fight earlier usually puts Kayle at a disadvantage.
notes.kayle-phase-tradeoff: Kayle’s strength depends heavily on her level, so protect your experience. Dying and leaving lane, losing a wave to a forced rotation, or joining an early counterjungle attempt all delay her power spikes. If your team can buy time, farming CS in a side lane is itself a contribution.
notes.kayle-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use Q (Radiant Blast), an E (Starfire Spellblade) empowered basic attack, then regular basic attacks. Q slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, making the follow-up hits stronger. E also extends the next attack’s range; press it just after a basic attack lands, before the recovery animation ends, to bring the next attack forward without breaking your rhythm.
notes.kayle-combo-stack: Before level 16, build maximum P (Divine Ascent) stacks on minions or jungle monsters before starting a fight. This lets Kayle open with her full attack speed bonus and, from level 11 onward, fire waves. Entering without stacks leaves her taking damage while she builds them.
notes.kayle-skill-q: Q Radiant Blast stops at the first enemy hit but also damages enemies behind them. Its slow and armor and magic resistance reduction help Kayle follow up on allied ganks or escape. Before level 6, Q is her only ranged tool and her only aid to escaping, so avoid spending it on wave clear or pointless poke when you may need it if the enemy jungler arrives.
notes.kayle-skill-w: W (Celestial Blessing) is more valuable for its movement speed than its early heal, which is too small to turn most trades. Use the speed to escape ganks or enemy engages. Without a selected target, W goes to the most injured ally, so target yourself directly when you need it to survive.
notes.kayle-skill-e: E (Starfire Spellblade) adds magic damage to basic attacks even when inactive. Activating it extends the next attack’s range and adds damage based on the target’s missing health, so it hits much harder after an opponent has already taken damage. It applies on-hit and magic item effects; from level 11, its explosion also makes it central to wave clear.
notes.kayle-skill-r: R Divine Judgment makes one ally, including Kayle herself, immune to damage and deals area damage around that target. Use it to survive when Kayle gets caught or to support an ally’s engage as it reaches the enemy team. The immunity does not prevent crowd control, so casting R while immobilized can waste its duration. Casting it too early wastes immunity before damage arrives, while casting it too late means the target is already dead; aim to use it just before the enemy’s burst damage lands or as your ally’s engage reaches the enemy team.
notes.kayle-laning: Before level 6, avoid trades, stay behind the wave, and take only safe last hits while saving Q (Radiant Blast) for escape. If your opponent engages, retreat with Q and W (Celestial Blessing). Below half health, stay within your turret’s range even if it costs CS, since one enemy jungle gank can kill you.
notes.kayle-laning-wave: Keep the wave near your turret before level 6; farming in front of the enemy turret exposes Kayle to ganks when she has no dash to escape. After level 11, use her area damage to push quickly, then join your team or keep the opposing laner occupied in a side lane.
notes.kayle-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the back and use Kayle’s increased range to keep attacking while your frontline stops enemy engages and her fire waves hit multiple targets. Decide before an assassin reaches you whether R (Divine Judgment) will go on Kayle or an ally who has engaged.
notes.kayle-situational-antiheal: Kayle’s sustained basic attacks can keep Grievous Wounds applied against opponents who rely on healing. Since her damage is primarily magic, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb first and upgrade to Morellonomicon when you can spare a core item slot. Avoid Executioner’s Calling; its attack damage does not suit Kayle’s scaling.
notes.vs-kayle-early: Kayle is at her weakest at levels 1–5, with melee range and the lowest magic resistance of any champion. Take control of the lane and keep denying her CS and experience to build an early lead. If you fail to open a gap then, time favors Kayle.
notes.vs-kayle-level6: Gain your laning advantage before Kayle reaches level 6. She gains ranged basic attacks at that point, so the melee trades you could win earlier no longer work the same way; afterward, engage with your jungler.
notes.vs-kayle-r: Kayle’s R (Divine Judgment) blocks damage, but its target can still be affected by crowd control. When she casts it, hold the target in place instead of committing damage, then resume attacking after the immunity ends. Start a full fight once Kayle has already used R.
notes.vs-kayle-dive: Kayle has no dash or defensive skill, making her vulnerable to surprise ganks and dives from outside her vision. Call your jungler repeatedly, and land immobilizing crowd control before dealing damage so she cannot escape with W (Celestial Blessing)’s movement speed.
notes.vs-kayle-late: Kayle gains area fire waves at level 11 and permanent maximum range at level 16. Avoid direct teamfights against her after level 16: secure objectives and turrets to end the game before then, or force a fight with a numbers advantage on the side of the map away from her.
notes.vs-kayle-teamfight: Kayle stays at the back in teamfights and deals damage with basic attacks, so find a route to reach her directly from a flank or outside her vision instead of spending time fighting through the frontline. Coordinate allied crowd control to land as you engage, accounting for the immunity she can gain from R (Divine Judgment).
notes.kayn-combo-gank: For a standard gank, approach through a wall with E (Shadow Step), slow the target with W (Blade's Reach) as you emerge, then close in with Q (Reaping Slash), land a basic attack, and finish with R (Umbral Trespass). R can only target an enemy Kayn has recently damaged, so land W or Q first.
notes.kayn-combo-r: Kayn is untargetable while inside a target with R (Umbral Trespass), making it both a finisher and a way to dodge an enemy's key ability as it arrives. Keep attacking when you emerge, and choose an exit position toward your escape route during the cast.
notes.kayn-combo-shadow-assassin: Shadow Assassin deals bonus damage only for a short window after entering combat with an enemy champion. Get right next to the target and fit Q (Reaping Slash), a basic attack, and W (Blade's Reach) into that window instead of spacing your abilities out like poke; if the damage is insufficient, pull back with R (Umbral Trespass) and re-enter when the bonus damage window returns.
notes.kayn-skill-passive-form: Choosing a form is Kayn's biggest decision. Fighting enemy champions grants transformation orbs: melee champions fill the Darkin (Rhaast) side, while ranged champions fill the Shadow Assassin side. If you want a particular form, plan your route around ganking that type of champion.
notes.kayn-skill-passive-pick: Choose your form based on both team compositions. Shadow Assassin suits a match with many squishy enemy damage dealers and an existing allied frontline; Darkin is better when the enemy team is mostly melee or durable and fights will last longer, since he heals from ability damage. Hitting multiple enemies with his abilities increases that healing, making him valuable in teamfight compositions.
notes.kayn-skill-e: E (Shadow Step) lets Kayn pass through terrain, but nearby enemies see an indicator showing which wall he is inside. Don't wait there for long; emerge as soon as you have an opening. Its duration is greatly reduced while fighting enemy champions, so don't rely on it to escape a fight.
notes.kayn-skill-q: Both the dash and strike of Q (Reaping Slash) deal damage, with bonus damage against minions and jungle monsters. Start camps with Q to clear faster, but save it to close the gap if you're about to gank. Since Q and E (Shadow Step) are Kayn's only movement tools, don't enter the enemy jungle with both on cooldown.
notes.kayn-skill-w: W (Blade's Reach) is a straight-line ability with a cast animation, so predict the enemy's movement to land it. Its slow lets you chase even without Q (Reaping Slash), making it a good first ability in a gank. Before transforming, a missed W can ruin the gank, so use it after an ally lands crowd control or the enemy has used their mobility ability.
notes.kayn-skill-w-form: W (Blade's Reach) changes with Kayn's form: Shadow Assassin can move while casting it to extend its reach, while Rhaast knocks up enemies it hits. As Shadow Assassin, follow the enemy to narrow their dodge angle and land W; as Rhaast, aim to knock them up just before an ally engages.
notes.kayn-skill-e-form: E (Shadow Step) ends immediately if Kayn is immobilized or stays outside terrain too long. An enemy root or stun can knock him out of a wall during his approach, so don't stay inside one for long while those abilities are available. In Shadow Assassin form, E also grants movement speed and slow immunity, letting him cross the same wall faster.
notes.kayn-phase-early: Kayn is weak in fights before transforming, so prioritize clearing camps and collecting orbs over early skirmishes. Avoid risky jungle invades that could set you back.
notes.kayn-phase-form: Kayn's power spike begins when he transforms. Shadow Assassin's assassination power peaks from immediately after transformation through the mid game, but he dies easily in late teamfights. Darkin is underwhelming right after transforming, then gains more teamfight sustain as he builds items, so your form affects when you should aim to end the game.
notes.kayn-laning-clear: Plan your route around using E (Shadow Step) to cross walls between camps and save travel time. Kayn’s clear is not slow, so completing a full early jungle clear to speed up his transformation is safer than forcing risky early ganks.
notes.kayn-laning-gank: For a gank, approach through a wall behind the lane with E (Shadow Step) to cut off the enemy's escape. Because enemies can see Kayn inside the wall, enter as your ally starts trading damage and emerge immediately instead of waiting there. Fighting an enemy champion earns orbs, so even a gank without a kill has value.
notes.kayn-teamfight: Shadow Assassin should not start teamfights. Once the enemy has used its crowd control, flank or circle behind them with E (Shadow Step), focus on one damage dealer, and use R's (Umbral Trespass) untargetable window to disengage after the kill. Entering at the wrong time can get you killed before you accomplish anything.
notes.kayn-teamfight-rhaast: Darkin fights up front, hitting multiple enemies with abilities and sustaining through healing. Look for angles that catch as many enemies as possible with W (Blade's Reach) and R (Umbral Trespass), and enter after the enemy has used its key crowd control on your frontline. Since healing is his only means of survival, engage more cautiously against enemies with healing reduction.
notes.vs-kayn-r-condition: Kayn can cast R (Umbral Trespass) only on a target he has damaged first. Dodge the straight-line hitbox of W (Blade's Reach) to keep him from enabling R at range.
notes.vs-kayn-e: Damaging Kayn during E (Shadow Step) shortens its duration, while immobilizing him ends it immediately. Interrupt him inside the wall instead of waiting for him to emerge.
notes.vs-kayn-wall-warning: When Kayn is inside nearby terrain, a warning indicator appears along that wall's edge. If you see it, he already has a gank angle, so stop trading damage and retreat toward your turret.
notes.vs-kayn-early: Kayn is noticeably weak before transforming. Pressure his jungle route and force objective fights early to delay his transformation and power spike; giving him early kills brings that transformation forward.
notes.vs-kayn-r-exit: An ally caught in Kayn’s R (Umbral Trespass) cannot help for its duration. Kayn exits near the target, so prepare crowd control there when he goes in and use it the moment he comes out.
notes.kennen-combo-stun: For the basic stun combo, land Q for the first mark, use a basic attack with W’s passive ready for the second, then cast W for the third. Keep that order to secure the stun; using your abilities haphazardly lets the marks go to waste.
notes.kennen-combo-teamfight: In a teamfight, enter with E, then use R, W, and Q in that order. Activate R immediately so its repeated marks have time to build toward an area stun. E restores energy if it hits at least one enemy, letting you use the next ability right away, so choose an entry path that passes through someone.
notes.kennen-skill-passive: Three stacks of Mark of the Storm stun the target, but the stacks expire over time. Before applying the second mark, make sure you can follow with a third; if you cannot, it is better to delay the first mark altogether.
notes.kennen-skill-q: Q hits only the first enemy it strikes, so it cannot reach an opponent standing behind minions. Use it as your main lane poke and to apply the first mark, prioritizing a hit over damage when the mark is your goal. Its cooldown drops significantly as you level it, letting you poke more often.
notes.kennen-skill-w: W’s passive periodically adds damage and a mark to a basic attack, while casting W hits nearby marked enemies at once. Use the empowered basic attack before casting W; casting it before the passive is ready leaves you with only one mark.
notes.kennen-skill-e: E lets Kennen pass through units and marks enemies he passes through, then grants attack speed when it ends. Decide whether to use it to enter or escape, since it is his only way out. Hitting at least one enemy restores energy and makes an engage efficient, but Kennen is vulnerable to being caught once E is gone.
notes.kennen-skill-r: R repeatedly damages and marks all nearby enemies throughout its duration, setting up an area stun while granting Kennen armor and magic resistance. It helps him survive after entering the middle of the enemy team, so save it if your angle would catch only one enemy.
notes.kennen-laning-poke: Against melee opponents, use your range to poke with Q alone. Keep them at no more than two marks, then complete the stun with a basic attack and W when they step forward for a last hit. Stunning them early wastes the chance to follow up with damage.
notes.kennen-laning-wave: W’s passive lets you clear waves with basic attacks alone. Since E is Kennen’s only escape, pushing without vision leaves him vulnerable to ganks. After pushing, secure river vision first and keep E ready to respond to a gank.
notes.kennen-phase: Putting points into Q for poke makes Kennen strong against melee opponents early, and level 6 gives him his first chance at a solo kill when R becomes available. He peaks in the mid game with an engage item and ability power. Late in the game, his health is among the lowest of all champions, so making one successful engage becomes crucial.
notes.kennen-teamfight-entry: Before activating R, find an angle into a group of opponents. Enter only when an ally has caught an enemy or you can flank from outside their vision; walking in from the front risks getting caught before you can activate R.
notes.kennen-teamfight-exit: Hold E after activating R to land an area stun and get out. If you use E to engage, your allies need to follow immediately; otherwise, you’ll land the stun and be left alone. Deciding whether to use E to engage or escape is the key choice in Kennen’s teamfights.
notes.kennen-situational-banshee: If the enemy’s damage is mostly magic, fit Banshee’s Veil between your core items. Kennen tends to take a targeted ability as soon as he enters, and blocking that first hit is worth more than the magic resistance alone.
notes.vs-kennen-marks: Three stacks of Kennen’s marks stun you. Once you have two, move out of his range or put minions between you to stop the third. The stacks expire over time, so backing off briefly resets them and denies his finishing blow.
notes.vs-kennen-q: Kennen’s Q hits only the first target in its path. Standing behind minions blocks his lane poke and prevents the first mark that leads to a stun. Plan your movement so you are exposed only briefly when stepping up for a last hit.
notes.vs-kennen-e: Kennen has some of the lowest health among champions, and E is his only escape. Counterattack when he uses it to enter recklessly: once E is down, he has no way out. Even if you take some poke, it is better to draw out E before approaching.
notes.vs-kennen-r: R is most effective when Kennen enters the middle of your team, and its resistances help him survive briefly. Anticipate his entry angle and spread out to avoid a shared area stun. Keep vision on his likely entry points to deny him the chance to start a teamfight with R.
notes.vs-kennen-cleanse: Kennen’s decisive damage follows his area stun, so use a cleanse to remove it if you have one. Physical damage dealers should consider Mercurial Scimitar, and ability power champions should consider Quicksilver Sash. If you cannot remove the stun, avoid standing together with allies in his entry path.
notes.khazix-combo-assassination: Start an isolated-target assassination from outside the enemy’s vision: use brush or R to activate Unseen Threat, then close in with E and use Q → empowered basic attack → W as soon as you land. Use Q immediately after E so its damage overlaps with Leap’s landing damage, without another action between them.
notes.khazix-combo-r-reload: R’s Void Assault lets Kha’Zix escape or refresh Unseen Threat by disappearing from enemy vision during a fight. Use R, move to the side, then follow with an empowered basic attack and Q to repeat the combo; saving R only for escape gives up that damage.
notes.khazix-combo-gank: When ganking, it is usually better to walk in, slow the target with W, and use Q up close while saving E to follow their Flash or escape. If you use E to engage, you cannot follow when the target Flashes.
notes.khazix-skill-isolation: Kha’Zix’s decision to fight hinges on isolation: a marker appears when no allied units are near the target, and Q deals nearly double damage to a marked target. Check the visible marker before engaging; an enemy near a wave, allied units, or jungle monsters is not isolated.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-q: Each time you rank up R, you can evolve one ability for an added effect. Evolving Q increases the range of Q and basic attacks and reduces Q’s cooldown against isolated targets, making it a good default first evolution for dealing damage from beyond counterattack range and clearing camps faster.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-e: Evolving E increases Leap’s range and resets its cooldown when you participate in a champion takedown. The extra range opens more ways to engage, while the reset lets you escape after an assassination or move straight to the next target. Prioritize E more when the enemy formation is tight and escaping after you engage will be difficult.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-w: Evolving W fires spikes in three directions, adds a slow, and reveals targets; the slow is stronger against isolated enemies. Choose it when you can only poke from a distance, need to keep a fleeing target within reach, or face grouped enemies who are hard to isolate.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-r: Evolving R extends its stealth duration and gives it more uses, letting you engage, leave, and reengage once more. Consider it when you need to enter a teamfight twice or dense enemy vision makes approaching difficult; give it lower priority when assassinating one target is enough.
notes.khazix-skill-w-sustain: Void Spike (W) heals Kha’Zix when he is within its explosion radius. Fire it while close to a monster during jungle clears to reduce health loss.
notes.khazix-phase: Level 6, when Kha’Zix gains his first evolution, is his first power spike. Until then, spend time on camps and vision instead of forcing early fights. He is strongest in the mid game with two or more evolutions, but his impact drops sharply if enemies stay grouped late and leave no isolated targets. As the game goes on, focus on catching enemies who split off rather than teamfighting.
notes.khazix-jungle-path: Choose jungle paths that create isolated targets: an enemy ahead of the wave in a side lane or a jungler clearing a camp alone can be isolated. Kha’Zix is strong in a one-on-one encounter in the enemy jungle, and if you can read the opposing jungler’s path, taking a camp on the opposite side and leaving gives you an advantage.
notes.khazix-gank-angle: Set up ganks from beyond a wall. E’s Leap crosses terrain, so avoid river entrances the enemy has vision of, wait behind a wall, then jump over. If the target is close to allied minions, they are not isolated and the chance of a kill is lower, so look for a moment when the wave has pushed toward the enemy turret.
notes.khazix-teamfight: Wait on a flank or behind the enemy rather than entering a teamfight from the front, and engage only when a backline damage dealer separates from the formation and the enemy has used their targeted crowd control. After engaging, break vision with R, pull back, and go in again. Do not remain in the fight hitting a tank with unevolved abilities.
notes.khazix-situational-antiheal: If an assassination target can heal enough to offset your burst damage, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items.
notes.vs-khazix-isolation: Kha’Zix’s damage can vary by nearly double depending on isolation, so stay near allied champions or minions to cut his Q damage to roughly half. Spend less time moving alone through side lanes, and keep him from predicting where you clear jungle camps alone.
notes.vs-khazix-e: E (Leap) is Kha'Zix's only mobility ability, so save crowd control and Flash for the moment after he uses it to engage—that is your chance to counterattack. If he has evolved E, though, its cooldown resets when he participates in a takedown; once an ally has been picked off, assume that counterattack window is gone.
notes.vs-khazix-passive-vision: When Kha’Zix is out of sight, his next basic attack deals bonus magic damage and slows. Maintain vision in brushes to deny that empowered attack and slow, prioritizing brushes by the river and jungle entrances.
notes.vs-khazix-r: Control Wards do not reveal Kha’Zix during Void Assault (R). When he disappears, cast area-of-effect abilities along his expected approach path or stay close to allies and apply crowd control as soon as he appears. The brief moment when stealth ends and he becomes visible is your chance to counterattack.
notes.vs-khazix-teamfight: Group up and start teamfights in narrow areas where you have vision. Keeping backline damage dealers beside tanks prevents isolation and denies Kha’Zix an opening to engage. When contesting an objective, avoid sending teammates out of vision one at a time.
notes.vs-khazix-phase: Before level 6 and his first evolution, Kha’Zix is an ordinary jungler. Pressure his jungle early or take objectives first to delay his evolution timing and gain the advantage; once he has two or more evolutions in the mid game, stop acting alone.
notes.kindred-combo-basic: Apply E to a target, weave in Q for its attack speed boost, and keep basic attacking that same target to trigger Wolf's pounce sooner. Switching targets resets E's progress, so stay focused on one target.
notes.kindred-combo-w-zone: Place W where the enemy will stand before starting a fight. Inside its zone, Q's cooldown is much shorter, letting you reposition repeatedly, and Wolf can only fight there. Using W first improves both damage and survival; stepping outside its zone interrupts your Q rotations.
notes.kindred-skill-passive: Kindred's growth depends on marks: participating in a takedown grants one, and each permanent mark strengthens their basic abilities. Collecting enough also increases basic attack range, so prioritize marks over kills in the first few minutes. Missing two or three marks can leave Kindred unable to fill a ranged damage dealer's role later.
notes.kindred-skill-passive-choice: The champion you choose to mark shapes your route: a marked enemy jungle monster gives you a reason to counterjungle, while marking a champion gives you a reason to gank their lane. Enemies can see marks too, so the opposing jungler may be waiting. Only pursue a mark deep in unseen enemy territory when your allies have lane priority.
notes.kindred-skill-q: Q combines a short leap with arrow damage, making it useful for both dodging and attacking. Save it for an escape outside W's zone, where its cooldown is long; inside the zone, its short cooldown makes frequent use worthwhile. While clearing, reposition with Q between monster attacks to take fewer hits.
notes.kindred-skill-w: W is central to both damage and clear speed. Wolf deals extra damage to jungle monsters but attacks only inside the zone, so place W in the middle of a camp. Movement and attacks also build passive stacks; once full, your next basic attack heals you based on your missing health. Using that heal when low can let you clear another camp.
notes.kindred-skill-e: E slows enemies and sets up Wolf's pounce, which deals more damage the more health its target is missing. The pounce is stronger later in a fight, but its conditions cannot build until E is applied, so applying it as you engage and following with basic attacks is the reliable approach. Use E early for the slow if the enemy looks ready to escape with a mobility ability.
notes.kindred-skill-r-basic: R creates a zone at a chosen location where allies, enemies, and monsters cannot die. Once someone's health falls near zero inside it, they receive neither damage nor healing until the zone ends, when everyone still inside is healed. Use it to waste an enemy finishing ability or Ignite.
notes.kindred-skill-r-timing: Timing is everything with R (Lamb's Respite) because it saves enemies too: use it too early and you may spare an opponent your team was about to kill; use it too late and your allies may already be dead. Activate it just after an enemy engages on your team's main damage dealer, or as an opponent moves in to use Smite at an objective. Keep dealing damage inside the zone to lower the enemy's health, then finish them as it ends.
notes.kindred-jungle-pathing: Kindred has some of the lowest movement speed in the game, so wasted trips are costly. Check where the mark appears and clear camps toward it instead of walking in the opposite direction and doubling back. W (Wolf's Frenzy) helps clear camps quickly with its bonus monster damage, so when a gank is uncertain, farming and counterjungling for marks is the better bet.
notes.kindred-ganking: With only E's slow for crowd control, Kindred struggles to make a gank work alone. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or an enemy has pushed too far up the lane; otherwise, clear vision and pressure through counterjungling. Kindred is prone to early deaths, and one overaggressive engage can derail mark progress.
notes.kindred-teamfight: Do not engage first in a teamfight. Once your allies start the fight, place W behind them and basic attack while repositioning with Q inside its zone. Kindred has low health and only R as a reliable way to avoid death, so standing at the front while an enemy engage ability is available can leave you unable to contribute, regardless of your marks.
notes.kindred-phase: Early Kindred is fragile and slow, making encounters with the enemy jungler easy to lose. Duels become viable in the mid game after Kindred gains several marks and attack speed items; once marks begin increasing their range, they can fight melee champions without taking hits back. Missing marks on time can erase that growth, so prioritize marks and farming over early fights.
notes.kindred-situational-antiheal: Build Grievous Wounds against strong healing. Because Kindred deals sustained damage through basic attacks, Mortal Reminder provides both armor penetration and Grievous Wounds while disrupting the core build less.
notes.vs-kindred-mark: Kindred's growth depends on marks. When a jungle monster is marked, clear its camp first or ward nearby to keep Kindred from claiming it. Delaying several marks noticeably reduces Kindred's damage and range in the mid to late game.
notes.vs-kindred-early: Kindred's fragility and low movement speed make them vulnerable to early pressure. Ward their jungle and repeatedly disrupt their route to force cautious farming and delay their marks. If you encounter Kindred, close in before they place W.
notes.vs-kindred-r-inside: When Kindred activates R (Lamb's Respite), move into its zone: no one can die inside it, so even allies at near-zero health survive and receive healing when it ends. Waiting outside only to get caught after the zone expires is the worst outcome.
notes.vs-kindred-r-displace: If you have a displacement ability, push or pull Kindred—or the ally they are trying to save—out of R's zone. The zone stays in place, so leaving it removes the protection from death.
notes.vs-kindred-e: Kindred's major burst comes from Wolf's pounce after consecutive hits on a target marked by E. If you are marked, create distance or break line of sight to prevent it from triggering. Its damage scales with your missing health, making it especially dangerous when you are already low.
notes.vs-kindred-w: Inside W's zone, Kindred can reposition repeatedly with Q's shorter cooldown while Wolf also deals damage. Push Kindred outside it to interrupt those Q rotations and remove Wolf's damage; a knockback or movement impairment can keep them there.
notes.kled-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use E (Jousting) to close the gap and land Q (Bear Trap on a Rope), then stay close while attacking with W (Violent Tendencies) active. Once Q pulls the target in, finish W’s fourth hit with your remaining basic attacks and recast E to disengage. The recast travels only toward the target hit by the first E, so you must land that cast on your opponent if you want to use it to get out.
notes.kled-combo-q-hold: Landing Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) is only the start: stay close for a short time afterward to trigger its pull and heavy damage. Use E (Jousting) or W (Violent Tendencies) to keep up as soon as the trap lands, since your opponent will try to escape. If they use a mobility ability to get out of range, the follow-up effect is lost.
notes.kled-skill-dismount: When Skaarl runs out of health, Kled dismounts, leaving him with very low health and reduced damage against champions. He gains movement speed toward enemy champions, plus armor and magic resistance based on how many are nearby. Stay close and attack to build Courage after dismounting; running away at this point weakens him most.
notes.kled-skill-courage: Attacking champions builds Courage fastest, though attacking epic monsters or structures and killing minions also fills the bar. Once it is full, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts, effectively gaining a second health bar. If you have nowhere to run while dismounted, attack a turret or minion wave for Courage; if you can stay close to an opponent, attack them to build it much faster.
notes.kled-skill-pistol: While dismounted, Q becomes Pocket Pistol, a ranged attack whose recoil pushes Kled backward, opposite the direction he aims. Aim at an opponent to retreat while building Courage, and immediately after dismounting, account for the recoil so it carries you toward your escape route. Pocket Pistol is your only way to build Courage while fleeing.
notes.kled-skill-w: W (Violent Tendencies) puts maximum-health damage on its fourth landed attack, so activate it when you can land all four rather than when your opponent is about to escape. Every basic attack reduces W’s cooldown, with a larger reduction against champions; staying close and continuing to attack during a fight can bring it back for another use.
notes.kled-skill-e: E (Jousting) pulls minions and small monsters in front of Kled as he dashes, letting you draw a wave toward you or group a jungle camp. Hitting a champion or large monster grants movement speed and allows a recast shortly afterward toward the same target. You can use that return trip to avoid an opponent’s ability and then go back in.
notes.kled-skill-r: Because R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) can start from very far away, aim for where the enemy team will be when you arrive. Its shield forms during the charge and lasts briefly afterward, helping you survive the burst that follows your engage. Skaarl charges only the first enemy champion along the path, so you cannot pass a tank to hit the back line.
notes.kled-laning: Kled trades well from level 1 thanks to his high attack damage, but his own health is the lowest of any champion. Treat Skaarl’s health bar as his effective health: if Skaarl is nearly depleted, back off instead of trading and build Courage. An enemy jungler arriving while Kled is dismounted can kill him outright.
notes.kled-laning-wave: Step forward in lane when Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) is available; without the trap, Kled has no way to hold an opponent in place for a trade. While Q is unavailable, use E (Jousting) to pull the wave toward your side and basic attacks to reduce W (Violent Tendencies)’s cooldown. After winning a trade, turn that advantage into turret pressure.
notes.kled-phase: Kled peaks in lane and mid-game skirmishes, where early kills and turret plates can build a lead. In late-game teamfights, he can lose Skaarl soon after engaging with R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!), and his reduced champion damage while dismounted weakens his sustained damage. Build on your early lead and aim to decide the game through turrets and objectives in the mid game.
notes.kled-teamfight: Open teamfights with R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) along a path your allies can follow, since they also gain movement speed on its route. If Skaarl is lost after the engage, stay in the skirmish to build Courage instead of retreating immediately. Survive long enough to remount and start a second fight.
notes.kled-situational-mr: Kled’s level 1 magic resistance is among the lowest, so magic damage can strip away Skaarl quickly. If the enemy’s main damage is magic, fit Maw of Malmortius between your core items; its shield and magic resistance help you survive after dismounting.
notes.kled-situational-antiheal: If an opponent’s healing lets them survive W (Violent Tendencies)’s maximum-health damage, buy Executioner’s Calling earlier. Kled stays close and keeps attacking, making it easy to apply Grievous Wounds consistently.
notes.vs-kled-courage: Watch Kled’s Courage bar when he is dismounted: once it fills, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts, effectively gaining a second health bar. If you can reliably kill him, do it before he remounts; otherwise, keep your distance so he cannot build Courage.
notes.vs-kled-courage-source: Kled gains Courage not only by hitting champions, but also by killing minions and attacking structures or epic monsters. If left alone in lane while dismounted, he can remount by farming minions and attacking the turret, so after knocking him off Skaarl, zone him out of lane and deny him farm to keep your advantage.
notes.vs-kled-w: Kled is much more dangerous when W (Violent Tendencies) is ready: its fourth landed basic attack deals damage based on your maximum health, making that hit especially costly for high-health champions. When he activates W, back off before he lands all four attacks, then move in again.
notes.vs-kled-q: Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) does not pull you immediately; Kled must stay close for a short time after it catches you. Save your mobility ability or Flash for that moment and escape before the pull. If you have no way out, move toward your minion wave or allies to make it harder for him to follow.
notes.vs-kled-r: Kled can engage with R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) from far outside vision, so keep vision on the flanks to spot him early. If you cannot stop the engage, remember that Skaarl charges only the first enemy champion along the path. With a tank in front, the backline will not be hit directly; hold your formation.
notes.vs-kled-late: Kled has very low health while dismounted and deals less damage to champions. He weakens sharply after the laning phase and mid game, so avoid giving him an early lead and extend the game.
notes.kogmaw-combo-basic: For a basic trade, activate W and start auto-attacking from outside the enemy’s response range, then use Q once you’ve closed in so its armor and magic resistance reduction overlaps with W’s on-hit damage. Keep auto-attacking afterward; if you use Q first, W’s duration runs down while the enemy backs away.
notes.kogmaw-combo-kite: Kite by walking backward and placing E along your retreat path, then resume auto-attacking when the enemy steps on the trail and slows. Because E leaves a trail wherever its projectile passes, you do not need a direct hit; aim where the enemy is about to move.
notes.kogmaw-combo-finish: To finish an enemy, cut off their escape route with E, then fire R repeatedly. R’s damage rises sharply once their health falls below a certain threshold, so a burst of shots is most efficient after they reach it; firing repeatedly at a high-health target only drains your mana.
notes.kogmaw-skill-w: W defines Kog’Maw: it temporarily extends his range and adds magic damage based on maximum health to his auto-attacks, but it has a long cooldown. Spend it on wave clear and you lose its range advantage for the fight. Its damage against monsters is capped, so damage to objectives comes mainly from auto-attacks and items.
notes.kogmaw-skill-q: A point in Q grants passive attack speed, while landing it reduces the target’s armor and magic resistance. That reduction also benefits your allies, so apply Q to the enemy frontline just before a dragon or Rift Herald fight to increase your team’s damage.
notes.kogmaw-skill-r-mana: R’s mana cost rises in steps when you cast it repeatedly within a short time. Spamming it for poke in lane can leave too little mana for a fight, so stop after one or two shots and fire repeatedly only when you can secure a kill. R also reveals targets that are not stealthed, making it useful for checking brush.
notes.kogmaw-skill-passive: After dying, Kog’Maw can briefly move through units before exploding for true damage that armor and magic resistance cannot reduce. This is your last chance to deal damage; if enemies retreat, walk toward your allies or an objective to deny that area instead of chasing them.
notes.kogmaw-laning: Kog’Maw has some of the lowest movement speed among champions and no mobility ability, making him especially vulnerable to ganks. When W is down, stay behind the middle of the lane and move forward only while it is active. Always consider both W’s cooldown and the enemy jungler’s position before advancing.
notes.kogmaw-laning-wave: Do not force the wave forward. E can clear enemies in a line, but using it on the wave puts your gank escape slow on cooldown. Let the wave come to you, farm near your turret, and push forward only where your support has established vision.
notes.kogmaw-phase: Kog’Maw is weakest at levels 1–2. His range advantage grows as W gains levels, and he peaks in the mid to late game once he has at least two attack speed and damage items. As a hypercarry built around range and attack speed, he benefits from longer games and can recover from an early deficit by continuing to farm.
notes.kogmaw-teamfight: Kog’Maw’s condition for joining a fight is positioning: attack from behind your frontline at W range and stay within reach of your allies’ protective abilities, since you cannot escape a diver on your own. If your frontline collapses, stop dealing damage and retreat.
notes.kogmaw-teamfight-target: Because W deals damage based on maximum health, attacking a high-health frontline target is worthwhile. Moving forward to reach the backline can get you killed, so focus the nearest enemy within range.
notes.kogmaw-situational-antiheal: If the enemy’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce it. Kog’Maw’s sustained auto-attacks keep the healing reduction active.
notes.kogmaw-situational-qss: Reliable immobilizing crowd control can kill Kog’Maw as soon as it catches him. Against it, fit Mercurial Scimitar between core items so you can free yourself.
notes.vs-kogmaw-w: Kog’Maw’s extra range lasts only while W is active; without it, he has ordinary ranged attack range. Wait for W to expire before closing in, and if he approaches with it active, let its duration run out to win the trade.
notes.vs-kogmaw-mobility: With low movement speed and no mobility ability, Kog’Maw can be caught by a single immobilizing crowd control effect. Make him your first target for jungle ganks and roams, and focus him first in teamfights if your team has an engage composition.
notes.vs-kogmaw-passive: Walk away from Kog’Maw’s body immediately after killing him. His delayed explosion deals true damage that defensive stats cannot reduce, and he can move through units to follow you even after death.
notes.vs-kogmaw-r: R can arrive from off-screen and deals sharply increased damage to low-health targets. If your health is low, leave Kog’Maw’s vision before healing; a hit also reveals your position and can set up a follow-up gank.
notes.vs-kogmaw-q: Q reduces both armor and magic resistance, increasing the damage from Kog’Maw’s follow-up auto-attacks and his allies. Block its projectile with a minion or dodge sideways; if it hits, keep your distance until the brief resistance reduction ends.
notes.vs-kogmaw-late: Kog’Maw is a hypercarry who grows stronger over time. Take objectives and turrets in the early to mid game to finish quickly, and keep pressuring him in lane to disrupt his farming.
notes.leblanc-combo-basic: The basic combo is to apply Q (Sigil of Malice), dash in with W (Distortion) to detonate the mark, then recast W to return. The mark only detonates when another ability hits the target, so landing Q alone deals only half the damage.
notes.leblanc-combo-full: The full combo is W in → Q → R to mimic W and detonate the mark → W back. R mimics the most recently used ability, so place the ability you want to mimic immediately before it; otherwise, R will mimic a different ability.
notes.leblanc-combo-e-lock: The most reliable combo is to land E (Ethereal Chains), then use Q (Sigil of Malice) into W (Distortion) as the root activates. The chain must remain attached for a while before it roots, so stay within its range until then.
notes.leblanc-combo-w-return: W (Distortion) lets you return only for a short time after dashing. Check that the return point is safe before going in, then decide whether to press forward or return based on the enemy’s remaining counterattack abilities. If the return window expires, you lose that escape option.
notes.leblanc-skill-q: If a Q (Sigil of Malice) hit or mark detonation kills the target, it refunds all the mana spent and reduces Q’s remaining cooldown. That makes Q relatively inexpensive for clearing waves or securing last hits, letting you push the lane quickly.
notes.leblanc-skill-passive-clone: P (Mirror Image) briefly turns LeBlanc invisible and creates a clone when her health falls below a certain threshold. You can control the clone separately; when escaping, send it in the opposite direction to throw off pursuers.
notes.leblanc-skill-r-choice: Choose what R (Mimic) will copy before starting your combo: copy Q (Sigil of Malice) when a kill is certain, W (Distortion) when you need another engage or escape, or E (Ethereal Chains) when you need guaranteed crowd control.
notes.leblanc-phase: LeBlanc is strongest from just after learning R (Mimic) at level 6 through the mid game, when kill opportunities are most frequent. Late in the game, enemies have magic resistance and vision, and a failed assassination leaves her vulnerable to a counterattack; without an earlier lead, her impact drops sharply.
notes.leblanc-laning-push: Push the wave before roaming. Clear it quickly with Q, then join a fight in a side lane or the jungle; stay in lane if you have not pushed the wave.
notes.leblanc-laning-trade: Trade only right after the enemy uses a key ability. LeBlanc is fragile and loses extended damage trades, so keep exchanges short: go in with W (Distortion) and return every time. Never engage unless the W return is available.
notes.leblanc-teamfight: Do not go in first in a head-on teamfight. Once the fight starts and the enemy focuses on your allied tank, enter from the side, eliminate one chosen backliner, then disengage with W (Distortion). Going in without a target will get you killed.
