notes.leblanc-teamfight-pick: LeBlanc gets more value from picks than from teamfights. Root and eliminate an enemy traveling alone through an area without vision using E (Ethereal Chains), and you can take an objective for free. Look first for a pick that prevents a teamfight from happening.
notes.leblanc-situational-banshee: If the enemy mid laner is a mage with targeted burst damage, buy Banshee’s Veil to block the first ability in their combo. Once LeBlanc is locked down, she cannot counterattack, so blocking that opening ability changes the fight.
notes.vs-leblanc-clone: The clone created by P (Mirror Image) cannot deal damage. If a low-health LeBlanc suddenly splits into two, do not waste an ability on either one at random; follow the one that actually attacks.
notes.vs-leblanc-mark: If the Q (Sigil of Malice) mark remains on you, the next ability to hit you deals double damage. Back away instead of moving forward and give the mark time to disappear.
notes.vs-leblanc-e: E (Ethereal Chains) roots only after the chain has remained attached, not on impact. If it hits you, get out of chain range before the root activates; use Flash or a movement ability immediately to escape it.
notes.vs-leblanc-w: After LeBlanc dashes in with W (Distortion), she can return to her original position only for a short time. Instead of immediately counterattacking and letting her slip away, close in and fight after that return expires or has been used.
notes.vs-leblanc-roam: LeBlanc roams after pushing the lane. Alert your team immediately if she disappears from mid vision, and secure river vision before moving forward in a side lane.
notes.leblanc-skill-e-aim: E (Ethereal Chains) must stay connected for 1.5 seconds to root, so a straight shot is easy to break. Cast from a bush or behind minions while out of sight, or use W (Distortion) to get beside the enemy and narrow the angle before casting. Landing E also grants true sight, which helps you track a fleeing target.
notes.leesin-skill-passive-weave: After Lee Sin uses an ability, Flurry increases the attack speed of his next two basic attacks and restores energy. Weave those attacks between abilities instead of using abilities back to back to deal more damage and maintain energy; use this ability–attack–attack rhythm when clearing the jungle and fighting.
notes.leesin-skill-q: Q's first cast, Sonic Wave, is a skillshot projectile that minions and jungle monsters can block. Gank from the side to avoid the wave, and avoid firing it into empty space to check vision, since that costs you your engage. A hit grants true sight, keeping the target visible even if they flee into brush.
notes.leesin-skill-q2-timing: Q's second cast, Resonating Strike, deals more damage the more health the target is missing. After landing the first cast, let allied crowd control and basic attacks lower their health before using the second cast to finish them, but act before its short recast window expires.
notes.leesin-skill-w: W's first cast, Safeguard, can dash to allies or your own wards, letting Lee Sin create his own engage and escape routes. A ward over a wall can set up an engage from an unseen angle or a retreat when danger comes; decide which route you need before placing it.
notes.leesin-skill-w-recast: W's second cast, Iron Will, increases omnivamp, helping Lee Sin sustain through jungle clears and heal during skirmishes. After engaging with the first cast, use it as you begin basic attacking.
notes.leesin-skill-e: E's first cast, Tempest, deals area damage around Lee Sin and detects stealthed enemies, so it can check unwarded brush or reveal a hidden opponent. Its second cast, Cripple, slows enemies; hold it after landing the first cast, then use it to keep up once the opponent uses an escape ability.
notes.leesin-skill-r: Direction is everything with R, Dragon's Rage: it holds the target in place during the cast, then knocks up enemies the target hits while flying backward. Kick an opponent toward your allies or through a group for a knockup on multiple enemies; simply kicking someone away can let them escape.
notes.leesin-combo-basic: For a basic gank, use Sonic Wave (Q) → basic attack → Tempest (E) → basic attack → Resonating Strike (Q), then Cripple (E) if you need the slow. Weave Flurry-empowered basic attacks between abilities, and use Resonating Strike after lowering the opponent’s health.
notes.leesin-combo-ward-jump: To ward jump, place the ward first and press W before it lands. A ward over a wall or behind an opponent lets you close the gap from outside Q range; when escaping, place one over a wall toward your team instead.
notes.leesin-combo-insec: For an Insec, land Q's first cast, get behind the opponent with Q's second cast or a ward and W, then use R to kick them toward your allies. If using Flash to change the kick's direction, cast R first and Flash during its cast for the most reliable timing. Check that your allies are close enough to follow up before starting.
notes.leesin-combo-r-q2: When your allies are far away, land Q's first cast but hold the second, kick the opponent toward your team with R, then use Q's second cast to follow and catch them again. This lets Lee Sin close the gap created by the kick and keep the opponent within his team's reach.
notes.leesin-phase-early: Lee Sin's level-one attack damage and armor rank among the highest of all champions, making early jungle duels and counter-jungling his strongest phase. After your first two or three camps, look to disrupt the enemy jungler's route; once R becomes available at level 6, an Insec can break open an entire lane.
notes.leesin-phase-late: As the game goes on, Lee Sin contributes less damage and can no longer reliably kill an opponent alone. Shift toward using R to isolate an enemy or knock away someone diving your backline, creating a favorable fight for your fed allied carry.
notes.leesin-laning: Plan your jungle route to turn Lee Sin's early strength into an advantage. His high movement speed and many ways to engage make it easy to steal camps or affect a lane when the enemy jungler is occupied on the opposite side. Once both Q and W are spent, he has no escape, so keep at least W available when venturing deep into the enemy jungle.
notes.leesin-teamfight: In teamfights, Lee Sin's value comes from moving an enemy backliner toward his allies. Engage only when they can follow up immediately; if they have yet to enter the fight, save R to knock away an enemy who engages. Since Lee Sin cannot hold the frontline for long, plan a way out with W or Q's second cast before diving in.
notes.leesin-situational-antiheal: Against champions who survive through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Lee Sin needs to win duels early, and failing to reduce that healing lets his window of advantage pass.
notes.vs-leesin-q-block: Most of Lee Sin's engages start with Q's first cast, Sonic Wave, a projectile blocked by minions and jungle monsters. If you expect a gank, keep the wave between you and him to deny a straight shot; when Q misses, he has virtually no way to reach you.
notes.vs-leesin-ward-jump: Lee Sin can use W, Safeguard, on his own wards to cross walls. Treat an unwarded area beyond a wall as a possible engage route: clear his wards there with a Control Ward or stand a step away from the wall.
notes.vs-leesin-q2: Lee Sin's Q second cast, Resonating Strike, hurts more the more health you have lost. If its first cast has hit you and your health drops below half, treat your remaining health as much lower than it looks and move toward an allied turret or your team during the short recast window.
notes.vs-leesin-r-position: Lee Sin's R, Dragon's Rage, is most threatening when he has room to get behind you. Stand with a wall or your frontline at your back so a kick sends you toward your team, and spread out before a teamfight: allies struck by the knocked-back target will also be knocked up.
notes.vs-leesin-early-duel: Lee Sin's level-one attack damage and armor are among the highest of all champions, so accepting an early duel puts you at a disadvantage. Retreat if you meet him in the jungle early, then use objective and lane advantages to buy time until his strength fades in the late game.
notes.vs-leesin-w-sustain: Lee Sin can recover health in skirmishes through the omnivamp from W's second cast, Iron Will. If he survives longer than expected in an extended fight, apply healing reduction. Focus your damage immediately after he uses W to engage, when he has neither its shield nor its omnivamp available.
notes.leona-combo-engage: For a basic engage, land E Zenith Blade to root the target, activate Q Shield of Daybreak as Leona arrives, stun with an auto attack, then use W Eclipse. Have both E and Q ready so the crowd control lasts continuously; if you engage with only one, the enemy can escape between them.
notes.leona-combo-flash: Q Shield of Daybreak is not consumed when cast; it empowers your next auto attack, so you can activate it before approaching. With Q ready, Flash in to land the stun without giving the enemy time to react to its activation. The effect expires if you do not auto attack within a certain time.
notes.leona-skill-passive: Leona cannot trigger a P Sunlight mark herself; an ally must hit the target. Engage first to apply the mark, then let an ally attack that target. Do not waste it on someone your allied damage dealer cannot see.
notes.leona-skill-w: W Eclipse reduces damage and grants armor and magic resistance, then explodes when its duration ends. The defensive stat increase lasts longer only if the explosion hits at least one enemy, so W is most useful while you are close to them. Activate it just after reaching an enemy, rather than immediately before engaging, to keep them nearby when it explodes.
notes.leona-skill-e: E Zenith Blade travels in a straight line and dashes to the last enemy champion it hits. If another champion stands behind your intended target, it can pull you farther in and leave you isolated, so check how many enemies are in its path before casting.
notes.leona-skill-r: R Solar Flare stuns enemies in its center but only slows those in its outer area. Cast it over a target already caught to secure the center hit; a freely moving enemy can easily dodge that area if you use R on its own. Its long range also lets you join an engage from outside the lane when you have vision.
notes.leona-phase: Leona has one of the highest level 1 armor values of any champion, letting her absorb damage in early trades. Look for kills at levels 2–3, once both Q and E are available, and at level 6, when R becomes available. Her damage falls off afterward, so focus on engaging and applying crowd control.
notes.leona-laning-timing: Engage as the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit, using E Zenith Blade during their auto-attack animation to leave them no time to react. First check that your allied marksman is close enough to follow up and has damage abilities ready; Leona lacks the damage to go in alone.
notes.leona-laning-cooldown: A failed engage can leave you in enemy range with both E and Q unavailable. Since E is an engage tool rather than an escape, keep Flash available when taking a risky angle. Once your abilities are down, pull the wave toward your turret to deny a counterattack.
notes.leona-roaming: Leona's engage is strongest when it starts before the enemy sees her. Keep looking for E angles from brush or areas without enemy vision; if the lane stalls, establish vision in the river and look to roam mid. She has little damage, but her crowd control can hold a target long enough for a kill, making her a valuable roamer.
notes.leona-teamfight-engage: In a teamfight, Leona can open the enemy formation with E and R or stop enemies diving her carry with Q and E. If your team has less damage than the enemy, protect your carry instead of engaging first. After an engage, stay in the fight while W lasts to absorb focused attacks and draw out as many enemy abilities as possible.
notes.leona-teamfight-target: Choose a target your allies can actually reach and attack, rather than simply one who could be killed. Only allied attacks trigger P Sunlight marks, so diving beyond your allies' reach leaves Leona dealing virtually no damage.
notes.leona-situational-cc: If the enemy team uses crowd control to shut down your carry, prioritize Mikael's Blessing to save them.
notes.leona-situational-thorn: If an enemy physical damage dealer sustains through auto attacks, buy Thornmail to apply reflected damage and Grievous Wounds in close combat.
notes.vs-leona-w: Leona's W Eclipse takes time to explode after activation. Move out of its area before then to avoid the damage and prevent her bonus defensive stats from lasting longer; staying close lets her survive much longer.
notes.vs-leona-r: Leona's R Solar Flare stuns only enemies in its center; its outer area merely slows. Move sideways as soon as the indicator appears to avoid the stun.
notes.vs-leona-e: Leona's E Zenith Blade passes through targets in a straight line and dashes to the last champion it hits. In lane, the marksman and support should avoid standing in line with its path, or Leona can dash past the first target to reach the one behind.
notes.vs-leona-q: Leona can approach with Q Shield of Daybreak already activated. Even if she has not used a skill, do not assume you are safe; keep her out of range to reach you.
notes.vs-leona-armor: Leona has one of the highest level 1 armor values of any champion, so early physical damage trades against her are usually unfavorable. Wear her down with magic damage or ranged poke, then counterattack once her engage abilities are down.
notes.vs-leona-passive: An ally of Leona must hit you to trigger a P Sunlight mark. Treat the mark as a warning that enemy damage is coming: retreat immediately instead of moving forward.
notes.lillia-combo-gank: For a gank, bounce E off a wall or roll it into the target, use the slow to land W's center, then finish with Q. Keep that order: without E's slow, W's center is almost impossible to land.
notes.lillia-combo-r: R Lilting Lullaby puts only enemies marked with dream dust to sleep, so land an ability first and use R only when your allies can wait through the delay from drowsiness to sleep. A sleeping enemy wakes when hit by a single instance of damage, so avoid placing a persistent damage area on them.
notes.lillia-combo-r-setup: The best time to use R is before a teamfight begins: mark several enemies from afar with Q and E, then cast R from outside their vision so they cannot react. In a head-on fight, damage is already being exchanged, and they will wake as soon as they fall asleep.
notes.lillia-skill-q: Q has a short cooldown and stacks movement speed each time it hits. Since those stacks power Lillia's chases and escapes, keep casting Q during fights and hit anything you can. Its edge deals true damage, so it remains effective against enemies with high defenses.
notes.lillia-skill-w: W Watch Out! Eep! has a visible windup, and its damage rises sharply when the center hits. Aim it at slowed or sleeping enemies, or stationary targets such as jungle monsters. W cannot cross terrain, so it cannot reach an enemy beyond a wall.
notes.lillia-skill-e: E Swirlseed rolls until it hits an enemy or terrain. Send it down a long, straight corridor or along a wall to hit enemies outside your vision; its best use is to roll it ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path. It reveals enemies on hit, so you can also use it to check jungle entrances without vision.
notes.lillia-skill-passive: Applying passive dream dust to a champion or large jungle monster restores health. When low, clearing a large camp is better for both healing and time than recalling. That healing lets Lillia keep clearing the jungle despite her low defensive stats.
notes.lillia-phase: Lillia clears and scales well early, but her solo ganks are weak, as reflected by high early CS and low kill numbers. Once she learns R at level 6, coordinated ganks with allies become possible; she peaks in the mid to late game when items strengthen her damage over time and movement speed. Early on, focus on clearing camps quickly instead of forcing kills.
notes.lillia-laning-clear: For jungle clears, position so Q's edge catches the monster pack, then hit the large monster with W's center. Passive healing keeps health loss low, so clear camps back to back early without interrupting your route.
notes.lillia-laning-gank: For the best gank angle, wait until the enemy moves farther into the lane, then roll E along a wall. Just before entering, hit a camp or minion with Q to build movement speed stacks; Lillia's base movement speed is low, making a chase difficult without them.
notes.lillia-teamfight: Lillia is not a frontliner: her armor is very low, so cast Q from the side to apply passive damage over time to several enemies, and slow enemy divers with E to keep them away from your damage dealers. Getting caught while trying to land W's center from the front is a common mistake.
notes.lillia-teamfight-r: If you open a teamfight with R, set the order in which your team will wake the sleeping enemies so an area ability does not wake them all at once. Each takes extra damage on waking, making it better to focus and finish them one at a time.
notes.lillia-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to prepare for being caught while using Q up close.
notes.lillia-situational-rylai: Against mostly ranged compositions that keep their distance, choose Rylai's Crystal Scepter to slow enemies with Q hits and stay close longer.
notes.vs-lillia-r-condition: Lillia's R Lilting Lullaby puts only enemies marked with dream dust by her abilities to sleep. Her Q and E poke therefore sets up R, so dodge both even when you have plenty of health.
notes.vs-lillia-w: Lillia's W Watch Out! Eep! has a visible windup and deals much more damage only when its center hits. When the windup starts, a small step sideways is more likely to avoid the center than backing away. Lillia cannot cross terrain with W, so it cannot reach you through a wall.
notes.vs-lillia-speed: Each ability hit gives Lillia a movement speed stack, and she becomes impossible to catch once they build up. With no stacks, her base movement speed is low; keep dodging her abilities, then close in to chase her.
notes.vs-lillia-squishy: Lillia has very low armor and must get close to deal sustained damage. In teamfights, save an immobilizing crowd control ability for her: catching her once as she comes in from the side can bring her down quickly.
notes.vs-lillia-e: Lillia's E Swirlseed rolls until it hits an enemy or a wall, making it nearly impossible to dodge in narrow corridors. If you do not know where she is, avoid walking straight through jungle entrances or river passages.
notes.vs-lillia-r-drowsy: Lillia's R does not put you to sleep immediately. You can still move while drowsy, so use that time to reach safety or remove the movement-impairing effect; miss that window and you will be stuck asleep.
notes.lissandra-combo-engage: To engage, cast E (Glacial Path) forward and recast it to teleport to the claw, then root the enemy with W (Ring of Frost) before using Q (Ice Shard) and R (Frozen Tomb), in that order. Press W almost as soon as you arrive so the enemy has no chance to escape; waiting to assess the situation until after you arrive is too late.
notes.lissandra-combo-self-r: Press your self-cast key and R together to cast R on yourself instantly. Check the key setting beforehand: opening the targeting prompt and trying to click yourself can get you killed.
notes.lissandra-skill-q: Q shatters on the first target it hits and pierces enemies behind it; if it hits nothing, it does not shatter. Against an opponent using minions as a shield, aim at a minion so the shattered Q reaches the champion behind it.
notes.lissandra-skill-w: W instantly roots enemies around you, but its short range means you have to get close. At low levels, a miss leaves you vulnerable throughout its long cooldown, so avoid using it carelessly to clear waves and save it for a certain engage or jungle follow-up.
notes.lissandra-skill-r-offense: Casting R on an enemy stuns them and spreads black ice that slows nearby enemies. It is most valuable for stopping an enemy engager as they come in; when enemies are grouped, target someone in the middle so the ice spreads through them.
notes.lissandra-skill-r-defense: Casting R on yourself makes you invulnerable during stasis and restores health, with a larger heal the more health you are missing. Hold it until an enemy finishing ability or delayed damage is about to hit, but account for the fact that you cannot act during stasis.
notes.lissandra-skill-passive: When an enemy champion dies nearby, Lissandra’s passive creates a Frozen Thrall that slows surrounding enemies and explodes after a short delay. After the first kill, factor that slow and area damage into your pursuit of another target.
notes.lissandra-phase: Once W and R are both available at level 6, Lissandra can look for a guaranteed engage. She is strongest in the mid game with one core item; later, her raw damage falls short of other mages, so shift from dealing damage to stopping engages and applying crowd control.
notes.lissandra-laning: Lissandra’s movement speed is among the lowest, and her short ability ranges put her at a disadvantage in ranged poke fights. Use Q to last-hit and clear waves while keeping up in levels, and trade only when E and W are both available. Using E to poke leaves you especially vulnerable to a jungle gank immediately afterward.
notes.lissandra-laning-roam: Push the wave with Q, then use E to cross terrain and roam to a side lane. The roam depends on having W and R available, so stay in lane if you have already used them there.
notes.lissandra-teamfight: Before a teamfight, decide whether to engage with E and W to root multiple enemies or answer an enemy engage with R. If you are unsure about going in, reserve R for the enemy engager; if you commit, be ready to follow E and W with R. Standing indecisively at the front is the worst option.
notes.lissandra-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier for its ability power and defense.
notes.lissandra-situational-banshee: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, build Banshee's Veil between core items to block one targeted ability before engaging.
notes.vs-lissandra-e: Lissandra throws E and can recast it to teleport to the claw. Immobilize her while it is traveling, before she recasts, to stop the teleport.
notes.vs-lissandra-w: Lissandra’s W has a long cooldown at low levels. Move in and trade right after she uses it on the wave or misses.
notes.vs-lissandra-r: Lissandra’s R stuns an enemy when cast on them and makes her invulnerable during stasis when cast on herself. If she still has R, a single burst can be wasted on that stasis, so space out your damage to hit her when it ends.
notes.vs-lissandra-mobility: Lissandra has one of the lowest movement speeds and no escape besides E (Glacial Path). Once she has used it, she is simply a slow mage, so check whether E is spent before deciding to engage.
notes.vs-lissandra-q: Lissandra’s Q must hit a first target to shatter and pierce through enemies behind it. If you stand in line with your allied minions, you are in its path; farm from an offset angle instead.
notes.lissandra-skill-e: E works for both engaging and escaping: recast it at any point while the claw is traveling to teleport to its position. Casting it and running the other way makes your destination harder to predict, but being immobilized before the recast stops the teleport. If the enemy still has crowd control available, recast promptly.
notes.locke-combo-basic: For a basic trade, land Q and consume the nails with basic attacks. Since only basic attacks detonate them, work out how many follow-up attacks you can land before using Q.
notes.locke-combo-allin: To engage, use Q, teleport with E, then land the dashing basic attack and follow up with more basic attacks. E's teleport and the dash on your next basic attack are separate steps: position yourself first, then dash onto the target while the nails are still embedded to concentrate your damage.
notes.locke-skill-q: The more nails embedded in a target, the more damage each basic attack deals. Unconsumed nails refund Q cooldown according to how many remain, so if you cannot reach the target, let them expire rather than forcing a chase.
notes.locke-skill-w: W boosts your attack speed and movement speed while draining your health. When it ends, you recover health based on the damage you took and the health you lost during it. Activate it just before a fight where you need to consume nails quickly, and let it run its full duration unless you urgently need health; recasting it early reduces the healing.
notes.locke-skill-w-cc: You can activate W even while under crowd control. If you use it when you cannot act, you will still receive its healing and attack speed once the control ends, so press W when you get caught.
notes.locke-skill-e: E teleports you to a chosen location and damages nearby enemies; your next basic attack then dashes to its target and hits enemies along the path. Use the teleport to cross terrain and the attack to close in. Since a takedown resets E's cooldown, use it when you have a certain kill.
notes.locke-skill-passive: Your passive adds more damage to basic attacks the more health an enemy has lost. Against a wounded target, keep attacking instead of using more abilities, and do not wait for cooldowns when finishing them off.
notes.locke-skill-r: R heavily slows and marks enemies in its area. A marked enemy is sealed if their health falls below the threshold, and a sealing drops a relic on the ground. Picking up relics permanently raises the execution threshold, so collect them after the fight.
notes.locke-phase: Locke's melee range and high early mana costs make back-to-back combos difficult at levels 1–2. During the laning phase, he ranks among mid champions with the most takedowns but among those with the least CS, building leads through kills more than farming. Once he learns R at level 6, look for executions; collecting relics keeps improving his ability to finish enemies into the late game.
notes.locke-laning: As a melee champion, accept some lost CS against ranged opponents. Use Q to embed nails in your opponent instead of clearing minions, then trade with basic attacks. If they refuse to trade, use E's teleport to find an angle and force the engage.
notes.locke-laning-e-save: E is Locke's only escape tool in lane, so save it while you do not know where the enemy jungler is. A takedown resets its cooldown, though, allowing you to engage with E and use it again to escape when you can secure the kill.
notes.locke-teamfight: In teamfights, wait for your allies to damage the enemy before engaging with E and concentrating your missing-health-based passive and nail damage. Aim R at grouped enemies so it marks several of them.
notes.locke-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has healing, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Locke needs time to deal damage by consuming nails with basic attacks, and healing during that window can keep the target above his execution threshold.
notes.vs-locke-q: Locke's basic attacks deal rapidly increasing damage if you keep taking them while nails are embedded in you. If you are hit by nails, prioritize getting out of his basic attack range over dodging further abilities.
notes.vs-locke-e: Locke's E does not end with the teleport: his next basic attack dashes to its target and hits enemies along the path. Once he teleports, position yourself so your allies are not lined up along his dash path.
notes.vs-locke-e-reset: When Locke participates in a takedown, his E cooldown resets, allowing him to dive in again. The moment after an ally is picked off is especially dangerous, so retreat immediately and regroup as soon as the first ally dies.
notes.vs-locke-w: With W active, Locke gains a large boost to attack speed and movement speed while draining his own health, then recovers a substantial portion of that lost health when it ends. If you cannot finish him during W, retreat before the healing triggers.
notes.vs-locke-r: If your health falls below the threshold while marked by R, you are sealed. Retreat with more health remaining than usual when you see the mark, and account for the threshold rising as Locke collects relics.
notes.lucian-combo-weave: After Lucian uses an ability, his next basic attack fires twice. Alternate abilities and basic attacks to deal full damage; using abilities back to back triggers the double shot only once.
notes.lucian-combo-lane: For lane trades, use Q (Piercing Light), a double-shot basic attack, E (Relentless Pursuit) to reposition, another double-shot basic attack, then W (Ardent Blaze). Using E mid-combo makes up for Lucian’s short range and gives him another double shot.
notes.lucian-combo-q-minion: Q (Piercing Light) extends beyond its displayed range and pierces through targets. Cast it on a front minion to hit a champion behind it while appearing to farm.
notes.lucian-combo-r: Lucian can use E (Relentless Pursuit) during R (The Culling) to maintain his firing angle or move to safety. Since he cannot change R’s aim once it starts, line up directly with the target before casting rather than firing from an angle.
notes.lucian-skill-vigilance: When an ally heals or shields Lucian, or a nearby enemy is immobilized, his next two shots gain bonus damage. Time your basic attacks with your support’s shields or crowd control to deliver a burst of damage.
notes.lucian-skill-w: Hitting an enemy marked by W (Ardent Blaze) increases Lucian’s movement speed, even if an ally lands the hit. Apply the mark just before engaging or chasing to help close the gap despite his short range.
notes.lucian-skill-e: Each double-shot basic attack reduces E’s cooldown, but using it early just to cycle it faster can leave Lucian without a dash when he needs one. Prioritize saving it for a moment when that dash could keep him alive.
notes.lucian-skill-r-usage: R (The Culling) has uses beyond dealing damage: while escaping, fire it down a narrow passage to block an enemy’s path, or use it to clear a minion wave quickly when enemies siege an allied turret.
notes.lucian-skill-r-cancel: Lucian can recast R (The Culling) to stop it, and casting it prepares a Lightslinger double shot. If attacked from another angle, cancel R and retaliate with the double-shot basic attack instead of continuing to fire.
notes.lucian-phase-early: Lucian has short range for a marksman, but his double shot and E make him strong in early trades. With both kills by 14 minutes and damage per minute ranking near the top, he needs to build a lead in lane.
notes.lucian-phase-late: Lucian excels at short bursts of damage rather than sustained damage, and other marksmen outperform him in prolonged teamfights. Look for repeated brief engagements: move in, deal your burst, then retreat with E (Relentless Pursuit).
notes.lucian-laning: Lucian’s short range makes him easy to poke, so push the wave and use E (Relentless Pursuit) to avoid the enemy support’s engage. Trade only when both Q (Piercing Light) and your double shot are ready, then retreat behind your minions immediately.
notes.lucian-teamfight: In teamfights, approach from the side or follow up to finish a target already under crowd control rather than entering head-on. Mark the target with W (Ardent Blaze) before closing in for the movement speed boost, and save E (Relentless Pursuit) to disengage.
notes.vs-lucian-extended: Lucian relies on burst damage rather than sustained damage. Weather his first combo and extend the fight; his damage drops sharply once his abilities are spent, giving you a window to counterattack.
notes.vs-lucian-r: Lucian cannot change the aim of R (The Culling) during its cast. Sidestep out of its firing path instead of running straight back.
notes.vs-lucian-q: Lucian’s Q (Piercing Light) extends beyond its displayed range and pierces through targets. When he uses it to farm, step out of the line behind his target minion to avoid the poke.
notes.vs-lucian-vigilance: When the enemy support shields or heals Lucian, or one of your allies is immobilized, Lucian’s next two shots are empowered. Back off briefly and avoid trading into those shots.
notes.vs-lucian-e: Each double-shot basic attack reduces the cooldown of Lucian’s E, Relentless Pursuit. The longer you let him trade basic attacks, the sooner E returns, so engage in the brief window right after he uses it to catch him.
notes.lucian-skill-tower: Lightslinger’s double shot also works on turrets, so weave abilities between basic attacks to damage them faster.
notes.lulu-combo-peel: When an ally is caught, use W (Whimsy) to polymorph the attacker, then E (Help, Pix!) to shield your ally and Q (Glitterlance) to slow the enemy. W must come first to silence the enemy's follow-up ability immediately after the engage; time E for the damage that follows so its short duration is not wasted.
notes.lulu-combo-ult: R (Wild Growth) instantly increases an ally's maximum health, so cast it just before they die to absorb an entire burst of damage. It also knocks up enemies around them: use it on an ally being engaged on to stop the initiation, or on your tank to help initiate.
notes.lulu-combo-q-angle: Q (Glitterlance) fires bolts from Lulu and Pix at different angles. The closer you place the cursor to Lulu, the more narrowly the bolts overlap; the farther away you place it, the wider they spread. Keep it close to reliably hit one target or farther away to clip several.
notes.lulu-skill-w-ally: Casting W (Whimsy) on an ally increases both movement and attack speed, making it useful for chasing, escaping, or focusing damage on the enemy carry. If the enemy has a reliable engage that you need to interrupt, save W for them.
notes.lulu-skill-w-enemy: Casting W (Whimsy) on an enemy silences them and prevents them from attacking, but does not stop their movement. A dashing enemy will still reach you if you cast it mid-dash, so time W for when the dash ends and they attempt a follow-up ability to break their combo.
notes.lulu-skill-e: E (Help, Pix!) shields an ally and moves Pix to them. Cast it on a ranged ally who attacks frequently so Pix's bolts keep adding to their damage. Against an enemy, E grants true sight, letting you reveal their position in brush or while stealthed.
notes.lulu-skill-e-timing: E (Help, Pix!) has a short-lived shield that can expire before the damage arrives if cast too early. Watch the enemy's cast animation and practice timing E to meet the incoming damage; this is central to mastering Lulu.
notes.lulu-skill-passive: Other units can intercept Pix's bolts. If minions stand between you and the enemy, they absorb the bolts from your basic attack harass, so attack when the enemy steps out beside the minions.
notes.lulu-phase-early: Lulu’s Q (Glitterlance) poke and slow are strong early, but her health, armor, and attack damage are among the lowest, so she crumples if caught. Keep your poke advantage in lane without stepping forward to force the first opening.
notes.lulu-phase-scaling: At level 6, R (Wild Growth) lets Lulu reliably save an ally and punish an enemy who overcommits to an engage. She grows stronger into the late game as her allied carry grows stronger, so prioritize protecting the carry's growth over your own.
notes.lulu-laning-bait: Lulu is strongest when the enemy commits heavily to an engage. Give them an opening to come in, then counter with W (Whimsy) and E (Help, Pix!); if Lulu overcommits first, she lacks the damage to finish the fight and loses out.
notes.lulu-laning-mana: Q (Glitterlance) and E (Help, Pix!) cost a lot of mana, and repeated pointless poke can leave you unable to protect an ally when it matters. Save E for its shield rather than using it to poke; when your mana runs low, avoid overcommitting and find a chance to recall.
notes.lulu-teamfight: In teamfights, stay close to your most fed ally and focus W (Whimsy), E (Help, Pix!), and R (Wild Growth) on them. Position to see who the enemy engages on and respond, rather than trying to initiate yourself.
notes.lulu-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that holds allies in place, buy Mikael’s Blessing earlier. Lulu’s W (Whimsy) and E (Help, Pix!) cannot remove crowd control once it has landed, so she needs the item’s cleanse to fully protect her allies.
notes.vs-lulu-passive: Other units can intercept Pix's bolts. Stand behind minions to avoid much of the extra damage that accompanies Lulu's basic attacks.
notes.vs-lulu-commit: Lulu excels when enemies commit heavily all at once. Use steady poke to push her and her lane partner out of lane instead of forcing a committed engage.
notes.vs-lulu-w: Lulu's W (Whimsy) silences its target and prevents them from attacking. A dash engage is shut down while W is available, so bait her into using it on another ally before going in.
notes.vs-lulu-r: Lulu's R (Wild Growth) instantly increases its target's health and knocks up nearby enemies. Someone who looks certain to die can survive with a single R, so while it is available, target Lulu herself or someone other than the ally she would protect.
notes.vs-lulu-squishy: Lulu has some of the lowest health, armor, and attack damage in the game, with no dash to escape. Look to catch her when her shield and Pix are on an allied carry.
notes.lux-combo-full: For a kill combo, land Q Light Binding, place E Lucent Singularity without detonating it, then use R Final Spark, auto-attack, detonate E, and auto-attack again. Weave auto-attacks between abilities to keep consuming Illumination marks; delaying E’s detonation lets you land both attacks.
notes.lux-combo-poke: In lane, placing and detonating E, then auto-attacking to consume Illumination, is enough for poke. Save Q for kill opportunities and stopping engages, since Lux has no way to fight back while it is down.
notes.lux-skill-passive: Lux’s damaging abilities apply Illumination, which her auto-attacks consume for bonus magic damage. R consumes the mark on hit and then reapplies it, so follow R with an auto-attack for more damage. Skipping auto-attacks after landing abilities gives up a substantial share of her damage.
notes.lux-skill-q: Q Light Binding fully roots the first two enemies it hits, so angle it through a tank to catch a carry standing behind them. A miss can leave the rest of Lux’s abilities ineffective and Lux defenseless, so choose your openings carefully.
notes.lux-skill-w: W Prismatic Barrier shields on both its outward and return paths, and the two shields stack. Since allies’ movements are harder to predict than enemies’, throw it toward a group of allies instead of aiming at one person. While fleeing, cast it in the direction you are running to receive the returning shield sooner.
notes.lux-skill-e-zone: Leaving E Lucent Singularity in place before detonating it controls an area: place it ahead of time on enemy entry or escape routes to hinder movement, or throw it into a brush to check for an ambush. Though E is Lux’s most reliable ability to land, it costs a lot of mana; casting it every time it comes off cooldown will leave you short of mana midway through lane.
notes.lux-phase: A landed Q root can create a kill opportunity from level 1. Level 6 is Lux’s first power spike, when R lets her finish enemies beyond her usual range; her strongest burst comes in the mid to late game after she builds ability power. Later, enemy assassins can reach her, so positioning matters more than damage.
notes.lux-laning-safety: Lux has some of the lowest armor and health in the game and no mobility ability, leaving her with almost no answer to an ambush. Play at the edge of your range, and check brush without vision by throwing E before entering.
notes.lux-laning-wave: As support Lux, hitting minions with E pushes the lane and exposes you to enemy jungle ganks. When you need the wave to push toward you, aim E only at enemy champions; place it over the wave only when you need to push.
notes.lux-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your frontline, use Q to stop engages, E to block routes, and W to shield allies from burst damage. Hitting multiple targets with your abilities is the only way to justify their mana cost, so avoid angles that catch just one.
notes.lux-situational-assassin: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against assassins. Without mobility, Lux has only W’s shield to help her survive once caught.
notes.lux-situational-antiheal: When enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Morellonomicon to reduce it. E and R cover an area, so they can apply its healing reduction to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-lux-q: Lux relies on Q Light Binding: a hit guarantees her remaining abilities, while a miss leaves her defenseless. Bait out Q, dodge it, and then engage.
notes.vs-lux-q-line: Q Light Binding roots the first two enemies it hits, so an ally standing in front will not block it for you. Avoid lining up with teammates; spread sideways instead.
notes.vs-lux-e: Lux’s E, Lucent Singularity, controls an area. If you group up and approach from one spot, it can block you all at once, so spread out and approach from different directions to keep Lux from locking down a single area.
notes.vs-lux-r: R Final Spark shows a red targeting line before the beam fires. When retreating at low health, avoid running in a straight line and be ready to dodge sideways as soon as the line appears.
notes.vs-lux-passive: Lux’s abilities apply Illumination, which her auto-attacks consume for bonus damage. Leaving her auto-attack range immediately after an ability hits you noticeably reduces the damage you take.
notes.vs-lux-squishy: Lux has some of the lowest armor and health in the game and no mobility ability. Getting into range is the hard part; once you reach her, you can take her out quickly, so focus on finding an approach through a brush or from the flank.
notes.lux-skill-r: Lux’s R, Final Spark, has a cast time, and a red targeting line appears before it fires. When layering it into a combo, account for that delay or the beam will fire after the preceding root wears off. Its cooldown is relatively short, so as you level up, you can use it once per teamfight.
notes.lux-teamfight-ult: R pierces enemies in a straight line, so prioritize angles that catch several grouped enemies. Its relatively short cooldown makes it better to use immediately for a certain finish or a hit on multiple enemies than to hold it, increasing your total damage.
notes.malphite-combo-trade: Against melee opponents, activate W, then use a basic attack → E → basic attack for a short trade. W empowers the next attack and adds an aftershock to each attack for the next few seconds, so land both attacks before backing off. Use E after your opponent starts a basic attack to reduce their retaliation.
notes.malphite-combo-ult: For an ultimate burst combo, use R → W → basic attack → Q → E. Q and E are guaranteed to hit during R’s knockup, so you need not worry about them being dodged. Activating W immediately after R empowers the attack between abilities without wasting an attack opportunity, and one full combo can finish off a squishy target.
notes.malphite-skill-armor-scaling: For Malphite, armor increases damage as well as defense: both W and E scale with it. W’s passive raises his armor, with a much larger bonus while Granite Shield is active. An armor item therefore improves both survivability and damage, making it costly to leave armor out of any build entirely.
notes.malphite-skill-passive: Granite Shield regenerates only after Malphite goes without taking damage for a while, so start trades with it charged and back off to recharge it once it breaks. Higher armor makes physical attacks deplete the shield more slowly, letting the two reinforce each other; against melee opponents, use the shield to absorb their first basic attack as you approach. Ranged poke can repeatedly interrupt its regeneration, so you need another way to sustain in lane.
notes.malphite-skill-e: E Ground Slam deals area damage and reduces the attack speed of enemies it hits, making it especially effective against opponents who rely on basic attacks. Use it just after an enemy marksman or basic attack-focused duelist starts attacking to reduce their damage throughout the fight. Save it for a target you intend to fight instead of spending it on cooldown to farm.
notes.malphite-skill-r-utility: R Unstoppable Force makes Malphite unstoppable during the cast, ignoring most crowd control as he dashes to the target location. Alongside engaging, you can use it to escape a gank or pass through an incoming skillshot. Its long cooldown leaves you without a way to start a fight while it is unavailable, so decide in advance whether to spend it on escape or save it for an engage. Ability haste lets you poke with Q and use R more often.
notes.malphite-phase: Malphite is weakest before level 6: without R, he has little way to kill an opponent, and limited mana restricts his poke. His power spikes immediately after learning R and peaks again in the mid game with two or three armor items. As his damage contribution falls off late, focus on starting teamfights with R.
notes.malphite-situational-armor: When the enemy’s main damage is physical, stack armor heavily: it improves survivability and boosts W and E damage, so none of the stat goes to waste. Buy Glacial Buckler early, then build Plated Steelcaps, Thornmail, Frozen Heart, and Randuin’s Omen to make it extremely difficult for physical damage dealers to break through Malphite. If the enemy has plenty of healing, finish Thornmail first to apply Grievous Wounds.
notes.malphite-situational-mr: When the enemy’s main damage is magic, Malphite’s low base magic resistance means an armor-only build will leave him vulnerable. Hollow Radiance provides magic resistance while preserving his ability to farm; choose Spirit Visage if allies provide healing or shields, or Force of Nature if several enemies deal magic damage. Keep at least one armor item, since building only magic resistance sacrifices W and E damage.
notes.malphite-situational-ap: Choose an ability power build when your team already has a frontline tank and the enemy backline is squishy. R’s high ability power scaling lets Malphite eliminate the backline in one cast; Rylai’s Crystal Scepter helps keep enemies close afterward, while Rabadon’s Deathcap and Void Staff raise R’s damage further. Zhonya’s Hourglass provides both ability power and armor and buys time for allies to join you after you engage, making it especially well suited to this build. Liandry’s Torment can apply damage over time to multiple enemies through R’s area effect. This build gives up tankiness, so avoid it if your team has no other frontline.
notes.malphite-laning: In lane, poke with Q, then back off long enough to recharge Granite Shield. Q steals your opponent’s movement speed, making it harder for them to follow after the poke, while the restored shield keeps trades in Malphite’s favor. This cycle stops when you run out of mana, so at low Q ranks, time casts around a source of mana restoration instead of using Q on cooldown. Because Malphite struggles to gain a lead through kills in lane, push the wave and chip away at the turret to turn an advantage into lasting gains.
notes.malphite-teamfight: Teamfights hinge on where Malphite lands R. Engage only when it is available, looking to knock up at least two grouped enemies or eliminate a key damage dealer who steps out alone. If your allies have area-of-effect ultimates, coordinate their timing with R so they can hit the knockup location instead of chasing a kill on your own.
notes.vs-malphite-r: Malphite’s R is an unstoppable dash that crowd control cannot interrupt, so avoid giving him an opening. It can come from an unwarded bush or behind a wall; while you do not know where he is, avoid standing close to allies near lanes or objectives.
notes.vs-malphite-early: Take lane control and arrange a jungle gank before Malphite reaches level 6, while he has no R, little way to kill an opponent, and limited mana. Delaying his scaling during this window is most effective; once he has R and armor items, he becomes harder to beat one-on-one.
notes.vs-malphite-passive: Malphite can swing trades in his favor by keeping Granite Shield ready. Break it before starting your combo so you damage his health, then use damage over time or frequent poke to prevent it from regenerating and sharply reduce his lane sustain. If his Q hits you, it steals your movement speed, making it hard to engage or retreat, so avoid starting a trade immediately afterward. Q is targeted, so hiding behind minions will not stop it; avoid lingering within its range.
notes.vs-malphite-e: E Ground Slam cuts the damage output of champions who rely on basic attacks by reducing their attack speed. If you play one of those champions, stay behind your allies and keep your distance outside E’s range when fighting Malphite, then move in and deal damage after he uses it.
notes.vs-malphite-grouping: Malphite’s R knocks up multiple enemies around the end of his dash. Spread out before a teamfight so even a well-placed R catches only one person, then counterattack hard immediately after he uses it, when his team is weakest.
notes.malzahar-combo-basic: For a basic trade, apply E, summon Voidlings with W, then use Q to silence the target and refresh E. Both Q and R reset E’s duration when they hit an affected target, so following that order keeps E dealing damage as the enemy retreats. If you use Q before applying E, you have no way to refresh it and deal less than half the damage.
notes.malzahar-combo-ult: To secure a kill, apply E, summon Voidlings with W, then suppress the target with R. R refreshes E, so it keeps dealing damage after the suppression ends while the Voidlings attack throughout it. R’s zone remains around the target, so cast it from a position that forces the enemy toward your team.
notes.malzahar-skill-w: W gains a stack each time you use another ability, and more stacks summon more Voidlings. Use it once you have prepared for the fight: build stacks with Q and E, then summon the Voidlings as the enemy enters range. Casting W early with nothing nearby to attack only wastes their duration.
notes.malzahar-skill-passive: Void Shift returns after Malzahar goes without taking damage for a while. While active, it greatly reduces incoming damage and makes him immune to immobilization and interruptions, so avoiding poke is itself a form of defense. Check whether it is active in lane as often as you check your health; even minor damage from minions or jungle monsters can remove it and leave you vulnerable to the next gank.
notes.malzahar-skill-q: Q (Call of the Void) creates two portals, and its hit area is the line segment between them rather than a line from Malzahar to his target. Place it across the enemy’s path to land it. Because its silence can interrupt an ability as the enemy begins to cast it, save Q against champions with engage abilities to stop their entry rather than deal damage.
notes.malzahar-skill-e: When a target affected by Malefic Visions (E) dies, E spreads to the nearest enemy and restores mana to Malzahar. Early on, apply it to a minion to clear the wave through successive spreads while recovering mana. The wave pushes toward the enemy as E spreads, though, so pushing blindly without vision leaves you open to a gank.
notes.malzahar-skill-w-wave: Voidlings deal much more damage to lane minions affected by E. Apply E to the wave before using W to clear it noticeably faster and secure last hits more reliably. This also gives you time to roam or work on objectives after pushing the lane.
notes.malzahar-skill-r: Nether Grasp (R) suppresses its target, preventing movement, abilities, and basic attacks; most escape abilities cannot break free. Malzahar must maintain the cast, however, and immobilizing crowd control on him ends the suppression early. Cast R where your teammates can protect you, after the enemy’s follow-up engage has ended.
notes.malzahar-laning: Malzahar’s goal in lane is to avoid losing while keeping his opponent tied to it. Continually pushing with E and W forces the enemy mid laner back to farm and gives you time for objectives or vision. His range is short, so don’t step forward to harass.
notes.malzahar-laning-defense: Malzahar has no mobility ability and short range. Against ranged poke champions, keeping Void Shift active is worth giving up a few CS; against melee engage champions, save Q’s silence for the moment they go in. In either matchup, using your abilities first in lane puts you at a disadvantage.
notes.malzahar-phase: Malzahar is weak at levels 1–2, when he has to get by with just one ability. Leveling E makes farming more reliable, and gaining R at level 6 sharply increases his ability to kill an enemy alone. His impact in fights then depends heavily on R’s cooldown, so don’t force a fight after using it.
notes.malzahar-teamfight: In a teamfight, Malzahar’s job is to take one key enemy out of the fight. If the enemy carry is out of reach, use R (Nether Grasp) on an engaging champion to stop the engage instead. Summon Voidlings before the fight and save Q for the moment the enemy casts an engage ability. With R available, you can defend a side lane alone if you have vision, since the enemy will need to send two champions.
notes.malzahar-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early against an assassin who can engage instantly. Once Void Shift breaks, Malzahar has no way to escape, so he needs Zhonya’s to avoid the engage while waiting for his team.
notes.malzahar-situational-antiheal: Against champions with strong healing, fit Morellonomicon into your core item order. Malzahar’s sustained damage from E and Voidlings can keep Grievous Wounds applied continuously.
notes.vs-malzahar-e: Don’t stand near a minion affected by E (Malefic Visions): when it dies, E moves to the nearest enemy, so trying to last hit beside the wave can leave you taking unwanted damage repeatedly. If Malzahar applies E to the wave, step back and wait for the minions to be cleared.
notes.vs-malzahar-passive: Once Void Shift is removed, crowd control and burst damage become effective.
notes.vs-malzahar-r: Mobility abilities and shields cannot break R’s suppression. Remove it with Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar; without either item, your only option is for an ally to immobilize Malzahar and interrupt his cast. When his R is available, don’t walk alone through areas without vision.
notes.vs-malzahar-w: Malzahar is much more dangerous while his Voidlings are active. Close in when they have disappeared or have yet to be summoned; if they are already out, clear them with an area ability before engaging.
notes.vs-malzahar-q: Q (Call of the Void) hits along the line segment between Malzahar’s two portals. Sidestepping can keep you inside that line, so move toward the outside of a portal to escape quickly. Since the silence prevents you from using your engage ability, delay its cast when you see Q being cast.
notes.vs-malzahar-gank: Malzahar pushes the lane quickly, but he has no mobility ability and a short range. Call for a gank while he is pushing; Void Shift is his only response, so going in after removing it makes the gank highly likely to succeed. It is much easier to kill him with your jungler than to try to beat him in lane.
notes.maokai-combo-q-direction: Q knocks nearby enemies outward from Maokai. To push an enemy toward your team, use W to pass through them, land on the far side, then cast Q. To peel an enemy off your carry, stand between the two and cast Q instead. That positioning is what lets the same ability serve as either an engage or protection.
notes.maokai-combo-ult: R's root lasts longer the farther its wall travels, so casting it right in an enemy's face gives only a brief root; start as far away as possible to let the wall travel. Hitting an enemy champion with the wall also grants Maokai movement speed, letting him follow R immediately with W.
notes.maokai-skill-passive: Using an ability or being hit by an enemy champion's ability reduces the cooldown of Sap Magic's heal, so it becomes available more often as a fight intensifies. That healing helps Maokai withstand focused attacks: in teamfights, keep landing basic attacks whenever a target is available instead of backing away. In lane, it is his only way to regain health without spending mana, so use the empowered attack even on a minion to keep the heal cycling.
notes.maokai-skill-w: Maokai cannot be targeted while casting W, making it both an engage tool and a way to dodge targeted abilities and basic attacks. Casting it just as an enemy’s targeted finishing ability arrives negates that ability, so save W to close in while dodging a key ability instead of spending it on a blind engage.
notes.maokai-skill-e-brush: Saplings thrown into brush last longer and produce much larger explosions. Stacking several in one spot is inefficient, so place them one at a time along separate routes. Even a single sapling where enemies must pass, such as river brush or the tri-brush, provides vision and deters an approach.
notes.maokai-skill-e-cooldown: When a sapling hits an enemy champion or epic monster, it further reduces Sap Magic’s healing cooldown. Place saplings along the enemy’s approach just before an objective fight: they provide vision, hinder the enemy’s entry, and let Maokai heal more often. Using them only as vision wards misses that value.
notes.maokai-laning: In bot lane, start by controlling the brush: place saplings with E in both bushes to keep the enemy bot lane from using them. When an enemy steps forward to last-hit, root them with W so your ADC can add basic attacks. Maokai lacks the damage to engage alone, so use W only when your ADC is in range to attack. Q costs a lot of mana; wasting it to clear minions can leave it unavailable when you need to counter an enemy engage.
notes.maokai-laning-wave: Don’t force the wave to push. Maokai’s trades depend on holding enemies in place for an allied damage dealer, and the closer the wave is to your side, the easier it is to get out after engaging with W. If you push near the enemy turret and engage with W, you have no way back once the root ends.
notes.maokai-phase: Level 2, when both Q and W become available, is your first chance to trade. At level 6, R gives you a way to force engages and take control of roams and objective fights. Later, health items increase both sapling explosion damage and Maokai's durability, so he can keep filling the engage role as the game goes on.
notes.maokai-teamfight-ult: Casting R head-on gives enemies time to see it and retreat, so use it from the side or behind, or when they enter a narrow passage with nowhere to dodge. If you can choose where to fight, a spot with walls on both sides, such as the entrance to the dragon or Baron pit, can change how many enemies R hits.
notes.maokai-teamfight-peel: When an engage is unfavorable, switch to protecting your carry. Stand beside them; as an enemy reaches them, knock the attacker away with Q, then root them with W to leave them isolated. Maokai deals little damage, so protecting the space your carry needs is always more valuable than chasing one enemy.
notes.maokai-situational-mikael: If the enemy can immobilize and kill your carry, buy Mikael's Blessing before Locket of the Iron Solari. Maokai can stop an engage, but he has no way to remove crowd control once it has affected an ally.
notes.maokai-situational-armor: If the enemy's damage is mostly physical, choose Dead Man's Plate or Thornmail to survive longer and get more use from Sap Magic's heal.
notes.vs-maokai-sapling: A sapling chases the first enemy that comes close, then explodes after a few seconds or when it collides with another enemy. Saplings planted in brush have much larger explosions, so take care when entering brush. If one is chasing you, lead it away from your team toward minions or monsters to make it explode.
notes.vs-maokai-passive: The more abilities you hit Maokai with, the sooner Sap Magic's heal comes back, so repeatedly poking him can help him heal more often. Use your abilities on the enemy carry instead; ignore Maokai or deal with him using basic attacks.
notes.vs-maokai-w: Maokai cannot be targeted while dashing with W, so targeted abilities and basic attacks used during the dash are wasted. Use those abilities after he lands, or wait until W is down to trade.
notes.vs-maokai-ult: The farther R's wall travels, the longer its root lasts, so taking a wall from long range head-on results in the longest root. When you see it, move perpendicular to its path or cross it while it has traveled only a short distance. Narrow passages leave no room to dodge, so fight Maokai's team in open terrain.
notes.vs-maokai-cooldown: Maokai's threat comes from W and R. Once you make him use W without effect, he has no way to close in or force a play in lane; step forward and trade immediately. When W is ready, stay out of its range near brush.
notes.maokai-combo-engage: The basic engage is W → basic attack → Q: close in and root the enemy with W, land a Sap Magic-empowered basic attack during the root to restore health, then finish with Q. Keep that order, since using Q first knocks the enemy back and creates distance.
notes.masteryi-combo-basic: For a standard engage, activate E (Wuju Style), add R (Highlander) if needed, then enter with Q (Alpha Strike) and follow up with basic attacks. E and R do not lose duration during Q or W (Meditate), so activating them before you engage costs nothing; waiting until after Q to activate E delays your basic attacks.
notes.masteryi-combo-q-dodge: Master Yi cannot be targeted while casting Q (Alpha Strike), so use it as targeted crowd control or a finishing blow comes in. Against an enemy with guaranteed crowd control, walk in and save Q to dodge it; using Q only to engage gives up that option.
notes.masteryi-combo-q-cd: Each basic attack reduces Q (Alpha Strike)’s cooldown, even when it hits a jungle monster, so hit a camp before a fight or objective to bring Q back sooner. With no other targets nearby, Q repeatedly hits the same enemy for maximum single-target damage; in a 1v1, draw the enemy away from minions and monsters.
notes.masteryi-combo-w: W (Meditate) restores health and reduces damage taken, so activate it as the enemy’s burst damage lands. Double Strike stacks build during the channel, making the basic attack immediately afterward stronger, while E and R durations pause. Immobilizing crowd control interrupts W, so use it after the enemy has spent that crowd control.
notes.masteryi-skill-passive: Double Strike makes a basic attack hit twice after a set number of attacks. Its stacks persist when you switch targets, letting you build them on jungle monsters or minions before attacking a champion. They also build during W (Meditate)’s channel, making the first basic attack after it ends especially strong.
notes.masteryi-skill-e: E (Wuju Style) adds true damage to basic attacks. Armor does not reduce that damage, so it accounts for more of your damage against enemies who build defensive stats. Its duration pauses during Q and W, allowing you to activate it before engaging, but because it lasts only a short time, wait until you have a target.
notes.masteryi-skill-r: R (Highlander) increases movement and attack speed and makes Master Yi immune to slows, letting him close the gap against enemies who rely on slows to keep their distance. A takedown extends R and greatly reduces basic ability cooldowns, so activate it when you can secure a kill and carry that momentum to the next target. Using it before an opening appears leaves you with nothing.
notes.masteryi-jungle-clear: Master Yi’s early game is for clearing the jungle. Q (Alpha Strike) deals bonus damage to monsters, basic attacks reduce its cooldown, and his movement speed is among the highest of all champions, saving time between camps. Use that clearing speed to build a growth lead rather than chase kills early.
notes.masteryi-jungle-gank: Master Yi has no crowd control, so gank only when an ally has already applied crowd control or the enemy has spent their mobility and escape abilities. Otherwise, steal enemy jungle camps or prepare an objective. In games with frequent fights, plan your route around the long stretches when you cannot help lanes.
notes.masteryi-jungle-counter: Avoid meeting the enemy jungler head-on. Early on, Master Yi has only basic attacks to fight with, making him easy for junglers with crowd control to catch. Attempt to counterjungle only after securing vision and confirming that the enemy jungler is at camps on the opposite side.
notes.masteryi-phase: From level 1 until you learn R (Highlander), focus on farming; fights are usually unfavorable. Once you have R, takedowns bring your abilities back sooner and let you snowball. Master Yi peaks in the mid to late game with at least two items providing attack speed and penetration, then weakens again when the enemy has both crowd control and defensive items.
notes.masteryi-teamfight: Do not engage first in teamfights. Wait out of vision until the enemy has used its immobilizing crowd control on your allies, then use Q (Alpha Strike) to reach the backline. Take down the first target, use R (Highlander)’s takedown effect to bring Q back, and move to the next; if you fail to secure that first takedown, you die. Pressuring a side lane and waiting for the enemy to split makes this opening easier to find than a head-on standoff at an objective.
notes.masteryi-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Master Yi’s repeated basic attacks keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.masteryi-situational-qss: If the enemy has several sources of guaranteed crowd control, consider buying Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar before damage items. Master Yi cannot act while locked down, and Q (Alpha Strike)’s untargetability cannot remove crowd control that has already landed.
notes.vs-masteryi-q: Master Yi cannot be targeted during Q (Alpha Strike), so targeted crowd control or a finishing blow used then is wasted. Wait until Q ends and he lands before using it; reflexively pressing an ability as soon as he engages is the biggest mistake.
notes.vs-masteryi-w: W (Meditate) is a channel that immobilizing crowd control can interrupt. Save one of your team’s crowd control abilities for the moment Master Yi activates it: a stun, root, or knockup will stop both its healing and damage reduction.
notes.vs-masteryi-r: Slows do not affect Master Yi during R (Highlander), making kiting to create distance with slows useless while it lasts. Stop him with immobilizing crowd control or a movement ability, or escape around terrain. Only a takedown extends R, so it expires on its own if nobody dies.
notes.vs-masteryi-reset: A takedown greatly reduces Master Yi’s basic ability cooldowns, letting him reach the next target immediately. Above all, avoid leaving an ally isolated in a teamfight. Stay grouped and layer crowd control to catch him on his first engage.
notes.vs-masteryi-truedamage: Master Yi’s basic attacks deal some true damage while E (Wuju Style) is active, making armor alone less effective than you might expect. Build health alongside crowd control and ways to keep him from closing in.
notes.vs-masteryi-early: Early on, Master Yi is weak in the jungle and has very little gank potential, so you can fight him if you meet him in his jungle. Secure early objectives quickly to slow his growth, and press your early advantage rather than delaying it: he grows stronger as the game goes on.
notes.mel-combo-basic: Land E's root, place Q on the rooted target, then auto; use R if you have enough Overwhelm. Q continues exploding after its first blast, so the target must remain in place to take every hit. Confirm the root before casting Q instead of trying to land E afterward.
notes.mel-combo-passive: Each ability adds extra projectiles to your next auto, and casting several abilities in a row can load that single auto to the maximum. Use your abilities first, then weave in an auto at the end of the combo so the stored projectiles do not go to waste.
notes.mel-combo-execute: Ability and auto damage both stack Overwhelm, with no stack limit. Once its stored damage exceeds the target's remaining health plus shields, your next attack executes them. A shield raises that threshold, so attack just after it breaks or expires.
notes.mel-skill-q: Q is a targeted bombardment that pays off when the opponent has reason to stay in its blast area: while rooted, among minions for a last hit, or trapped in a narrow passage. In lane, use it regularly to clear the wave and harass at the same time.
notes.mel-skill-w-mana: Leveling W reduces both its cooldown and mana cost, but the statistically preferred skill order maxes it last, leaving it costly and slow to recharge throughout lane. Save it for a reflection in the early and mid game; once mana is no longer a concern later on, you can use it more freely for defense.
notes.mel-skill-e: E roots only targets hit by the center of its orb; the surrounding area slows and deals damage over time. Even if the root misses, the area lingers briefly and can cut off an opponent’s path. Its reduced damage to minions makes it inefficient for waveclear, so do not use it to farm.
notes.mel-skill-r: R hits every enemy with Overwhelm regardless of distance, letting you finish fights in other lanes or around objectives when you have vision. Enemy champions must still have Overwhelm when you cast it, but if you can add another stack before they expire, wait for the extra damage. Learning R also increases Overwhelm's damage, bringing targets to the execute threshold sooner.
notes.mel-laning: Mel's long range and Q waveclear make it easy for her to gain lane priority. Stand behind your minion wave so melee opponents have farther to travel to reach you.
notes.mel-laning-trade: In trades, stack Overwhelm with Q and push the opponent back, then land E as they approach. Save E from early harass so you can stop the opponent's engage.
notes.mel-phase: Mel is weakest at levels 1–2: high mana costs prevent constant ability use, and W has a long cooldown. At level 6, R increases Overwhelm's damage and gives her a long-range finisher, enabling roams and involvement in distant fights. Her win rate is low with only one core item but rises sharply as she completes her core build, so play safely early and wait for those items.
notes.mel-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the back and cast Q into grouped enemies to apply Overwhelm to several at once. Use W the moment an enemy engage ability comes toward you; if you miss that chance, do not step forward. Wait to cast R until enemies have lost health and several have Overwhelm stacks so it can finish multiple targets together.
notes.mel-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier in your core build. W only reflects projectiles, so dashes and targeted engages still reach Mel; with armor among the lowest, she cannot rely on W once caught.
notes.mel-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps raising the execute threshold, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Overwhelm checks stored damage against the target's remaining health plus shields, so cutting healing helps bring them into execute range.
notes.vs-mel-w-reflect: Mel's W reflects projectiles for a brief moment. If she looks ready to use it, bait it out with a low-value ability or auto before casting your main skillshot, or it may be reflected back at you. Dashes, targeted abilities, and area effects already on the ground cannot be reflected, so use those first if you have them.
notes.vs-mel-passive: Every hit from Mel adds Overwhelm stacks. If their stored damage exceeds your remaining health plus shields, her next attack executes you, so having more than half your health is no guarantee of safety after repeated hits. If you have taken several hits of harass, back off based on how many times she has hit you rather than the number on your health bar.
notes.vs-mel-e: Mel's E roots at the center of its orb but only slows at the edges, so sidestep the center instead of moving straight back. A root sets up an immediate Q barrage; save a movement ability or cleanse for that moment.
notes.vs-mel-r: Mel's R has no range limit: if Overwhelm stacks remain on you, she can finish you from across the map. After leaving a fight, wait somewhere safe until the stacks expire, and avoid walking near an objective while low on health.
notes.vs-mel-early: Mel has armor among the lowest and no movement ability, so a melee champion or one with a dash can gain an advantage by closing the distance in lane. Her win rate is low before she completes her core items; pressure her early to delay that point.
notes.mel-skill-w: W is chiefly for reflecting projectiles, not for its shield. Its window is brief, so time it as an enemy skillshot projectile approaches, ideally a key ability: reflected damage uses the original caster's stats. It cannot reflect dashes or area effects already on the ground. Missing the timing leaves you vulnerable through its long cooldown, so pick one enemy grab ability to watch for and reflect.
notes.milio-skill-q-aim: Q knocks back the first enemy it hits, then bounces up and explodes at that spot. Because the knockback lands in a different place from the area damage and slow, aim differently when peeling an enemy off an ally than when slowing a clustered group. Hitting a champion refunds some mana, greatly reducing Q’s effective cost.
notes.milio-skill-q-peel: Q is Milio’s only displacement tool, so save it to peel an engaging enemy off your allied marksman instead of spending it on lane poke. Without Q, Milio has no way to stop an enemy who engages.
notes.milio-skill-w-follow: W follows the ally closest to where it is cast. It does not target an ally directly, so place it on the ground near the ally you want it to follow; if it attaches to the wrong one, recast it to switch. Recast it immediately during a teamfight if that ally retreats or falls.
notes.milio-skill-w-timing: W’s real value is its attack range increase, not its healing. Cast it as your allied marksman starts attacking the enemy frontline to get the full range benefit; using it early just to heal missing health leaves that range unavailable when the fight starts.
notes.milio-skill-e-charges: E has two charges that stack on the same target. Use both on one ally for a larger shield, or split them between two allies to give each movement speed. If a fight is coming, keep one charge ready: spending both at once leaves you unable to protect allies until E recharges.
notes.milio-skill-e-speed: E’s movement speed boost is used more often than its shield. Apply it before an ally roams, moves toward an objective, or dodges an enemy skillshot to give them more options. It is more valuable before they get hit than afterward.
notes.milio-skill-passive: Milio’s passive adds bonus damage to the next attack of an ally touched by one of his abilities. Apply E just before a trade to increase that ally’s damage; W reapplies the passive at regular intervals while it lasts. As a rule, start lane trades by using an ability on an ally.
notes.milio-skill-r: R heals allies in an area, cleanses immobilizing effects, and grants tenacity. It cannot cleanse airborne effects, so do not hold it to remove knockbacks or knockups. Time it for when several allies are immobilized, but do not sit on it until the last moment when there is nothing to cleanse: the healing alone is valuable.
notes.milio-combo-trade: In lane, cast E on an ally, let their basic attack trigger the passive, then use Q to knock the enemy back if they counterattack and close in. Opening with Q pushes the enemy out of your ally’s attack range and ends the trade, so use it to finish the exchange rather than start it.
notes.milio-laning: Against a hard engage opponent, move forward only after securing vision of the brush.
notes.milio-laning-early: Once E can hold two charges in the early levels, your allies become noticeably better at weathering poke. When the enemy support steps up to harass, absorb it with E and maintain the wave; take a head-on fight only while W is active and giving your allies a range advantage.
notes.milio-phase: Milio ranks near the bottom in both early kill participation and damage. Focus on keeping allies alive instead of starting fights early; his shields and healing grow as he gains items. He is strongest in late teamfights where his allied marksman can keep attacking from within range, making an unnecessary early death especially costly.
notes.milio-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your team’s main damage dealer, extend their range with W, and spread E among allies. R is available only once, so use it right after enemy area crowd control lands, and reserve Q for champions who engage on your allies. Plan your ability sequence ahead of time or you will be too late during the fight.
notes.milio-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of sustained crowd control, fit Mikael's Blessing between core items for a cleanse besides R.
notes.vs-milio-focus: Use an engage ability to catch Milio first and cut off the enemy team's sustain.
notes.vs-milio-q: Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back the first enemy it hits and is Milio’s only escape tool. Once he has used it, you can close in on him, so check whether Q is down before deciding to engage.
notes.vs-milio-w: W, Cozy Campfire, increases allies’ attack range. If the enemy marksman suddenly starts attacking from farther away, W is active; delay the frontline fight and let its duration run out.
notes.vs-milio-r: R, Breath of Life, cleanses immobilizing effects but cannot remove airborne effects. If your composition has airborne crowd control, you can still find an opening to engage even while Milio has R available.
notes.vs-milio-early: Milio’s composition grows stronger over time. During the early laning phase, the most reliable response is to drain his mana through poke and take control of the wave. If his healing starts to become a problem, get healing reduction sooner.
notes.missfortune-combo-lovetap: Love Tap triggers only when you basic attack a target different from the previous one. In lane, harass by alternating basic attacks from a minion to the enemy champion and back to a minion; repeatedly attacking the same target greatly reduces your harass damage.
notes.missfortune-combo-q-bounce: Use Q Double Up on a front minion to bounce it onto the champion behind it. If Q kills the first target, the bounce always critically strikes the second, so targeting a low-health minion greatly increases your harass damage.
notes.missfortune-combo-teamfight: Start a fight by slowing and holding the enemy formation with E Make It Rain, then pour R Bullet Time into them. If an ally’s area crowd control lands first, save E and start R immediately to give yourself time to channel it.
notes.missfortune-skill-passive: Each Love Tap trigger reduces the cooldown of W Strut. Alternating attacks between minions and champions in lane keeps W coming back, so if it is still on cooldown, try hitting a different target once.
