notes.missfortune-skill-q: Q Double Up is targeted, so it cannot miss, but its high mana cost will leave you out of mana by the middle of the laning phase if you use it too often. Casting it on a minion without an angle to bounce onto a champion only pushes the lane, so wait until the enemy champion stands behind a minion.
notes.missfortune-skill-w: W Strut’s movement speed reaches its maximum only after you spend time without taking damage. Miss Fortune’s base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions, making this bonus vital for surviving and roaming; activate W for trades that need attack speed or when taking down a turret, rather than to escape.
notes.missfortune-skill-e: E Make It Rain is more valuable for its slow and vision than its damage. Use it to stop an enemy engage, reveal a brush, or block an escape route; placing it on the enemy’s approach just before a teamfight can discourage them from engaging altogether.
notes.missfortune-skill-r: If R Bullet Time’s channel is interrupted, all remaining waves are lost. Cast it only when at least one condition is met: you are at the edge of its range, you have a wall or brush behind you, or an ally has just landed crowd control. Its cone direction locks when you cast it, so aim along the line that will catch the most enemies before they spread out.
notes.missfortune-phase: Miss Fortune is an early-game marksman who can gain a harass advantage from level 1 with Love Tap and Q Double Up. Once she learns R Bullet Time at level 6, a single crowd control effect from her support can create a kill opportunity. Later, her lack of a dash and average range make it hard to position alone, so use the lead built in the early and mid game to end the match.
notes.missfortune-laning-wave: Harassing with Q Double Up inevitably pushes the lane toward the enemy, leaving you open to ganks if you keep pushing without knowing the enemy jungler’s path. Without vision, save Q and harass only with Love Tap basic attacks. If you intend to push, clear the minions quickly with Q, then use W Strut’s movement speed to get river vision or recall.
notes.missfortune-laning-roam: Miss Fortune can return from base and rejoin the lane faster than other marksmen because W Strut’s movement speed reaches its maximum as she walks without taking damage. After pushing the enemy out of lane, look for chances to move toward mid or an objective.
notes.missfortune-teamfight: In teamfights, deal area damage from the back line. Once your team has absorbed the enemy engage, cast R Bullet Time when the enemies group up in one direction; using it before their formation overlaps can scatter them and sharply reduce its damage. When R is unavailable, use E Make It Rain to discourage engages and rely on basic attacks to get through the fight.
notes.missfortune-situational-antiheal: If an enemy champion has healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Each hit of R Bullet Time reapplies the effect, making the item especially effective on Miss Fortune.
notes.missfortune-situational-qss: If enemy stuns keep interrupting R Bullet Time, buy Quicksilver Sash before other defensive items. Miss Fortune’s teamfight impact depends heavily on completing the channel.
notes.vs-missfortune-q: Q Double Up hits a front target, then bounces to one behind it, so standing directly behind a lane minion exposes you to free harass. Stand to the side, out of line with the minion, to avoid the bounce.
notes.vs-missfortune-r: R Bullet Time is channeled, and a single crowd control effect can interrupt it and cancel all remaining waves. If you have no crowd control, use a wall or brush to break vision or move out through the side of the cone. Its direction locks when cast, making a sideways escape better than retreating straight back.
notes.vs-missfortune-w: Taking damage resets Miss Fortune’s W Strut movement speed bonus, so a single hit can slow her enough to catch her as she flees. Save damage-over-time or long-range abilities for the chase.
notes.vs-missfortune-mobility: Miss Fortune has no mobility ability, and her base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions. If your champion has an engage ability, get onto her after level 6 and try to kill her; if you cannot reach her, use vision to deny her an attack angle instead of fighting over range.
notes.vs-missfortune-e: Avoid starting a fight inside E Make It Rain. Its slow delays both engaging and disengaging, and R Bullet Time layered over it can deal heavy damage. When E is placed, delay your engage and lure the enemy out of its area.
notes.wukong-combo-eq: Dash in with E (Nimbus Strike) and buffer Q (Crushing Blow) during the dash. Because Q empowers your next basic attack, activating it before you arrive lets the attack land immediately; waiting until you arrive delays it.
notes.wukong-combo-rw: Use W Warrior Trickster immediately after starting R Cyclone. The clone will mimic Cyclone, while Wukong can retreat invisibly and avoid the enemy’s counterattack.
notes.wukong-combo-r-flash: Wukong can move during R (Cyclone), so Flash into the middle of the enemy team while spinning to make up for its short range. Reach them before they spread out to knock up multiple enemies at once.
notes.wukong-skill-r: R (Cyclone) increases your movement speed while spinning, so walk into grouped enemies instead of standing still. You can cast it again before it goes on cooldown: use the first cast to signal your team to engage and the second to finish enemies or hinder their escape. Stuns and roots interrupt it, so wait until the enemy’s main crowd control has been used.
notes.wukong-skill-w: W (Warrior Trickster) is a short dash that briefly makes you invisible and leaves a stationary clone where you cast it. Save it after engaging so you can draw targeted abilities toward the clone or disappear from sight and disguise your direction. Turrets and true sight reveal you while invisible.
notes.wukong-skill-q: Q (Crushing Blow) is a longer-range empowered basic attack that reduces the target’s armor, increasing your allies’ physical damage too. Each attack by Wukong or his clone reduces Q’s cooldown, making it available more often in extended fights, so save it for champion fights instead of spending it on a wave or camp beforehand.
notes.wukong-skill-passive: Each hit on a champion or jungle monster builds a stack of P (Stone Skin), increasing both armor and healing. Hit a nearby jungle monster a few times just before a fight to start with those stacks, and remember that clone attacks build them too.
notes.wukong-skill-e: E (Nimbus Strike) is a targeted dash that enemies cannot dodge, but its short range means you must first find an opening to get close. As Wukong’s only way to engage, save it while the enemy’s mobility ability is available, then follow up immediately with basic attacks to use the attack speed gained on arrival.
notes.wukong-phase: Wukong’s early clear speed and damage per minute are average, and he is especially vulnerable to magic damage. Build an advantage through early ganks; his strongest points come when he gains R Cyclone at level 6 and when he completes his first core item in the mid game.
notes.wukong-jungle-path: Move between jungle camps without letting your P (Stone Skin) stacks expire to clear faster. Although R (Cyclone) deals heavy damage to camps, its long cooldown means using it to clear can cost you the next fight, so save it for combat.
notes.wukong-objective: Decide whether to start an objective fight based on whether R (Cyclone) is available. Without it, Wukong struggles to engage or disengage, so secure vision and retreat; once it is ready again, force the objective fight.
notes.wukong-teamfight: In teamfights, wait for an opening to land R (Cyclone). When two or more enemies overlap, close in with E (Nimbus Strike) and spin, timing your engage with your team’s crowd control so you do not arrive late and get picked off alone.
notes.wukong-teamfight-clone: Enemies have a hard time distinguishing Wukong’s W (Warrior Trickster) clone from the real Wukong. Using it in a teamfight buys time while they attack the clone, letting you circle around the side and enter their backline. Near death, use W as a last resort to escape while deceiving them.
notes.vs-wukong-clone: W (Warrior Trickster) leaves a clone in place while the real Wukong turns invisible and retreats in another direction. When the clone appears, check where Wukong is likely to go instead of mistaking it for him and spending your abilities on it; the clone stays in place, which helps you identify it.
notes.vs-wukong-r: R (Cyclone) knocks up multiple enemies at once and deals damage based on maximum health. Spread out while Wukong’s R is available, and leave enough room to retreat from both its second cast and the clone that copies it.
notes.vs-wukong-e: E (Nimbus Strike) is a targeted dash, so it cannot be dodged; staying outside its range is the way to prevent Wukong from engaging. Once he closes in, Q (Crushing Blow) reduces your armor and makes subsequent trades unfavorable.
notes.vs-wukong-passive: Each hit on a champion or jungle monster builds Wukong’s P (Stone Skin) stacks, increasing his armor and healing. He gains the advantage the longer a close fight lasts, so take repeated short trades and disengage instead of committing to an extended duel.
notes.vs-wukong-mr: Wukong’s base magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions. If you play a champion that deals primarily magic damage, you can gain a substantial lead in early trades, so fight back aggressively when he closes in.
notes.vs-wukong-r-window: Wukong has a harder time engaging and disengaging without R (Cyclone), so force an objective or a fight immediately after he uses it. If he disappears from vision while R is available, spread out your grouped formation first.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-basic: For a basic trade, pull the enemy in with E to close the gap, land Q on them alone, then weave in basic attacks. Q deals much more damage to a single target, so aim from an angle that avoids minions; without E first, the enemy can walk out of Q range.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-passive: The passive aura activates after three ability or basic attack hits on an enemy champion or jungle monster, with each basic attack counting as one hit. Weave a basic attack between E and Q instead of relying only on abilities to activate it in time; once active, the aura also grants movement speed to keep the chase going.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-w: W stores damage dealt and taken, then converts it into a shield when activated. Using it at the start of a fight gives you a thin shield, so wait until you have exchanged damage, but use it before the stored amount decays after the fight. Recasting W restores health based on the remaining shield; if you expect no more incoming damage, convert it while the shield is still large.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-duel: R Realm of Death takes one target into another space and forces a one-on-one duel for its duration. Neither side's allies can intervene there, and Mordekaiser steals some of the target's key stats, giving him a chance to beat an opponent he could not defeat outside R.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-target: Choosing the right R target is central to playing Mordekaiser. Taking an enemy frontliner leaves your allies facing the remaining damage dealers, while taking a damage dealer leaves them facing only the frontline. Pick the most important enemy champion you can kill within R's duration, excluding high-health frontliners and opponents with instant-cast invulnerability who would survive the timer.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-defense: Protect your allies by taking an enemy diver into R as soon as they reach an allied damage dealer. Killing the target inside R lets you keep the stolen stats until they respawn.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-cast: R is a short-range targeted ability, so use it immediately after pulling an enemy in with E or close the gap with Flash before casting it. Commit it to a clear target instead of holding it until the chance to cast it is gone.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-e: E Death's Grasp grants magic penetration passively, even when you do not cast it, so do not delay putting points into it: each rank increases your overall damage. When cast, it pulls every enemy in its area, letting you group multiple opponents within Q and passive aura range in a teamfight.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-q: Q Obliterate deals much more damage when it hits only one target. In lane trades, angle it around minions to hit the enemy champion alone; when using it to clear a wave, account for losing that single-target bonus. Trying to trade and farm with the same Q compromises both.
notes.mordekaiser-phase: Look for trades from level 3, once you have both E and Q; at level 6, R creates a clear chance for a lane kill. This is not a statistically strong win-rate phase, so save R for a reliable opportunity instead of forcing an early dive. Later, R can remove only one enemy, making its impact heavily dependent on the opposing composition.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-melee: Against a melee opponent, start a trade with E as they step forward to last-hit. Stay close and weave in basic attacks until the passive aura activates, then keep up the pressure while it is active.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-ranged: Against a ranged opponent, avoid pushing the wave and farm safely with Q. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so forcing your way close will only cost you health. The most reliable chance to fight back is to pair your level 6 R with an allied jungler's gank.
notes.mordekaiser-teamfight: In teamfights, use E to group multiple enemies, activate the passive aura, and hold your ground among them. It is safer to cast R on a key opponent after they use their main abilities than immediately when the fight starts. Choose your entry position carefully: without a mobility ability, you cannot easily close the gap again after backing off.
notes.mordekaiser-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Morellonomicon. The passive aura's continuous damage makes its healing reduction easy to maintain, especially when you force a duel inside R.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-r: If Mordekaiser catches you in R Realm of Death, your allies cannot help for its duration. He also steals some of your stats, so you may lose a duel you would win outside it. Do not enter his R range alone while it is available.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-passive: Mordekaiser's passive aura requires three ability or basic attack hits to activate. Trade only one or two hits before backing off to avoid both its sustained damage and movement speed boost; once it activates, every moment spent close to him works against you.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-w: The more damage Mordekaiser deals and takes, the larger his W Indestructible shield becomes, and he can convert the remaining shield into health. Pouring damage into him immediately after he activates it can leave him with more shield to turn into healing, so focus your damage after the shield wears down or he converts it.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-e: E Death's Grasp pulls every enemy in its area at once. Standing in a narrow passage or clustered with allies in front of Mordekaiser lets him pull several of you into both Q and his passive aura, so spread out.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-mobility: Mordekaiser has no mobility ability and struggles to close gaps. Slows and good spacing let you fight outside E range, and if you force him to back off, he cannot easily get close again. Prioritize staying where he cannot catch you over dealing more damage.
notes.morgana-combo-basic: For a kill, land Q (Dark Binding), place W (Tormented Shadow) under the target, then use R (Soul Shackles). Time R’s stun to trigger as Q’s root ends, leaving no chance to escape; if Q misses, don’t reverse the order and lead with R, since the target can simply walk away.
notes.morgana-combo-r-flash: Flash into the enemy team immediately after casting R (Soul Shackles) to keep the chains connected and catch more enemies. The movement speed Morgana gains during R lets her push in after activating it.
notes.morgana-combo-r-survive: If Morgana dies before R (Soul Shackles) stuns, the chains break. Use Zhonya’s Hourglass to survive until the stun triggers; without a way to stay alive after activating R, use it only once an ally has already held the enemy in place.
notes.morgana-skill-q: Q (Dark Binding) roots only the first target it hits, so minions will block it. Fire along a clear line beside the wave or through a jungle entrance, rather than trying to shoot through the wave. Morgana’s other abilities gain value when Q lands, so creating a clear angle for it is the focus of laning.
notes.morgana-skill-w: W (Tormented Shadow) deals more damage the more health its target has lost, making it a threat to wounded enemies. Use it to force them out of an area as well as to deal damage. Each time Morgana heals through her passive, W’s cooldown decreases, so use it freely during fights.
notes.morgana-skill-e-timing: E (Black Shield) blocks crowd control and immobilizing effects while the shield remains. Its duration is short, so watch for the enemy’s cast and apply it at that moment instead of using it early. Its key purpose is to stop the crowd control the enemy uses to engage.
notes.morgana-skill-e-self: You can cast E (Black Shield) on yourself when an enemy engages on you, blocking the crowd control and buying time to activate R (Soul Shackles). That leaves your allied damage dealer unprotected from the next engage, so decide which one of you needs the shield.
notes.morgana-skill-e-vs-engage: Against enemies who start combos with a pull or knockback, save E (Black Shield) specifically for that ability. Using it elsewhere before their engage ability is spent leaves you vulnerable to one-sided trades throughout lane.
notes.morgana-skill-r: R (Soul Shackles) affects an area around Morgana, so move among enemies to catch them. Because its stun takes time and Morgana must survive until it triggers, activate R only when allies can follow up immediately. It also grants vision of every affected enemy.
notes.morgana-phase: Morgana’s laning strength depends directly on whether Q (Dark Binding) lands. Learning R (Soul Shackles) at level 6 gives her the first reliable kill opportunity; once she has items in the mid game, E (Black Shield) and R let her start or stop teamfights. Her early kill participation is statistically low, so don’t force early kills.
notes.morgana-laning-wave: In bot lane, avoid pushing the wave unintentionally with W (Tormented Shadow). Place it under an enemy champion to poke and deny space, and use it on the wave to push only when leaving lane to ward or roam. When holding a lane alone, use W to farm.
notes.morgana-laning-mana: Repeatedly missing Q (Dark Binding) can drain your mana and leave you unable to act. Hold it when the angle is uncertain; poke with W (Tormented Shadow) and conserve mana instead. Whenever the enemy can engage, make sure you have enough mana for E (Black Shield).
notes.morgana-teamfight: In teamfights, first use E (Black Shield) to block the enemy engage champion’s crowd control, then use R (Soul Shackles). Failing to use both leaves Morgana with little impact on the fight. Since Q (Dark Binding) is difficult to land once fighting starts, look for an angle before the fight begins.
notes.morgana-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Morellonomicon to reduce it. Morgana’s sustained damage with W (Tormented Shadow) and R (Soul Shackles) makes the healing reduction easy to maintain.
notes.vs-morgana-q: Morgana’s Q Dark Binding roots only the first target it hits, so keep the minion wave between you and her; moving along a line that overlaps the wave will block it most of the time.
notes.vs-morgana-w: Morgana’s W Tormented Shadow hurts much more when you’re missing a lot of health. If you’re low, getting caught in it can kill you on its own, so avoid crossing an area she has placed while retreating.
notes.vs-morgana-e: Don’t waste crowd control on a target protected by Morgana’s E Black Shield. Track its cooldown and engage while it’s unavailable; that’s the most reliable way to break through a Morgana composition.
notes.vs-morgana-r: R (Soul Shackles) stuns after a delay, rather than when the chains first connect. If you see the chains, use a movement ability or Cleanse to get out of range before the stun. If you cannot escape, kill Morgana first to prevent it from triggering.
notes.vs-morgana-phase: Morgana poses little threat unless Q (Dark Binding) lands, but one hit sets up W (Tormented Shadow) and the rest of her combo. In lane, prioritize positioning to dodge Q over calculating damage.
notes.naafiri-combo-q: Q’s two casts can be spaced apart. The second deals extra damage based on missing health only if the target is still bleeding, so apply the bleed with the first, then line up the second before it expires. The first hit also sends the pack leaping at the target, helping Naafiri close the gap.
notes.naafiri-combo-allin: For an all-in, activate W before engaging for its attack damage, movement speed, and two extra packmates, then land the first Q, close in with E, and follow with the second Q and an auto attack. If you spend E too early, you cannot follow an enemy who backs away.
notes.naafiri-combo-r: R is a targeted dash to a champion. A takedown reveals nearby enemies and allows a second cast, which grants a shield; engage only when you can secure the first takedown, then use that second R to escape or move to the next target.
notes.naafiri-skill-pack: The pack provides a significant share of Naafiri’s damage. Packmates replenish slowly, one at a time, but hitting a champion or large monster with an ability speeds up regeneration, so land an ability before a fight to build up the pack, even if you have to throw one out for that purpose. With every packmate dead, Naafiri is a melee champion whose damage falls far short.
notes.naafiri-skill-pack-target: The pack attacks Naafiri’s designated target. Hitting a minion just before a trade sends the pack after it, delaying all of its damage against the enemy champion; target that champion or hit them with Q before closing in to send the pack ahead.
notes.naafiri-skill-e: E recalls the pack and fully restores its health, so if area damage has hurt your pack, use E during the fight to heal it as well as to close the gap. When the pack is at full health, you can use E purely to engage.
notes.naafiri-skill-w: W briefly makes Naafiri untargetable and recalls the pack, but it does not restore the pack’s health; use E when you need to heal it. Time W’s untargetability to avoid targeted crowd control or a finishing ability.
notes.naafiri-skill-w-aoe: Recall your pack with W or E before an enemy area-of-effect ability hits. Recalled packmates become untargetable, so they avoid the damage and rejoin the fight at full strength once the ability passes. Against opponents with many area-of-effect abilities, this sequence alone can decide the fight.
notes.naafiri-skill-r-vision: R requires a takedown before you can cast it again, making it a way to chain engages after a kill. The takedown also reveals nearby enemies so you can choose your next target; if you engage without a secure takedown, you have no way back.
notes.naafiri-laning: As a melee mid laner, Naafiri struggles to farm against ranged opponents, but her pack helps attack minions and Q’s bleed can secure last hits from range. Clear waves the enemy pushes toward you with the pack and Q to keep up in levels, and close in only after the enemy has used a skillshot.
notes.naafiri-laning-roam: Naafiri’s high movement speed, boosted further by W, lets her roam quickly. Push the lane, then move to a side lane or the enemy jungle to create a numbers advantage and build a lead; staying mid to farm alone wastes that strength.
notes.naafiri-phase: Even early on, the pack helps Naafiri clear waves and harass. Learning R at level 6 gives her many more kill opportunities through its targeted dash, while mid-game roams and flanks are her strongest plays. In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage can wipe out the pack and cut her damage, so build on your lead before the game goes long.
notes.naafiri-teamfight: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Approach from the side or behind, use R to take out a backline target, then spend the second cast earned from the takedown to reach another target or escape. Before engaging, check your pack count and the enemy’s area damage; if the pack is hurt, restore it with E first.
notes.naafiri-situational-antiheal: If an enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Naafiri wears targets down with bleed and her pack, so if their healing goes unchecked, she cannot secure the assassination.
notes.vs-naafiri-pack: Clearing the pack sharply reduces Naafiri’s damage, so use area damage to remove it first. Because E can fully restore the pack’s health, counterattack right after Naafiri uses E, and save your area damage while the pack is recalled.
notes.vs-naafiri-w: Naafiri is untargetable for a short time while W is active, so wait until it ends before using targeted crowd control or a finishing ability; using either during W wastes it.
notes.vs-naafiri-q: The second Q deals sharply increased damage if it hits while the first Q’s bleed is active. If the first hits you, keep your distance until the bleed ends; closing in while bleeding lets Naafiri land the second Q and the pack’s attacks together.
notes.vs-naafiri-r: R is a targeted dash to a champion and cannot be dodged, so do not travel alone while Naafiri has it available. If an ally has just died, retreat immediately: Naafiri may have a second R and can take you out next.
notes.vs-naafiri-range: Ranged champions outrange Naafiri, who must fight in melee. Harass and farm from behind your minions while denying her an opening to close in with E, and you can maintain an advantage throughout lane. Her pack helps clear waves, though, so fully freezing the lane against her is difficult.
notes.vs-naafiri-late: In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage can wipe out Naafiri’s pack and reduce her damage. Stay together rather than getting picked off alone to deny her a route to your backline, and maintain broad vision during her more dangerous mid-game roaming phase.
notes.nami-combo-engage: To engage, knock the enemy up with R, then place Q where they will land. Because R travels slowly, wait to confirm the hit before throwing Q; its stun will begin as the knockup ends, leaving no time to react.
notes.nami-combo-trade: For lane trades, cast E on your ADC when they are in position to land basic attacks, throw Q as the enemy steps forward, then use W during the stun. E empowers a fixed number of attacks, so casting it after the enemy has backed away wastes it.
notes.nami-combo-w-bounce: W bounces between allies and enemies, hitting each target only once. It gets the most value when they are close together, so choose whether to start on an ally for healing or an enemy for damage. It only bounces to visible enemies, making it less effective without vision.
notes.nami-skill-q: Q takes time to land, so enemies can dodge a casual throw by walking away. Cast it as an enemy starts a last-hit animation, onto existing crowd control, or in time with an ally's dash. Its long cooldown leaves you unable to intervene for a while if it misses.
notes.nami-skill-q-terrain: Q lands at a targeted location and can cross walls. Predict the path of an enemy fleeing into a bush or behind a wall to catch them even without vision, but vary your angle because enemies know Q can come over walls.
notes.nami-skill-w-mana: W costs a lot of mana and provides Nami's lane sustain. Using it only to poke can leave you without mana when an ally needs healing, so early on, save it until an ally's health is actually at risk. During trades, use it only when it can bounce between an ally and an enemy.
notes.nami-skill-e: E lasts only a short time and empowers a fixed number of attacks, so cast it after a fight starts instead of in advance. Its slow can hold an enemy in place during a chase even without immobilizing crowd control; when escaping, cast it on an ally to slow pursuers.
notes.nami-skill-passive: P increases an ally's movement speed when Nami's abilities touch them, so W's healing and E's enhancement also help allies engage or disengage. Allies hit by R receive twice the movement speed bonus; even if R will miss the enemy, you can send it through allies to help them engage.
notes.nami-phase: Nami is weak at level 1 because she has only one way to intervene, but gains an advantage through lane sustain once she learns W. R gives her a first engage tool at level 6, and ability power strengthens her healing and buffs. Her health is among the lowest of all champions, though, so standing in front can get her caught even late in the game.
notes.nami-laning: In lane, sustain with W's healing and look for Q when the enemy steps forward. While Q is unavailable, keep your distance and avoid pushing the lane. Nami's top-tier 14-minute death metric reflects the value of staying alive and holding the lane.
notes.nami-roaming: When roaming, Nami is better at following her mid laner's crowd control with Q and R than catching enemies on her own. She has no mobility ability, so the trip out and back takes time; roam only after pushing the wave in to keep the enemy bot lane occupied. Going into the river without a purpose can get her caught.
notes.nami-vision: Nami has low health and no mobility, so entering an area without vision can get her killed before she has a chance to react. Clear enemy vision with a Control Ward, check the enemy’s position before entering a bush, and choose your route for placing vision carefully; that route is what keeps her alive.
notes.nami-teamfight: In teamfights, stand behind your ADC, keep E on them, and use W to heal allies. Using R to stop an enemy engage is safer than opening a fight with it; because it blocks an entire path, it can also cut off a fleeing enemy's escape. If Nami has to move to the front to open with R, her team is already positioned poorly.
notes.nami-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down allies, use Mikael's Blessing to free them. Nami can heal, but she cannot cleanse crowd control herself, so she needs this type of item to save an ally who has been caught.
notes.vs-nami-q: Q falls slowly and has a long cooldown. When its warning indicator appears, a step sideways can dodge it; immediately after it misses is the best time to target Nami and her ADC.
notes.vs-nami-r: R has very long range but travels slowly, so move sideways as soon as you see it and save your mobility ability for the Q that follows. The danger of getting hit by R is being caught by the rest of the combo, not R's damage itself.
notes.vs-nami-e: Do not fight an enemy affected by E head-on. Its duration is short, so back off, let it expire, then fight again; trying to escape while its slow is active can get you caught.
notes.vs-nami-squishy: Nami has some of the lowest health among all champions and no mobility ability. Secure vision and find an angle onto her to disrupt the lane; targeting Nami is better than targeting her ADC.
notes.vs-nami-heal: Nami relies entirely on W's healing for lane sustain. Apply healing reduction with Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon to undermine her ability to hold the lane.
notes.nasus-combo-basic: In fights, use W Wither → E Spirit Fire → Q Siphoning Strike. W keeps the target in E’s area while E greatly reduces their armor, letting Q deal its full physical damage. Using Q first deals noticeably less damage, even with the same stacks.
notes.nasus-skill-q-stack: Nasus’s damage comes almost entirely from Q Siphoning Strike stacks, so prioritize Q last hits throughout the laning phase. Killing champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q grants far more stacks, making those opportunities especially important; the stacks you build now largely determine your late-game damage.
notes.nasus-skill-q-tower: Q Siphoning Strike triggers on-hit effects when it deals damage, and its bonus damage applies to turrets. Once you have built up stacks, you can push a lane alone and take turrets quickly, giving you the option to pressure through split-pushing instead of teamfighting.
notes.nasus-skill-w: W Wither slows more strongly over time and reduces attack speed as well as movement speed, making it especially effective against champions who rely on basic attacks. Because it targets one enemy and has a substantial cooldown, choose an enemy carry carefully; without a dash, Nasus also relies on W to stop enemies from kiting him.
notes.nasus-skill-e-mana: E Spirit Fire reduces armor and boosts Q Siphoning Strike damage, but it costs a lot of mana and pushes the wave. During lane, save E for gank follow-up and fights; casting it whenever it is ready can leave you without enough mana for W → E → Q when your jungler arrives.
notes.nasus-skill-e-wave: Using E Spirit Fire near your turret pushes the wave away and costs you several Q Siphoning Strike last hits. While holding out under your turret, skip E entirely and focus on last-hitting with Q.
notes.nasus-skill-r: R Fury of the Sands increases maximum health, armor, and magic resistance, deals continuous damage to nearby enemies based on their maximum health, and greatly reduces Q Siphoning Strike’s cooldown. Activate it at the start of a teamfight for sustained area damage and repeated Q attacks; in a skirmish, it is better to wait until the enemy commits, then activate R at the last moment to use the health increase.
notes.nasus-skill-r-objective: R Fury of the Sands grants health and defenses that, together with P Soul Eater’s life steal, let Nasus tank and attack an objective alone. His team can attempt Baron earlier than other teams, so time objective calls for when R comes off cooldown.
notes.nasus-phase: Nasus is weakest at levels 2–3, when he loses head-on fights against most bruisers and has only W Wither to fight back. He becomes much stronger in the mid to late game once he has built Q Siphoning Strike stacks and can activate R Fury of the Sands; late in the game, he is very difficult to face head-on while R is active.
notes.nasus-laning-freeze: An enemy pushing the wave can work in your favor: last-hitting with Q Siphoning Strike under your turret is the safest way to build stacks. Avoid forcing the wave forward; catch incoming waves, collect Q last hits, and conserve mana.
notes.nasus-laning-zoned: If enemy pressure makes even Q Siphoning Strike last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap instead of trying to hold on alone. Nasus will not grow stronger over time without stacks, so leaving him unable to farm is the worst choice.
notes.nasus-teamfight: Nasus has no dash or guaranteed crowd control, making him highly vulnerable to kiting. Enter after your teammates initiate, use W Wither to pin down the enemy carry, and land Q Siphoning Strike while the target stands in E Spirit Fire. If an enemy ignores Nasus and goes for your backline, holding that enemy with W alone can turn the teamfight.
notes.nasus-situational-defense: Without enough defensive stats, Nasus can fall quickly to focused attacks even while R Fury of the Sands is active. Include at least one survival item, such as Dead Man’s Plate, even in a damage-focused build.
notes.nasus-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling. Because Q Siphoning Strike triggers on-hit effects, a single hit applies healing reduction.
notes.vs-nasus-r: While R Fury of the Sands is active, Nasus gains health and defensive stats and becomes stronger than most champions. Unless you have a clear advantage in numbers or damage, avoid starting a fight until R ends.
notes.vs-nasus-w: With more ranks, W Wither reduces both movement and attack speed enough to largely shut down champions who rely on basic attacks. Getting caught alone leaves you unable to escape, so avoid moving alone within Nasus’s range.
notes.vs-nasus-kite: Nasus is vulnerable to kiting. Even at full health, keep your distance and attack instead of taking him head-on; with only W Wither to close the gap, he will lose most opportunities to engage.
notes.vs-nasus-early-allin: Go all-in at levels 2–3, when Nasus is weaker than most bruisers. Poking alone is insufficient: bring him to half health with the first all-in, then go in again for the kill when your cooldowns return. Ignite suits this strategy. Champions with weak early games cannot create this opening, so avoid picking them into Nasus.
notes.vs-nasus-wave: Do not push the wave toward Nasus: under his turret, he can build Q Siphoning Strike stacks most easily. Let the wave push toward your side and call for a jungle gank. With no escape besides Flash, even one successful gank can turn the entire laning phase around.
notes.nautilus-combo-engage: For a standard engage, land Q, auto attack immediately after the pull, then use E → W. That first attack applies Nautilus’s passive root as the Q stun ends, keeping the target under crowd control; skipping it breaks the chain.
notes.nautilus-combo-flash-q: To catch an enemy outside Q range, Flash first and throw Q immediately, before they can react. If it lands, follow with a passive auto attack → E. Nautilus is among the slowest champions, so the longer you spend lining up Q without Flash, the more time the enemy has to escape.
notes.nautilus-combo-gank: During a gank or when entering a narrow passage, aim Q at terrain beside the enemy to close the gap more reliably, then use E immediately. Hitting terrain refunds a substantial portion of Q’s cooldown and mana cost, so a failed attempt costs less.
notes.nautilus-combo-ult-chain: After R knocks an enemy up, auto attack to apply your passive root, then save Q for the moment they try to escape. R → passive auto attack → Q keeps one target locked down for as long as possible.
notes.nautilus-skill-q: Q affects only the first target it hits, so minions can block it. In lane, throw it when a gap opens between minions or from a brush or the side; lining it up openly from the front risks hitting a minion first.
notes.nautilus-skill-q-terrain: Hitting terrain with Q refunds some of its cooldown and mana cost, letting you use it to travel along walls when returning to lane, roaming, or joining an objective fight.
notes.nautilus-skill-w: W grants a shield and adds area damage around the target of your auto attacks while it lasts. Weave in attacks to make full use of it, and activate W just before the enemy’s burst damage hits so the shield does not go to waste.
notes.nautilus-skill-e: E explodes in several waves, with a delay before the first. Leave it behind while fleeing to slow pursuit, or place it ahead of time along the enemy’s approach to make them hesitate before engaging.
notes.nautilus-skill-r: R follows its targeted enemy and knocks up other enemies along its path. When targeting a backline carry, angle the path through the enemy team to knock up those in front and open a way for your team to engage.
notes.nautilus-phase: Nautilus gains kill pressure at level 2, when both Q and E become available, and is strongest at level 6, when R gives him a reliable engage. He deals very little damage of his own late in the game, so focus on engaging and shutting down the enemy carry.
notes.nautilus-laning-mana: Using Q without hitting anything costs a lot of mana.
notes.nautilus-laning-level2: Reaching level 2 first opens Nautilus’s strongest trading window: Q → passive auto attack → E keeps the enemy locked down for a long time. Push the first wave quickly to reach level 2 first, then check that your ADC can follow up before starting the trade.
notes.nautilus-teamfight: Prioritize the enemy’s main damage dealer when engaging a teamfight. If there is no opening, do not force Q; hold the front line with W and E and draw out the enemy’s engage. Once they have used their engage ability, use R as the signal for your team to go in.
notes.vs-nautilus-e: If Nautilus uses E right next to you, stay in place until all its waves have ended. Running too soon takes you into later explosions, dealing extra damage and slowing you.
notes.vs-nautilus-w: With W active, Nautilus’s auto attacks deal area damage around their target. If you have time, stay close enough to break his W shield before continuing the fight.
notes.vs-nautilus-q: Q (Dredge Line) is Nautilus’s only direct engage tool and creates most of his kill opportunities. Keep minions between you and him to block it; if he misses, trade safely during its long cooldown.
notes.vs-nautilus-passive: Nautilus’s first auto attack roots its target. After a trade, leave his auto attack range promptly: even one hit can hold you in place for his follow-up abilities.
notes.vs-nautilus-r: R (Depth Charge) follows its targeted enemy, so it cannot be dodged, and also knocks up allies standing along its path. While Nautilus has R available, avoid lining up with allies along his engage path.
notes.vs-nautilus-mobility: Nautilus is among the slowest champions and has no mobility apart from using Q on terrain. Save your engage ability to create distance after he uses Q; once it is spent, he cannot easily catch up.
notes.neeko-combo-basic: The basic combo is E root → Q → auto attack. Place Q after the root so the target stays in its area through the bursts; Q bursts again when it damages a champion, allowing one root to hold them for every explosion. If you throw Q first, they can simply walk out.
notes.neeko-combo-e-minion: E grows larger and moves faster after hitting something, and its root lasts longer. In lane, angle it through a minion toward your opponent: it is easier to land and more effective than walking around the wave to avoid it.
notes.neeko-combo-r: Approach in disguise, begin preparing R, then use E or an ally’s crowd control to hold the target for R’s landing. Opponents cannot see the preparation animation while Neeko is disguised, giving them no cue to react, but the disguise wears off shortly after R is cast and reveals where you began preparing it.
notes.neeko-skill-passive: P lets Neeko disguise herself as an allied champion or nearby unit. Immobilizing crowd control, a damaging ability, or damage equal to the disguised unit’s health breaks the disguise, so use it to approach rather than to stay hidden during a fight, and plan your angle knowing your first damaging ability will reveal you.
notes.neeko-skill-q: Q bursts again in the same spot when it kills a unit or damages a champion or large monster. Place it over the wave to chain bursts through minion kills, clearing and harassing at once; if it hits nothing, it ends after the first burst. Its repeated bursts also make it valuable in objective fights when it hits a large monster.
notes.neeko-skill-w-passive: W’s passive adds damage and a brief movement speed boost to every third auto attack. Count the cycle in lane so the empowered hit lands on the enemy champion instead of a minion: attack minions twice, then hit your opponent with the third attack.
notes.neeko-skill-w-active: Casting W briefly turns Neeko invisible and sends a clone running in the chosen direction. Use that invisibility to interrupt targeted abilities and disrupt enemy aim, or send the clone the opposite way while escaping to mislead pursuers. The clone also copies Neeko’s ability and recall animations, so you can leave it appearing to recall.
notes.neeko-skill-r: R leaps only after its preparation animation ends and stuns an area when Neeko lands. If enemies scatter during the preparation, you can miss everyone and end up alone in their midst. A sturdy frontline with strong crowd control still available can prevent the engage entirely, so wait for an allied engage or your own E root to hold enemies before using R.
notes.neeko-laning: Neeko’s lane depends on landing E: without its root, Q and R are not guaranteed to land. If you have no angle, save E and wear the enemy down with W’s empowered auto attacks while you wait; also account for the enemy’s chance to engage once E is on cooldown.
notes.neeko-laning-roam: Support Neeko gets her greatest value from roaming. Push the lane, then disguise yourself as an ally on the way to establish vision across the river; even if enemies see you, the disguise can delay their reaction long enough to secure E and R. Making that disguise part of your vision route improves your chances of a successful gank.
notes.neeko-teamfight: In teamfights, start with E from the backline and finish with R after your allies’ engage holds the enemy in place. Casting R first and diving in alone leaves you vulnerable during its preparation animation; Neeko’s armor is among the lowest, and once caught, W’s invisibility is her only way out.
notes.neeko-phase: At levels 1–5, Neeko’s armor is among the lowest, making trades against melee champions who dive in difficult. At level 6, R combined with her disguise gives her the power to turn a fight around, and she peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power. In the late game, she has little left after using E and R, so the order in which she engages matters even more.
notes.neeko-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing can undo your burst damage, buy Morellonomicon between core items to apply Grievous Wounds during a single engage.
notes.vs-neeko-disguise: An enemy champion appearing somewhere unexpected may be Neeko. Check whether that champion was already visible elsewhere and whether they have a reason to be there; a lone enemy approaching after Neeko disappears from vision is a common sign of a disguised engage.
notes.vs-neeko-e: E is most powerful when it roots several people at once. It grows larger and faster after its first hit, making someone behind the first target easier to catch, so spread out from your allies and limit each cast to one target.
notes.vs-neeko-r: R only goes off after Neeko walks in and completes its preparation animation. A sturdy frontline with reliable crowd control held in reserve can stop her from entering, and moving out of the area when you see the animation can avoid it. Because the preparation is hidden while she is disguised, spread out early when a suspicious opponent gets close.
notes.vs-neeko-early: Neeko’s armor is among the lowest, and before level 6 she has no way to turn a fight around. If you play a melee champion who dives in, close the gap and force a trade immediately after she uses E.
notes.neeko-skill-passive-credibility: Disguise yourself as an ally the enemy cannot currently see; if that ally is already visible elsewhere, the deception is immediately obvious. Walk a route they would plausibly take, ideally blending in and moving with your allies.
notes.vs-neeko-clone: Shapesplitter’s clone is easy to identify because it never attacks. Chasing it gives the real Neeko time to find an angle, so if you judge it to be the clone, ignore it and keep watching your original target.
notes.nidalee-combo-gank: For a gank, land Javelin Toss from long range in human form to apply Hunted and reset Aspect Of The Cougar’s cooldown, then transform, close in with an empowered Pounce, and use Takedown followed by Swipe. If the spear misses, you get neither the reset nor the empowered effect, so don’t force the engage.
notes.nidalee-combo-cougar: In cougar form, the standard sequence is to close in with Pounce, use Takedown to finish the target, then deal any remaining damage with Swipe. Takedown empowers your next basic attack, so wait until you are in basic attack range before using it.
notes.nidalee-skill-q: Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther it travels, making a point-blank hit nearly worthless; look for an angle to land it at maximum range. A hit also grants true sight of the target, keeping them visible even in a bush and making pursuit much easier.
notes.nidalee-skill-w-trap: Bushwhack lasts a long time in human form and reveals enemies who step on it. Set traps at river entrances and jungle junctions ahead of time to track the enemy jungler’s route; when one is triggered, it applies Hunted and lets you follow up with a chase combo.
notes.nidalee-skill-e-heal: Primal Surge heals more the more health its target is missing, so wait until some health has been lost before using it. Cast it on an allied damage dealer just before an objective fight to grant attack speed as well.
notes.nidalee-skill-cougar-q: Takedown in cougar form deals more damage as the target’s health falls and is stronger against a Hunted target. Save it to finish a low-health enemy instead of using it first on someone at full health.
notes.nidalee-skill-pounce: Pounce in cougar form can cross terrain, making it an escape tool as well as a way to engage. As a rule, save a use for getting out instead of spending every Pounce going in; its longer leap toward a Hunted enemy also makes pursuit easier.
notes.nidalee-skill-r-form: Aspect Of The Cougar switches forms, has a short cooldown, and resets immediately when you apply Hunted in human form. Switch to cougar form to close in and back to human form to heal or create distance; your basic attacks become ranged again, letting you deal damage while retreating.
notes.nidalee-skill-passive-brush: Prowl increases movement speed when you pass through bushes or have a Hunted target. Routing through bushes speeds up your jungle movement, and moving in and out of them helps you position during fights.
notes.nidalee-phase: Cougar form gives Nidalee a fast early jungle clear, and she can pressure objectives with Javelin Toss poke even before level 6. Her low health and magic resistance make a single catch deadly, so avoid fighting the enemy jungler head-on. She peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power, but loses impact late if she cannot land Javelin Toss.
notes.nidalee-jungle-path: Nidalee has no crowd control, so her ganks depend on allied laners. Prioritize lanes where an ally can lock down the enemy; if none can, gain an advantage by farming or invading the enemy jungle instead.
notes.nidalee-teamfight: Avoid engaging head-on in teamfights. Throw Javelin Toss from the side or behind in human form to apply Hunted, then enter in cougar form only after the enemy’s main damage dealer has lost enough health; finish them and escape with Pounce. Nidalee is fragile enough to die if caught by a single crowd control effect.
notes.nidalee-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has healing, build Morellonomicon. Nidalee relies on a burst of damage from her spear and cougar combo, so healing between fights can take away her chance to finish a target with Takedown.
notes.vs-nidalee-spear: Javelin Toss hurts more when it travels farther, so be especially careful to dodge spears thrown from long range. Keep minions or your allied frontline between you and Nidalee to block them.
notes.vs-nidalee-hunt: Only Javelin Toss and Bushwhack apply Hunted. Dodge both to prevent her cougar abilities from being empowered and avoid the true sight that makes her pursuit easier.
notes.vs-nidalee-pounce: Once Nidalee has marked you, Takedown follows when she closes in with Pounce. Save crowd control or defensive abilities for that moment, and have a defensive ability ready as soon as a spear hits you.
notes.vs-nidalee-nocc: Nidalee has no crowd control and is fragile; once caught, Pounce is her only escape. Immobilize her to secure the catch, and remember where she emerged to throw a spear so you can find an angle to attack.
notes.vs-nidalee-trap: Assume Nidalee has placed Bushwhack traps at jungle entrances and along the river. Clear them with a Control Ward or an area-of-effect ability before entering so you do not start a fight marked by Hunted.
notes.nilah-combo-eq: Nilah’s key combo is to cast Q during E. Pressing Q while Slipstream passes through a target sends a wave that hits every enemy along the path. Its hit detection differs from casting Q after the dash, so always use Q during E when several enemies overlap.
notes.nilah-combo-trade: For a short trade, land Q on a minion or opponent to gain its range and attack speed buffs, then basic attack. Q must hit something to grant the buffs, so using it on a minion before closing in can briefly offset Nilah’s short range.
notes.nilah-combo-allin: For an all-in, enter with E, cast Q during the dash, basic attack, activate W once the opponent’s basic attacks and sustained damage begin, then pull them together with R to finish. Using W as soon as you enter wastes it before it blocks anything.
notes.nilah-skill-passive: When Nilah last-hits a minion, the nearest ally regains half the experience lost from sharing it. Keep your support close during lane so both of you level faster; if the support leaves, that benefit disappears entirely.
notes.nilah-skill-passive-heal: Nilah amplifies healing and shields allies give her, and the ally who provided them also receives the amplified effect. She benefits most from a support with healing or shields, so staying within that support’s range during fights helps keep her alive.
notes.nilah-skill-q: Q's passive grants armor penetration and basic attack lifesteal based on critical strike chance, so building critical strike items sharply improves Nilah's damage and ability to stay in a fight. Excess healing becomes a shield, making it worthwhile to attack minions even at full health.
notes.nilah-skill-w: W lets Nilah dodge all basic attacks for its duration, so use it when an opposing marksman or another basic attack focused champion starts dealing damage rather than spending it for movement speed on entry. It also lets her pass through units to escape a wall of minions. Allies she touches during W gain the same dodge effect, so entering along a path that brushes past your marksman or support can protect both of you from basic attacks.
notes.nilah-skill-e: E dashes through a targeted unit, including a minion, and serves both as an entry and an escape. Spending every use to get in leaves Nilah no way out, so check which unit you can dash through to escape before committing; an enemy minion wave can provide routes in both directions.
notes.nilah-skill-r: Use R to pull together and finish opponents who are already grouped, rather than to initiate. Damage dealt to champions heals Nilah and nearby allies, so hitting more enemies restores more health to the team; pulling only one also reduces the healing. Prioritize a position that gathers enemies into your allies’ area abilities.
notes.nilah-laning: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles even to last-hit against ranged opponents. Avoid forcing your way in: use Q to secure last hits from range and keep up in levels, then enter with E only when an opponent steps forward to attack a minion. The goal in lane is to get through it without falling far behind.
notes.nilah-laning-trade: Nilah can take 2v2 fights because her support’s shields and healing are amplified, but her melee range leaves her vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Enter only after the opponent has used their key skillshot crowd control.
notes.nilah-phase: Nilah is very weak at levels 1–2 because she is disadvantaged in both range and health. As critical strike items build up, Q grants more penetration and lifesteal, making her much stronger from mid game; in late game teamfights, W and R can also help keep her allies alive. Survive the early game and time favors Nilah.
notes.nilah-teamfight: In teamfights, enter second. After an opponent engages on an ally, move in with W to shut down basic attack damage, then use R when enemies group up to pull them together and heal your allies. Taking the front line first exposes Nilah to all their crowd control and can get her killed.
notes.nilah-situational-antiheal: If an opponent survives through healing, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. Nilah has to stay close and attack for a long time, and unchecked healing makes those fights difficult to finish.
notes.vs-nilah-range: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles to last-hit when harassed from outside her range. During lane, deny Nilah chances to close in and harass her from outside her range.
notes.vs-nilah-w: When Nilah activates W, all basic attacks miss her. When Nilah activates W, respond with ability damage instead of basic attacks. Resume basic attacks after Nilah's W ends. Allies who touch Nilah while her W is active also gain its basic attack dodge effect.
notes.vs-nilah-r: If Nilah catches several champions with R, her team gains both damage and healing. Spread out while it is available; if it has already pulled you in, attack Nilah immediately to stop her from maintaining the cast rather than trying to scatter.
notes.vs-nilah-heal: Nilah amplifies healing and shields from allies and shares the effect with the ally who provided them. If her support provides healing, a Grievous Wounds item is especially valuable: buy Executioner’s Calling or Morellonomicon early, whichever suits your scaling.
notes.vs-nilah-q: After Q hits, Nilah briefly gains attack range and attacks in a cone. Do not assume you are safe at the edge of her usual range; take another step back while the Q buff is active.
notes.vs-nilah-cc: Nilah has low health and is highly vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Her real opening comes when both E and W are down, so use targeted crowd control after she enters and spends W.
notes.noct-combo-gank: For a standard gank, land Q to lay a trail, run along it to close in, apply E, then trigger your passive with a basic attack. Enemies hit by Q leave a trail too, so their escape route becomes Nocturne’s path of pursuit.
notes.noct-combo-ult: Activate R to cut off vision, recast it to dash to your target, turn on W just before landing, then apply E and follow with basic attacks. W stays active during the R dash, so activating it early can block crowd control the target uses in a hurry.
notes.noct-combo-e-hold: E only triggers fear if the tether holds, so apply it after closing in. Landing E once you are already beside the target on the Q trail leaves little room to escape its range; from farther away, the target can break the tether simply by walking back.
notes.noct-skill-passive: Your passive periodically adds area damage and healing to your next basic attack. Each basic attack reduces its cooldown, with a larger reduction when you hit a champion or jungle monster. Keep attacking while clearing camps: those attacks bring the healing back sooner and help preserve your health.
notes.noct-skill-q: Q deals damage and provides mobility: on its trail, Nocturne moves through units and gains movement speed and attack damage. The trail remains even if Q misses, so you can use it outside combat to close a gap or escape. When ganking, lay it along your approach in advance to reach the target faster.
notes.noct-skill-w: W briefly shields Nocturne from one enemy ability; blocking it doubles his attack speed, making W both a defensive tool and a damage boost. Time it for a key immobilizing ability, since letting the shield expire without blocking anything gives only half the attack speed benefit.
notes.noct-skill-w-monster: W also blocks monster abilities. Blocking something like a dragon attack activates the attack speed boost and lets Nocturne damage the objective much faster. Keep this in mind before an objective fight, but save the shield if the enemy jungler is likely to arrive.
notes.noct-skill-e: E triggers fear only after its tether to the target holds for a set time. Once the target is feared, Nocturne gains a large movement speed boost when moving toward them, making that the easiest moment to chase. Draw out their mobility ability or force them toward a wall before applying E to improve your chances of landing the fear.
notes.noct-skill-r: R reduces every enemy’s vision radius and stops them from sharing vision, so it can conceal an ally’s engage or the start of an objective even without a dash. At a decisive moment, activating it is worthwhile even if you cannot dash in.
notes.noct-skill-r-target: R’s dash targets an enemy, so you must be able to see someone in range. Ideally, wait for enemies to scatter in the darkness and choose an isolated target; diving into the middle of a group leaves you with more damage to survive than one shield can handle.
notes.noct-phase: Nocturne’s jungle clear is average at levels 1–2, but the Q trail and W’s attack speed make camps go faster. Learning R at level 6 is his first power spike, allowing him to gank anywhere on the map. He peaks in the mid game after completing his first core item; late in the game, his fragility means a poor engage can get him killed immediately.
notes.noct-laning: Before level 6, gank success depends on your ally’s crowd control, so prioritize lanes where they can hold the enemy in place. Lay down Q’s trail along your approach and enter from a brush or out of vision, then use E once you are close. If there is no gank opportunity, clear camps to reach level 6 sooner.
notes.noct-laning-r-timing: After level 6, use R when the lane state calls for it instead of holding it. If an enemy laner has pushed the wave and stepped forward, and your ally can follow up, you can cut off vision with R and engage even from the opposite side of the jungle. Enemies cannot see their allies during the darkness, which greatly improves the chance of a successful dive.
notes.noct-teamfight: In teamfights, Nocturne’s job is to pick off one backline enemy in the darkness rather than fight the frontline. After activating R, wait for reduced vision to make the enemies split up before dashing in. Engage after your allies start the fight, using W on entry to absorb the enemy support’s crowd control so the shield gets its value.
notes.vs-noct-r-group: When Nocturne activates R and the screen darkens, immediately move toward your teammates. He looks for isolated targets, so grouping up makes his engage costly. Scattering and fleeing separately while shared vision is cut off is the worst choice.
notes.vs-noct-e: Nocturne’s E only triggers fear if the tether stays connected; moving far enough away breaks it. Save a mobility ability or Flash for the moment he applies E, and getting out of range will leave you taking only the damage, without the fear.
notes.vs-noct-w: Nocturne’s W blocks one ability completely and doubles his attack speed if it does. Use a low value ability to remove the shield before applying your key crowd control.
notes.vs-noct-q: If Nocturne’s Q hits you, you leave a trail that lets him chase quickly. Running straight away lays a path for him, so angle toward your allies or a turret until the trail disappears.
notes.vs-noct-vision: Nocturne thrives where there is no vision. Keep the river and jungle entrances warded and position yourself before he activates R, so you can judge where to retreat even after darkness falls.
notes.nunu-combo-gank: For a gank, start rolling W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) far from the lane and outside enemy vision, build it to maximum speed, then hit the target. Throw E (Snowball Barrage) during the knockup and finish with R (Absolute Zero). Starting W near the enemy gives it too little size or speed, making it easy to dodge.
notes.nunu-combo-wer: While E's root is delayed, use R's slow to keep the enemy from walking out of range. Against enemies without a dash, combining E and R makes the root nearly guaranteed.
notes.nunu-combo-r-setup: R (Absolute Zero) is channeled, so casting it alone lets enemies walk away and take almost no explosion damage. Pair it with W’s knockup, E’s root, or an ally’s immobilizing crowd control. If the target tries to escape with a cleanse, recast R immediately to detonate it instead of waiting for maximum damage.
notes.nunu-skill-w-timing: W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) starts its cooldown when you begin rolling, not when you release the snowball. Once it reaches full size, hit the enemy right away if you’re confident it will connect. In a wide open area, you can instead keep rolling in a circle to deny enemies entry to a particular area.
notes.nunu-skill-w-momentum: Movement speed bonuses multiply the size and speed W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) gains as it rolls. Terrain effects or ally buffs that increase movement speed produce a much larger, faster snowball over the same distance. Taking a wide route around the river also gives it room to grow while hiding your approach angle.
notes.nunu-skill-q-heal: Q (Consume) heals far more from a minion or monster than from a champion, so if you need sustain, click the minion precisely to keep your cursor from targeting the champion. Healing increases further below half health; when you’re low, biting a jungle monster can be more valuable than running away.
notes.nunu-skill-e: E throws snowballs three times; enemies hit by all three are slowed, then rooted after a delay. The root rarely triggers if you have no way to keep the enemy in place, but if their escape route is clear, land all three hits in advance and give chase. Because E is not targeted, you can also use it to reveal stealthed enemies.
notes.nunu-skill-passive: P (Call of the Freljord) grants attack speed and movement speed to Nunu & Willump and one nearby ally. Its duration starts when you damage a large monster, so stand beside your allied marksman while attacking an objective to share the buff. Empowered basic attacks also hit around the target; at jungle camps, position so they strike multiple monsters.
notes.nunu-laning-jungle: Your first gank comes after learning W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) at level 3. After a lane gank, you can grow another snowball while rolling around the Rift Scuttler and immediately gank again. Q (Consume) clears camps quickly with its fixed damage to monsters, but CS and damage per minute both rank near the bottom statistically, so get value from objectives and ganks instead of competing in farm.
notes.nunu-phase: Ganks become strong when you learn W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) at level 3, and objective fights peak after you add R (Absolute Zero) at level 6. Early damage ranks among the lowest statistically, making solo kills difficult. As you build health and ability power in the mid and late game, Q’s sustain and R’s burst both improve; you can still engage fights and protect allies late.
notes.nunu-teamfight: Nunu & Willump start a teamfight when the snowball reaches the enemy backline, but their low damage makes a solo engage easy to punish. Roll W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) in only when allies are close enough to follow. If there is no engage angle, cast R (Absolute Zero) in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy’s approach.
notes.nunu-situational-slowresist: Rolling W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) also slows Nunu himself. Slow resistance helps the snowball reach maximum speed sooner and makes it easier to land E’s root on a fleeing enemy. If the opposing team has many slows, Mercury’s Treads and Unflinching become especially valuable together.
notes.vs-nunu-w-dodge: The W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) snowball travels forward much faster than it turns sideways, so running away will let it catch you. Instead, walk toward it and escape through the spot Nunu just left. Its range is very long, making a straight sprint away unlikely to work.
notes.vs-nunu-gank: Nunu & Willump can gank with a snowball from level 3. If you push the lane and stand too far forward, a snowball rolled in from outside your vision can hit you, so secure river vision before choosing your lane position early on. They can also roll around the Rift Scuttler and return immediately after a gank.
notes.vs-nunu-heal: Nunu can repeatedly heal with Q (Consume) on minions and monsters, with even more healing below half health. Without healing reduction, you may win a damage trade but fail to finish him off, so get Executioner’s Calling or Morellonomicon early.
notes.vs-nunu-magic: Virtually all of Nunu & Willump’s damage is magic damage, while most of their threat comes from the snowball’s crowd control. Options that provide both magic resistance and tenacity are especially effective.
notes.vs-nunu-e: If E (Snowball Barrage) hits and slows you, its root follows after a delay. Leave the area immediately, using a mobility ability during that window if you have one. Simply trying to run from the same spot can leave you caught by R’s slow and then rooted.
notes.nunu-skill-w-cleanse: W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) slows Nunu while he rolls it, so account for the fact that he turns sideways more slowly than he moves forward.
notes.nunu-skill-r-peel: Cast R (Absolute Zero) beneath your allied carry to stop an enemy engage, even if the explosion deals no damage. Nunu also gains a shield while channeling, making him harder to kill.
notes.vs-nunu-r: R (Absolute Zero) is channeled, and interrupting it with immobilizing crowd control prevents the explosion damage. If you cannot interrupt it, walk out of range, though its slow grows stronger the longer you remain inside, reaching up to 95%. A Nunu who has built only health will not be taken down during the channel, so leave the area instead of forcing an attack.
notes.olaf-combo-basic: For a basic trade, throw Q in the direction your opponent is moving to slow them, then close in along the axe’s landing path, pick it up to reduce Q’s cooldown, land a basic attack, and use E. Missing the axe leaves a long gap before your next Q and opens you to a counterattack, so throw it only where retrieving it also lets you approach.
notes.olaf-combo-allin: When going all in, land Q, close in for a basic attack, activate W, and finish with E. Its true damage still goes through if the opponent builds armor or magic resistance, so save it for the final hit.
notes.olaf-combo-ult: R is for clearing the opponent’s crowd control, not for starting an engage; activate it just before the control lands or immediately after it does. Each basic attack or E hit on a champion extends R’s duration, so stay close and keep attacking once it’s active.
notes.olaf-skill-q-axe: The Q axe stays on the ground, and picking it up greatly reduces its cooldown, so its landing spot determines Olaf’s path. When chasing, throw it ahead of the opponent and retrieve it as you follow; when retreating, throw it behind you along your escape route and pick it up as you leave. Check the terrain before throwing it over a wall, or you may be unable to retrieve it.
notes.olaf-skill-q-armor: Champions hit by Q briefly lose armor. In a teamfight, time it to land as allies who mainly deal physical damage engage, increasing the team’s total damage instead of using it only for your own.
notes.olaf-skill-w: W grants both attack speed and a shield, and the shield grows stronger the more health you have lost. Activating it early at full health wastes that value; take the opponent’s combo first, then use W’s attack speed and shield together to counterattack.
notes.olaf-skill-e: E costs Olaf health to deal true damage, but refunds that cost if it kills the target. Each basic attack reduces E’s cooldown, so keep using it while you stay close; if you’re low on health and the kill is uncertain, hold it or its health cost could kill you first.
notes.olaf-skill-r: R prevents movement impairing effects, but damage still gets through. There’s no reason to activate it after the opponent has used their crowd control, while using it too early lets them hold that ability until R expires; activate it a beat after their crowd control comes out.
notes.olaf-phase-early: Olaf’s level 1 attack damage and movement speed are among the highest of all champions, making him strong in trades against melee opponents from the start. He is strongest from levels 3 to 6, when Q and E are both available, but struggles later against long range compositions that prevent him from closing in.
notes.olaf-phase-lowhp: Berserker Rage increases Olaf’s attack speed and lifesteal as he loses health. Falling below half health does not always mean he should retreat: if a target he can lifesteal from is within reach, that can be his strongest moment, especially with W and R active together.
notes.olaf-laning: Against melee opponents, close in early to win trades. Drop Q between you and the opponent instead of beyond the wave, so retrieving it and approaching become one movement. Olaf has limited mana, making an unretrieved Q a costly trade.
notes.olaf-laning-vs-ranged: Against ranged opponents, don’t force an approach; use Q to secure last hits and keep up in levels and growth. Activate R and engage only after they have used their poke ability or when your jungler can follow up, and avoid poking from a position where you cannot retrieve the axe, since that trade costs you.
notes.olaf-teamfight: In teamfights, don’t spend time fighting the frontline: use R to ignore crowd control and run straight at the backline damage dealers. If the approach is narrow, throw Q behind your target first, then push toward the axe to slow them and retrieve it during the engage.
notes.olaf-situational-antiheal: If the opponent’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Olaf stays close and attacks for a long time, allowing him to keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-olaf-lowhp: Olaf gains attack speed and lifesteal as his health gets lower, so closing in on him at half health can get you killed. Save crowd control that can reliably stop him for the finishing stage.
notes.vs-olaf-axe: In lane, focus on keeping Olaf from retrieving his Q axe. Moving away from where it lands denies him both a quicker poke cooldown and his approach path.
notes.vs-olaf-ult: Stuns, roots, and other movement impairing effects do not work on Olaf while R is active. Its duration is short, so create distance behind a wall or your allies, wait it out, and apply crowd control as soon as it ends. Avoid taking basic attacks or E hits during R, since each one extends its duration.
notes.vs-olaf-e: Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce the true damage from Olaf’s E, Reckless Swing. When low on health, rely on shields, healing, or distance instead of defensive stats.
notes.vs-olaf-scaling: Olaf is strongest early and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid giving him early kills and stall until the matchup turns in your favor; if you have a range advantage, simply keeping your distance is enough to win.
notes.orianna-skill-ball-position: All of Orianna’s abilities depend on the ball’s position: Q sends it to a target location and leaves it there, W and R activate where it sits, and E attaches it to an ally. Decide where the ball needs to go before choosing an ability.
notes.orianna-skill-ball-return: The ball returns automatically if it gets too far from Orianna. While it is away, she loses the armor and magic resistance from E’s passive, making her most vulnerable right after casting Q. Retrieve the ball before moving through dangerous areas.
notes.orianna-combo-poke: For basic poke, use Q to send the ball toward your opponent, then press W immediately so it activates as the ball arrives. Pressing W first makes it activate near Orianna, out of reach; the order determines whether the poke lands.
notes.orianna-combo-e-delivery: E is the only way to send the ball beyond Q’s range. Cast it on an engaging ally so the ball follows them, then activate R or W where they arrive. Since this can place the ball much deeper than Q can reach, always consider this route first before a teamfight.
notes.orianna-combo-ult: For an R combo, place the ball beyond or beside the enemy group, then use R → Q → W. R pulls enemies toward the ball, so position it to pull them toward your team; a misplaced ball can pull them away instead.
notes.orianna-combo-flash-ult: If you cannot get the ball where you want it for R, Flash to move Orianna into position, then cast R. If the ball is already near the enemy or attached to an ally and gives you the same angle, save Flash.
notes.orianna-skill-w: W deals area damage and slows enemies around the ball while giving allies there movement speed. Use it for more than damage trades: when an ally engages or you retreat together, place the ball near your allies and activate W to help them move.
notes.orianna-skill-e: E gives its target a shield and delivers the ball; an ally carrying it also gains armor and magic resistance from its passive. Attach the ball to your engaging ally before a teamfight, or cast E on yourself if you expect to be targeted to retrieve the ball and gain a shield.
notes.orianna-skill-passive: P adds magic damage to basic attacks, increasing with consecutive hits on the same target. Orianna wins short basic attack trades against other mages, so early in lane, trade back when one starts attacking you.
notes.orianna-phase: Orianna’s level 1 health, armor, and magic resistance are all among the lowest of any champion, so an early catch can take her down at once. She grows stronger as Q’s cooldown shortens and again at level 6 when she gains R, then peaks in the mid to late game once she has enough items to turn a teamfight with a single R.
notes.orianna-laning: In lane, manage your mana while using Q for both last hits and poke. Keep the ball near your opponent while standing farther back, and send Q where the opponent overlaps with the backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time.
notes.orianna-laning-wave: Orianna’s short range and very low movement speed leave her exposed to jungle ganks if she pushes the wave all the way in. Without vision, hold it near the middle and poke with Q instead.
notes.orianna-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to pull multiple enemies toward your team. The most reliable setup is to attach the ball to an engaging ally with E and cast R the moment they reach the enemy. Casting R with the ball on Orianna requires you to walk up to the enemy team, so treat it as a last resort.
notes.orianna-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who can dive in, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. Orianna is most vulnerable immediately after using R, so surviving that moment helps your team deal damage.
notes.vs-orianna-ball: Judge Orianna’s threat by the ball’s position. If it is not nearby, R cannot pull you from where you stand; if you stand near it, you can be pulled at any time. Watch the ball, rather than Orianna herself, when positioning.
notes.vs-orianna-no-ball: Orianna loses the armor and magic resistance from E’s passive while the ball is away from her, so trade damage right after she casts Q.
notes.vs-orianna-peel: Orianna has several ways to defend herself: W's slow, E's shield, and R's pull. Trying to make Orianna use her defensive tools one by one delays the fight.
notes.vs-orianna-auto: Orianna’s P adds magic damage to basic attacks, increasing with consecutive hits on the same target. If you play an ability power champion, avoid early basic attack trades and trade damage only with abilities.
notes.ornn-combo-pillar: Ornn’s basic engage is Q → E: a magma pillar rises at the end of Q’s path, and charging into it with E shatters it, releasing a shockwave that knocks up nearby enemies. This is his only way to set up a knockup himself in open terrain, so decide where the pillar needs to stand before casting Q.
notes.ornn-combo-brittle: For a damage trade, use W → auto attack. Only enemies hit by W’s final flame become Brittle; an auto attack against them then deals bonus damage and knocks them back. Move close enough for that final flame to connect, or the combo loses half its value.
notes.ornn-combo-order: Ability order changes how much you get from a combo.
