Brittle extends immobilizing crowd control, so if you’re already close, apply it with W before the knockup from E’s shockwave or an R headbutt. When landing W reliably matters more, use E or R to lock down a target with a mobility ability first, then follow with W.
notes.ornn-combo-ult: R has two casts. The spirit first travels toward Ornn, slowing enemies it passes through and making them Brittle; only when he recasts R to headbutt it does it change direction and knock enemies up. Summon it behind the target so it passes through the enemy team, then meet it from the other side and send it back toward your allies.
notes.ornn-skill-forge: Ornn’s P, Living Forge, lets him spend gold to craft items anywhere, which is his entire laning advantage: opponents must recall to shop, while he can stay to farm CS and pressure the turret. Crafting takes time, so avoid it when an enemy is close or the jungler’s location is unclear.
notes.ornn-skill-masterwork: Masterwork upgrades are worth more to Ornn’s allies than to Ornn himself: they strengthen allies’ completed items at no gold cost, raising the whole team’s power for free. Prioritize a main damage dealer who already has plenty of items and allies whose upgraded item could directly change a teamfight’s outcome. As Ornn levels up, he can have more upgrades granted at once, so use each one as soon as it becomes available unless you have a reason to save it.
notes.ornn-skill-q: Q’s fissure stops when it hits an enemy champion, placing the pillar near their feet; if it misses, the pillar rises at maximum range. Aim to hit your opponent when farming or poking, but cast past them when you need the pillar in a specific spot for E’s shockwave. Keep those aims distinct so the pillar lands where you intend. It also acts as terrain, so placing it where an opponent must approach to farm CS or along the enemy jungler’s entry path can block that area entirely.
notes.ornn-skill-w: Ornn is Unstoppable while advancing with W, making it a way through opponents who try to stop his engage with slows or knockbacks. Its direction is fixed and its movement is slow, though, so the final flame will miss someone who escapes with a mobility ability. Use W just after they use that ability or when they’re cornered against a wall.
notes.ornn-skill-e: E is both Ornn’s engage tool and a way to destroy terrain. It only knocks enemies up when it hits terrain; against an opponent without a wall behind them, it merely deals damage as Ornn passes through. It can also clear enemy-created walls blocking your allies’ escape route. Using E to engage leaves no way to disengage, so save it when your allies aren’t nearby.
notes.ornn-laning: Ornn’s early damage is among the lowest of top lane champions. Rather than seeking an advantage in lane, farm safely with Q and aim to keep up in CS and levels. If your opponent pushes, let the wave come in and farm under your turret; when they recall, finish an item with Living Forge to reverse the item gap.
notes.ornn-phase: Ornn is weakest at levels 1–2, when his cooldowns are long and his damage is low. R gives him a way to force an engage with allies at level 6, while his real power window comes in mid game after he has built two or three defensive items. Late in the game, his contribution comes from the Masterwork upgrades granted to his allies rather than his own damage, so his value to the team grows as the game goes on.
notes.ornn-teamfight: Start teamfights near terrain. In a narrow passage with walls, the most reliable sequence is to hit a wall with E for the knockup, then apply Brittle with W. If you must fight in the open, send the R spirit through the opponents first and follow with E. Ornn is no damage dealer: hold position in front of your carries, counter the enemy engage, and protect them instead of chasing the enemy backline.
notes.ornn-situational-thornmail: If the enemy’s main damage is physical and they wear Ornn down with auto attacks, buy Thornmail earlier. He already takes hits on the front line, so its reflected damage and healing reduction get direct use.
notes.ornn-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps Ornn’s sustained damage from finishing them, build healing reduction. His damage is magic, so start with Oblivion Orb and upgrade it to Morellonomicon; the health it provides also suits his front line role. Executioner’s Calling offers only attack damage, a stat Ornn cannot use well. His fights last long enough to keep healing reduction applied.
notes.vs-ornn-wall: Stand away from walls: Ornn’s E knocks enemies up with its shockwave only if he hits terrain, and otherwise merely deals damage as he passes through. When you see him prepare E, retreat toward open ground away from the wall.
notes.vs-ornn-pillar: Ornn’s Q pillar also counts as a wall for him, so standing near it leaves you open to an E knockup even in otherwise open terrain. Once it appears, move clear of the entire area around it.
notes.vs-ornn-forge: When Ornn tries to craft an item in lane, close in and attack him. Interrupting the craft eventually forces him to recall, removing his only laning advantage: finishing an item without going back.
notes.vs-ornn-brittle: Ornn’s final W flame applies Brittle. While it lasts, immobilizing crowd control from Ornn’s team lasts longer and deals bonus damage, so keep your distance and don’t move forward until it wears off. An auto attack from Ornn can also knock you back and separate you from your allies during this time.
notes.vs-ornn-ult: The spirit summoned by R approaches slowly at first, so you can sidestep it. The danger comes after Ornn recasts R to headbutt it: stay off the straight line between him and the spirit, and even after it passes, position with its possible return from the other side in mind.
notes.vs-ornn-early: Ornn’s early damage is very low, so you should rarely lose lane to him. Press your advantage as much as possible early, then keep up the pressure to end the game before his items and his allies’ Masterwork upgrades accumulate.
notes.pantheon-combo-allin: The basic engage is W, an empowered basic attack, E, then a tap Q. W targets an enemy and cannot miss, making it a reliable way to start; if Mortal Will is fully stacked when W lands, the empowered basic attack hits multiple times.
notes.pantheon-combo-poke: Tap Q to thrust, greatly reducing its cooldown so you can farm and stack Mortal Will. Hold Q to throw the spear and poke when you cannot get close enough; choosing between the two is fundamental to playing Pantheon.
notes.pantheon-skill-passive: Mortal Will empowers your next basic ability after enough ability uses and basic attacks. Before a fight, stack it with tap Q and basic attacks, including attacks on minions, then decide whether to empower W or E and use that ability last.
notes.pantheon-skill-e: E only blocks damage from the direction Pantheon faces and cannot block turret damage. Keep facing the enemy while using it; if you are surrounded from multiple directions, it is almost useless. Recasting E ends it early and brings forward the finishing strike, so if there is nothing left to block, end it immediately and move to your next action.
notes.pantheon-skill-w: W is Pantheon's only way to engage and moves him toward an enemy, so it cannot be used to escape. Using it commits you to the fight; check the enemy's mobility abilities and where your allies are positioned to help before you go in.
notes.pantheon-skill-q-finish: Thrown Q deals much more damage to low-health enemies, so use it to finish a fleeing target while they are in range instead of chasing them down. Save Q until then during a chase.
notes.pantheon-skill-r: R makes Pantheon leap and land at a chosen location, damaging an area. You need vision there to aim the landing accurately, so land toward an allied ward and time your descent with allied crowd control, since enemies have time to move away before you land.
notes.pantheon-phase: Pantheon's level 1 base stats are among the best, making him strongest early. Tap Q's short cooldown lets you poke throughout the laning phase, and learning R at level 6 lets you influence other lanes. As items build up, his damage and durability fall behind, so use your early lead to end the game.
notes.pantheon-laning: Chip away at the enemy's health with held Q, then close in with W when they focus on last-hitting. Pantheon's short range makes the approach risky, so use brush to set up your angle and engage only right after the enemy uses their counterattack ability.
notes.pantheon-laning-support: As support, prioritize repeated poke over fights that risk your life. Pantheon support has very high kill participation but also dies often, and a failed engage can put the enemy marksman ahead. Use W only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
notes.pantheon-laning-top: In top lane, use tap Q to secure CS while stacking Mortal Will, then go in with W right after the enemy uses their poke ability. Against ranged enemies, use E like a shield to close the gap; if you cannot get close enough, switch to poking with held Q instead of forcing the engage.
notes.pantheon-teamfight: In teamfights, push through the frontline and lock down the enemy carries: use E to block damage from the front as you move in, then W to reach a priority target. You have no way out after W if you engage alone first, so go in after an ally lands crowd control or land with R alongside your allies.
notes.pantheon-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner's Calling early if the enemy can heal. Pantheon deals damage in a short burst, and healing during the fight can erase your chance to secure a kill.
notes.vs-pantheon-e: Pantheon's E (Aegis Assault) blocks damage only from the direction he faces; attacks from his side or behind still hit, and it cannot block turret damage. Move around him to attack, or wait until E ends before attacking from the front.
notes.vs-pantheon-w: Pantheon's W is a targeted stun that cannot be dodged, so stay out of its range. Stand even farther back when an ally with crowd control is beside him, since they can keep you in place for his combo.
notes.vs-pantheon-q: Pantheon's held Q deals reduced damage to enemies behind the first target it hits, so keep minions between you and him when he pokes to reduce your losses in lane.
notes.vs-pantheon-r: Pantheon needs vision of an area to aim R's landing accurately, so stepping into brush makes his aim harder. When the landing warning appears, you can avoid most of the attack simply by walking out of its area.
notes.vs-pantheon-phase: Pantheon’s base stats are among the best in the game at levels 1–2, so trading blows with him early is almost always a losing proposition. His impact drops sharply as the game goes on, though, and simply buying time without giving him early kills can turn the matchup in your favor.
notes.poppy-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use E to stun the enemy against a wall, then follow with Q and a basic attack. The E stun holds them in Q’s lingering zone long enough for both the initial hit and the detonation to land. If you use Q first, they can walk out before the zone detonates, so lead with E whenever you have a way to hold them in place.
notes.poppy-combo-e-angle: E pushes its target in the direction Poppy is facing, so line up Poppy, the enemy, and a wall to secure the stun. If there is no wall behind them, move around first to create the angle. In lane, the shorter angle is usually toward a side wall rather than straight ahead.
notes.poppy-combo-passive: Iron Ambassador’s shield tends to land near a wall, so the path to collect it often follows naturally from pushing an enemy into that wall with E. After the stun, walk forward to pick it up and continue trading with a shield. If you kill the target, the shield returns immediately, so there is no need to collect it.
notes.poppy-skill-passive: When Iron Ambassador is ready, your next basic attack gains substantial range. It is one of melee Poppy’s few ways to harass a ranged opponent, so do not spend it on a minion. An enemy can destroy the dropped shield by stepping on it; if it rolls toward them, give it up rather than overextend to collect it.
notes.poppy-skill-q: Q deals damage immediately, then its lingering zone detonates once more after a short delay; if you cannot keep the enemy in place, only half the damage lands. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it more valuable against high-health enemies, but a damage cap against minions and monsters keeps its farming efficiency average. Since the zone’s slow also helps you chase, you can cast Q first to pin down an enemy when setting up a finish.
notes.poppy-skill-w: Activate W when you see the enemy dash. Enemies stopped by W briefly cannot use movement abilities. W's passive Armor and Magic Resist increase as Poppy's health gets lower.
notes.poppy-skill-e: E is both Poppy’s engage tool and her only guaranteed stun, so do not spend it just to move. Without terrain to knock the target into, it only pushes them and provides neither a stun nor bonus damage. You can still use it to start a fight without a wall stun by positioning to push the enemy toward your team.
notes.poppy-skill-r: R has two uses: cast it without charging for a quick knockup on enemies in front of you that can interrupt a counterattack in a 1v1, or charge it fully to lengthen the fissure and knock every enemy hit far away, splitting up a teamfight. Poppy slows down and her movement is obvious while charging, so start behind a wall or out of enemy vision. When peeling an enemy off your damage dealer, plan for the knockback to send them toward the Nexus.
notes.poppy-laning-melee: When a melee opponent steps forward to last hit, use E from an angle that puts a wall behind them. The stun guarantees a follow up Q and basic attack, making the trade one sided. If the angle is unavailable, save E and harass only with Iron Ambassador’s shield; keep W ready while the enemy still has an engage ability available.
notes.poppy-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing an engage with E; use the passive shield’s extended range to harass while securing CS. Poppy moves relatively quickly, so when an opponent has just used a poke ability, walk forward to close the gap and save E for that moment. Picking up the shield for its protection also helps you stay in lane longer.
notes.poppy-jungle-gank: For a jungle gank, the approach angle must give you a wall stun. Enter from behind the lane and position to push the enemy into a side wall with E; charging straight at them may only push them away. Drawing them toward a nearby wall, such as one at a river entrance or beside a turret, is key to a successful gank.
notes.poppy-teamfight: Poppy’s role in a teamfight is to guard her backline rather than dive in first. Stand in the enemy engager’s path, stop their dash with W, then stun them against a wall with E. Using E to engage takes you away from the ally W needs to protect, so if your damage dealer is likely to be targeted, save E to intercept the attacker.
notes.poppy-phase: At levels 1–2, Q’s long cooldown limits your harass, and without E you have little ability to force a fight. Once you learn E and Q’s cooldown shortens, you can pressure melee opponents; after learning R at level 6, you can also take part in dives and teamfights. Poppy gains substantial health and Armor with levels, making her especially valuable with items in the mid to late game. Her raw damage falls behind late, so focus on stopping enemy damage dealers rather than trying to deal damage yourself.
notes.poppy-situational-antiheal: Against a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce it, then upgrade it into a completed item if you are building defensive items. Poppy stays close to enemies for extended periods, making Grievous Wounds relatively easy to maintain.
notes.vs-poppy-w: When Poppy activates W, it stops dashes into the area around her, and enemies it stops briefly cannot use movement abilities. If your champion engages with a dash, wait until W ends or approach on foot instead of dashing in while it is active. W lasts only a short time, so waiting is almost always worthwhile.
notes.vs-poppy-r: When Poppy starts spinning her hammer, she is charging R. A longer charge extends the fissure and knocks enemies farther away, so move sideways out of the line directly in front of her when you see it. Poppy also slows down while charging, making it easier to create distance.
notes.vs-poppy-e: Poppy’s E only stuns and deals bonus damage if it knocks you into terrain. Keep your back away from walls and narrow passages and position in open space, where E will only push you. In lane, what is behind you can determine the outcome of a trade.
notes.vs-poppy-passive: Poppy’s thrown shield lands on the ground and is destroyed if an enemy steps on it. Denying the pickup prevents her from gaining a shield, which can greatly change the outcome of a lane trade. It tends to land near walls, so anticipate the path Poppy will take to retrieve it and step on it first.
notes.vs-poppy-q: Poppy’s Q leaves a zone where it hits that detonates again shortly afterward. Its damage scales with maximum health, so it hurts champions who build health more; if the first hit lands, walk out of the zone immediately.
notes.vs-poppy-lowhp: As Poppy’s health falls, the Armor and Magic Resist from W’s passive increase. A low health Poppy can turn an attempted finish into a counterattack, so go for the kill only when you are sure your guaranteed damage is enough.
notes.pyke-combo-qe: For a basic kill combo, hold Q to pull the target, use E as soon as they are pulled in, then follow with a basic attack and R. E must come immediately after Q lands so the phantom stuns them just as they can move again; leave a gap and they can escape with Flash.
notes.pyke-combo-r-engage: R can also start an engage: immediately after arriving, hold Q to pull the target or follow up with E. Enemies with plenty of health are less likely to expect R, giving them less time to react.
notes.pyke-skill-passive: P stores some of the damage Pyke takes from enemy champions and heals him when he leaves their vision. After going in, break vision with W or a brush to heal before engaging again; if the healing has not started, the enemy can still see you.
notes.pyke-skill-passive-ad: Pyke converts all bonus maximum health into attack damage, regardless of its source, so health items improve both durability and damage. Armor or magic resistance alone adds no damage.
notes.pyke-skill-q: Tap Q to stab forward, or hold it to throw a harpoon that pulls the target. You do not need to throw from maximum range: even a half charged harpoon at close range pulls the same distance. If the channel ends early or Q hits an enemy champion, you recover most of its mana cost, so canceling a poor attempt costs little.
notes.pyke-skill-w: W camouflages Pyke until he enters an enemy champion’s detection range, letting him cross a route he would normally have to go around and approach from an unexpected angle. In a one on one trade, it is often better to save W to trigger P’s healing after taking damage.
notes.pyke-skill-e: E stuns when the phantom left at Pyke’s starting point returns to him, rather than during the dash itself. Keep the target on the line between your starting and ending points to land the stun. Because E serves as both an engage and an escape, decide before going in whether E or allied crowd control will give you a way out.
notes.pyke-skill-r: R teleports Pyke to and executes enemies below its health threshold within the X shaped area, but deals only half damage to those above it. The execution threshold rises with bonus attack damage and lethality, expanding your kill opportunities as you gain items. If a target is still too healthy to execute, lower their health with Q and E before using R.
notes.pyke-skill-r-gold: When Pyke kills an enemy with R, the last ally who assisted receives the full kill gold, while Pyke gets a separate reward. Use it without hesitation on targets an ally has damaged. If an enemy champion dies within R’s X shaped area, you can cast it again for a short time, so execute the lowest health target first in teamfights to keep the recasts going.
notes.pyke-phase: Kill opportunities begin at level 2, when Pyke has both Q and E, and his power rises sharply at level 6 when he learns R. He peaks on completing his first core lethality item; from then on, roam to pressure other lanes. Late in the game, enemies with more health are harder to bring below the execution threshold, and Pyke is fragile enough to die first in teamfights.
notes.pyke-laning: Pyke is a support who takes almost no CS and grows through kills. In lane, move between brushes and blind spots to keep opponents under pressure within Q range, then look to engage together after your ADC pushes the wave. One heavy hit can erase that opportunity, so avoid forcing the first attack.
notes.pyke-laning-w-pressure: Simply activating W can make opponents back away as they worry about a gank, a close range Q, or getting caught. Use that pressure to secure river vision or roam mid, even without closing in. Roam only when the wave is pushing toward the enemy and your ADC can hold the lane alone.
notes.pyke-teamfight: In teamfights, Pyke should eliminate the most dangerous enemy in the backline. After allied crowd control lands and holds the enemy’s attention, enter from the flank with W while leaving yourself an escape route. If other enemies are grouped around a low health target, aim R to secure the execution and area damage together.
notes.vs-pyke-w-vision: When Pyke uses W nearby, a shark shadow circles beneath your feet. Seeing it means he is already in range, so move toward your allies or retreat under your turret. Cover brush entrances with control wards to limit his W approach angles.
notes.vs-pyke-e: Prioritize dodging E: its phantom stuns along the line between Pyke’s starting and ending points, so move sideways off his path to avoid it. If E misses, Pyke is left where he cannot easily continue the engage or escape.
notes.vs-pyke-r: Do not stand next to a low health ally. If Pyke executes them with R, anyone else in the X shaped area takes damage, and he can use R again immediately. Wounded allies should spread out in teamfights to break the chain of executions.
notes.vs-pyke-passive: Pyke heals his stored health only after leaving vision. After a trade, ward toward him as he retreats or follow while keeping him in sight to prevent the healing from starting.
notes.vs-pyke-antiheal: Pyke’s sustain comes entirely from P’s healing, and he builds little in the way of defensive stats. Grievous Wounds disrupts his repeated engage and disengage cycle, so if you deal physical damage, buy Executioner’s Calling earlier than usual.
notes.vs-pyke-late: Pyke struggles to bring high health targets below his execution threshold, and a champion with health items will not die to a single R late in the game. Keep squishy allies he might target behind the frontline and move together.
notes.pyke-combo-w-approach: To approach from outside vision, use W to close in while camouflaged, tap Q once in range, then use E. A tapped Q casts much faster, so there is no need to charge it at close range.
notes.qiyana-skill-element: Qiyana’s decisions start with the element she takes using W: river ice adds a root to Q, wall or rock adds damage against enemies below half health, and brush makes her invisible and faster inside the area created by Q, helping her approach or escape. Before a fight, decide which element you need and move toward that terrain first.
notes.qiyana-skill-w-reset: W is a movement ability that also resets Q’s cooldown. After using Q, take a different element with W to use Q again immediately. Taking a new element also resets Royal Privilege’s cooldown on every target, letting you deal its bonus damage twice to the same enemy. Using W only as a dash gives up much of your combo damage.
notes.qiyana-skill-q-range: Without an element, Q is a short melee swing; holding one extends its range. Avoid putting Q on cooldown without an element out of habit, or it may be unavailable when you need to close the gap. Even when farming with Q, first check for nearby terrain you can target with W. E costs a lot of mana, so clear waves with the bonus basic attack damage and attack speed you gain while holding an element instead.
notes.qiyana-skill-e-autotarget: E dashes through its target, carrying Qiyana behind them. Press Q during an E dash toward a champion and it automatically targets that champion, so follow E immediately with Q to land it without having to aim. E is your only targeted way in; do not waste it on minions.
notes.qiyana-skill-r-terrain: R sends out a shockwave that knocks enemies back. If it reaches a wall, river, or brush, the entire edge of that terrain explodes, so aim along the line between the enemy and the terrain. Hitting a long stretch of river extends the explosion’s area, while the stun lasts longer the farther the shockwave travels. Look to fight in narrow passages or by the river.
notes.qiyana-combo-basic: For a basic assassination combo, take an element with W, dash to the target with E, cast Q during the dash, and land a basic attack. Then use W on a different terrain type to reset Q’s cooldown and Royal Privilege before casting Q again. Use E before that second W so it provides both the reset and an escape route. While holding an element, Qiyana gains attack speed and bonus basic attack damage, so always weave basic attacks between abilities.
notes.qiyana-combo-ult: To finish an enemy, use R to knock them into a wall and stun them, then switch elements with W and land Q and a basic attack during the stun. Saving R until the end can leave you pushing away an enemy who is already ready to escape. If you use Flash, reposition first, then cast R toward the terrain.
notes.qiyana-combo-bush: Brush element Q makes Qiyana invisible inside the area it creates. While the enemy has lost sight of you, use E and W to set up an ambush; when chased, use it to break pursuit. You are revealed as soon as you leave the area, so plan your W path to the next piece of terrain while still inside it.
notes.qiyana-laning-trade: In lane, keep trades short and use brush to approach: take the brush element, land E and Q, then immediately use W on different terrain to get out. Staying in the middle of the lane after spending all three abilities leaves Qiyana open to retaliation. Her level-one health is relatively low, so avoid extended fights against ranged opponents and strike when they step forward to last-hit a minion.
notes.qiyana-laning-wave: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Qiyana ranks low in CS at 14 minutes but near the top in damage per minute and kills. She gains advantages by pushing waves and moving to side lanes and the jungle, rather than staying in lane to farm CS. After pushing a wave toward the enemy turret, travel along the river to pick up an element naturally; leaving while the wave is pulled toward your side leaves you at a disadvantage.
notes.qiyana-phase: Qiyana becomes much stronger when she learns R at level 6. Before then, she is a melee champion limited to short trades; afterward, she can use terrain to secure a stun and get a solo kill. She peaks in the mid game with one or two core items. Later, defensive items make enemies harder to burst down, and her low durability makes engaging riskier. Use a mid-game lead to take objectives and push towers to close out the game sooner.
notes.qiyana-teamfight: In a teamfight, choose between opening with R to knock the enemy team into terrain and cleaning up the backline. If enemies group in a narrow passage or near the river or brush, engage with R. Otherwise, wait for an ally to engage and draw out enemy abilities, then use W and E to reach the backline. Go in once the enemy has used its targeted crowd control and defensive abilities on your engaging ally, and identify terrain you can target with W to retreat before committing.
notes.qiyana-situational-antiheal: If enemies sustain through healing, that healing can stop your assassination damage, so buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.qiyana-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team has a lot of crowd control that can lock down Qiyana when she engages, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item.
notes.vs-qiyana-terrain: Qiyana relies on terrain to take elements with W and trigger R’s explosion. Against her, stay in open ground away from walls, brush, and the river, where both are harder for her to use. Take routes through wide areas to avoid meeting her by the river or in a narrow passage.
notes.vs-qiyana-r: Qiyana’s R explodes when its knockback shockwave reaches terrain, and its stun lasts longer the farther the shockwave travels. Do not face her with your back to a wall. If R hits you, use a movement ability away from the terrain, since the explosion spreads along its entire edge.
notes.vs-qiyana-element: Watch Qiyana’s current element to anticipate her next move. If she approaches with the river element, back out of Q’s root range; if she disappears while holding the brush element, move into your allies’ vision. When you are below half health, keep your distance from a Qiyana holding the rock element before she can get close enough to finish you.
notes.vs-qiyana-cooldown: Qiyana is a fragile melee assassin, and once she has used W and E to engage, she is highly vulnerable to a counterattack. If you avoid her combo, strike back immediately afterward. In lane, trade with her if she remains forward after using all her abilities.
notes.vs-qiyana-lategame: Qiyana is strongest in the mid game and becomes relatively weaker later. Avoid giving her an advantage in the early and mid game, then build defensive stats and move together so she struggles to dive in and burst someone down alone. When grouped, prioritize standing away from terrain to deny her an R angle.
notes.quinn-combo-harrier: When a Harrier mark appears, hit the target with an auto, use the attack and movement speed from W's passive to land one or two more, then knock them back with E and retreat. Consuming the mark sooner brings the next one sooner, so keep trades short and repeat them in time with the mark cycle.
notes.quinn-combo-allin: For an all-in, dash with E, land an empowered auto as soon as you land, then follow with Q and more autos. E applies a Harrier mark directly to the target, so that first auto is always empowered and triggers W's passive for faster follow-up attacks. Saving E for the end loses that sequence.
notes.quinn-combo-e-direction: E reaches the target, then sends Quinn backward to land, so your approach determines where she ends up. Use it from the far side of an enemy to knock them toward your team while retreating to safety; with your back to a wall, you can also land on the other side of the terrain.
notes.quinn-skill-q: If Q first hits a non-champion, only that target is disabled; champions receive neither the mark nor reduced vision. In lane, wait for your opponent to step clear of the minion line before aiming at them. Q deals greatly increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for clearing camps or contesting objective steals.
notes.quinn-skill-w: W's passive is the core of the ability: attacking a Harrier-marked target grants both attack speed and movement speed, helping Quinn deal damage in a trade and get away. Save the active to locate the jungler or check vision around objectives and in bushes.
notes.quinn-skill-e: E follows its target even if they Flash or use a mobility ability to retreat deeper into enemy territory, which can leave Quinn landing in the middle of the enemy team. Before engaging, check whether the opponent's mobility ability is down and your team can follow up. Quinn has very low health and can die to a single crowd control effect.
notes.quinn-skill-r: R is a travel tool, not a damage ability. It activates only after the channel completes, and damage from anything other than minions ends its movement speed bonus, so take routes outside enemy vision. Push your lane before using R to reach another side lane, or use it to push the opposite lane right after a teamfight.
notes.quinn-skill-passive: Harrier periodically marks nearby enemies, and consuming a mark on a minion restarts the mark cycle too. If your opponent is within trading range, save the mark for them instead of using it on a minion; whether a mark is available can decide the trade.
notes.quinn-laning: Quinn has the range advantage over melee opponents in top lane. When one steps up for a last hit, land a marked auto and retreat immediately, repeating these short trades to chip away at their health. If they close in to retaliate, knock them back with E and escape. Marked poke alone can build a lane advantage without committing to a large trade.
notes.quinn-laning-wave: Quinn gets value after pushing her lane: shove the wave into the enemy turret, then use R to reach another lane or the enemy jungle and create a numbers advantage. If you lose ground in top lane while roaming, push it back out from the side. Holding the wave near your turret and playing defensively gives up Quinn's strengths.
notes.quinn-phase: Quinn's lane phase is strong as early as levels 1–2, when marked autos can pressure melee opponents. At level 6, R gives her mobility rather than damage and opens up the whole map; she peaks in the mid game after her first core item. Her low health and lack of sustained damage sharply limit her role in late-game front-to-back teamfights, so aim to end the game in the mid game or keep up side-lane pressure.
notes.quinn-teamfight: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Come in from the side or behind to finish targets your team has already caught, and save E to knock back an enemy who closes in and escape. Landing in the middle of the enemy team will get Quinn killed.
notes.quinn-teamfight-split: Pushing the opposite side lane is always an option instead of taking a front-to-back teamfight. If a fight looks likely, R lets you delay the decision to join: keep pushing if your team can hold out, but join early if they are likely to collapse.
notes.quinn-situational-antiheal: If your opponent sustains through your poke with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Quinn relies on short trades, and that poke loses its value if the opponent heals back the damage.
notes.vs-quinn-harrier: Quinn's poke hurts most when you have a Harrier mark. If you are marked, step outside her auto range and let it expire, then farm or start a trade while the mark is unavailable.
notes.vs-quinn-e: Quinn backs away as soon as E reaches you, making an immediate counterattack difficult, but she has no escape while E is down. Engage right after she uses it; until then, do not force your way in.
notes.vs-quinn-r: Damaging Quinn while she travels with R ends her movement speed bonus. If you lose track of her, place vision along side lanes or jungle routes and warn your team early when you spot a roam. After level 6, she excels at creating numbers advantages away from her own lane.
notes.vs-quinn-teamfight: Quinn has very low health and lacks staying power in front-to-back teamfights. Force fights as a team instead of taking her on one-on-one in a side lane; if she comes in from the flank, catch her with crowd control.
notes.vs-quinn-melee: Quinn outranges melee champions throughout lane, so focus on collecting CS and preserving health early. Do not try to engage her alone without jungle help; start a trade only after her E is down or your jungler arrives.
notes.vs-quinn-q: If Quinn's Q hits a minion first, it will not reduce a champion's vision, so stand behind the minion wave to block it. If your vision is reduced, hold your skillshots and focus on deciding whether to move in or back off.
notes.rakan-combo-engage: Open with W Grand Entrance to knock the enemy up, then use Q Gleaming Quill and an auto attack. W has two stages—a dash followed by a leap to its landing spot—so the enemy has time to move aside during the cast. Start from brush or outside vision and keep the travel distance short to land it.
notes.rakan-combo-r-w: After level 6, start an engage by touching an enemy with R The Quickness to charm them, then immediately knock them up with W Grand Entrance. R grants another large movement speed boost when it touches the first champion, and Rakan’s dash speed scales with his movement speed, so W travels farthest and fastest at that moment.
notes.rakan-combo-e-w-e: For an in-and-out combo, use E Battle Dance to reach an ally and move forward, knock the enemy up with W Grand Entrance, then recast E to return to your ally. The recast costs nothing but is available only for a short time after the first cast, so check that it is still available before using W.
notes.rakan-combo-q-heal: When Q Gleaming Quill hits a champion or epic monster, it heals Rakan and nearby allies after a short delay; touching an ally triggers the heal immediately. During trades, make a habit of landing Q and then using E Battle Dance to reach an ally, skipping the wait for the heal. W Grand Entrance can also bring you toward an ally right after Q.
notes.rakan-skill-passive: P Fey Feathers periodically grants Rakan a shield, and each auto attack or ability that hits an enemy champion reduces its cooldown. Poke with Q Gleaming Quill a few times before engaging so the shield is ready when you go in; having it up makes a substantial difference to your survival.
notes.rakan-skill-q: Q Gleaming Quill damages only the first enemy it hits, so a minion in front will absorb it. Throw Q from an angle clear of the minion line. Since its heal triggers only on a champion or epic monster, you must hit an enemy champion to get both poke and lane sustain.
notes.rakan-skill-w: W Grand Entrance is Rakan’s only way to force an engage and effectively his only escape. Using it to poke leaves you without a way to respond to a gank or counterattack. You can use W to engage when an ally is nearby for E Battle Dance, so check for an E target before committing.
notes.rakan-skill-e: E Battle Dance can only be cast on an allied champion, not a minion. Away from allies, Rakan is a melee champion without a mobility ability, so do not cross the jungle or areas without vision alone.
notes.rakan-skill-r: Activating R The Quickness gives Rakan a large movement speed boost and charms enemies he touches while rushing; the path you take determines whom it hits. Approach from an angle that lines up several enemies to charm them all, or use the speed to escape even if you touch no one.
notes.rakan-phase: Rakan’s poke is weak at level 1, so play quietly until level 2, when having both W Grand Entrance and E Battle Dance lets you go all in and get back out. R The Quickness brings a second power spike at level 6. His mobility has the most impact in the mid game; late in the game, his low health and defenses mean getting caught once right after engaging can kill him.
notes.rakan-laning: In lane, use Q Gleaming Quill to chip away at the enemy’s health while reducing the cooldown of P Fey Feathers’ shield. Start an all-in only when W Grand Entrance is available and an allied E Battle Dance target is close. Do not force the wave to push; catch the enemy marksman with W when they step in front of the minion line.
notes.rakan-laning-roam: With two mobility abilities, Rakan is one of the most effective roaming supports. Head mid right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret, then use E on your allied mid laner on the way back to cut travel time. For vision, use W and E to move deep and return safely to an ally.
notes.rakan-teamfight: Before a teamfight, decide whether to engage or protect. If your team needs to catch the enemy carries, charm multiple enemies with R The Quickness and follow with W Grand Entrance to knock them up. If you need to protect your carries, save W to knock up a diving enemy, then hold out with E Battle Dance’s shield and Q Gleaming Quill’s heal. Trying to split your role between the two makes it hard to do either well.
notes.rakan-situational-cc: Crowd control right after an engage can leave Rakan unable to act despite his mobility abilities. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove a root that catches you immediately after engaging.
notes.vs-rakan-w: Rakan’s W Grand Entrance dashes and then leaps to a landing spot that is visible beforehand. Step sideways as he starts moving to dodge the knockup; the farther away he starts, the easier it is to avoid.
notes.vs-rakan-e: Rakan can use E Battle Dance only on allied champions. Away from allies, he is effectively a melee champion without a mobility ability, so look to catch him alone while he roams or sets up vision.
notes.vs-rakan-cc: Rakan relies on going in and getting back out, making him very vulnerable to immediate crowd control. Use a stun or root that does not require aiming right after W Grand Entrance lands to stop his mobility; skillshots alone have a harder time catching him.
notes.vs-rakan-r: With R The Quickness active, Rakan charms enemies he touches as he passes. His movement speed makes escaping on foot impossible, so put terrain between you and him or apply crowd control before he touches you. Standing in a line lets him charm several of you at once.
notes.vs-rakan-passive: Rakan’s P Fey Feathers shield returns periodically, and each time he lands poke, it returns sooner. Trading while the shield is up puts you at a disadvantage; he is most vulnerable immediately after it breaks.
notes.rammus-combo-basic: The basic engage is to roll in with Q (Powerball), collide to knock back and slow the target, then use E (Frenzying Taunt) on a priority enemy, activate W (Defensive Ball Curl), and auto-attack. Turn on W just after the enemy starts hitting Rammus so its duration is not wasted before the engage.
notes.rammus-combo-qr: Use R (Soaring Slam) while Q (Powerball) is still rolling to knock enemies at the center of its area airborne; if Q has already collided and stopped, the knockup is lost. Cast R just before reaching the enemy, ideally after Q reaches maximum speed, since higher movement speed also expands R’s area.
notes.rammus-combo-taunt-tower: Near an allied turret, E (Frenzying Taunt) makes the target auto-attack Rammus, causing the turret to attack them. It is his most reliable way to counter a dive, so taunt an enemy under your turret instead of knocking them back with Q (Powerball).
notes.rammus-skill-q: Q (Powerball) gains movement speed the longer it rolls, so start it out of vision before a gank to arrive at maximum speed; starting when the enemy comes into view leaves you rolling in slowly. Colliding with an enemy, minion, or neutral monster stops Q, so choose a clear path, and recast it early if you need to change direction. When escaping, likewise head away from enemies and minions so the roll does not stop midway.
notes.rammus-skill-w: W (Defensive Ball Curl) greatly increases armor and magic resistance for a fixed duration and reflects damage to enemies who hit Rammus. Activate it after they actually start attacking rather than waiting with it on, then recast to end it early and start its cooldown sooner when it is no longer needed.
notes.rammus-skill-e-taunt: E (Frenzying Taunt) is targeted, so it cannot miss: the affected enemy walks toward Rammus and can only auto-attack. It interrupts casts and channels, preventing that enemy from damaging your team for the duration. Save it for one of the opposing team’s main damage dealers; casting it just as they try to escape with a mobility ability also renders that ability useless.
notes.rammus-skill-passive: Rammus’s passive, Spiked Shell, converts armor and magic resistance into attack damage, so building defensive stats also raises his auto-attack damage and turret destruction speed without forcing in offensive items. The stats gained while W (Defensive Ball Curl) is active count too.
notes.rammus-skill-r-tower: R (Soaring Slam) deals double damage to turrets. Combined with auto-attacks boosted by the stats from W (Defensive Ball Curl), it lets Rammus destroy turrets quickly on his own later in the game. If a teamfight stalls, disengage and attack structures.
notes.rammus-skill-r-zone: After Rammus lands, R produces repeated aftershocks in the same spot, stacking slows. It works as area denial rather than a burst of damage: place it in a narrow path enemies must cross or inside an objective pit, since using it where they have already escaped has no value.
notes.rammus-laning-jungle: Rammus ranks near the bottom overall in early CS and damage per minute, so he cannot win by competing on farm. Clear camps quickly, then use Q Powerball’s long engage range to spend time on ganks and objectives. His death rate is also among the highest, so when there is no good opening, the default is to use Q to get out.
notes.rammus-phase: At levels 1–2, Rammus clears camps slowly and deals almost no damage alone. Ganks become viable once he has both Q (Powerball) and E (Frenzying Taunt), and after learning R (Soaring Slam) at level 6, he can force fights over objectives. Defensive items also increase his damage through Spiked Shell, making the mid to late game his peak; later, turret destruction gives him another way to apply pressure.
notes.rammus-teamfight: In teamfights, Rammus aims to neutralize a main damage dealer in the enemy backline with E (Frenzying Taunt). Engage with Q (Powerball), taunt the target, and use R (Soaring Slam) to lock down that area. If no taunt target is reachable, stand in front of your carry instead and counter the enemy engage with Q’s knockback and E’s taunt.
notes.rammus-teamfight-vs-marksman: Against a ranged damage dealer who relies on auto-attacks, Rammus’s presence alone creates pressure: W (Defensive Ball Curl)’s reflected damage and E (Frenzying Taunt) mean they can neither safely attack him nor ignore him. Stay in their vision to keep them from auto-attacking, even without committing to an engage.
notes.rammus-situational-mr: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, stacking only armor is a disadvantage. Spiked Shell also converts magic resistance into attack damage, and W (Defensive Ball Curl) raises magic resistance, so buying Spirit Visage or Banshee’s Veil earlier does not reduce Rammus’s damage.
notes.vs-rammus-w-window: Rammus’s defensive stats become exceptionally high while W (Defensive Ball Curl) is active, but without it he is slightly less durable than a typical tank. Back off briefly when he activates W, then focus your damage the moment it ends.
notes.vs-rammus-armor: Rammus stacks armor to extreme levels and converts it into attack damage, so trying to bring him down with physical damage wastes time. Let allies with magic damage, true damage, or damage based on maximum health handle him.
notes.vs-rammus-autoattack: Auto-attacking Rammus while W is active deals reflected damage to the attacker, and faster attackers suffer more. Attack another target while W is up; unless you must kill Rammus, it is better to wait for it to end.
notes.vs-rammus-taunt: E (Frenzying Taunt) is targeted and cannot be dodged; once it lands, you cannot issue movement commands or use abilities. Fight outside its range, and plan to use Flash or a mobility ability immediately after the taunt ends rather than before it lands. Do not begin channeling an ability while Rammus is close.
notes.vs-rammus-q-block: Q needs time to build speed and stops where it hits something. To block Rammus's approach, stand behind a minion wave or inside a narrow passage.
notes.vs-rammus-r-range: R (Soaring Slam)’s area grows with Rammus’s movement speed, so an R cast from Q (Powerball) at maximum speed reaches much farther than it may appear. If you see him rolling toward you, give the expected area plenty of room and back away; after he lands, leave that spot immediately because repeated aftershocks stack slows there.
notes.reksai-skill-q: Unburrowed Q (Queen's Wrath) empowers Rek'Sai's next three basic attacks to hit nearby enemies, and each attack refreshes its duration. Keep attacking without interruption to make the most of its area damage when clearing jungle camps or fighting grouped enemies. Burrowed Q (Prey Seeker) instead fires soil from range and reveals enemies it hits. It is Rek'Sai's only ranged option, and damaging an enemy with it meets R's targeting requirement, letting her begin a catch from beyond melee range.
notes.reksai-skill-w-knockup: Using W to emerge while burrowed knocks up nearby enemies. Burrowed W is Rek'Sai's only guaranteed crowd control. Track the moving enemy's direction, move beneath them, and emerge with W.
notes.reksai-skill-e-fury: Unburrowed E deals true damage at maximum Fury. Build Fury with basic attacks and abilities, then finish with E. E's true damage at maximum Fury ignores the enemy's armor.
notes.reksai-skill-e-tunnel: Tunnels made with burrowed E last a long time and can be used again. Tunnel entrances are visible to enemies and break when they step on them. Dig a tunnel for escape before the fight starts.
notes.reksai-skill-r: R leaps to an enemy Rek'Sai has recently damaged. Rek'Sai cannot be targeted while underground during R. R's leap cannot be stopped midway. R deals damage based on maximum health. Landing with R resets W's cooldown.
notes.reksai-combo-gank: For a gank, approach while burrowed, emerge beneath the enemy with W to knock them up, then press Q immediately to land all three empowered basic attacks. Build Fury with attacks before finishing with E. If the target is already caught, walk up while unburrowed and start attacking instead; this deals more damage.
notes.reksai-combo-ult: Hit a fleeing enemy with burrowed Q, leap to them with R, then knock them up with W after landing. Right after damaging an enemy, use R to dodge a targeted ability, then escape through a tunnel you dug earlier. Before pressing R, check whether the landing spot is in the middle of the enemy team.
notes.reksai-laning-tunnelmap: Rek'Sai is not a jungler who gets ahead through farming alone. Early on, dig tunnels leading to lanes to create routes into multiple lanes. Dig tunnels in the enemy jungle to use for invasions and escapes.
notes.reksai-phase: Rek'Sai can influence the game through ganks from level 3, when she has W's knockup, through level 6, when she gains R; her peak comes in the mid game with her core items. Her relative damage falls later, and she is not especially durable, making it difficult to eliminate the backline alone. Build a lead through ganks and objectives early and in the mid game to end the game sooner, then shift to engaging with R and knocking up an enemy in late-game fights.
notes.reksai-teamfight: In teamfights, land behind the enemy team with R, then open the fight with a W knockup. Go in when your allies can follow up immediately and the enemy has used their crowd control to respond. Do not overcommit to chasing backline enemies; catch tanky enemies too.
notes.reksai-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rek'Sai stays close and keeps basic attacking, allowing her to maintain Grievous Wounds throughout a fight.
notes.reksai-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has plenty of crowd control that can lock Rek'Sai down on entry, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item. Getting caught immediately after going in with R can get her killed, so breaking that one lockdown is more valuable than adding more attack damage.
notes.vs-reksai-knockup: Rek'Sai's guaranteed crowd control is the knockup from W while burrowed. Use a mobility ability as Rek'Sai emerges to dodge the knockup. If you dodge Rek'Sai's W knockup, she loses her way to catch you.
notes.vs-reksai-tunnel: Rek'Sai's tunnel entrances are visible and break when an enemy steps on them. If you spot one near a lane or in your jungle, step on it as you pass. Destroying a tunnel removes both the gank route and the escape route it provides.
notes.vs-reksai-r: Rek'Sai's R can leap only to an enemy she has recently damaged. If her burrowed Q hits you, stay near your allies for the next few seconds, when she may leap in. She cannot be targeted during the leap, so save targeted abilities and place untargeted crowd control at her landing spot in advance.
notes.vs-reksai-phase: Rek'Sai aims to build a lead through early- and mid-game ganks and end the game quickly. Her farming and sustained-damage numbers are low, so denying her early kills and extending the game makes her easier to deal with. Early on, avoid pushing your lane too far or traveling alone through areas without vision.
notes.rell-combo-engage: For a standard engage, activate E Full Tilt to speed up alongside an ally and close the gap, knock enemies up with W Ferromancy: Crash Down, stun them with Q Shattering Strike, then pull them together with R Magnet Storm. E’s explosion triggers on whichever lands first, your next basic attack or Q, so using Q immediately after W delivers the stun and explosion together.
notes.rell-combo-remount: W lets Rell knock enemies up in both forms: after landing with Ferromancy: Crash Down, press W again to remount, gain movement speed, and knock up an enemy with your next basic attack. Remount only after the shield from Crash Down is depleted or when you need to catch a fleeing enemy, since the shield disappears as soon as you remount.
notes.rell-skill-q: Q Shattering Strike thrusts in a straight line, briefly stuns enemies, and destroys every shield on targets it hits. Against a support who grants shields, save Q until a shield appears; it cannot destroy monster shields.
notes.rell-skill-w: W switches between mounted and armored forms. While mounted, Rell gains movement speed to approach enemies; dismounting increases her armor, magic resistance, attack speed, and basic attack range but slows her sharply. Use armored form to withstand a fight already underway, then remount before moving to find the next one.
notes.rell-skill-e: E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one ally, with the increase doubling when they move toward an enemy or each other. Activate it just before engaging to close the gap; retreating after a fight no longer meets that condition and halves its effectiveness. Because Rell’s base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions, do not look for an engage while E is unavailable.
notes.rell-skill-passive: P Break the Mold steals and stacks an enemy’s armor and magic resistance whenever Rell hits them with a basic attack or ability. After using her crowd control, keep weaving in basic attacks in armored form to maintain the stacks and increase your allied damage dealer’s damage.
notes.rell-skill-r: R Magnet Storm pulls nearby enemies toward Rell and continues pulling briefly. Its range is short, so walking in to cast it alone leaves her exposed; use it immediately after W’s knockup or after an ally has already engaged to keep enemies from scattering.
notes.rell-phase: Rell starts with W’s knockup at level 1, and gaining Q at level 2 creates her first strong window: chaining the knockup into a stun can force the enemy marksman to use an escape tool. R at level 6 brings a second power spike, and she peaks in the mid game as she builds defensive items. Late in the game, her short range and lack of an escape after engaging mean a solo engage can get her killed.
notes.rell-laning: Rell struggles to reach enemies on foot, so laning depends on vision and brush. Pull the wave toward your turret and engage from brush only when an enemy enters W Ferromancy: Crash Down range. Once you close the gap, stay in armored form and keep trading with basic attacks, which gain range and attack speed.
notes.rell-laning-roam: Activate E Full Tilt when setting out to roam: moving toward the river or mid with your marksman speeds up both of you. Roam right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret, and account for Rell’s slow movement speed when timing your return so you do not lose the bot turret.
notes.rell-teamfight: In teamfights, Rell’s job is to group enemies for her allies’ area abilities. Engage only when your allies are ready to follow and at least two enemies will be within R Magnet Storm range when you cast it. If the enemy team is spread out, stay in armored form in front of your allied damage dealer and absorb the dive.
notes.rell-situational-mr: Rell’s level 1 magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions. If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance first and move Spirit Visage earlier in your build; if a single burst is the problem rather than sustained damage, use Banshee’s Veil to block one engage ability.
notes.rell-situational-armor: If the enemy’s physical damage is strong, buy Plated Steelcaps and build armor first. Against a team that deals damage through basic attacks, prioritize Frozen Heart over Thornmail to protect your allied damage dealer too.
notes.vs-rell-w: Rell’s only forced engage is W Ferromancy: Crash Down, which has very short range. When mounted, she is looking to engage; after dismounting into armored form, her movement speed is among the slowest in the game. Stay outside Crash Down range, then create distance as soon as she uses W to leave her isolated.
notes.vs-rell-q: Rell’s Q, Shattering Strike, destroys every shield it hits, so wait until after she uses it to shield yourself; you can also dodge its straight-line thrust by stepping to the side.
notes.vs-rell-e: If Rell and an ally suddenly speed up together, E Full Tilt is active and an engage is coming. The speed increase doubles when Rell runs toward you, so stop trading at that moment and retreat beyond W Ferromancy: Crash Down range.
notes.vs-rell-r: R Magnet Storm is most effective when it pulls several nearby enemies together, so spread out from your allies before a teamfight engage to limit it to one target. If you have already been pulled in, do not try to walk out against the continuing pull; use a movement ability or cleanse while it lasts.
notes.vs-rell-early: Rell has one of the lowest early magic resistance values of any champion and no way to heal in lane. If your team can poke with magic damage, keep wearing her down from outside her engage range until she has to recall first.
notes.rell-combo-flash: W Ferromancy: Crash Down immediately hits the area around Rell, making it effective with Flash: close the gap with Flash, press W to knock enemies up, then follow with Q Shattering Strike to stun them.
notes.renata-combo-q: Q (Handshake) roots the first enemy it hits, then can be recast to throw them in a chosen direction. Enemies struck by a thrown champion are stunned, making Q a way to start a fight with multiple stuns: throw a target into grouped enemies to stun several, or toward your allies when they need to close the gap.
notes.renata-combo-q-direction: Without a recast, Q (Handshake) only roots its target. Throw a fleeing enemy toward your allies to close the distance, or throw one who has jumped onto an ally in any direction that moves them away. The cursor determines the throw direction, so move it as soon as the root lands, then recast.
notes.renata-combo-order: To start a fight, slow the target with E (Loyalty Program), root them with Q (Handshake), then recast Q to throw them where you want; E’s slow helps the slow Q projectile land. To save an ally, use W (Bailout) before E’s shield, since W cannot be used after they die.
notes.renata-skill-passive: Your basic attack mark can be on only one target at a time; when an ally hits that target, the mark is consumed and deals bonus damage. Because the damage scales with maximum health, it works against the enemy frontline too. In lane, a single basic attack on the enemy marksman leaves a mark that increases your allied marksman’s trade damage.
notes.renata-skill-w-nature: W (Bailout) strengthens an ally and delays their death. If they die, they briefly revive at full health before gradually losing it, and a takedown during that time lets them survive. W is a bet on whether that ally can secure a takedown now, so use it on someone currently dealing damage rather than someone certain to die.
notes.renata-skill-w-timing: W has a long cooldown. Use W on your main damage dealer just before a fight to increase their attack speed and movement speed. W's duration refreshes when its target gets a takedown.
notes.renata-skill-e: E (Loyalty Program) fires missiles that damage and slow enemies while shielding allies. When an ally and enemy line up, fire through your allied damage dealer toward the enemy to affect both at once. Its short cooldown makes E your main lane trading tool, and its slow can also start a fight.
notes.renata-skill-r-frenzy: Enemies hit by R are forced to attack nearby units, prioritizing their own allies. Use R when the enemies it hits are close enough to attack one another. Don't use R on an isolated enemy.
notes.renata-skill-r-timing: Land R right after the enemy engage composition jumps in together. Enemies hit by R gain a large amount of attack speed. Move an isolated ally near an enemy hit by R out of the berserk range.
notes.renata-laning: Renata Glasc’s level-one health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, so stay back. In lane, support your ally’s trades with E (Loyalty Program)’s shield and briefly apply your basic attack mark. Save Q (Handshake) for when the enemy support steps forward or a gap opens between minions.
notes.renata-laning-trade: Hit the enemy with E (Loyalty Program) as they step forward to last-hit. It damages and slows them while shielding your allied marksman, letting one cast start and finish the trade. Stay back while E is on cooldown.
notes.renata-phase: Renata Glasc is weak at level one with only one ability, but learning Q (Handshake) creates kill opportunities. Her strength rises sharply at level six, when R (Hostile Takeover) can shut down an enemy engage composition. She deals almost no damage herself late in the game, yet saving allies and disrupting the enemy formation remain useful until the end.
notes.renata-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your allied frontline instead of engaging. Use Q to interrupt the enemy's engage. Use Q to throw an enemy damage dealer toward your allies. Use W and E to help allies survive fights.
notes.renata-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing your allies’ damage, buy Blighting Jewel first to apply healing reduction. Renata Glasc can keep it active with steady damage from her basic attack mark and E (Loyalty Program).
notes.vs-renata-r: If Renata Glasc’s R (Hostile Takeover) hits you, you briefly lose control and attack nearby allies. Cleanse it immediately if you can; otherwise, move away from your allies as soon as it hits to reduce the damage. Save Cleanse or Quicksilver Sash while you are within R’s range.
notes.vs-renata-r-spacing: Enemies affected by Renata Glasc’s R (Hostile Takeover) prioritize attacking their own allies, so grouping up makes it more damaging. While R is available, leave space between teammates as you engage and avoid charging in with all five players lined up together.
notes.vs-renata-q: Renata Glasc’s Q (Handshake) roots only the first target it hits, so stand behind minions or your frontline to let them take it. If you are rooted, decide immediately whether to escape with Flash or a mobility ability, since Renata Glasc chooses where to throw you. The throw can stun your allies too.
notes.vs-renata-w: An enemy affected by Renata Glasc’s W (Bailout) briefly revives and keeps fighting after dying; a takedown during that time lets them survive. After killing a W target, back away to keep your allies from dying nearby. Overcommitting to kill the revived enemy again can give them the takedown they need to live.
notes.vs-renata-e: Renata Glasc’s E (Loyalty Program) shields allies while damaging and slowing enemies. It travels in a straight line, so dodging sideways can also spoil its shielding angle. Since Renata Glasc herself deals little damage, targeting her is quicker than focusing only on dodging E.
notes.vs-renata-body: Renata Glasc has among the lowest level-one health and attack damage of any champion and no mobility ability of her own. If your composition can reach her, killing her first is the surest answer. Pressuring Renata Glasc directly in lane also leaves her less room to use her engage abilities.
notes.renekton-combo-basic: In lane, engage with E → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q → E to disengage. W replaces your next basic attack, so weaving it between attacks costs nothing; the first E dash must hit a unit to unlock the second. This engage, trade, disengage sequence is Renekton’s basic poke pattern. If you expect to lose a longer trade, shorten it to E → W → basic attack → Q → E.
notes.renekton-combo-allin: For a kill, build Fury, then use E → empowered W → Q → basic attack → E. Empowered W stuns long enough to land both Q and the attack; empowered abilities generate no Fury, so pack your damage into that stun. From level 6 onward, activate R just before engaging. It grants bonus maximum health and steadily generates Fury, giving you resources for a second combo or a dive even if you started with none. Its bonus health disappears when R ends, so make use of its duration.
notes.renekton-skill-fury: Basic attacks build Fury in fixed amounts, and Q, W, and E also generate it when they hit enemies; out of combat, it steadily drains. Build it with minion last hits and basic attacks just before trading. If you lack enough Fury, engage with E, hit both your opponent and minions with Q, then follow with empowered W. Choose empowered Q for its increased healing in a simple trade or when you need sustain, and empowered W for its longer stun when you have kill pressure. Ability haste is especially valuable to Renekton because it speeds up both Fury generation and spending.
notes.renekton-skill-q: Q Cull the Meek hits everyone nearby, healing Renekton for each target struck; empowered Q increases both its damage and healing. Using it where a minion wave overlaps an enemy champion can restore a lot of health, letting you bait the opponent in by appearing low on health and turn the fight with a single empowered Q. With nothing to hit, it provides no sustain, so use it only when targets are in range.
notes.renekton-skill-w: W, Ruthless Predator, replaces Renekton’s next basic attack, cancels its animation, activates immediately, and reaches slightly farther. Against an opponent walking away, use W after a basic attack to catch them; Flash → W can also deliver a surprise stun. Empowered W breaks the target’s shield before its third hit, making it especially useful against opponents who rely on shields.
notes.renekton-skill-e: The first E, Slice and Dice, must hit a unit to unlock the second dash. Before engaging, choose a minion or opponent to hit so you retain a way out. Its empowered armor reduction applies only to the second cast, so spending Fury on E is a low priority unless an allied physical damage dealer will keep attacking the same target.
notes.renekton-phase: Renekton poses little threat at levels 1–2 while his abilities are incomplete, but spikes at level 3 with Q, W, and E and again at level 6 with R. He can dominate lane and objective fights through the mid game as core items arrive. With no sustained damage abilities and generally long cooldowns, though, he struggles if a fight continues after his combo. His value drops sharply late, so turn an early lead into objectives and lane pressure.
notes.renekton-situational-armor: If your opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps early. If you keep losing trades, get Chain Vest first to survive lane; against multiple enemy physical damage dealers, follow up with Randuin’s Omen for armor and health.
notes.renekton-situational-antiheal: If an opponent’s healing turns trades in their favor, fit Executioner’s Calling between core items. Renekton relies on short combos, and he loses that advantage when the opponent heals back a combo’s damage.
notes.renekton-laning: In lane, keep your Fury near half full through last hits and Q farming, but avoid hitting minions so often that you push the wave and expose yourself to a gank. Engage just after your opponent uses a poke ability. Once you have used W and E, avoid aggressive positioning until both are off cooldown.
notes.renekton-teamfight: In teamfights, Renekton’s job is to land empowered W on a key enemy damage dealer and disengage with E, rather than stand at the front. His threat fades after his combo because he lacks sustained damage, so plan both a target for the first E dash and your R timing before going in. If the enemy frontline is sturdy, approach from the side and target the backline instead of forcing your way through.
notes.vs-renekton-fury: Watch Renekton’s Fury bar to judge his threat. Above half, stay out of range of empowered W’s long stun; just below half can be even more dangerous, since one basic attack or Q may give him enough Fury for an empowered ability. Force a trade when the bar is empty and his damage is much lower.
notes.vs-renekton-deny-fury: Renekton needs to fight to build Fury. Keep poking without giving him a target to engage on, and he will rarely get to use empowered abilities while his Fury drains out of combat. When he steps forward to hit minions for Fury, use that opening to poke him.
notes.vs-renekton-post-combo: Renekton has no sustained damage abilities and his cooldowns are long. If you survive his first combo, counterattack while Q, W, and E are on cooldown and he has only basic attacks left. He is especially vulnerable just after using E to disengage.
notes.vs-renekton-e: Renekton gets a second E dash only when the first hits a unit. Avoid standing in or behind your minion wave: those minions can let him engage from farther away. If you are the only target, he can instead hit you to unlock his escape. After taking his combo, retreat in a direction with no unit for his E to hit.
notes.vs-renekton-shield: Renekton’s empowered W Ruthless Predator breaks the target’s shield before dealing damage. When he has Fury built up, a shield cannot absorb his combo; use shields for sustain after taking the combo and backing away.
notes.vs-renekton-scaling: Renekton becomes much more threatening at levels 3 and 6. While R is active, its bonus health and Fury generation make a one-on-one fight dangerous, so wait out its duration. Farm without giving him kills through the mid game, and the matchup improves as his value falls.
notes.rengar-skill-passive-leap: Leaping from brush with no Ferocity grants one stack.
notes.rengar-skill-q: Q Savagery empowers your next basic attack and increases attack speed; it is not a separate damage ability. Press Q right after a basic attack to fill the gap between attacks, since pressing it early wastes the time before the empowered attack lands. At maximum Ferocity, Q grants much more damage and attack speed, so use it only when you can reliably stay on the target.
notes.rengar-skill-w: W Battle Roar restores some of the damage taken in the recent past, so use it immediately after a heavy hit to heal more. At maximum Ferocity, W removes crowd control; save Ferocity for it if the enemy still has an immobilizing ability. It also deals bonus damage to jungle monsters and restores a large portion of damage taken, making it central to managing your health while clearing.
notes.rengar-skill-e: E Bola Strike briefly reveals the location of the first enemy it hits, making it both a damage ability and a scouting tool. If you lose sight of someone during a chase, throw it along their expected path to locate them; it can also find enemies hiding in brush. At maximum Ferocity, E roots instead of slowing, so spend Ferocity on it when you need to hold an enemy without a mobility ability in place. E has no cast time during a leap, allowing you to throw it in midair.
notes.rengar-combo-burst: Use W in a combo right after the enemy retaliates.
notes.rengar-combo-choose: Choose where to spend Ferocity based on how the enemy can survive: use empowered E to root someone who can escape, empowered W to remove an immobilizing counterattack once you have reached them, or empowered Q to maximize damage if they can neither escape nor retaliate. Make that choice before engaging so you can act immediately after the leap.
notes.rengar-laning-clear: Focus on W when clearing the jungle: it deals bonus damage to monsters and restores much of the damage Rengar has taken, keeping him healthy. Because his resource is not mana, ability costs do not limit him, allowing him to clear camps in succession and gank often.
notes.rengar-laning-gank: Engaging with E first from an angle without brush gives the enemy time to react before you reach them.
notes.rengar-phase: Before level 6, Rengar’s ganks depend on brush and can be inconsistent; statistically, his deaths by 14 minutes are also relatively high among junglers. He is strongest in the mid game, once he has R and his first core item, and should use that window to pick off backline enemies. As enemy vision and defensive items make engages much harder late in the game, use the lead built in mid game to finish it.
notes.rengar-teamfight: In teamfights, Rengar’s job is to kill backline enemies. Use R’s vision to locate a target, then circle around to engage from the side or behind once the enemy has used its immobilizing abilities on your frontline. Plan an escape route before going in: after dealing burst damage, use W’s healing and empowered W’s crowd control removal to get out.
notes.rengar-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rengar deals damage in a short burst, so a single heal just before a kill is secured can easily turn the outcome.
notes.vs-rengar-ferocity: When Rengar’s resource bar is full, his next ability is empowered: Q deals more damage, E roots, and W removes crowd control. He is a very different threat with a full bar, so trade with him only when it is empty.
notes.vs-rengar-r: R, Thrill of the Hunt, gives Rengar camouflage and a large movement speed boost, so do not travel alone while injured. His camouflage ends when he enters an enemy champion’s detection range; stay close to allies and overlap your detection ranges to reveal him before he leaps. R also ends with a leap toward the nearest enemy, so keep the backline behind the frontline to divert him from his intended target.
notes.vs-rengar-w: Use immobilizing abilities and burst damage right after Rengar uses W.
notes.vs-rengar-e: Use mobility abilities after Rengar misses E.
notes.vs-rengar-punish: E is Rengar’s only immobilizing ability, and he has low health. Counter his engage, then hold him in place with an immobilizing ability; W’s healing alone will not keep him alive. Backline champions should stay behind their frontline and within allied vision so that the frontline becomes the target of his leap.
notes.rengar-skill-passive-ferocity: Each non-ultimate ability builds Ferocity. At maximum stacks, your next ability is empowered. Using an empowered ability briefly increases your movement speed. Choose carefully whether to use the empowered ability on Q, W, or E. Using empowered abilities carelessly drops your damage to that of an average melee champion. Each time you help take down a different enemy champion, your necklace gains a trophy, permanently increasing your attack damage. Prioritize a certain kill over other gains.
notes.rengar-skill-r-scout: R Thrill of the Hunt does not camouflage you immediately: there is a brief delay during which you gain vision around the nearest enemy champion. Use that vision to locate your target before approaching. You become visible if you enter an enemy's detection range while camouflaged, so take a wide route around the side or back instead of approaching from the front.
notes.riven-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use Q1 → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q3. The key is weaving in basic attacks, not memorizing the order: casting Q repeatedly leaves no time for them and cuts your damage in half.
notes.riven-combo-cancel: Press Q (Broken Wings) before Riven’s basic attack animation ends to cancel its recovery with the Q dash, then cancel Q’s recovery with a basic attack, E (Valor), or W (Ki Burst). Her damage comes from fitting more basic attacks into the same window through these cancels, not from ability scaling. If you haven’t mastered them, reliably landing one basic attack will deal more damage than forcing a cancel.
notes.riven-combo-burst: For a kill, close in with E, then use Q1 → basic attack → W stun → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → Q3 knockup. Activate R while the target is airborne and finish with Wind Slash; it deals more damage the more health the target has lost, so use it at the end of the combo.
notes.riven-skill-q-cursor: If your cursor is over a champion when you cast Q, the dash direction locks toward them. To dash past an opponent, place the cursor beyond them; casting Q with the cursor over them stops you in front.
notes.riven-skill-passive: Each ability charges Riven’s blade through Runic Blade (P), and basic attacks consume those charges. Because charges have a cap, using abilities repeatedly without basic attacks wastes any additional charges. Even while clearing a wave, leave yourself a chance to spend them on the opposing champion.
notes.riven-skill-w: W is a stun with a very short radius around Riven, so get close with Q or E before using it or it will miss. It can also interrupt channeled ultimates; if the opponent is poised to channel an ability, save W instead of spending it in a trade.
notes.riven-skill-e: E (Valor) gives Riven both a dash and a shield. Because the shield scales with bonus attack damage, it remains useful for defense into the late game even if you build only attack items. E cannot cross terrain; use the third Q (Broken Wings) to go over walls. If you use E to engage, account for having only your third Q left to disengage.
notes.riven-skill-r: Activating R increases Riven’s attack damage and the range of her basic attacks and abilities, letting her Q and basic attacks reach farther than the opponent expects. Wind Slash can be used only once while R is active, so save it unless it will secure the finish and keep fighting with R’s bonus attack damage.
notes.riven-laning: Riven uses no resources and can trade whenever her abilities come off cooldown, but she is most vulnerable just after spending all her Q casts to clear minions. When pushing a wave, save at least one cast so you can respond to a counterattack.
notes.riven-phase: Riven is weak at levels 1–2 because she has only one or two abilities and long cooldowns. With Q, W, and E available at level 3, she can look for a kill with a full combo; adding R at level 6 gives her first power spike. She is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability haste and attack damage, but in the late game she cannot break through a frontline with increased health and armor alone, so choose your engage carefully.
notes.riven-teamfight: Riven should avoid fighting the frontline head-on. Aim to reach the enemy backline from a flank or out of vision with E (Valor) and the third Q (Broken Wings), checking before you engage whether you’ll have a Q cast left to disengage. She has no self-healing, and her E shield is her only protection, so if there’s no opening to engage, pushing a side lane is the better choice.
notes.riven-teamfight-multi-melee: Riven fares well in scrappy fights against multiple melee champions because Q3 and W can hit several enemies at once.
