A ranged damage dealer attacking from a safe distance is her worst situation; if you cannot close the gap, wait for another opening rather than forcing an engage.
notes.riven-situational-antiheal: If the opponent is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early. Riven relies on burst damage in a short window, and active healing can keep the target alive even after the full combo lands.
notes.vs-riven-mobility: Riven can travel a long distance by chaining three Q dashes and one E dash, so if you have pushed too far beyond vision, first check whether all her dash abilities are available. Each dash is short, though; if you back away as soon as you see the first one, the remaining dashes are unlikely to reach you.
notes.vs-riven-cc: Riven’s combo depends on chaining abilities and basic attacks closely together. A root or silence after the combo begins interrupts her remaining Q and W casts and greatly reduces her damage, so save crowd control until just after she reaches you.
notes.vs-riven-physical: All of Riven’s damage is physical, so building armor alone can change the outcome of a trade. If she starts getting ahead, buy armor items earlier.
notes.vs-riven-wave: Counterattack when Riven uses Q to clear minions: spending it on the wave removes both her main damage source and an escape tool. Before she gets ability haste items, its long cooldown leaves a substantial opening, so take advantage of that moment, especially early on.
notes.vs-riven-ult: While R is active, Riven gains attack damage and range, allowing her abilities to reach you from farther away. She is especially dangerous while Wind Slash is available because it deals more damage the more health you have lost, leaving you unsafe even near your turret when your health is low. Keep your distance until R expires.
notes.vs-riven-channel: Riven’s Q3 and W can interrupt channeled ultimates. Avoid starting one while she is close; wait until you have seen her use up Q or spend W.
notes.riven-skill-q-terrain: Only Q’s third cast can cross terrain, and it knocks up nearby enemies. To escape or chase over a wall, use the first two casts beforehand and save the third; spending Q3 on damage during a trade removes that escape route.
notes.rumble-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use E → E → Q: the first E slows the enemy, and landing the second on that slowed target greatly amplifies the slow and magic resistance reduction, letting you keep them in range of Q’s short cone for its full duration. If you activate Q after only one E, they can simply walk away.
notes.rumble-combo-heat: In fights, land one E to enter the Danger Zone, then activate Q. Most of Rumble’s damage comes from the empowered Q; using it outside the Danger Zone costs the same cooldown but delivers only half the value. Casting abilities without a plan can push Heat close to overheat and leave no room to activate Q when you need it.
notes.rumble-combo-r: Use R to cut off the enemy’s escape route, then slow them with E and follow with Q. You can drag during R’s cast to change its trajectory, so watch where they will flee before setting the final angle. If you are already winning the fight, R is more valuable as a barrier to their escape than as a source of damage.
notes.rumble-skill-passive: Heat rises whenever you use an ability and falls when you do nothing. Staying in the Danger Zone is central to playing Rumble, so choose your ability order based on your current Heat instead of pressing each ability as it comes off cooldown. If you can secure a kill at melee range, you can deliberately overheat for empowered basic attacks, but account for the silence: you will have no ability to help you escape.
notes.rumble-skill-q: Q projects a continuous cone while active, so move and turn to keep the enemy inside it. It deals reduced damage to minions, making it inefficient for wave clear; spending the whole cast on farming leaves Q unavailable when a trade starts. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it especially strong against tanks.
notes.rumble-skill-w: W grants a shield and a brief movement speed boost. Because Rumble has no mobility ability, that speed is effectively his only way to engage or disengage, and both the shield and boost grow stronger in the Danger Zone. Build Heat first, then use W as you close in rather than activating it hurriedly just before taking a hit.
notes.rumble-skill-e: E is Rumble’s ranged poke and his only source of reach, with up to two shots stored. Landing both in succession amplifies the slow enough to keep an enemy within Q range, while the magic resistance reduction also benefits allied mages. If you stand in front of the wave after spending both shots, you have no way to close in or escape.
notes.rumble-skill-r: R is an area denial tool before it is a damage tool. It is more reliable when drawn between the enemy frontline and backline to separate them, or across their retreat path after a fight has begun, than when used to open a teamfight. It is most valuable in narrow passages, so inspect the terrain around objectives beforehand.
notes.rumble-laning: Rumble has no separate resource to spend, so he can keep casting, but Q has short range and he has no mobility ability. In lane, chip away safely with E, then slow the enemy with E and move in with Q only when they step forward to last-hit. Activating Q without an opening to get close builds Heat without dealing damage.
notes.rumble-laning-gank: Rumble is very vulnerable to ganks because he has no mobility ability and needs to step forward to play. If you have pushed the lane too far, check river vision first. In areas without vision, save W for escape.
notes.rumble-phase: Rumble’s magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions, putting him at a major disadvantage against magic damage from levels 1–2. His health and armor rank high, though, so he can take early trades against physical damage melee opponents. His ability to influence lanes rises sharply when he learns R at level 6, and he peaks in the mid game as he builds ability power; late in the game, he can die before reaching the enemy.
notes.rumble-teamfight: In teamfights, position just in front of the enemy frontline so Q’s cone covers multiple targets. Rumble has no way to dive the backline, so avoid assassination attempts and use E to lower enemies’ magic resistance, increasing allied mages’ damage as well. Always enter after your frontline.
notes.rumble-situational-mr: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, Rumble’s extremely low magic resistance becomes a weakness. Buy Force of Nature between core items to survive longer while staying close. Since Rumble must remain near enemies to deal damage, more time alive means more damage.
notes.rumble-situational-antiheal: If an enemy’s self-healing offsets Q’s damage over time, buy Morellonomicon to reduce that healing. Rumble deals damage by burning enemies continuously rather than in one burst, so applying healing reduction can greatly increase the damage that sticks over the same period.
notes.vs-rumble-range: Q deals damage in a close-range cone, and Rumble has no mobility ability. Whether you play a ranged or melee champion, limiting how long he stays close removes most of his damage. Set up trades that force him to walk forward.
notes.vs-rumble-e: Getting hit by both E shots in succession greatly amplifies the slow, making it impossible to walk away, and reduces your magic resistance, increasing the damage that follows. Decide what to do as soon as the first shot lands: create distance immediately instead of holding your ground, or use a mobility ability before the second shot arrives.
notes.vs-rumble-w: W grants Rumble a shield and a brief movement speed boost. Bursting him immediately after he activates it wastes much of your damage on the shield, so let its short duration pass before going in. Once he has used W, his means of escape is also spent.
notes.vs-rumble-hp: Q deals damage based on the target’s maximum health, so building only health works against you when facing Rumble; choose defensive items with magic resistance instead. His magic resistance is also among the lowest of all champions, giving magic damage champions an early laning advantage.
notes.ryze-combo-core: Every combo starts with E → Q: Q deals increased damage to an E-marked target and bounces to nearby marked enemies. Each other ability resets Q’s cooldown, so Ryze’s damage depends on ability order, not how quickly you press the keys.
notes.ryze-combo-root: Use E → W for a guaranteed root; without an E mark, W only slows. Even when you need to stop someone quickly, don’t use W first or you’ll lose the chance to lock them down.
notes.ryze-combo-full: For an all-in, use E → W (root) → Q → E → Q. The first Q consumes the mark, so reapply it with E before using the reset Q; account for both E casts when calculating the combo’s mana cost.
notes.ryze-combo-rune-ms: Q grants a large movement speed boost when cast with two runes charged. To close in or escape, stack two runes with E and W before using Q; whether you need maximum damage or a way out determines when to cast it.
notes.ryze-skill-e-spread: E has a very short cooldown, and its mark spreads around the enemy it hits. Just before a fight, use it on a minion or frontliner to spread marks and increase the area damage from one Q. Avoid spending mana on E without a purpose, but use it to prepare for a teamfight.
notes.ryze-skill-q-aim: Q travels in a straight line and hits only the first target, so minions will block it against an opponent standing in the wave. Apply the mark with E, then use Q as they step out; without a mark, Q has neither increased damage nor a bounce.
notes.ryze-skill-passive-mana: Through Ryze’s passive, bonus mana also increases his damage. Running low on mana makes it harder to complete a combo and effectively reduces the damage of your remaining abilities, so check how much you have before spending it on a poke in lane.
notes.ryze-skill-r-cast: R Realm Warp activates after a short delay. Moving or using other abilities while it charges will not cancel it, but being immobilized or prevented from using abilities will. Cast it from a safe spot outside enemy vision and deal damage while it charges.
notes.ryze-skill-r-use: R Realm Warp moves Ryze and nearby allies rather than dealing damage. Use it to ambush at objectives, join separated allies, or leave after a teamfight. Using it only to escape alone wastes its value, and you need to tell allies beforehand or Ryze may travel without them.
notes.ryze-phase: Ryze needs both levels and items to become strong. Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so his kill stats are among the lowest. His early CS stats rank near the top. Early on, focus on keeping up your growth rather than getting kills. From the mid to late game, once key mana items are completed, the damage from one combo cycle increases.
notes.ryze-laning: In lane, focus on farming: clear the wave with E and secure last hits with Q. Poke with a quick E → Q and back off only after your opponent uses an ability on the wave. If your mana falls below half, stop trading damage and manage the wave.
notes.ryze-laning-push: E clears waves quickly, making it easy to push, but Ryze has no mobility ability, so roaming on foot costs him a lot. After level 6, push the lane and use R to join your allies.
notes.ryze-teamfight: In teamfights, spread E marks through the frontline before dealing area damage with Q. Ryze’s range is not especially long, so you may need to step forward; move in second, after an ally uses an engage ability.
notes.ryze-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has a diving assassin, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier, between your core items. Ryze has no mobility ability, so once he is caught, he has no way to buy time for his combo.
notes.vs-ryze-flux: Ryze’s damage starts with E’s mark: Q deals increased damage to a marked target and bounces to nearby enemies. If E hits you, move away from allies and keep your distance until the mark expires.
notes.vs-ryze-root: Ryze’s W roots only a target already marked by E; otherwise, it merely slows. Prioritize dodging E.
notes.vs-ryze-ult: R Realm Warp takes time to activate, and immobilizing Ryze or preventing him from using abilities during that delay cancels it. When you see it, anticipate what may arrive at its destination or interrupt Ryze.
notes.vs-ryze-noescape: Ryze has no mobility ability, and his armor ranks among the lowest. Reach him first with a gap closer or strong crowd control to deny him time for a combo. Giving him space to deal sustained damage lets his marks keep refreshing and puts you at a disadvantage.
notes.vs-ryze-early: Early on, Ryze lacks both mana and damage, leaving his kill stats near the bottom. The most reliable response is to pressure him in lane before he completes his items and slow his growth.
notes.samira-skill-passive-grade: Style rises one rank when you hit an enemy champion with a different type of attack from your previous hit. Repeated basic attacks or two Q uses in a row stall it, so alternate attacks—basic attack → Q → basic attack → W → basic attack → E—to climb all six ranks from E to S in one fight. Each rank also grants movement speed, making Style management a source of damage and survivability.
notes.samira-combo-eq: Press Q during Wild Rush (E) to strike every enemy along the dash’s path at once after it ends, combining your engage, area damage, and a Style increase. Use this combination whenever you dash into a group; casting Q separately after E ends hits only one target.
notes.samira-skill-melee-range: Although Samira is a ranged champion, she deals her full damage only within melee range. There, Flair (Q) becomes a sword slash instead of a gunshot, and Daredevil Impulse adds magic damage that increases with the target’s missing health. Staying back to basic attack leaves her with less range than other marksmen, so look for an opening to get close.
notes.samira-combo-cc-dash: Basic attacking an immobilized enemy makes Samira dash to them even from maximum basic attack range; if they are airborne, she rises with them and keeps them there. Allied crowd control, especially a knockup, therefore gives her a way in and extends the hold, so be within basic attack range when your support uses an engage ability.
notes.samira-skill-r: R can only be used at Style rank S. Using R immediately resets your Style rank. Use R as soon as you reach Style rank S. Each shot of R applies life steal, so hitting more enemies increases your healing.
notes.samira-skill-w: Blade Whirl (W) destroys enemy projectiles that enter its area, making it a defensive tool when timed against a marksman’s basic attacks or projectile abilities. It also builds Style, so holding it indiscriminately delays R. If the enemy has a crucial projectile, build Style with basic attacks, Q, and E, and save W for defense.
notes.samira-skill-e: E (Wild Rush) dashes through enemies and structures, letting you chase or escape past turrets. If an enemy champion you damaged dies shortly afterward, its cooldown resets, so you can use it to engage when a kill is certain and still have a way out. If the kill is uncertain, save E as your only escape. Much of playing Samira comes down to that choice.
notes.samira-combo-allin: When your support lands crowd control in lane, close the gap with a basic attack, then build Style with a close-range Q (Flair) slash → basic attack → E (Wild Rush) to get behind the enemy → basic attack → W (Blade Whirl). Use R (Inferno Trigger) the moment you reach S. Delaying while you build Style gives enemy backup time to arrive, so alternate attack types from the moment you get in range.
notes.samira-laning: Samira has short range for a marksman, so trading into ranged poke usually puts her behind. In that matchup, give up on building Style and farm under your turret until the enemy support steps too far forward or your jungler intervenes, then engage all at once. Against a melee composition, or alongside a support with engage crowd control, take control from level 2.
notes.samira-laning-trade: A worthwhile damage trade requires melee range, which also puts Samira within the enemy support’s ability range. Using E to enter removes her escape, so close in only when your support’s crowd control or Flash is available. Repeated short trades—getting close, gaining two or three Style ranks, then backing off—will keep wearing down the enemy.
notes.samira-phase: Getting Q and E at level 2 opens Samira’s first all-in opportunity, and R at level 6 lets her turn a fight around on her own. She peaks in the mid game as she builds critical strike items and, statistically, has the highest 14-minute kill count among marksmen, making early gains essential. Her damage holds up late, but enemy defensive items and crowd control make reaching melee range harder, so she needs allies to create an opening.
notes.samira-teamfight: Never engage first in a teamfight. Once your frontline has stopped the enemy with crowd control, move in, alternate attack types to build Style, and use R (Inferno Trigger) the moment you reach S. Its life steal makes the middle of several enemies the safest place to be, but only when your Style is already at S; going in at a lower rank leaves Samira a fragile ranged carry.
notes.samira-situational-cc: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, fit Quicksilver Sash between core items. Samira fires Inferno Trigger (R) from one spot for its duration, so being immobilized partway through costs her every remaining shot after Style has already reset.
notes.samira-situational-antiheal: If the enemy frontline sustains through healing, use Mortal Reminder in your armor penetration slot. Samira fights up close for extended periods, so ongoing enemy healing keeps her in melee range longer, and her abilities provide no Grievous Wounds. If you only need armor penetration, keep Lord Dominik’s Regards.
notes.vs-samira-grade: Samira can use Inferno Trigger (R) only at the highest Style rank. Because she gains ranks by landing different types of attacks in succession, taking one hit and disengaging or moving out of range stops her progress. Keep her time within close range short to prevent the ultimate.
notes.vs-samira-cc-dash: Basic attacking an immobilized enemy makes Samira dash to them, so getting caught by the enemy support’s crowd control signals her engage. Prioritize dodging engage abilities from enemies near her; if an ally is immobilized, expect Samira to dash to them and respond.
notes.vs-samira-w: Blade Whirl (W) destroys projectiles while Samira is spinning. When you see her swing her blades, wait until the spin ends before using projectile abilities or basic attacks; instant and area abilities that are not projectiles can still hit her during it.
notes.vs-samira-e-reset: Wild Rush (E) resets immediately if an enemy Samira damaged dies shortly afterward. Once someone starts to fall in a teamfight, she can keep dashing to the next target, so do not leave a low-health ally behind as you retreat. If she uses E to engage and no one dies, that is your chance to take her down.
notes.vs-samira-range: Samira has short range for a marksman and deals her real damage only within melee range. If you outrange her, keep poking without stepping forward to deny her chances to build Style. In lane, watch for openings that would let her walk into range.
notes.vs-samira-r-interrupt: Inferno Trigger fires for 2 seconds, during which Samira heals through life steal. Interrupt it with immobilizing crowd control or a knockback to cancel the remaining shots; her Style has already reset, so rebuilding her strength takes time. When you see the ultimate, interrupt it instead of running away.
notes.sejuani-combo-gank: For a gank, use Q to dash in and knock the target up, land all of W to build Permafrost stacks, then stun with E once the stacks are full. Follow the stun with one auto-attack: missing it forfeits the passive’s bonus damage based on the target’s maximum health.
notes.sejuani-combo-walkup: If the target has a mobility ability, save Q instead of opening with it. Its knockup is brief enough to give them time to react, and using it to engage leaves you without a way out. Walk in, build stacks with W, and stun with E first; then use Q to follow as they try to escape with their mobility ability, making the kill more reliable.
notes.sejuani-combo-r: R stuns longer the farther it travels before hitting, so throw it from as far away as possible rather than at close range. Its area slow lingers after impact, giving you time to follow with Q, W, and E. Only the first champion hit is stunned, so approach from the side to avoid hitting a champion in front of your intended target.
notes.sejuani-skill-passive: Frost Armor activates after Sejuani goes a set time without taking damage from champions or large jungle monsters, granting slow immunity and defensive stats. Before a fight, avoid hitting a camp and wait briefly so you enter with the armor active; that wait before a gank is preparation. Her first auto-attack against an enemy she has stunned also deals bonus damage based on their maximum health, so make a habit of attacking after the stun.
notes.sejuani-skill-q: Q is a movement tool, a way to start fights, and a means of interrupting channeled abilities. It stops on contact with an enemy champion, so make sure none is in your path when crossing a wall or escaping. Minions do not stop the charge, allowing you to engage through a lane.
notes.sejuani-skill-w: W swings twice, with most of its damage and its slow on the second hit. Finish the cast: backing off after the first hit gives you only half the stacks and damage. The first hit pushes minions and jungle monsters, which can scatter a camp and make clearing less efficient. W is commonly maxed first because of the second hit's damage and how quickly it builds stacks.
notes.sejuani-skill-e: E can only be used on a target with full stacks, which build from Sejuani's W and auto-attacks as well as nearby allied melee champions' auto-attacks. Watch whom a melee ally is attacking to see where a stun is becoming available, and position your cursor to select the intended target, since E targets the enemy closest to it. Stacks cannot build on an enemy for a while after E stuns them, so choose the target carefully.
notes.sejuani-skill-r: When no allies are nearby, use Q to buy time instead of R.
notes.sejuani-laning-path: Sejuani’s jungle path should focus on safe camp clears and gaining levels rather than early kills. Her kills at 14 minutes and damage per minute rank near the bottom, while her deaths rank among the highest, so her win rates favor starting fights only in lanes where an ally already has the advantage. Keep Frost Armor active while moving as basic protection against counterjungling.
notes.sejuani-laning-gank: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret, where the opponent has a long way to retreat. Avoid hitting a camp just before engaging so Frost Armor is active. In a lane with an allied melee champion, their auto-attacks can build stacks for you and bring out the E stun much sooner; the more melee champions on your team, the more likely your ganks are to succeed.
notes.sejuani-phase: Before level 6, ganks are slow because Sejuani must fully stack Permafrost to stun. Once R becomes available at level 6, she can reliably start a fight in any lane regardless of stacks. Her passive grants bonus defensive stats that scale with her armor and magic resistance, while W scales with maximum health, making defensive items a source of both damage and survivability. Win rates also rise sharply when she completes her three core items.
notes.sejuani-teamfight: Your role is to start teamfights. With Frost Armor active, throw R from an angle that reaches an enemy backline damage dealer, then follow a hit with Q and hold the target down with W and E. Engage only when your damage dealers are positioned to damage the R target immediately. Otherwise, use W from the front to slow the enemy's engage and save R for the next fight.
notes.sejuani-situational-mr: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, include Spirit Visage in your core build order to make use of the passive's magic resistance increase.
notes.sejuani-situational-armor: If the enemy has strong physical damage and many champions who stick to targets with auto-attacks, buy Thornmail early to build up reflected damage while taking hits.
notes.vs-sejuani-frost: Permafrost stacks come from Sejuani’s W and auto-attacks as well as the auto-attacks of her melee allies. A stun may be building even when Sejuani is not hitting you herself, so being close to one of her melee allies while she is nearby is dangerous. Move away immediately when the stack indicator fills.
notes.vs-sejuani-passive: With Frost Armor active, Sejuani is immune to slows and has increased defensive stats. Taking damage removes the armor shortly afterward, so if you need to escape, hit her first, even with a low-value ability, to remove her slow immunity before using your escape tool.
notes.vs-sejuani-q-r: Dodging Q and R is central to fighting Sejuani. Q stops when it hits a champion, so if an ally in front takes the hit, those behind them are safe. R stuns longer the farther it travels, so if it is going to hit you, closing the distance reduces the stun. Both abilities have visible windups and can be dodged by moving sideways.
notes.vs-sejuani-w: W swings twice, with most of its damage and the slow on the second hit. If the first hit lands, moving out of range before the second can negate more than half of the damage trade.
notes.vs-sejuani-e: Stacks cannot build on a target for a while after E stuns them, creating a brief safe window once the stun has been used. Sejuani's first auto-attack after stunning you deals bonus damage based on your maximum health, though, so create distance as soon as the stun ends to avoid that hit.
notes.vs-sejuani-scaling: Sejuani’s damage and defenses scale with her health and defensive stats. Given time, she can become hard to kill while repeatedly locking down your allies, so take early jungle control and objectives to delay her item completion. Her early kills and damage rank near the bottom, leaving plenty of opportunity to take those resources.
notes.senna-skill-souls: Senna grows by collecting Mist through her passive, Absolution. When a unit dies near her, it has a chance to leave a soul that she must attack to collect. Souls disappear over time, so watch where they land and walk over to claim them; for support Senna, this is her only way to gain attack damage without taking CS.
notes.senna-skill-mist-champ: Senna also gains Mist by hitting the same enemy champion twice with attacks or abilities, dealing bonus damage based on their current health. Poking is therefore part of her growth: take safe opportunities, and combine one attack with Q to collect Mist in a single approach.
notes.senna-skill-range-growth: At certain Mist thresholds, Senna gains both attack range and critical strike chance. By late game, her range lets her attack before other marksmen, changing how she should position compared with the early game; step forward to land attacks and make use of that growth.
notes.senna-skill-q: Q, Piercing Darkness, travels in a straight line through a targeted ally or enemy. You can target an allied champion or a minion in front of an opponent to hit them even when they are outside Q's direct targeting range. Its cast range scales with attack range, while its cast time improves with attack speed, so Mist and attack speed make Q stronger.
notes.senna-skill-q-cooldown: Each attack reduces Q's cooldown, so follow Q with two attacks to bring it back sooner. Weaving in attacks lets you use Q more often than holding it solely for an urgent heal on an ally.
notes.senna-skill-w: W Last Embrace attaches to the first target it hits, then roots nearby enemies after a short delay. Minions can block it, so in lane, fire through gaps between them or from a side without minions. Aim where your opponent is going rather than where they stand, and look for grouped opponents to root several at once.
notes.senna-skill-e: E, Curse of the Black Mist, is most valuable for starting an engagement. Allies inside the mist are camouflaged, and those who leave it become wraiths that conceal their identities. Approach together just before a teamfight to make it harder for opponents to target your allies; saving E only for escapes gives up that team benefit.
notes.senna-combo-pick: For a kill combo, land W (Last Embrace) to set up the root, then time Q (Piercing Darkness) and a basic attack to hit as it takes hold. Sync the delay between W’s hit and its root with an ally’s engage so the target is locked down twice in a row. If W misses, use Q first to slow the target, then look for another W.
notes.senna-combo-teamfight: To start a teamfight, approach with allies using E, root opponents in the center of their formation with W, then use R, Dawning Shadow, to help finish the fight while shielding allies. Its shield covers a wider area than its damage hitbox, so aim the beam to include allies instead of focusing only on a kill.
notes.senna-skill-r: R (Dawning Shadow) is a wide beam that reaches beyond the screen, letting Senna influence fights in other lanes. Use it to shield allies in a losing fight as well as to finish enemies. The shield absorbs more damage as she collects Mist, so growth from her passive directly strengthens R.
notes.senna-phase: Senna's level-one health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, making an early catch potentially fatal. Her impact rises sharply from mid game as Mist increases her damage and range; late game, that range lets her deal damage from a safe position. Focus on collecting Mist without dying early.
notes.senna-laning-souls: Stepping forward for a soul is especially dangerous. Check its position and the range of enemy abilities, and move up only while key enemy abilities are on cooldown; be willing to give up souls near the enemy turret. Avoid last-hitting minions so your allied marksman gets the CS, but collect the souls.
notes.senna-laning-trade: Senna attacks slowly and has a long pause after each attack, so trying to land consecutive attacks while poking in lane invites retaliation. Land an attack, follow it with Q to collect Mist, then retreat immediately and repeat that rhythm.
notes.senna-teamfight: In teamfights, stay in the backline, healing allies with Q and adding attacks from your increased range. Hold W to stop an enemy engage; if no approaching enemy gives you that opportunity, use it when it lines up with an ally's engage ability. Senna's low health makes stepping forward dangerous, so advance to engage only when using E.
notes.vs-senna-souls: Senna's growth depends on collecting souls, which forces her to step forward when one appears. Watch where a soul lands, wait nearby, and harass her as she approaches. Forcing her to give up one soul matters more than denying a few CS.
notes.vs-senna-mist-stacks: If Senna hits you twice with attacks or abilities, she gains Mist and deals damage. After the first hit, retreat immediately to a position where she cannot land the second.
notes.vs-senna-w: Senna's W, Last Embrace, shows a mark during the delay between impact and the root. If it marks you, move away from your allies immediately so they are not rooted with you. In lane, standing behind minions can block W.
notes.vs-senna-q: Senna's Q, Piercing Darkness, extends in a straight line through a targeted ally or minion. Avoid lining up with Senna and one of her allied champions, or with Senna and a minion in front of you, to avoid much of her poke.
notes.vs-senna-early: Senna has the lowest level-one health of any champion and very low attack damage. Pressure her hard in lane to stop her collecting Mist and limit her late-game growth; if left alone early, her range and attack damage will keep increasing.
notes.vs-senna-e: When Senna activates E (Curse of the Black Mist), allies inside it can also approach while camouflaged. If you see the mist, don’t hold your position against it: immediately retreat to an area where you have vision, or cast an area ability into the mist to deny the approach.
notes.seraphine-combo-cc-chain: E Beat Drop roots enemies who are already slowed and stuns those who are immobilized. Apply a slow from Seraphine or an ally first to guarantee the root; without that setup, E only slows.
notes.seraphine-combo-passive-echo: P Stage Presence casts every third basic ability twice. When both casts of an Echoed E Beat Drop hit, the first slows and the second roots. Count your casts before a fight so Echo lines up with E or W.
notes.seraphine-combo-ult-range: R Encore extends its range when it hits an allied champion. In teamfights, aim through allies lined up in front of you to reach much farther; allies hit also gain a full stack of Notes.
notes.seraphine-combo-ult-follow: After charming an enemy with R (Encore), follow up with E (Beat Drop) to hold them in place as they walk toward you, then use Q (High Note) to finish them once their health has dropped. Using Q first loses damage based on their missing health.
notes.seraphine-skill-q: Q (High Note) deals more damage the more health the target has lost, so poking a full-health enemy with it is inefficient. Use it to finish a wounded enemy or clear a wave instead.
notes.seraphine-skill-w-double: W Surround Sound also heals if you cast it again while your shield is still active. An Echoed W gives you both a shield and a heal in one cast, so line up Echo with W before a major fight.
notes.seraphine-skill-w-timing: W (Surround Sound) also boosts your allies’ movement speed. Use it as you begin to engage or retreat so you benefit from both the speed boost and shield, rather than waiting until everyone has taken damage and using it to heal.
notes.seraphine-skill-e-save: E (Beat Drop) is Seraphine’s only reliable crowd control. Save it for an ally’s engage or to stop an enemy dash: spending it on poke leaves you without a way to answer an enemy engage. It deals reduced damage to minions, so don’t use it to clear waves.
notes.seraphine-phase: Seraphine can poke comfortably in lane thanks to her ability range and Notes from allies, but struggles to secure kills alone. Her teamfight impact rises sharply once she learns R at level 6, and she is strongest in the mid to late game as she builds ability power. Her health and movement speed are very low, so never stand in front at any stage of the game.
notes.seraphine-laning-notes: Passive Notes stack based on the number of nearby allies, increasing basic attack range and damage.
notes.seraphine-laning-mana: Q and W cost a lot of mana, so excessive early poke can leave you unable to cast E and W when you need them. Trade only when the enemy stops to last-hit a minion; otherwise, focus on positioning and vision.
notes.seraphine-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and shield them with W, then send E through grouped enemies to root them. Use R when you have an angle to reach the enemy backline, casting it just before your allies engage to prevent the enemy from responding.
notes.seraphine-teamfight-ult-defense: R is also valuable defensively: its charm can turn an engaging enemy back. If your carry gets jumped, cast it immediately rather than waiting for a chance to hit multiple enemies and losing your ally.
notes.seraphine-situational-mikael: If the enemy team has a lot of reliable crowd control, buy Mikael’s Blessing earlier. Seraphine’s job is to keep allies alive, but a controlled ally may die before her shield and heal reach them.
notes.vs-seraphine-e: Seraphine’s E Beat Drop roots enemies who are already slowed and stuns those who are immobilized. If you are slowed while standing directly in front of her, it can root you, so move out of its path as soon as the slow lands.
notes.vs-seraphine-ult: Seraphine’s R Encore extends its range each time it hits one of her allies. If your team stands in a line, its charm can reach players farther back, so spread out sideways in teamfights.
notes.vs-seraphine-passive: Seraphine needs nearby allies to stack Notes, which increase her basic attack range and damage. Engage and trade when she is standing alone, away from her marksman.
notes.vs-seraphine-fragile: Seraphine has very low health and movement speed, with no mobility ability. Once her E is down, she has virtually no way to defend herself, so engage immediately after she misses it.
notes.sett-combo-basic: For a basic trade, activate Q, land two basic attacks, then pull enemies together with E and follow up with W. Q has no cast time, so you can use it between attacks or while moving without breaking your attack rhythm; activate it as soon as you can land an attack rather than before you get in range. E pulls the targets in front of Sett, letting you aim W along the same line immediately afterward for a guaranteed center-line hit.
notes.sett-combo-r: For an R engage, grab and throw the target with R, then use E at the landing point, W, and Q-empowered basic attacks. R carries the target forward in the direction Sett is facing, so move behind the enemy and face your allies before throwing them to land them in the middle of your team. The strong slow around the landing point makes the immediate follow-up E easier to aim.
notes.sett-skill-passive: Sett’s passive, Pit Grit, makes his right punch faster and stronger than his left. If you start attacking, land the right punch before backing off; leaving after only the left loses you damage in the trade. His health regeneration also increases with missing health, making it possible to stay in lane and recover after taking damage.
notes.sett-skill-q: Q (Knuckle Down) empowers Sett’s next two attacks and grants movement speed while he walks toward enemy champions, making it useful for both chasing and dealing damage. Activate it as you start pursuing a fleeing enemy, and land both empowered attacks on the champion rather than spending them on minions. Each punch has a damage cap against monsters, so Q contributes less to jungle clearing than you might expect.
notes.sett-skill-w-grit: W (Haymaker) stores the damage Sett takes as Grit, which rapidly decays shortly after he takes damage. Use it right after getting hit, especially by a major enemy ability, when both its shield and damage are strongest. With empty Grit, W provides almost no shield; deliberately taking some poke in lane can build the gauge.
notes.sett-skill-w-aim: W (Haymaker) deals true damage only along its center line and physical damage outside it, so line up the center precisely against high-armor tanks. Its shield applies before the punch, though, so if you urgently need to survive, you can use W for the shield without taking time to aim.
notes.sett-skill-e: E (Facebreaker) stuns only when it grabs at least one enemy on each side of Sett; grabbing enemies on just one side only slows them. Any enemy unit counts, so position with a minion wave on one side and the opposing champion on the other to land a stun even in a 1v1. Using E straight ahead without setting this up wastes its cooldown on a slow.
notes.sett-laning-trade: Against melee opponents, let them use an ability first, turn the damage into Grit, then trade back with Q (Knuckle Down) empowered attacks and W (Haymaker). If Sett engages first, his Grit is empty and the same combo delivers only half its value.
notes.sett-laning-ranged: Before unlocking R (The Show Stopper), Sett has no way to close the gap on ranged opponents. Give up trades, pull the wave toward your turret and farm; use E (Facebreaker) and R for guaranteed crowd control only when your jungler arrives. Forcing your way in merely builds Grit while you lose health outside your attack range.
notes.sett-phase: Sett is weak at levels 1–2 with only one or two abilities available. His first two power spikes come at level 3, when Q (Knuckle Down), W (Haymaker) and E (Facebreaker) are all available, and level 6, when he gains R (The Show Stopper). His Grit capacity grows with his health, making the mid game, as he builds health items, his peak. Late in the game, he struggles to reach ranged formations, so his impact depends on where he uses his one R.
notes.sett-teamfight-entry: Sett works best entering a fight already underway while building Grit, rather than starting the teamfight himself. In a narrow passage, pull multiple enemies into a line with E and place W’s center line over them for maximum damage. Walking straight into a fight in open space can get you killed before you reach anyone.
notes.sett-teamfight-r: R (The Show Stopper) deals more damage based on the grabbed target’s bonus health, so grabbing a frontline enemy with health items produces a harder hit. The target is suppressed and cannot escape with movement abilities. Disrupting the enemy formation can be more valuable, though: if you can throw a key damage dealer into the middle of your team, choose that angle over extra R damage.
notes.sett-situational-mr: Sett has one of the lowest level 1 magic resistance values among champions, making him especially vulnerable to magic damage. Buy an early Null-Magic Mantle to reduce losses in early trades, then build a magic resistance item after completing your first core item.
notes.sett-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the enemy’s healing is strong enough to turn trades around. Sett spreads damage across multiple empowered attacks, making healing reduction easy to maintain.
notes.vs-sett-w: Sett’s W (Haymaker) grows stronger with the damage he takes, making the moment after you use major abilities on him especially dangerous. Once you have dealt damage, back away briefly to let his Grit decay before approaching again. If you cannot avoid W entirely, at least step sideways out of its center line to avoid the true damage.
notes.vs-sett-e: Sett's E only stuns if it grabs enemies on both sides. To avoid E's stun, avoid standing opposite an ally with Sett between you. Sett's E only applies a brief slow if it grabs enemies on just one side.
notes.vs-sett-r: Being grabbed by Sett’s R (The Show Stopper) suppresses you; Flash and Cleanse cannot remove it, but a removal item such as Mercurial Scimitar can. R’s damage scales with the grabbed target’s bonus health, making frontline champions who build health particularly vulnerable. While Sett has R available, stand together with your allies to leave him no space to throw you.
notes.vs-sett-mobility: Sett has no way to close the gap apart from R (The Show Stopper), so keep your distance and repeatedly poke him in lane. When he starts walking toward you, retreat before his movement speed increases, and account for the poke damage becoming his W (Haymaker) shield.
notes.vs-sett-mr: Sett’s early magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions. As a magic damage champion, you can trade aggressively around level 3; building a health advantage then also gives him fewer chances to build Grit.
notes.shaco-combo-box-camp: Place W Jack In The Box before starting each jungle camp, then attack while the monsters are feared. Its fear lasts much longer on monsters than on champions, letting Shaco finish his early clear with little health lost; the cooldown is short enough to use a box at every camp without slowing the clear.
notes.shaco-combo-gank: For a gank, place W Jack In The Box along the target’s escape route, then use Q Deceive to appear behind them, land the empowered basic attack, and finish with E Two-Shiv Poison. The attack after Q is a critical strike when it hits from behind, so position the teleport accordingly while the box blocks their retreat.
notes.shaco-skill-passive: P Backstab activates when Shaco attacks from behind and applies to E Two-Shiv Poison as well as basic attacks. Its bonus damage on E grows as the target’s health falls, so getting behind them directly increases Shaco’s damage.
notes.shaco-skill-q: Q Deceive gives Shaco a short teleport and invisibility, allowing him to cross walls and escape places that seem to have no exit. His first basic attack from stealth is empowered and critically strikes from behind, making Q an engage tool and the start of his burst. Its long cooldown leaves him without the same escape during that fight, so save it for disengaging unless you can secure the kill. Turrets and true sight reveal him while invisible.
notes.shaco-skill-w-vision: W Jack In The Box disappears from sight shortly after placement and lasts a long time, serving as both a trap and a source of vision. Set boxes in advance at entrances to your jungle, around objectives, and in bushes enemies may pass through to spot and block their approach. Leveling W also extends its fear against champions, making the investment more valuable if you plan to rely on boxes.
notes.shaco-skill-w-objective: Before starting Dragon or Rift Herald, place W Jack In The Box at every entrance enemies could use. Fear can throw off an enemy jungler’s Smite timing during a steal attempt, and a triggered box warns you of their approach. Delay the objective if you need more time to set up the boxes.
notes.shaco-skill-e: While E Two-Shiv Poison is off cooldown, Shaco’s basic attacks slow. Hold it while chasing to keep that slow available, then use its active from range to finish a target whose low health makes it deal much more damage.
notes.shaco-skill-r: Shaco briefly disappears while creating his R Hallucinate clone, which can let him dodge a targeted ability. The clone takes increased damage and does not last long, but on death it explodes and leaves three small boxes that trigger immediately. It also applies on-hit effects, so item choices affect its damage. Hold Alt and right-click to control it separately.
notes.shaco-combo-r-teamfight: In teamfights, send the R Hallucinate clone toward the enemy backline to draw attention while Shaco uses Q Deceive to get behind them from the opposite side. Engage as the clone explodes and its three small boxes trigger fear, scattering the enemy formation. Keep the clone away from Shaco so the same area-of-effect ability does not hit both.
notes.shaco-jungle-path: Shaco gets ahead through kill participation rather than farming. Clear camps safely with W Jack In The Box, then spend the health you saved on ganks and jungle invades. A box in front of an enemy camp also helps you prepare for invades and provides vision against counter-invades.
notes.shaco-phase: At levels 1–2, clear camps safely with W Jack In The Box; once Shaco has both Q Deceive and E Two-Shiv Poison at level 3, he can make his first gank. His burst peaks with two items in the mid game, when he can pick off enemy backliners alone. Late game, his solo fighting weakens and enemy vision limits his engage angles, so use boxes and the R Hallucinate clone to disrupt vision and apply pressure. Without an early advantage, he can fall behind the pace of the game.
notes.shaco-teamfight: Avoid head-on teamfights: Shaco is fragile enough to fall to a few area-of-effect abilities. Draw the fight into an area where W Jack In The Box is already set, send the R Hallucinate clone ahead to draw attention, and approach the enemy backline from the side. Wait to engage until an enemy damage dealer steps forward.
notes.shaco-situational-antiheal: If a target you need to pick off can survive through healing, buy Executioner's Calling early. Shaco's burst needs to finish the kill quickly; if they heal during that window, you may fall short on damage and be left committed to the engage with no way to escape.
notes.shaco-situational-cc: Consider Quicksilver Sash when the enemy has plenty of crowd control that prevents movement. Q Deceive is Shaco’s only way out, so being immobilized before he can teleport leaves him easy to catch where he engaged.
notes.vs-shaco-q-commit: After Shaco engages with Q Deceive, he cannot immediately use it again to escape. Focus him with your allies as soon as he appears; that is the window to catch him before he recovers and disappears out of vision again.
notes.vs-shaco-box: Assume W Jack In The Box is waiting in bushes without vision and around objectives. It becomes invisible shortly after placement, so clear boxes in advance with Control Wards and Oracle Lens. If you cannot clear them, start the objective only from a position that gives you room to retreat if feared; fighting while feared can disrupt your Smite timing.
notes.vs-shaco-backstab: Shaco deals much more damage when he attacks from behind, and his first basic attack after Q Deceive’s stealth critically strikes from that position. If he is nearby, put your back to a wall or face your allies to make it harder for him to get behind you.
notes.vs-shaco-clone: The R Hallucinate clone takes increased damage and dies faster than Shaco, then explodes and leaves three small boxes that trigger immediately. Step back as soon as you kill it to avoid the explosion and fear. Watch how the health bars react to distinguish the clone from Shaco instead of pouring your damage into it.
notes.vs-shaco-execute: E Two-Shiv Poison deals much more damage to targets on low health, so a dagger from outside your vision can finish you after a fight. If you have little health left, avoid jungle areas and bushes without vision.
notes.vs-shaco-early: Shaco gains advantages through early ganks and invades rather than farming. Avoid giving him kills early, take objectives, and buy time: his ability to win solo fights falls off late game. Keeping vision at entrances to your jungle also disrupts much of his early plan.
notes.shen-combo-basic: The basic combo is Q → E to taunt → three basic attacks. Q empowers several of Shen’s next basic attacks instead of dealing immediate damage, so using it and backing off deals almost none. Cast Q before E to spend the full taunt duration landing empowered attacks; casting both abilities also triggers the passive shield, reducing the health lost when you engage.
notes.shen-skill-blade: Shen’s play revolves around the spirit blade’s position. Q calls it toward him and hits enemies in its path, W creates its zone where the blade is, and R moves Shen and the blade together. Always check where the blade is before deciding which ability to use.
notes.shen-skill-q: Twilight Assault (Q) deals far more damage when the returning blade passes through an enemy champion: its empowered basic attacks gain substantially more maximum health damage and attack speed. Position the blade to pass through your target when trading with a tank. Q also deals increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for camps and objectives.
notes.shen-skill-w: Spirit’s Refuge (W) blocks basic attacks, but ability damage passes through it. Use it against opponents who rely on basic attacks; placing it in front of allies against a mage will not help. If no allied champion is inside the zone to protect, it takes a moment to activate, so casting it early on an empty spot only wastes the cooldown.
notes.shen-skill-e: Shadow Dash (E) is both Shen’s taunt and his only mobility tool. Using it to engage leaves no way out, so generally save it to counter an opponent’s engage and go in first only when you are sure you can win. A missed E gives the opponent time to counterattack.
notes.shen-skill-passive: Ki Barrier grants Shen a shield whenever he uses an ability, and hitting an allied or enemy champion with an ability reduces its cooldown. Keep landing abilities to sustain yourself; even clipping your lane opponent with Q brings the next shield back sooner.
notes.shen-skill-r-shield: Stand United (R) grants a larger shield the more health its target has lost, so use it after an ally starts taking damage rather than as soon as a fight begins. Before casting, judge whether they can survive the channel: if they die before it ends, nothing remains. Shen lands at the ally’s location, so a fleeing target can carry him somewhere unintended. Once you commit, tell the ally to hold their position.
notes.shen-laning: Shen is among the lowest of top lane champions in CS and damage per minute. Aim to get through lane evenly and use R to help other lanes win. Risky trades can leave you without enough health to use R when it matters, so manage the wave safely during laning phase.
notes.shen-laning-energy: Shen uses energy, which regenerates over time, and dealing damage with Q and E restores it. Against mana users, repeated short trades favor Shen: their resources run low while his recover.
notes.shen-laning-wave: Using R leaves Shen’s lane empty. If a fight looks likely elsewhere, push the wave toward the enemy turret beforehand to limit what you lose while away. An R without that preparation can save one ally at the cost of your lane.
notes.shen-phase: Shen is weakest at levels 1–5, when he lacks damage and mobility. Learning R at level 6 lets him affect the entire map; from then on, his impact follows R’s cooldown more than the state of his own lane. His real peak comes in the mid to late game as cooldown reduction builds up.
notes.shen-teamfight: In teamfights, Shen’s job is to turn back an enemy engage rather than deal damage. Use E to taunt enemies off your carries and position the spirit blade so W’s zone protects them. Stay back to guard your team’s backline; accepting a separate 1v1 leaves it exposed.
notes.shen-situational-thornmail: If the enemy’s main damage is physical and comes from basic attacks, buy Thornmail between core items. Shen’s W (Spirit's Refuge) also blocks basic attacks, so the two provide overlapping defensive value against opponents who rely on them.
notes.shen-situational-mr: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, W can block very little of it. Choose a magic resistance item such as Bandlepipes for your third item to survive longer.
notes.vs-shen-e: Shadow Dash (E) is Shen’s only mobility ability and his only hard crowd control. If you dodge it, he can neither close the gap nor escape, so counterattack as soon as it misses. If E taunts you, you’ll take his empowered basic attacks for the duration.
notes.vs-shen-r: From level 6, Shen can join an ally anywhere on the map. If he disappears from lane or starts channeling R, alert your team immediately; finish a dive or fight before he arrives, or do not start it. When he uses R, his lane is completely empty, so take advantage there.
notes.vs-shen-q: Most of Shen’s damage comes from basic attacks empowered by Twilight Assault (Q), and their strength depends on whether the returning spirit blade hits a champion. Step out of its path as it returns to Shen to greatly reduce Q’s damage. Because that damage scales with maximum health, defensive items that only add health are less effective against him.
notes.vs-shen-w: Spirit’s Refuge (W) blocks basic attacks, but ability damage passes through. As a marksman, keep your distance while the zone is active and resume attacking when it ends; basic attacks during that time are wasted. Champions who deal damage with abilities can keep using them through the zone.
notes.vs-shen-lane: Shen ranks near the bottom in top lane laning stats, making early trades favorable against him. Prioritize lane control over kills: push the wave to keep him occupied with CS, so using R to help another lane costs him his own. That creates a greater advantage for your team.
notes.shyvana-combo-clear: Start a jungle camp by detonating E Molten Burst on the large monster, then close in, activate W Inferno Aegis, and follow with a Q Emberstrike empowered auto attack. W is especially effective in the jungle because monsters do not run away and take its full duration; stay close while the shield lasts so its explosion also hits the camp.
notes.shyvana-combo-gank: After level 6, gank by passing through the enemy with R Dragon's Descent, then slow them with E as they retreat and finish with a Q empowered auto attack. R makes you unstoppable during its movement, so you can push through a narrow approach even if the enemy support has crowd control ready.
notes.shyvana-combo-w-recast: Reactivating W Inferno Aegis makes it explode immediately. If an enemy looks likely to escape before the shield expires, reactivate it as soon as you reach them; if they stay close, delay the explosion to keep the movement speed boost longer. In dragon form, the explosion heals you only when it hits a champion, making its timing vital to your survival.
notes.shyvana-skill-passive: Participating in a champion, large minion, or large monster takedown permanently adds armor and magic resistance through P Scalemail. The stacks persist through death, so even one extra camp early becomes durability later. Shyvana has very low health growth by level 18 and becomes fragile late in the game without enough stacks.
notes.shyvana-skill-q: Q Emberstrike empowers your next auto attack, so press it in time with the attack to avoid wasting it. Each auto attack that hits reduces Q's cooldown, which makes attack speed especially valuable for Shyvana. In dragon form, Q gains an extra cast that bites a single target; save that cast when focusing one champion.
notes.shyvana-skill-w: W Inferno Aegis grants a shield and movement speed that increases as you get closer to enemy champions. Activate it first when approaching a gank, since it speeds you up more while closing in than while escaping. Its shield also absorbs more damage for each nearby enemy champion, making it especially useful when entering a group.
notes.shyvana-skill-e: In human form, E Molten Burst stops and explodes on the first enemy it hits, so fire from the side to reach a champion behind a minion wave. In dragon form, the fireball grows larger, passes through enemies, and leaves flames in its path. Use it when enemies line up in a narrow passage to slow several of them and deal damage based on their maximum health at once.
notes.shyvana-skill-r-fury: R becomes available through Shyvana’s Fury gauge instead of a cooldown. Basic attacks and ability hits build Fury, but area damage against non-champions generates much less, while Fury builds much faster in dragon form. Clearing camps with area damage alone delays R, so mix in champion fights or single-target basic attacks to have it ready on time. Fill the gauge before an objective fight.
notes.shyvana-skill-r-timing: R serves both as an engage tool and as a period when Shyvana cannot be stopped. Generally, use it at the start of a fight to benefit from empowered abilities and bonus health throughout the fight. If the enemy has reliable crowd control to start an engagement, saving R to push through that ability is also reasonable. Without transforming, Shyvana’s damage and durability are both cut in half, so the worst outcome is holding R and never using it.
notes.shyvana-jungle-path: At level 5 or below, Shyvana has no immobilizing crowd control, so her ganks are less likely to succeed. Her movement speed is among the highest and W makes travel between camps even faster, so focus early on full clears and invading camps on the opposite side to build a lead. Begin ganking in earnest once you have R.
notes.shyvana-objective: Q's damage based on maximum health is effective against high-health epic monsters. Participating in a large monster takedown grants a P stack. Establish vision so you can start Dragon and Rift Herald before the enemy.
notes.shyvana-phase: Levels 1–5 are a farming phase with weak ganks because Shyvana has no crowd control. At level 6, R gives her engage and area damage, allowing her to start fights for the first time. She peaks in the mid game with attack speed and core items, but her low health growth leaves her fragile late in the game; without enough P Scalemail stacks and defensive items, she can be taken down first in teamfights.
notes.shyvana-teamfight: In teamfights, choose an entry angle that puts several enemies in R's path instead of heading straight for an enemy damage dealer. Stand among champions so dragon form W's explosion hits them and heals you, while piercing E gains value when enemies group together. Shyvana has no way to hold enemies in place, so let an ally apply crowd control before following up with R.
notes.shyvana-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Shyvana stays close and attacks for a long time, so sustained enemy healing prolongs trades, and none of her abilities apply Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-shyvana-distance: Keep your distance to avoid Shyvana's Q auto attack and W explosion. If you can keep your distance, be especially wary of Shyvana using R to close the gap.
notes.vs-shyvana-spread: In dragon form, all of Shyvana’s abilities can hit multiple enemies at once. If two or more players stand where R’s path, W’s explosion, and her piercing E overlap, they give Shyvana both damage and healing. Spreading out in teamfights alone cuts her damage in half.
notes.vs-shyvana-fury: Shyvana's Fury gauge shows whether she can transform. Pressure her or start an objective when the gauge is empty, her weakest moment; when it is full, do not start attacking an objective in front of her.
notes.vs-shyvana-r-unstoppable: Shyvana is unstoppable while flying with R Dragon's Descent, so crowd control cannot interrupt her entry. Apply it after she lands to hold her in place, then fight back when the transformation ends and she loses her bonus health and empowered abilities.
notes.vs-shyvana-early: At level 5 or below, Shyvana has no immobilizing crowd control, making gank kills difficult; instead, she quickly takes camps and objectives to build P Scalemail stacks. Invade early to steal her camps and take objectives first, denying those permanent stacks and exposing her low late-game health growth.
notes.singed-combo-fling-glue: The key combo is to use E Fling to throw the enemy behind Singed, then place W Mega Adhesive where they will land; they must land on it to be rooted. Placing W first gives them time to see it coming and retreat, so covering the landing spot after the throw is much more reliable. Since Fling sends the target behind Singed, check which way he is facing before using it.
notes.singed-combo-tower: Near a turret, use E Fling to throw an enemy into its range, then place W Mega Adhesive on them. They must walk out, and the adhesive delays their escape long enough for the turret to hit them several times.
notes.singed-combo-flash-fling: Flash turns the short-range E Fling into a way to force an engage. Press E during Flash so the Fling goes off as soon as Singed arrives, leaving the enemy no time to react. This is his only way to force an initiation, so use it only for fights you can win.
notes.singed-skill-q: Q Poison Trail toggles on and off and has no cooldown, but drains mana continuously while active. It leaves poison behind Singed, so standing still accomplishes nothing. Keep moving and guide enemies along a path they want to take through the poison, then turn Q off after the fight to save mana.
notes.singed-skill-w: W Mega Adhesive slows enemies, but its main value is preventing movement abilities. Against someone with a dash or blink to escape, placing it on their escape path can shut that ability down. Its cooldown is fairly short, so read where the enemy will retreat and throw it there instead of saving it.
notes.singed-skill-e: E Fling deals damage based on maximum health, so it hurts tanky enemies, but its real value is repositioning them. Throw an enemy carry toward your team or move an enemy attacking your carry away from them. Check where the target will land first: if they are already surrounded by your team, a Fling could send them to safety.
notes.singed-skill-r: R Insanity Potion raises several stats at once and makes Q Poison Trail reduce healing for its duration. Activate it to draw enemies through your poison while appearing to flee, especially when Singed looks close to death and they start chasing.
notes.singed-skill-passive: P Noxious Slipstream grants movement speed whenever Singed passes through an allied or enemy champion. Its cooldown is separate for each champion, so zigzagging through a group keeps refreshing the speed bonus. Diving into the middle of the enemy team may look reckless, but it is the route that makes him fastest.
notes.singed-laning-proxy: In lane, aim to keep your opponent there rather than beat them directly. Push a wave into the enemy turret, then go behind it and clear the next wave with Q Poison Trail; the opponent cannot leave lane while your teammates are free to move. Go behind the turret just after the enemy jungler is spotted on the other side of the map, since doing so without knowing their location can get you caught.
notes.singed-laning-trade: For a trade, pass by the enemy with Q Poison Trail active to lay poison, then use E Fling to catch them if they stand their ground. Singed loses if he stands still and trades basic attacks. Wait until the enemy has used their escape ability to clear a wave or for another purpose; if it is still available, they can get away immediately after the Fling.
notes.singed-phase: At levels 1–2, Singed has only Q Poison Trail, so his damage is low and he runs out of mana quickly. At level 3, W Mega Adhesive enables a combo with E Fling and gives him his first chance to catch an enemy; at level 6, R Insanity Potion completes his ability to escape and lure opponents. With two core items, he can keep pushing the lane and survive even when three enemies come for him, making this his most troublesome period. His health growth is relatively low later on, though, so he loses strength if time passes without more items.
notes.singed-teamfight: In teamfights, Singed's job is to disrupt the enemy formation rather than deal damage. Activate Q Poison Trail, run through their team, keep refreshing your speed with P Noxious Slipstream, and use E Fling to throw an enemy carry toward your allies. Keep moving afterward so several enemies chase you; the longer you stay alive while drawing them away, the easier the fight becomes for your team.
notes.singed-situational-armor: If most enemy damage is physical, build armor first. Dead Man's Plate provides armor and movement effects that suit catching enemies and running around, while buying Plated Steelcaps early helps you survive against opponents who rely on basic attacks.
notes.singed-situational-tenacity: Choose Quicksilver Sash if the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities. Singed needs to keep moving to survive, being held in place can mean death, and none of his abilities can directly remove crowd control.
notes.vs-singed-chase: Do not chase Singed just because he looks low on health. He leaves Q Poison Trail behind as he runs, and if R Insanity Potion is active, that poison also reduces healing. The pursuer is the one stepping in it, so let him go unless you have enough damage ready to kill him for certain.
notes.vs-singed-fling: E sends its target behind Singed.
notes.vs-singed-cc: Singed gets value by running close to the enemy team. Instead of committing several players to catch him, hold him in place with crowd control and attack his teammates while he is tied down. Chasing him all the way is exactly what he wants.
notes.vs-singed-glue: You cannot use movement abilities while standing on W Mega Adhesive. Before trying to dash away, check whether it is under your feet; getting hit by E Fling while on it also roots you, leaving you caught in the full combo. Go around the adhesive rather than stepping on it.
notes.vs-singed-proxy: If Singed disappears behind your turret, he is clearing the wave with Q Poison Trail. Chasing him into a one-on-one fight in the jungle favors him. Instead, push the empty lane to pressure the turret or move to another lane with your jungler to create a numbers advantage; Singed cannot create any pressure while he remains behind the turret.
notes.vs-singed-early: Pressure Singed at levels 1–2, when his damage is weak and his mana runs out quickly. Lower his health and force him to recall early; if you fail to do so, his core items will make him extremely hard to kill, and he can keep pushing the lane.
notes.sion-combo-setup: For basic poke, use E to slow the target, then land Q. The slow keeps them from escaping even if you charge Q fully, so treat E as setup for Q rather than a damage skill. Without E, the opponent has plenty of time to see Q coming and walk out.
notes.sion-combo-engage: When engaging, follow R's collision stun with Q, W, then E. There usually is not enough time to charge Q fully before the stun ends, so release it as soon as it gains the knockup to make sure it lands. Activate W's shield just before engaging, then detonate it once the opponents group up.
notes.sion-skill-q-target: Q deals reduced damage to minions but greatly increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for pressuring objectives and the jungle rather than pushing waves. When taking a large monster with your jungler, save Q for it to speed up the clear noticeably.
notes.sion-skill-w: W is a two-stage ability: it grants a shield that you can detonate with a recast after a short delay. Watch the indicator for how much shield remains and detonate it just before it disappears to get both protection and damage. Its passive also permanently increases your maximum health whenever you kill a unit, so securing last hits helps you scale.
notes.sion-skill-e: E stops at the first target it hits, but striking a minion or monster pushes that unit back and applies the same damage and effects to enemies it hits. Pushing a minion into your opponent is Sion's main lane poke. E also reduces armor, so use it first when engaging alongside an allied physical damage dealer.
notes.sion-skill-r: Sion is unstoppable during R, but its limited steering makes straight paths the best approach; avoid winding routes and walls, which stop the charge. Damage and stun duration increase with distance, so start from far away, and remember that you can recast R to stop before hitting the wrong target.
notes.sion-skill-passive: During his post-death revival, Sion's abilities are replaced by a single ability, his attack speed and life steal rise sharply, and his hits deal damage based on maximum health. Decide what to do before you die: usually attack a turret, push out a wave, or buy time for allies to retreat.
notes.sion-laning: At 14 minutes, Sion ranks among the champions with the fewest kills and deaths, so focus on safe farming and stacking maximum health through W rather than chasing kills in lane. Push minions into opponents with E to poke, use Q only when they are immobilized, and prioritize CS and turret plates even if you lose a trade.
notes.sion-phase: Sion struggles to apply pressure with a single ability at levels 1–2. His first power spike comes at level 6, after investing points in Q and unlocking R. He is strongest in the mid to late game, when the maximum health gained through W combines with defensive items; even if he dies, Glory in Death effectively lets him fight twice. If he falls far behind early, he lacks the damage to turn things around on his own.
notes.sion-teamfight-engage: Start R from fog of war or behind a wall and charge toward the enemy backline; a charge from straight ahead gives opponents time to sidestep. Check that your allies are close enough to follow, because arriving alone means landing one stun and dying.
notes.sion-teamfight-role: In teamfights, hold the frontline, reduce enemy armor with E, and keep opponents pinned down with Q's area stun and W's explosion. Since his passive lets him fight again after death, Sion is better off falling while blocking the path to his damage dealers than retreating to survive. That revival is most valuable around objectives, though, so dying without a reason still puts your team behind.
notes.sion-situational-thornmail: If an enemy physical damage dealer is sustaining through healing, build Thornmail earlier. Sion already takes hits on the frontline, putting him in an easy position to keep applying its reflected damage and healing reduction.
notes.sion-situational-spirit: If most enemy damage is magic, choose Spirit Visage as a defensive item. Its healing and shield amplification benefits both W's shield and Sion's life steal during his revival, giving it value beyond its defensive stats.
notes.vs-sion-q: Forcing Sion to release Q early denies its knockup and stun. His movement slows while he charges, so move sideways rather than backward to dodge most casts; if you cannot escape, get close and pressure him into releasing early to greatly reduce the damage.
notes.vs-sion-r: Sion's R travels almost straight and has limited steering, so sidestep it rather than running forward or backward, and avoid meeting him in narrow passages or along walls. Its damage and stun duration increase with distance; if you must block him, intercept him just after he starts charging.
notes.vs-sion-passive: Sion revives shortly after dying, attacks very quickly, and deals damage based on maximum health. When he falls, reposition until the revival ends instead of continuing to fight where he died. His life steal rises sharply during the revival, making healing reduction especially valuable then.
notes.vs-sion-w: Sion must wait a short time after activating W's shield before he can detonate it. Breaking the shield first prevents the explosion, so focus your damage on him as soon as he activates W.
notes.vs-sion-scaling: Sion permanently gains maximum health whenever he kills a unit, so letting him keep farming makes him harder to face over time even if you cannot kill him. Push the lane to disrupt his farming or use that time to gain an advantage in another lane; ignoring him and letting the game drag on is the worst choice.
notes.sion-skill-q-charge: Q deals more damage the longer you charge it, gaining a knockup after a certain point and a stun with further charge. Sion cannot move while charging, so opponents can walk out; in lane, releasing Q as soon as it gains the knockup is often the right call. A full charge is worthwhile only when the opponent is already immobilized.
notes.sivir-combo-w-reset: Activating W Ricochet resets Sivir’s basic attack timer, so use it right after an attack to land a second one immediately. Make basic attack → W → basic attack a habit, and don’t activate W in advance while waiting.
notes.sivir-combo-wave: To clear a wave, activate W Ricochet and attack a front minion to start the bounces, then finish with Q Boomerang Blade. Q deals progressively less damage to non-champion targets, but that reduction resets on its return, so line up both paths with the minion wave to hit it twice.
notes.sivir-combo-r: After activating R On The Hunt, each basic attack against a champion reduces your basic abilities’ cooldowns, so keep attacking to bring Q Boomerang Blade and W Ricochet back faster than usual. A takedown resets R’s duration; keep R active and continue basic attacking until you’re sure the teamfight is over.
notes.sivir-skill-q: Q Boomerang Blade returns to Sivir at maximum range. Move sideways after throwing it to change its return path and hit an opponent who dodged it on the way out. Its high mana cost makes a missed Q especially costly in lane.
notes.sivir-skill-w: W Ricochet prioritizes targets its bounces have not hit yet and can bounce to each target only a set number of times. Attacking the enemy front line can therefore damage the back line too. Low-health minions die immediately to it, so avoid attacking minions with W active when you don’t want to push the lane.
notes.sivir-skill-e: E Spell Shield is Sivir’s only defensive tool. Save it for abilities that root or stun you instead of spending it on poke. A successful block restores health and triggers the movement speed from Fleet of Foot, making that the moment to counterattack.
notes.sivir-skill-passive: Fleet of Foot sharply increases Sivir’s movement speed whenever she damages an enemy champion. She has no dash, so use that speed to dodge: reposition immediately after landing Q or a basic attack, moving between attacks.
notes.sivir-skill-r: R On The Hunt speeds up your entire team: activate it as your allies engage or retreat. Using it just to escape alone wastes its value, so check that your teammates are grouped first.
notes.sivir-phase: Sivir’s high Q mana cost makes extended laning difficult, though her wave clear is among the best. At level 6, R On The Hunt lets her team engage or disengage, and she is strongest during midgame sieges once she has attack speed and critical strike. With no dash, she is weak in late-game duels, so look for larger fights where she can maintain her range.
notes.sivir-laning: Sivir clears waves faster than almost any bot lane duo. Push your opponents under their turret and take its plates, but secure river vision first because pushing leaves you exposed to ganks. Save E Spell Shield for the enemy jungler’s engage ability.
notes.sivir-laning-e-bait: Opponents may feint an engage to draw out E Spell Shield. Use it when an ability actually comes toward you, rather than at the first sign of an engage; if you are unsure, back away. Sivir is easy to kill if caught while E is down, and opponents know it.
notes.sivir-teamfight: In teamfights, stay in the back line and attack the enemy front line with W Ricochet. Its bounces reach the back line, so there’s no need to overextend to hit enemy damage dealers directly. Activate R On The Hunt when your team signals an engage or retreat, then keep attacking to reduce Q and W’s cooldowns.
notes.sivir-objective: A Sivir composition wins through sieging. Clear waves quickly to pin opponents under their turret, then use R On The Hunt to bring your team forward and take it. If the opponents come out, use R to retreat; this gives Sivir’s team the first move during a standoff around an objective.
notes.sivir-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item. W Ricochet can bounce across multiple opponents, spreading Grievous Wounds through their team.
notes.vs-sivir-e: Sivir’s E Spell Shield completely blocks one ability. Repeatedly feint an engage and pull back to draw it out, then apply guaranteed crowd control. A targeted engage ability used without preparation while E is ready will simply be blocked.
notes.vs-sivir-q: Sivir’s Q Boomerang Blade costs a lot of mana, so dodging it puts her at a disadvantage. If it hits you on the way out, anticipate its return path and step off that line; she wants to hit you both ways.
notes.vs-sivir-push: Sivir’s wave clear is among the best, and leaving her alone in lane lets her damage your turret. Before leaving, push the wave or arrange for another teammate to catch it. Keeping Sivir tied to lane also lets you create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
notes.vs-sivir-mobility: Sivir has no teleporting mobility ability and relies only on the movement speed from her passive. When E Spell Shield is down, she is among the easiest marksmen to catch, so prioritize diving her.
notes.vs-sivir-r: When Sivir activates R On The Hunt, her entire team speeds up, making a chase or slow retreat likely to end badly. While R is active, take only short fights that use terrain and vision, and wait for it to end.
notes.skarner-combo-engage: Before engaging, activate Q on a minion or jungle monster so you can land empowered basic attacks immediately instead of spending time casting it after you enter. Charge through terrain with E, drag the target into a wall to stun them, and stack Quaking with Q-empowered basic attacks during the stun. As your allies close in, suppress the target with R and pull them toward your team.
