notes.skarner-combo-r-turn: Targets suppressed by Skarner’s R are dragged in the direction he moves. Just before it ends, turn back the other way: the target shifts to the opposite side of his model, extending the drag once more. Always use this final turn when pulling someone deep into your team.
notes.skarner-skill-q: Activating Q empowers your next few basic attacks and increases attack speed, with the final hit delivering the maximum-health-based damage and slow. Recasting it gives up the remaining hits to throw a rock that deals the same damage at range. If you can stay in basic attack range, land every empowered hit; throw the rock only after the target escapes that range.
notes.skarner-skill-w: W grants a shield based on Skarner’s maximum health and slows nearby enemies. Its short duration means casting it before engaging can leave you without a shield when the damage lands, so use it just before taking a hit or when you’ve already been caught. Health items increase the shield, letting tank items improve both defense and damage.
notes.skarner-skill-e: E charges through terrain and drags any champion or large monster it catches until the charge ends. To stun the target, you must slam into a wall together, so approach with the wall behind them. A successful wall hit greatly reduces E's cooldown, letting you use it again soon; if the angle is unavailable, recast E to end the charge early and limit the loss.
notes.skarner-skill-r-mechanic: R suppresses its target, so most mobility abilities and Cleanse cannot free them; because it is not a channel, stuns and silences cannot interrupt it either. Quicksilver Sash and Mercurial Scimitar can remove the suppression, so check the target's build before casting. R can also drag enemies across terrain, including from the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit into the pit.
notes.skarner-skill-r-target: R can suppress multiple targets in front of Skarner at once, but choose whom to catch. Suppressing an enemy engage champion stops their team's initiation, while pulling an enemy off your carry protects your damage dealer. Decide which use you need before the fight so you do not waste R in a rush.
notes.skarner-laning-path: Skarner's early jungle route is not built around kills: his kills at 14 minutes and damage per minute rank near the bottom, while his death statistic ranks near the top. Clear camps safely to gain levels and items, then take control of objectives. E routes through walls also help you avoid enemy vision when counterjungling.
notes.skarner-laning-gank: For the strongest gank, choose the wall you want to hit, then enter from the opposite side with E and push the target into it. E cannot stun in open ground, so there you must rely on Q's slow and your allies' crowd control. Delay ganks in lanes without a wall angle until after level 6.
notes.skarner-phase: Before level 6, Skarner can stun during a gank only if E slams the target into a wall. Once R becomes available at level 6, its guaranteed suppression makes ganks possible in any lane regardless of terrain. Q and E scale with health, while W grants a shield based on maximum health, so defensive items also increase his damage. Win rates rise sharply once three core items are completed; the more time Skarner has to build, the stronger he gets.
notes.skarner-teamfight: In teamfights, engage from the front to isolate a target rather than deal damage. Pull a key enemy toward your team with R to create a temporary numbers advantage, but commit only when your carry can damage that target immediately. Otherwise, hold R and buy time with Q's slow and W.
notes.skarner-situational-mr: If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, include Spirit Visage in your core item build to strengthen W's shield and your defenses.
notes.skarner-situational-attackspeed: If the enemy team has a champion with a large attack speed boost, consider Frozen Heart to reduce the basic attacks you take while dragging them with R.
notes.vs-skarner-e: Skarner's E charges through terrain but stuns a caught target only if he slams them into a wall. Avoid standing with your back to one: in open ground, E pushes you without stunning you. If he does land the wall hit, its cooldown drops sharply, so retreat with his next charge in mind.
notes.vs-skarner-r-cleanse: Skarner’s R suppresses its target, so movement abilities and most cleanses cannot break free. It is not a channel, either, and cannot be interrupted by stuns or silences. Quicksilver Sash and Mercurial Scimitar are effectively the only ways to remove it, so carries facing Skarner should decide in advance whether to include one in their build.
notes.vs-skarner-r-position: Skarner's R has short range. Skarner can drag a target across terrain with R. When trying to steal an objective, watch out for Skarner's R at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit.
notes.vs-skarner-range: Skarner deals his damage by staying close and stacking Quaking with Q-empowered basic attacks. Outside melee range, only the recast rock throw can hit you. Positioning where he cannot catch you can cut the damage you take by at least half.
notes.vs-skarner-scaling: Skarner's abilities scale with his health and defensive stats, so tank items increase both his damage and survivability. Given time, he becomes hard to kill while repeatedly locking targets down. Take early jungle control and objectives to delay his item completions.
notes.skarner-skill-passive: Basic attacks, Q, and R stack Quaking, which deals magic damage based on the target's maximum health at full stacks. That makes it worthwhile to stack on high-health frontline champions in teamfights. Since stacks expire, stay on the same target once you commit.
notes.smolder-skill-passive: Dragon Practice stacks when you hit a champion with an ability or kill an enemy with Q, and those stacks never expire. Every Q last hit is permanent growth, making each minion more valuable to Smolder than to most marksmen; even if you fall behind in lane, don't miss one.
notes.smolder-skill-q-evolve: Q evolves at certain Dragon Practice stack thresholds: it starts as single-target damage, then spreads damage around its target, sends explosions beyond the target, and finally burns the target for damage based on their maximum health over time. Each evolution brings a sharp increase in waveclear and teamfight impact, so the stacks remaining until the next one are a measure of your progress.
notes.smolder-skill-q-mana: Killing a target with Q refunds mana, so Smolder rarely runs out while farming, but repeatedly using it only on champions drains his mana quickly. When harassing, weave Q between minion last hits to recover mana.
notes.smolder-skill-w: W explodes only when it hits a champion and grants one stack per champion hit; using it on minions gives you neither explosion damage nor stacks. If it hits multiple champions, each successive explosion deals less damage, so line it up to hit your intended target first, even in a teamfight. Its slow also helps you disengage from enemies who get close.
notes.smolder-skill-e: E lets Smolder fly over terrain while automatically attacking the enemy with the lowest health. You cannot choose its target, so the enemy you want to hit must have the lowest health. As Smolder's only practical escape and way to cross walls, E should be saved for potential ganks instead of used early for damage.
notes.smolder-skill-r: R (MMOOOMMMM!) deals damage over a wide area, slows enemies at its center, and heals Smolder when its flames reach him. Cast it beneath yourself while retreating to gain both healing and a slow. In teamfights, center it on grouped enemies; if you’re in danger, cast it at your own position without hesitation.
notes.smolder-combo-trade: Start a trade by landing W (Achooo!) to gain a stack, then follow up with Q (Super Scorcher Breath) and a basic attack. Since Q is targeted and guaranteed to hit, use the less reliable W first to check for an opening before moving in. If W misses, give up the trade and back off.
notes.smolder-combo-escape: To escape, slow the enemy with W, fly over a wall with E, then cast R beneath yourself for healing if needed. Decide which way you'll cross the wall beforehand: E ignores terrain only briefly, and you can get stuck if that effect ends halfway through.
notes.smolder-laning: In lane, farm safely and build stacks with Q last hits.
notes.smolder-laning-wave: Before Q's first evolution, you have virtually no way to push a wave, so let it come toward your tower and last hit there. Once Q starts damaging enemies around its target, faster waveclear gives you lane priority; use that opening to secure vision and objectives.
notes.smolder-phase: Smolder is weakest at levels 1–2 and early on with few stacks. He grows noticeably stronger with each Q evolution and becomes a hypercarry late in the game as stacks and items accumulate. You can catch up by continuing to stack even when behind, so the further behind you are, the more you should favor farming over fighting.
notes.smolder-teamfight: Smolder is a backline damage dealer with no way to engage and low movement speed. Positioning is everything: stay behind your frontline and use Q whenever it is ready, saving E to survive rather than using it for damage.
notes.smolder-teamfight-target: Q targets an enemy directly, so its damage stays reliable even in a chaotic fight. Don't overextend to reach the backline; start with the closest enemy in range. Once Q evolves, hitting that frontline target also spreads damage to nearby enemies.
notes.smolder-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing Q's damage over time, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.vs-smolder-stacks: Smolder grows permanently stronger whenever he hits a champion with an ability or kills an enemy with Q (Super Scorcher Breath). Avoiding his poke and denying him CS is the only way to weaken his late game, so disrupting his farming in lane is often more important than getting a kill.
notes.vs-smolder-early: Smolder's level-one health and armor are among the lowest of any champion, and E is his only escape. Keep up the pressure in the early and mid game so he cannot stay in lane, and make him a top priority for jungle ganks.
notes.vs-smolder-e: E is Smolder's only escape over terrain, so the moment after he uses it is practically your only chance to catch him. Save immobilizing crowd control and Flash for that window. E also automatically attacks the enemy with the lowest health, so a low-health ally in front will draw its damage.
notes.vs-smolder-w: Smolder's W explodes and grants a stack only when it hits a champion. Stand behind minions or move sideways to dodge it, denying him both damage and growth. Prioritize avoiding W: its slow leaves you exposed to a follow-up Q and basic attacks.
notes.vs-smolder-r: Smolder's R covers a wide area and deals much more damage at its center. Its flames also heal him when they reach him, so chasing into an R cast beneath his feet helps him recover. Move out of its area, then approach again.
notes.vs-smolder-late: The longer the game goes, the more it favors Smolder. Take objectives and towers quickly to end the game in the mid game; if it looks likely to go late, have a way to engage and kill him as soon as a teamfight starts.
notes.sona-skill-aura-switch: Sona’s basic abilities each have an immediate effect and an aura that lingers briefly around her. Only the aura from her most recent ability remains, so casting abilities back to back replaces the previous aura; using all three at once wastes two. Choose the aura your team needs and keep it active. Because allies must enter its range to benefit, step toward them right after casting, then back away.
notes.sona-skill-powerchord: Power Chord empowers Sona’s next basic attack after she uses basic abilities a set number of times. Its effect depends on the last ability used: finishing with Q increases its bonus damage, while finishing with E slows the target. Choose the final cast accordingly—Q when a kill is within reach, or E when escaping or helping allies chase.
notes.sona-skill-accelerando: Effective basic ability casts permanently stack Accelerando’s ability haste; once it reaches its cap, further stacks directly reduce Sona’s ultimate cooldown. Q must hit a champion, while W must actually heal an ally or block damage with its shield. Casting into empty space earns no stack, so landing useful abilities in lane helps Sona use her ultimate more often later.
notes.sona-skill-q: Q, Hymn of Valor, automatically hits two nearby enemies and prioritizes champions, even when minions stand in front of them. Its aura empowers allies’ next basic attacks, so use Q when your AD carry can land one to get value from both effects. Q is also Sona’s main way to stack Accelerando during laning.
notes.sona-skill-w: W, Aria of Perseverance, heals immediately and grants a brief shield through its aura. The shield lasts too little time to apply well in advance, so cast W as an enemy ability is about to hit. It has the highest mana cost of Sona’s basic abilities; spamming it for small heals in lane can leave her unable to respond when a trade starts.
notes.sona-skill-e: E increases Sona's movement speed and also speeds up allies through its aura. If Sona takes no damage, E's self movement speed boost lasts longer. In a fight, use E when engaging or disengaging.
notes.sona-combo-lane: Hit the enemy with Q, let your AD carry land a basic attack empowered by Q's aura, then use W to absorb the counterattack. Use Q, W, then Q so the last cast gives you the bonus damage Power Chord.
notes.sona-combo-r: R, Crescendo, is a straight-line area stun that works for both engaging and disengaging. If the target is out of range, Flash and immediately cast R through the enemy formation, then use E to speed up your allies’ engage. If the enemy engages first, sweep R across the incoming champions to stop them. R does not set Sona’s aura; the last basic ability used before it does, so choose that aura in advance.
notes.sona-laning: Laning as Sona is a test of mana management: her health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, so taking hits leaves her at a disadvantage, while repeatedly healing with W (Aria of Perseverance) drains her mana first. Poke mainly with Q (Hymn of Valor) early and use W only when guaranteed enemy damage is coming in. Against a melee engage support, secure brush vision first to deny their opening.
notes.sona-roaming: E lets Sona join fights and roam quickly, but leaving lane exposes her AD carry. Roam when the wave is pushed or your AD carry has recalled; otherwise, spend time securing vision around the mid entrances and river to open a path for your jungler. After level 6, arriving mid with R ready improves the chance of a successful gank.
notes.sona-vision: Don't walk alone through areas without vision. Place wards from outside the brush, close enough to cover it without entering.
notes.sona-teamfight: In teamfights, stay back but close enough for your auras to reach allies. Use E (Song of Celerity) to speed up their engage before the fight starts, then alternate W (Aria of Perseverance) and Q (Hymn of Valor) while keeping your auras on them. Aim R (Crescendo) through multiple grouped enemies, unless you can reliably stop a single enemy engaging on your carry; that is more valuable.
notes.sona-phase: Sona is weakest early: her health and attack damage are among the lowest in the game, and her high mana costs make it hard to control lane. At level 6, R lets her start or stop fights. From mid game, Accelerando stacks and support items let her cycle abilities noticeably faster; late game, continuous aura use sustains her whole team through extended teamfights.
notes.sona-situational-cleanse: If the enemy team uses crowd control to lock down and kill an allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing between core items. W's shield lasts only briefly, making it hard to absorb damage while an ally is already under crowd control.
notes.vs-sona-r: Sona’s R, Crescendo, travels in a straight line and stuns everyone it hits. When she is visible, spread sideways instead of lining up with allies. Its range is limited, so treat her stepping forward as a warning that she may cast it.
notes.vs-sona-aura: Sona delivers healing, shields, and movement speed to nearby allies through her auras. Separate her from the group or push her back so those effects reach no one. Even if she survives, disrupting her position removes much of her team’s staying power.
notes.vs-sona-lane: Sona’s health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, and her abilities cost a lot of mana. Keep forcing trades in lane: using W (Aria of Perseverance) to heal through them will drain her mana first. The best time to catch her is when she steps forward to bring an aura to her allies.
notes.vs-sona-e: E helps Sona escape, and its movement speed boost lasts longer if she takes no damage. When targeting her, apply immobilizing crowd control first; a slow alone is insufficient. If her team retreats, decide whether to chase before she activates E, which can cut off the pursuit.
notes.vs-sona-powerchord: After Sona uses basic abilities several times, her next basic attack is empowered. If she suddenly enters basic attack range, assume she has it ready and create distance before she attacks: depending on the ability she used immediately beforehand, the hit can deal bonus damage or slow you.
notes.vs-sona-heal: Late game, Sona can keep cycling auras to heal her team, making prolonged teamfights harder to turn around. Have at least one anti-heal item on your team: physical damage dealers can buy Executioner’s Calling, while magic damage dealers can buy Morellonomicon.
notes.soraka-combo-qw: The basic sequence is to land Q on an enemy champion, then use W. A champion hit by Q grants Soraka Rejuvenation, which nearly eliminates W’s health cost and passes the effect to the ally she heals. Using W first costs far more of Soraka’s health for the same healing.
notes.soraka-combo-eq: E alone rarely roots an enemy. Land Q first to slow them so they cannot walk out before E's area expires, then place E over them; you can also place it over an enemy already slowed or caught in an ally's crowd control. The order is not E into Q.
notes.soraka-skill-q-lead: The farther Soraka casts Q, the longer the star takes to fall. At long range, aim for where the enemy will retreat after a last hit rather than where they are standing now. When landing Q is urgent, cast from as close to the enemy as possible to shorten its fall time.
notes.soraka-skill-q-vision: Q briefly reveals where it lands. If you want to save a ward or checking a brush yourself is risky, cast Q into the brush instead. For a support, this is Q's second use.
notes.soraka-skill-w-cost: W costs Soraka health rather than mana. Casting it repeatedly in a short time without Rejuvenation quickly drains her health, and she cannot cast it at all below a certain health threshold. If you have to spam heals during a trade, your positioning has already gone wrong.
notes.soraka-skill-e-interrupt: E casts instantly, so it can interrupt channeled abilities, and its silence can stop enemies from engaging through the area. In practice, placing it ahead of time on a path the enemy must cross or at a Teleport landing spot works more often than trying to land the root.
notes.soraka-skill-e-nowave: E does not damage minions or jungle monsters, so it cannot clear a wave. Save its cooldown for fights instead of spending it on wave management.
notes.soraka-skill-passive: P grants movement speed only while Soraka moves toward a heavily wounded ally. Its marker also identifies an ally who will receive increased healing from R, so use it to time R for maximum effect. Enemies can read Soraka’s sudden speed boost as a sign that a low-health ally is nearby, so take care when that ally needs to move discreetly.
notes.soraka-skill-r: R heals every ally regardless of distance, with more healing for those who have lost a large amount of health. Even during laning, use it to help fights in other lanes rather than holding it. Save it only when you are certain that just one ally will die and R cannot save them.
notes.soraka-laning: Soraka's laning relies on a cycle of restoring her health with Q and transferring it to an ally with W. During laning, keep landing Q poke to restore Soraka's health. If Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
notes.soraka-laning-position: Soraka has some of the lowest movement speed and health, with no mobility ability. Against an engage opponent, hold E to stop them as they come in instead of spending it on poke. The moment after you use E to poke is their best opportunity to engage.
notes.soraka-teamfight: In teamfights, stay out of enemy vision when possible.
notes.soraka-phase: At level 1, learn Q if you want to reach level 2 first or gain control through early poke; learn W if you plan to help leash your jungler or play defensively. After that, the usual approach, as the statistics indicate, is to prioritize healing. Soraka’s map-wide impact grows in the mid to late game as R’s cooldown gets shorter.
notes.soraka-teamfight-antiheal: Engage as soon as the enemy's healing reduction wears off.
notes.vs-soraka-e: Soraka's E has a long cooldown. If she uses it first to poke or push the wave, she has no way to stop an engage until it returns, so go in as soon as you see it used. Its area silences you, so use your engage ability before stepping into it.
notes.vs-soraka-w: W heals by consuming Soraka's own health. In lane, keep pressuring her marksman to force heals; her health will fall, and below a certain threshold she cannot heal at all. Preventing her from landing Q is what keeps that pressure going.
notes.vs-soraka-r: R heals all allies regardless of distance, so account for its cooldown even when looking for a kill in another lane. One cast can erase damage dealt gradually, but a short burst is harder to undo. Against a team with Soraka, do not split a kill attempt into smaller bursts.
notes.swain-combo-lane: In lane trades, place W in the enemy’s path ahead of time, land E while they are slowed, recast E to pull them in, then hit them with Q at close range. W comes first to deny them room to dodge E, rather than for its damage.
notes.swain-combo-q-close: Q fires several bolts that overlap up close, while only one hits at maximum range. Use it to finish an enemy after catching them rather than to poke from afar; using Q before pulling them in with E can cut its damage to half or less.
notes.swain-skill-e-range: E sends out a wave that returns, so aim to land it at maximum range. From that distance, the enemy has little time to react, making the root nearly certain and helping secure a Soul Fragment; up close, they can see the wave’s path and walk out of it.
notes.swain-skill-e-pull: Pulling an enemy after rooting them with E is optional. If you need to wait for an ally to engage, let the root hold them; if you need to move them toward your allies or out of turret range, recast immediately. The pull grants a Soul Fragment, so favor it when the other benefits are unclear.
notes.swain-skill-w: W takes time to land, but covers and reveals a wide area. Use it for information and to force a response: check brushes, interrupt recalls, track the enemy jungler’s path, or overlap it with E to force Flash. Clearing minions is its least valuable use.
notes.swain-skill-passive: Hitting a champion with W, pulling one with E, or an enemy champion dying grants a Soul Fragment, which permanently increases maximum health. Landing abilities on champions is itself a way to grow, so using W and E on champions throughout the laning phase instead of on minions builds a health advantage for later.
notes.swain-phase: Swain has E at level 1, but lacks the mana for repeated fights. Wave clear and poke strengthen as you level Q, and learning R at level 6 lets you win 2v2 fights. Soul Fragments steadily increase your health, making you tougher over time and preserving your late-game value as long as you do not fall too far behind early.
notes.swain-laning-poke: Swain ranks among the top supports in CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute, reflecting how central it is to his laning to hit both the wave and the enemy with Q. Cast Q as the opposing ADC steps forward to last-hit, poking them while clearing the wave.
notes.swain-laning-zone: Landing E keeps the enemy bot duo away from the wave for that window. Even without a kill, pressuring them whenever E comes off cooldown creates a CS lead, so use it to control the lane instead of saving it only for kill opportunities. While E is down, you have no way to catch them, so do not push the lane.
notes.swain-roaming: Swain has low movement speed and no dash or escape ability. The round trip for a roam costs too much, so stay in lane to maintain pressure and limit trips out to managing river vision; if the enemy jungler catches you while roaming, you have no way out.
notes.swain-teamfight: In teamfights, stand just behind your frontline and pull one enemy in with E. Activate R when the enemy engages as a group, where it can reach several champions and stay active. Swain cannot walk in first to start a fight without a dash.
notes.swain-situational-zhonya: Build Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier if the enemy has an engaging damage dealer who can kill Swain in an instant. His R gains value for as long as he stays alive, so surviving even one burst of damage can change the outcome of a fight.
notes.vs-swain-e: E’s wave travels forward and then returns. Dodging the first pass is not enough: stay out of its path until it disappears completely, or the returning wave can root you. Swain can then recast E to pull you in and land the rest of his combo.
notes.vs-swain-q: Q fires several bolts that overlap up close, while only one hits from far away. Keeping your distance sharply reduces Swain’s poke damage, so last-hit near the edge of Q’s range in lane.
notes.vs-swain-r: R stays active by draining nearby enemies, healing Swain as it does. When he transforms, leave its range rather than continuing to fight beside him; wait for his ultimate to end before reengaging.
notes.vs-swain-melee: Melee champions without a ranged way to last-hit lose substantial CS to Swain’s E pressure. Instead of trying to win trades, check summoner spell cooldowns and ward positions to create a gank opportunity for your jungler.
notes.vs-swain-mobility: Swain has no mobility or escape ability and moves slowly. If you dodge his E root, he cannot get away, so gank or force a fight right after he uses E.
notes.vs-swain-sustain: Swain permanently increases his maximum health by hitting champions with abilities and heals continually with R. He grows tougher over time, so take lane priority early to limit his growth, then apply Grievous Wounds before engaging him in late-game fights.
notes.swain-combo-ult: Activate R, root the enemy with E, recast E to pull them in, then recast R. Wait until you have gained as much drain and healing as possible before that final recast, even if it becomes available sooner.
notes.swain-skill-r: R stays active only while it keeps draining enemy champions. If they walk out of range, its demonic energy quickly runs out and it ends, so activate it only when you have a way to hold them nearby. With E on cooldown and no allied crowd control, there is nothing to drain and R’s time simply runs out.
notes.sylas-combo-basic: Close in with E's first cast, land the second chain to knock the target up, then use an empowered basic attack, Q, a basic attack, W, and another basic attack. Each ability grants one passive stack, so weave basic attacks between casts to deal the full damage instead of using your abilities back to back.
notes.sylas-combo-q: Q explodes after a short delay where the chains cross.
notes.sylas-skill-e: E starts with a dash, then throws a chain that pulls Sylas to the target and knocks them up. Using only the first cast to engage leaves you with no way out, so use only that cast when escaping and save the second; when engaging, dash only if you have a clear angle to land the chain.
notes.sylas-skill-w: W is both a dash and a heal, and its healing scales with missing health, so using it for damage at full health wastes the most value. In a trade, land it on an enemy champion after taking damage to turn the exchange around.
notes.sylas-skill-passive: Petricite Burst's empowered basic attack damages enemies around the target and grants attack speed while stacks remain. Save those attacks for trades and use them together instead of spending them on minions.
notes.sylas-skill-r-mechanic: R Hijack copies an enemy champion's ultimate. Its power depends on Sylas's own R rank and stats, and even an ultimate with attack damage scaling is converted to ability power scaling, so Sylas's ability power items still apply when he steals an AD champion's ultimate.
notes.sylas-skill-r-target: After stealing a champion's ultimate, you cannot steal from that champion again for a long time. Keep several targets available and steal from a different champion in each fight to keep using R; if you rely on just one, you will have no ultimate for the next fight.
notes.sylas-skill-r-priority: Prioritize area crowd control and engage ultimates. If your team lacks a way to engage, steal one that starts fights; if you need to pick off an enemy carry, choose one that holds them in place. Single-target execute ultimates are less valuable because Sylas has trouble finding an opening to use them.
notes.sylas-phase: Sylas is weak at levels 1–2 because of his short range and tight mana supply. His first power spike comes at level 6, when he can steal an enemy ultimate, and he is strongest in the mid game once he has built both ability haste and ability power. Late in the game, his short range and low durability make direct fights difficult, so look for an opening where one stolen ultimate can make an impact.
notes.sylas-laning: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so using them all on the wave quickly drains it. Clear minions with Q's explosion, but keep one ability cast for a trade and save W for lane sustain. Sylas ranks near the bottom in CS, so expect to fall behind in farm and plan to make it up through fights and roams.
notes.sylas-laning-wave: Do not push the wave too hard before level 6: Sylas's short range leaves him exposed to the enemy jungler when he stands in front of a pushed wave. Once you learn R, shift to pushing the lane and joining fights elsewhere or around objectives.
notes.sylas-teamfight: Sylas’s role in a teamfight depends on the ultimate he has stolen, so secure one with R before the fight starts. When diving in with E, follow an ally’s engage rather than entering first, or you may be killed before you have a chance to heal. In a chaotic fight, use W to heal as soon as you take damage instead of saving it to finish someone off; surviving longer is more valuable.
notes.sylas-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is enough to undo your trades, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.sylas-situational-cc: Against a team that locks you down before you can get close, buy Quicksilver Sash early.
notes.vs-sylas-ult: Sylas uses R to copy an enemy's ultimate. If yours can turn a fight, use it before Sylas activates R or keep your distance so he cannot get in range to steal it.
notes.vs-sylas-early: Before level 6, Sylas is weak because of his short range and tight mana supply. Take control of the lane and push during this window to severely disrupt his farming.
notes.vs-sylas-w: The more health Sylas is missing, the more W heals him. If you bring him down to half health but delay finishing him, a single W can bring him back; apply healing reduction just before it lands if you have it.
notes.vs-sylas-e: Sylas's E has two stages: a dash that deals no damage, followed by a thrown chain. If the chain hits you, Sylas pulls himself to you, knocks you up, and lands his full combo, so time mobility abilities and Flash to dodge the second-stage chain rather than the initial dash.
notes.vs-sylas-q: Sylas's Q explodes after a short delay where the chains cross. Even if the first chain clips you, leave the crossing point immediately to avoid most of the damage.
notes.vs-sylas-teamfight: Sylas is fragile and most vulnerable just after diving in with E. Crowd control and attack him as he engages so he goes down before he can heal with W.
notes.syndra-combo-stun: Place Q beyond the enemy, then push its Dark Sphere through them with E to stun them. The sphere must be past the enemy, rather than between you and them: E only stuns enemies hit by a sphere it pushes, and without one, E merely knocks them back.
notes.syndra-combo-wq: Hit an enemy with a sphere or minion thrown by W to slow them, then follow immediately with Q. Casting Q after the slow makes it much more likely to land.
notes.syndra-combo-burst: For a full combo, place a sphere with Q, pick it up and throw it with W, push a remaining sphere with E to stun, then finish with R. R also fires spheres on the field, so placing as many as possible with Q before casting it determines how much damage it deals.
notes.syndra-combo-self-peel: When an enemy closes in, place Q beneath yourself or where they will land, then use E for both a stun and a knockback to regain distance. Have this sequence ready against enemies with gap closers.
notes.syndra-skill-q: Q spheres linger briefly after casting and can be used by W, E, and R, making Q both a damage ability and a setup tool. If a fight is likely, place one in advance to create an angle even if it deals no damage; you can cast Q while moving, whether you are retreating or approaching.
notes.syndra-skill-w: W can pick up and throw enemy minions and normal monsters as well as spheres, so it remains a poke option while Q is on cooldown. If mana is tight in lane, throw minions to keep trading. Without a selected target, W picks up the nearest sphere.
notes.syndra-skill-e: E has a long cooldown and is Syndra's only defensive ability. Against an enemy with a gap closer, save it for their engage instead of spending it on poke; if they have no way to close the gap, look actively for stuns with Q and E.
notes.syndra-skill-r: R fires both the spheres orbiting Syndra and those on the field at one target, so it is much weaker without spheres. Place as many as possible with Q before casting it. Once you have enough Splinters of Wrath, R executes low health targets, changing when you can use it to finish a fight.
notes.syndra-skill-passive: Syndra gains Splinters of Wrath by putting points into abilities and hitting champions. Her abilities gain additional effects at certain splinter thresholds, so quickly maxing one creates a power spike. Gaining splinters also restores mana, making consistent hits on champions part of managing it.
notes.syndra-phase: At levels 1–2, mana costs and cooldowns limit how often Syndra can poke. As Q levels up, she gains an advantage in lane, and R gives her a first chance to secure a kill at level 6. She peaks in the mid to late game as she gains splinters and ability power, but her health and armor are among the lowest, so poor positioning can end a fight for her immediately.
notes.syndra-laning: Syndra's CS statistics are among the best, so prioritize safe farming with her long range over risky poke. Place Q where an enemy will step up to last hit for low risk harass, save E for their engage, and avoid fully pushing the wave into a position that gives their jungler a gank opportunity.
notes.syndra-teamfight: Start teamfights from the back, pressuring the enemy formation with Q and W while saving E to push away anyone who engages. Use R only on a target you can reliably kill. Placing Q spheres before the teams clash strengthens R and sets up a stun with E.
notes.syndra-situational-antiheal: Against enemies who sustain through damage, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Syndra aims to kill with one combo; if an enemy heals through it, she must wait for her cooldowns before trying again.
notes.syndra-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive their initial engage. Syndra has no mobility ability, and once an enemy closes the gap, a single E may not be enough to escape.
notes.vs-syndra-e: E has a long cooldown and is Syndra's only defensive ability, leaving her most vulnerable immediately after she uses it. Close in at that moment.
notes.vs-syndra-orb-stun: Syndra's stun comes from a Dark Sphere pushed by E, rather than E alone. If a sphere is near you or between you and Syndra, she has an angle to stun you, so move out of the path it would take when pushed.
notes.vs-syndra-orbs-ult: R also fires spheres on the field, making areas with many spheres especially dangerous. If Syndra has placed several Q spheres in an area, either enter prepared to take her ultimate or move elsewhere.
notes.vs-syndra-maxrank: Syndra's abilities gain additional effects and change visually when they reach max rank. When an ability's visual effect changes, reassess your spacing to account for its different power or range.
notes.vs-syndra-dive: Syndra has some of the lowest health and armor and no mobility ability. If your champion can close the gap, engaging when her E is on cooldown can be enough to win the lane.
notes.vs-syndra-boots: Syndra's Q, W, and E are untargeted abilities placed on or thrown at the ground. Buying boots early gives you the movement speed to dodge many of them by walking.
notes.tahmkench-combo-stack: Every Tahm Kench combo starts with counting An Acquired Taste stacks: basic attacks and Q each add one, and when the third lands, Q stuns the target and R can swallow them. Stacks expire over time, so build them quickly with a basic attack–Q–basic attack sequence while staying close, and aim to make Q the third hit to secure the stun.
notes.tahmkench-combo-qr: Press R while Q is in flight, and if it hits a target with three stacks, Tahm Kench swallows them from range. This is his only way to swallow someone without getting close, so prepare the Q–R combo against a target with two stacks and look for an angle to land Q.
notes.tahmkench-combo-allin: To engage at close range, emerge beneath the enemy with W (Abyssal Dive) to knock them up, build stacks with basic attacks, stun them with Q (Tongue Lash), then use R (Devour). W’s landing spot remains hidden from enemies briefly after its channel begins, making it useful for a surprise engage, and hitting a champion refunds part of its cooldown and mana cost. A miss leaves you without a way to engage or escape for a long time, so open with W only when you can land it reliably.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-ally: An ally swallowed with R (Devour) cannot be targeted while inside Tahm Kench and gains a large shield after being spat out. This is Tahm Kench’s greatest value, so swallow them just before an enemy’s finishing ability arrives rather than waiting until they are about to die. The ally can leave on their own at any time, so coordinate with them.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-taxi: While carrying an ally, Tahm Kench is rooted, but he can still use W (Abyssal Dive) and briefly gains movement speed. Swallow an ally with R (Devour), then use W to carry them out of danger or bring an ally with an engage ability deep into the enemy team. Before using it to engage, check that you can spit them out somewhere they can fight immediately.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-enemy: While swallowing an enemy with R (Devour), Tahm Kench is heavily slowed and rooted, leaving him vulnerable. Use it on an enemy only when your allies can kill them immediately or when you are in a safe position, such as under a turret; otherwise, save R to protect an ally.
notes.tahmkench-skill-e: E stores damage already taken as gray health and converts it into a shield, so pressing it with nothing stored does nothing. Using it before a fight is a waste; after taking heavy damage, press it just before the next burst for the most value. Several nearby enemy champions increase the share of damage stored, making the shield especially strong in teamfights. If you go without taking damage for a while, stored gray health restores your health on its own, so let it heal you between fights instead of using E.
notes.tahmkench-skill-q: Q is Tahm Kench’s only ranged poke and healing tool. Hitting a champion heals you based on your missing health, making it more effective the lower you are and potentially saving you in a crisis. If healing is not urgent, consider holding Q to stun a target with three stacks.
notes.tahmkench-skill-passive: Tahm Kench’s basic attacks deal bonus magic damage based on his bonus health. Health items therefore improve both his defense and damage, leaving little reason to add attack items just for damage. Weave basic attacks into lane trades to build stacks and deal damage at the same time.
notes.tahmkench-laning: Top lane is a fight over stacks. When an enemy with two stacks steps forward to last-hit, land Q (Tongue Lash) to secure the stun, then add a basic attack. Trading aggressively at close range with no stacks offers little benefit, so pressure them only while your stacks remain active.
notes.tahmkench-laning-bait: Even below half health, Q healing and E’s stored gray health make Tahm Kench much tougher than his health bar suggests. Enemies often dive based on that bar alone, so stay near your turret at low health and look to counter their engage with a stun and R.
notes.tahmkench-phase: At levels 1–2, Tahm Kench poses little threat before he builds stacks. At level 6, R (Devour) lets him save allies; he peaks in the mid to late game as health items increase both his basic attack damage and the amount E (Thick Skin) stores. He cannot end games alone at any stage, so stay with your allies.
notes.tahmkench-teamfight: In teamfights, prioritize staying beside your allied carry over engaging. The moment an enemy engage reaches them, swallow the carry with R to negate it, then use Q’s slow and W’s knockup to keep the enemy away. If Tahm Kench dies first on the front line, your team loses its way to protect the carry.
notes.tahmkench-situational-mr: If the enemy team’s damage is mostly magic, fit Spectre’s Cowl between your core items. Because E (Thick Skin) stores gray health in proportion to damage taken, magic resistance improves how effectively Tahm Kench stores it and helps him survive longer.
notes.vs-tahmkench-stacks: Three hits from Tahm Kench’s basic attacks and Q (Tongue Lash) open up both a stun and a swallow. If you have two stacks, move out of range and wait for them to expire; he poses little threat without stacks.
notes.vs-tahmkench-e: Some damage dealt to Tahm Kench is stored as gray health and comes back as a shield or healing, making small trades followed by a retreat largely pointless. Engage only when you can focus him down and kill him in one go. Grievous Wounds reduces how much stored gray health returns as healing, so buy Executioner’s Calling or Morellonomicon early, whichever suits your scaling.
notes.vs-tahmkench-r-ally: An enemy swallowed by Tahm Kench cannot be targeted while inside him and gains a shield after being spat out. Before committing targeted finishing abilities, check whether his R (Devour) is available. If he swallows your target, keep up pressure with untargeted area abilities or stop Tahm Kench himself first.
notes.vs-tahmkench-r-enemy: While your ally is swallowed, Tahm Kench is rooted and heavily slowed. Stay together and focus your damage on him to interrupt the swallow as quickly as possible.
notes.vs-tahmkench-w: When Tahm Kench uses W (Abyssal Dive), his landing spot is briefly hidden. As soon as you see the dive animation, spread out so the area knockup cannot catch several of you. Without W, he has trouble both engaging and escaping.
notes.vs-tahmkench-target: Trying to kill Tahm Kench first is usually a losing trade: he has high health and defensive stats, along with several ways to heal. It is better to ignore him and focus untargeted damage on the carry he protects, while accounting for the extra chance to survive that his R gives the carry when it is available.
notes.taliyah-combo-ewq: Place E, then use W to push the enemy across its rocks; they will be stunned when the rocks erupt, giving you time to land Q. Using W first only pushes the enemy without stunning them.
notes.taliyah-combo-gank: If the enemy is already fleeing, aim W (Seismic Shove) to push them toward your allies; Taliyah chooses the direction of the push.
notes.taliyah-skill-q-direction: Q’s shards fly in a fixed line in the cast direction, so an enemy moving sideways can dodge them all. Fire when they cannot change their direction of movement. Successive shards deal sharply reduced damage to the same target starting with the second, so landing every shard on one champion does not give each shard its full value.
notes.taliyah-skill-q-worked-ground: Using Q creates Worked Ground beneath Taliyah. Casting Q there again costs almost no mana and halves its cooldown, but fires one slowing boulder instead of shards. Use shards from fresh ground to clear jungle camps and minion waves, and the Worked Ground boulder when chasing champions or escaping.
notes.taliyah-skill-e: E alone only slows and deals a little damage; it stuns an enemy only when they dash or are pushed across its rocks. Use it to deny an area by placing it in a narrow passage or entrance ahead of time, so an enemy who dashes in stuns themselves.
notes.taliyah-skill-w-peel: W’s knockup briefly takes an enemy out of the fight, and pushing a melee champion away from your allied marksman can save a teamfight. Because W takes time to activate, cast it on the enemy’s approach path before they reach your ally.
notes.taliyah-skill-r-restriction: You cannot use R if you recently took damage from a champion or structure.
notes.taliyah-skill-r-wall: R is useful even if you do not ride the wall. In a teamfight, place it through the middle of the enemy formation to separate their frontline from their backline, or block a fleeing enemy’s escape route. Once the wall is complete, you can destroy it immediately by casting R again; do so without delay if it blocks your allies’ pursuit.
notes.taliyah-skill-passive: Rock Surfing increases your movement speed near walls while you are out of combat. Route your jungle clears and roams along walls to cover the same distance much faster, and stay close to a wall when crossing the river.
notes.taliyah-laning-jungle: When Q (Threaded Volley) shards hit different monsters, each deals damage without reduction, so clear camps quickly to build an early lead instead of forcing ganks, then look for counterganks where you can predict the enemy jungler’s route.
notes.taliyah-phase: At levels 1–2, Taliyah is very fragile and spends a lot of mana, so conserve your abilities. Her combo becomes available at level 3, when she has Q, W, and E; her first power spike comes at level 6, when R lets her move across the map to intervene. She is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power items, but her health and armor are among the lowest in the game, so allowing even one enemy engage late can mean death.
notes.taliyah-teamfight: In teamfights, Taliyah stays back and shapes the terrain: place E on an approach path to narrow the enemy’s way in, then use W to push away anyone who still enters. Use R to split the enemy formation, placing its wall where grouped enemies are entering or along the enemy backline’s escape route.
notes.taliyah-teamfight-objective: Taliyah is strongest in fights inside tight spaces such as the Dragon or Baron pit. Place E in the already narrow terrain and block the entrance with R to leave enemies no way in or out. Check R’s cooldown before committing to an objective fight.
notes.taliyah-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a champion who survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon after one core item. Taliyah’s sustained damage keeps Grievous Wounds applied for a long time after the first application.
notes.vs-taliyah-e-w: If Taliyah places E (Unraveled Earth) nearby, expect W (Seismic Shove) immediately afterward. Move away from the rocks as soon as E appears: W will stun you if it pushes you across them, and standing between the rocks and Taliyah is the most dangerous position.
notes.vs-taliyah-q-dodge: Taliyah’s Q flies only in its cast direction and cannot turn midflight. Approaching or fleeing from her in a straight line lets the shards hit you, while a step to the side makes most of them miss.
notes.vs-taliyah-dash: Before dashing at Taliyah, check for E’s rocks on the ground. Dashing across them stuns you and leaves you exposed to her full combo. If the rocks are there, walk in or approach from an angle that goes around them.
notes.vs-taliyah-squishy: Taliyah’s health and armor are among the lowest in the game, and she has no healing or shielding ability of her own. A single movement disabling crowd control effect can leave her easy to kill, so spend your resources creating an opening to close in on her rather than absorbing her combo.
notes.vs-taliyah-r: Taliyah cannot use R if she recently took damage from a champion or structure. Keep dealing damage to stop her from escaping with it. If you have not damaged her yet, pursue with the possibility that she could put up a wall and escape at any moment.
notes.vs-taliyah-roam: Rock Surfing’s speed near walls and R let Taliyah reach fights across the map quickly. If she disappears from the jungle, consider that she may be heading to another lane rather than a nearby camp, and back off early.
notes.talon-combo-reliable: For a reliable combo, leap in with Q, cast W at close range, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Starting with Q lets both the outgoing and returning hits of W land, filling the stacks so one basic attack triggers the bleed. Use this sequence when you need to land the combo reliably.
notes.talon-combo-fast: For a fast combo, cast W, then close in with Q just before W returns. Its return hit will land as Q lands, completing your Blade's End stacks so one basic attack immediately triggers the bleed. Do not basic attack before Q: doing so makes you wait for the next attack and throws off the timing.
notes.talon-combo-fastest: For the fastest combo, throw W, use Q just after its first hit passes, and activate R during the leap. The stacks will be full when you land, so one basic attack triggers Blade's End's bleed. Because using R to engage leaves you without its invisibility to escape, only use this combo when you're certain you can kill the target.
notes.talon-skill-q: Q lands a critical hit without leaping when used in melee range; outside that range, Talon leaps to the target. Getting close with Flash or E before using Q therefore deals more damage with the same ability. Killing a target with Q refunds half its cooldown, so use it to last-hit minions for lane sustain and mana efficiency.
notes.talon-skill-w: W's returning hit deals more damage than its outgoing hit and applies a slow. Cast it from close range to land both hits; throwing it out from afar for poke gets only half its value. W is your main laning ability, but its early mana cost is high, so avoid overusing it and leaving yourself unable to cast when a kill opportunity appears.
notes.talon-laning: Talon is a melee champion with very short range, so stepping forward first in lane puts him at a disadvantage. Chip away at the enemy with W, then close in with Q only when they step forward to last-hit. Once you start a trade, follow through with a basic attack to trigger Blade's End before backing off; retreating with only stacks applied wastes mana.
notes.talon-roam: Talon's greatest strength is roaming across terrain with E. Push the wave, cross jungle walls to reach a side lane, and create a numbers advantage. If the enemy has vision in the jungle, the ambush loses its value, so clear that vision with a Control Ward or choose an unseen route before moving.
notes.talon-phase: Talon deals high damage from levels 1–2. Push the wave quickly: reaching level 2 before your opponent creates his best early kill opportunity. If they level up first, do not step forward during that window. His roaming and burst peak after he learns R, but his impact falls as the game goes on; later, he can die where he engages even after killing a backline target. When ahead, keep applying pressure to end the game.
notes.talon-teamfight: Choose your target before a teamfight. Committing all of Talon's abilities to one enemy secures the kill, while spreading them across several can leave everyone alive and Talon exposed. Engage after the enemy has used their crowd control on your allies, and save R's invisibility for a safer escape. If a frontal fight is difficult, use E to flank the enemy backline.
notes.talon-situational-antiheal: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Blade's End deals bleed damage over time, making the healing reduction easy to maintain.
notes.vs-talon-armor: All of Talon's damage is physical, so even one inexpensive armor item such as Cloth Armor noticeably reduces his burst early on. Prioritize armor over magic resistance or health when facing him.
notes.vs-talon-w: Talon needs both the outgoing and returning hits of W to complete his Blade's End stacks. Dodging the return prevents a substantial share of the damage and the bleed, so if the first hit lands, make getting out of the blades' return path your top priority.
notes.vs-talon-r: Talon relies heavily on R's invisibility to escape fights, so counterattack once you confirm he has used it. Avoid chasing too far while R is available: he can disappear, evade pursuit, and kill you instead.
notes.vs-talon-early: Around level 2, Talon can deal enough damage in one trade to secure first blood. Stay back and farm safely behind your minions during that window, and push the wave first so he does not level up before you.
notes.vs-talon-roam: Talon roams exceptionally quickly by crossing terrain. Keep your allies informed of his location and establish vision along jungle routes to prevent ambushes. Pushing the lane can force him back to farm, while clearing enemy vision with a Control Ward can give you the information to catch him instead.
notes.vs-talon-late: Talon's impact falls off as the game goes on. In late-game fights, group up and layer crowd control as soon as he engages: even if he kills a backline target, he can easily die on the spot, making the trade favorable. The longer the game goes, the less it favors Talon.
notes.talon-skill-passive: Blade's End builds stacks through abilities and triggers with a basic attack. Only abilities add stacks, and they last 6 seconds, so land your abilities in quick succession to reach three stacks.
notes.talon-skill-q-aa: Immediately after a Q leap, the shorter basic attack windup lets the attack come out at once. When finishing a combo with Q, use it as your last ability and follow with a basic attack for the fastest sequence.
notes.talon-skill-e: E, Assassin's Path, crosses terrain, but you cannot cross the same piece again for a considerable time, especially early on. Plan which terrain you will use to escape and save it while roaming. E counts as a dash, so targeted chain abilities can interrupt it; it can also cross terrain created by allies or enemies, with the same restriction on crossing it again.
notes.talon-skill-r: R, Shadow Assault, grants stealth and increased movement speed. Ending the stealth with a basic attack or Q sends the blades toward that target instead of Talon, concentrating the damage on one enemy. If it ends without a target, the blades converge on Talon and reveal the direction he fled, so account for that when using R to escape.
notes.taric-skill-bravado: Bravado makes Taric’s next two basic attacks faster and stronger after he uses an ability, and those attacks reduce his basic ability cooldowns. His basic rhythm is ability, then two attacks; without the attacks, his ability rotation slows by half. Even when backing off after a trade, using both attacks on minions brings E back noticeably sooner.
notes.taric-skill-bravado-armor: Bravado’s bonus damage and E’s damage both scale with bonus armor, so building armor improves Taric’s offense as well as his defense. Combined with his level 1 armor, which ranks among the highest of all champions, this makes his early melee trades hit harder than you might expect.
notes.taric-skill-q: Q (Starlight’s Touch) stores charges, gaining one each time a Bravado basic attack hits. Its mana cost stays the same regardless of how many charges it uses, so spending them one at a time is inefficient. Unless healing is urgent, save them to heal several allies at once; using a one-charge Q solely to trigger Bravado wastes mana.
notes.taric-skill-w-link: W (Bastion) gives Taric a second point from which to cast: while the linked ally is nearby, all his abilities also activate at that ally’s position. Before a teamfight, link someone on the side you will not occupy to cover more of your team. Recasting W moves the link and grants a shield, so switch it to allies in danger while accounting for where your abilities will now activate.
notes.taric-skill-e: E (Dazzle) stuns after a short, clearly telegraphed delay, so aim at where the enemy will be when it activates rather than where they are now. Catch them as they step in to last-hit a minion, or follow an ally’s immobilizing crowd control to secure the hit.
notes.taric-combo-w-e: E also activates from the ally linked by W. Stand slightly apart from that ally to spread the two beams and leave enemies less room to dodge. Linking an ally who is about to dash in also lets you start a fight with E from their position, even if they move beyond Taric’s range, without following them in.
notes.taric-skill-r: R Cosmic Radiance makes all nearby allies invulnerable after a significant delay, so casting it only once they are in danger is too late. Use it just before a fight begins or right after E, anticipating the situation a few seconds ahead. The invulnerability blocks damage but not crowd control; if allies are locked down when it activates, its duration ticks away while they cannot act.
notes.taric-combo-engage: To start a fight, link W to the ally who is about to engage, cast R early, stun with E, land two Bravado basic attacks, then heal with Q. The key is to time R’s activation for the peak of the damage trade after E’s stun; with this sequence, your ally can deal damage while invulnerable just after the stun ends.
notes.taric-laning: As a melee champion, Taric has no way to reach enemies without E. Save it to open a trade instead of using it to poke. Against a ranged support, you must endure their poke while E is down, so stay back when there is no opening to land it.
notes.taric-laning-cs: Using Bravado basic attacks on minions can easily steal your ADC’s last hits, so avoid minions that are nearly dead and hit healthy ones or targets the turret has already struck. Skipping basic attacks altogether slows your ability rotation; the choice is what to hit, not whether to hit anything.
notes.taric-roaming: Taric’s relatively high movement speed among supports makes joining fights and roaming manageable, but E’s delay means casting it only after arriving at a gank is too late. Predict the enemy’s escape route and cast ahead, or follow your jungler’s engage ability to secure the stun. Avoid rushing in without vision, which is especially dangerous for a melee support.
notes.taric-teamfight: Taric usually stands on the front line in teamfights, using W to extend his abilities to a second position. If you are up front, link a backline damage dealer; if you need to stay back, link an ally who is engaging. Go in when E is ready and you can cast R early enough to account for its delay.
notes.taric-phase: Taric’s melee trades become strong at levels 2–3 once he has both E and Q. His armor is among the highest at level one, and Bravado’s damage scales with armor, making early head-to-head fights surprisingly strong. At level six, R can completely negate enemy dives and explosive engages. As armor items accumulate in the mid to late game, that same stat helps him frontline and deal damage.
notes.taric-situational-armor: If the enemy's physical damage is high, build Frozen Heart or Randuin's Omen to increase both survivability and Bravado and E damage.
notes.vs-taric-r: Don't pour damage into enemies after Taric's R makes them immune to damage.
notes.vs-taric-r-cc: Taric’s R blocks damage but not crowd control. If an enemy becomes invulnerable, hold them with crowd control while its duration runs out. Manage positioning and crowd control instead of dealing damage during the invulnerability, then attack as soon as it ends.
notes.vs-taric-bravado: Bravado basic attacks reduce all of Taric’s ability cooldowns. Kite him or displace him with a knock-up so he cannot reach anything to attack; denying those two attacks noticeably slows his ability rotation and delays his next E and Q. Managing the wave to keep him away from minions has the same effect.
notes.vs-taric-e: Taric’s E has a clear warning before its delayed stun activates, and a step sideways can dodge it. Once E is down, he has no way to reach you and is exposed to ranged poke. Bait it out, then poke and trade during that window.
notes.vs-taric-w: Taric’s abilities also activate from the position of the ally linked by W, so judging distance from Taric alone can leave you in range of a stun from that ally. Treat the area around the linked champion as dangerous, especially if they dash in: E may activate from their position as they reach you.
notes.vs-taric-early: Taric's Bravado damage is strong from the early game and grows with armor.
notes.teemo-combo-trade: The basic trade is to wait stealthed in brush, emerge with a surprise auto, apply Q Blinding Dart, land one or two more autos, then disengage with W Move Quick. Breaking stealth grants attack speed, making this stronger than walking up to start a trade; one auto also leaves E Toxic Shot’s poison ticking, so there is no need to stay close.
notes.teemo-combo-allin: For the finishing combo, use Q Blinding Dart to stop a retaliatory auto, land an auto to apply E Toxic Shot’s poison, then throw R Noxious Trap into the enemy’s retreat path. Predict where they will flee and place the mushroom there, rather than at their feet, to layer on the slow and finish off their remaining health.
notes.teemo-skill-passive: Teemo enters stealth through P Guerrilla Warfare after standing still briefly without acting, and he can remain stealthed while moving inside brush. Entering brush ahead of time sets up the ambush: breaking stealth grants attack speed, turning that preparation into damage.
notes.teemo-skill-q: Q Blinding Dart disables basic attacks but does not stop abilities. It can negate an entire trade against an auto attack reliant opponent, while serving mainly as poke against an ability reliant one. Cast it as the enemy begins an auto; using it early wastes part of the blind duration.
notes.teemo-skill-q-monster: Q Blinding Dart lasts much longer on minions and jungle monsters than on champions. When your jungler is clearing a camp or your team is fighting over a large monster, consider using Q on the monster first; a single cast can be more valuable there than on a champion.
notes.teemo-skill-w: W Move Quick’s passive movement speed ends when a champion or turret hits Teemo, while its active speed persists through hits. Use the passive to move before a fight and the active during one, whether to escape or take a favorable angle.
notes.teemo-skill-e: E Toxic Shot adds damage over time to Teemo’s autos, so a single hit keeps dealing damage after he backs away. Trade by repeatedly hitting and retreating rather than staying in range; if a poisoned opponent approaches to retaliate, disengage without hesitation.
notes.teemo-skill-r-bounce: Throwing R Noxious Trap onto an existing mushroom makes it bounce farther, letting you plant it over a wall or in an area without vision without exposing yourself. Because R stores charges, save them when there is no urgency and place several together to block an entire route.
notes.teemo-skill-r-place: R Noxious Trap mushrooms last a long time and reveal enemies who step on them, so planting them around objectives and along enemy jungle routes also provides vision. They clear waves well when you need to leave a side lane and rotate, but spending every charge on farming leaves none for the places where fights will happen.
notes.teemo-laning: Against melee opponents, use Teemo’s range and E Toxic Shot’s poison to chip away with repeated single autos followed by retreats. Save Q Blinding Dart for the moment they begin a retaliatory auto. His low defensive stats and movement speed make him highly vulnerable to ganks, so after pushing the lane, plant R Noxious Trap mushrooms in the river and brush before trading again.
notes.teemo-phase: From level 3 onward, Teemo is strongest in lane against melee opponents, but that same phase is a weakness against longer range poke. From mid game, he controls side lanes and the map with mushrooms; in late head on teamfights, he is too fragile to stand at the front. His high damage per minute reflects accumulated damage over time and mushroom damage.
notes.teemo-teamfight: Teemo should prepare the site of a teamfight with R Noxious Trap mushrooms rather than enter the fight himself. Once it starts, stay back and apply E Toxic Shot’s poison with autos; the mushrooms should already cover the enemy’s entry and retreat routes. Before an expected objective fight, spend all available charges planting them around the area.
notes.teemo-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your core build. Teemo has no mobility ability and is fragile enough to die once caught, but mushrooms already planted and poison already applied keep dealing damage, so surviving briefly with Zhonya’s can make the exchange worthwhile.
notes.vs-teemo-q: Teemo’s Q Blinding Dart stops basic attacks but leaves abilities usable. If blinded, deal damage with abilities or retreat until it ends instead of trying to auto. Champions that rely on autos should trade immediately after Teemo uses Q; engaging while it is available lets him use its cooldown to deny their damage.
notes.vs-teemo-e: A single Teemo auto leaves E Toxic Shot’s poison ticking even if you back away, so brief hit and retreat trades favor him. Stay outside his auto range until you are ready to commit; once you engage, close the distance in one move and stay on him.
notes.vs-teemo-r: Use Oracle Lens to clear mushrooms from key routes. Assume they are planted around objectives and in narrow passages, and avoid familiar shortcuts when retreating. Mushrooms last a long time, so even ones placed well before the fight may still be there.
notes.vs-teemo-mobility: Teemo has low defensive stats and movement speed, and W Move Quick is his only way to escape. Push the lane and engage him with your jungler; an early lead can deny him the time to place mushrooms. Give him that time, and half the map becomes his territory.
notes.vs-teemo-brush: Teemo can stay stealthed while moving inside brush, then gain attack speed as soon as stealth breaks, giving him an early edge in a trade. Avoid walking past brush without vision: use a control ward or take another route, and wait until he comes out before retaliating.
notes.thresh-skill-passive: Through Damnation, each soul Thresh collects permanently increases his armor and ability power, even if he did not kill the unit; those souls also strengthen Dark Passage (W)'s shield and Flay (E)'s damage.
notes.thresh-skill-passive-safety: Stepping forward to collect souls leaves Thresh vulnerable to attacks, so use Dark Passage (W)'s lantern to collect souls within enemy range.
notes.thresh-skill-q: Death Sentence (Q) has a long windup that enemies can see and dodge in the open, so cast it from brush or outside their vision, or while they are locked into a last-hit animation or ability cast. Landing it grants true sight of the target and reduces its cooldown.
notes.thresh-skill-q-recast: Recasting Death Sentence (Q) sends Thresh flying toward the enemy it hit, so leave it unrecast if allies cannot follow up. Once their engage is confirmed, recast it to close in, then follow with Flay (E) and The Box (R).
notes.thresh-skill-w: An ally must click the Dark Passage (W) lantern to travel with it, so coordinate its use beforehand. It can bring your jungler into lane from across a wall, and it shields Thresh and the first ally to take it; throw it just before enemy burst damage lands.
notes.thresh-skill-e: Thresh’s E, Flay, pushes or pulls enemies in the direction you sweep: sweep from behind an enemy to pull them toward your allies, or from in front to push them away. That means you use it in opposite directions when engaging and protecting allies; to peel an assassin off your allied carry, stand behind the carry and sweep outward.
notes.thresh-skill-e-passive: Flay (E)'s passive grows stronger the longer Thresh waits after his last basic attack, so save attacks until a trade and use them one at a time. In lane, pair one empowered attack with Flay to harass.
notes.thresh-combo-hook-first: After landing Death Sentence (Q), basic attack, pull the enemy toward your allies with Flay (E), then use The Box (R) to block their escape if needed. Time Flay for the moment Q's stun ends to keep the enemy immobilized.
notes.thresh-combo-flay-first: Death Sentence (Q) and Flay (E) work in either order. Against an enemy already close to you, pull them in with Flay first, then cast Death Sentence at close range, where it is easier to land immediately after their movement is disrupted.
notes.thresh-combo-dive: After landing Death Sentence (Q), recast it to engage, block the path behind the enemy with The Box (R), then push them toward your allies with Flay (E). Only engage this deeply when you can immediately bring an ally in with Dark Passage (W).
notes.thresh-phase-early: Thresh can initiate in lane and create kill opportunities with Death Sentence (Q) as early as levels 1–2. Early on, focus on forcing enemies out of lane and collecting souls rather than getting kills.
notes.thresh-phase-scaling: Thresh's late-game durability depends on how many souls he collects, so keep gathering them after laning by passing through fight locations and around jungle camps.
notes.thresh-laning: Secure brush first to find Death Sentence (Q) angles hidden from the enemy. If they pressure the brush, back off, collect souls, and protect your carry's CS.
notes.thresh-teamfight: Choose whether to engage or protect allies based on the teamfight setup. When your team fights from the back, hold Death Sentence (Q) and use Flay (E) to peel enemies off your carry; when an allied engage champion goes in first, target a backline enemy with Q.
notes.thresh-teamfight-r-escape: When allies are being chased, place The Box (R)'s walls across the pursuit route to slow the enemy, and angle them differently for a retreat than you would to trap opponents.
notes.thresh-situational-mikael: Against a composition that immobilizes your carry, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build to remove those effects; Dark Passage (W) and Flay (E) cannot remove immobilization already applied to an ally.
notes.thresh-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb first for healing reduction. Thresh's abilities have ability power ratios, so he can make use of the item's ability power.
notes.vs-thresh-q: Thresh's Death Sentence (Q) has a long windup, so move sideways as soon as you see him raise his scythe. Keep changing direction while facing him, and turn once more when stepping forward to last-hit in anticipation of Q.
notes.vs-thresh-souls: Much of Thresh's armor and damage depends on collected souls, so trade with him when he steps forward to pick them up.
notes.vs-thresh-lantern: Thresh can use Dark Passage (W) to rescue an ally in danger or bring in reinforcements, so when he throws its lantern, immediately use a finishing ability or disengage.
notes.vs-thresh-e: Flay (E) pushes or pulls enemies in the direction Thresh sweeps. Stay off the line between him and his allies to avoid being pulled in.
notes.vs-thresh-mobility: Thresh has limited ways to escape on his own, so close the gap and engage immediately after he uses Death Sentence (Q).
notes.thresh-skill-r: Only enemies who pass through a wall of The Box (R) take damage and suffer its heavy slow. Once one wall collapses, the others deal no damage and their slow duration is halved, so place The Box to cover both the enemy's escape route and the direction their reinforcements will come from.
notes.vs-thresh-r: Once one wall of The Box (R) breaks, the others deal no damage and their slow duration is halved. If trapped, immediately choose an escape route and have the tankiest ally deliberately break through one wall.
notes.tristana-combo-e-reset: E Explosive Charge resets Tristana’s basic attack animation: press it immediately after a basic attack lands, then attack again to fit an extra hit into the same window. Pressing E during an attack’s windup cancels that attack, so use them in sequence rather than at the same time.
notes.tristana-combo-burst: For a finishing combo, attach E Explosive Charge, build stacks with basic attacks, then activate Q Rapid Fire to stack it faster and detonate the final stack with W Rocket Jump. If the explosion helps secure a takedown as you jump in, W resets so you can jump straight back out.
notes.tristana-combo-jump-r: Jump over an enemy with W Rocket Jump, then use R Buster Shot to knock them toward an ally or allied turret. This is powerful, but it leaves you on the enemy’s side with W unavailable, so use it only when they cannot immediately retaliate. You can also cast abilities while airborne, allowing you to combine W and R to disengage.
notes.tristana-skill-w-dash: Despite its appearance, W Rocket Jump counts as a dash: traps at your landing spot trigger, and enemy crowd control can interrupt you while airborne. It works well for escaping area skillshots, but it will not let you ignore guaranteed crowd control.
notes.tristana-skill-w-reset: Getting a takedown resets W. Detonating E on a champion at maximum stacks resets W. Before jumping in with W, check whether you can trigger a reset. Manage your mana so you can still use W.
notes.tristana-skill-q: Q takes effect starting with the wait before your next basic attack. Activate Q just before a basic attack. Early on, when you lack attack damage, save Q for fights. Activate Q to take down a turret quickly.
notes.tristana-skill-e-passive: E Explosive Charge’s passive deals area damage when a basic attack kills an enemy. Since this is effectively your only early poke, last-hit a low-health minion on the side nearest the enemy champion to catch them in the damage. When minions are grouped, kill the weakest one first to make the remaining last hits easier.
notes.tristana-skill-e-charge: If you apply E Explosive Charge to a champion, build it to maximum stacks. Skip it if the enemy is about to escape; apply it as a fight begins so you have time to stack it, then keep hitting that target with basic attacks or abilities to increase the explosion damage.
notes.tristana-skill-passive-range: As Tristana levels up, P Draw a Bead increases both her basic attack and ability range. Late in the game, she can attack from farther away than most marksmen, so use that range advantage in teamfights without jumping in unnecessarily.
notes.tristana-phase: Tristana is weakest early, when her cooldowns are long and her damage is low. Farm safely through that stage with E Explosive Charge’s passive. Her burst remains underwhelming into the mid game until she gets attack damage items, but her damage with a completed build is among the best, so longer games favor her.
notes.tristana-laning-wave: E Explosive Charge’s passive naturally pushes the lane. Choose deliberately between accepting the push to pressure the enemy turret and secure vision, or keeping E’s damage off minions so the lane pushes toward you. Pushing without thinking leaves you vulnerable to the enemy jungler.
notes.tristana-laning-siege: When the enemy is absent from lane, push immediately to pressure the turret. Using Q Rapid Fire and E Explosive Charge together damages it quickly, making Tristana’s pushing power a strength. Do not start pressuring the turret while W Rocket Jump is on cooldown.
notes.tristana-teamfight: In teamfights, use your range advantage to basic attack from the back and save W Rocket Jump to disengage. Jump in only when the enemy formation has collapsed and a takedown is certain, then use the W reset to reach your next target.
notes.tristana-teamfight-r: R Buster Shot is primarily a knockback tool rather than a source of damage. Use it to peel an enemy off an ally or interrupt a dangerous cast; it can also knock several grouped enemies over a wall. You do not always need to send an enemy away, so consider knocking them toward your team when appropriate.
notes.vs-tristana-early: Push the lane toward Tristana's turret to make it harder for her to last-hit with E's passive.
notes.vs-tristana-e-splash: Do not stand close to allied minions, so you avoid Tristana's E area damage.
notes.vs-tristana-w-cc: W Rocket Jump is a slow dash that crowd control can interrupt while Tristana is airborne. If she has both W and R Buster Shot ready, engage only when you have crowd control available to hold her in place.
notes.vs-tristana-w-reset: Tristana’s W Rocket Jump resets on every takedown, allowing her to keep jumping in. If an ally falls in a teamfight, staying put can lead to more teammates being picked off, so retreat as soon as your team starts losing ground. Do not leave a squishy ally at the front as you withdraw.
notes.vs-tristana-late: Tristana is difficult to handle with a completed build, so aim to end the game before she reaches it. Ambush her when she pushes the lane and moves up to pressure a turret; if she disappears from vision, first consider whether she is pushing a turret elsewhere.
notes.trundle-combo-basic: For a basic trade, cast W under the enemy, then auto attack, use a Q empowered auto attack, and auto attack again.
notes.trundle-combo-e-cut: To chase, use W to gain movement speed and catch up, place E ahead of the enemy’s path, then hit them with Q after the pillar knocks them back. A pillar placed behind them blocks nothing, so set it where they are headed; when disengaging, place it between yourself and your pursuer.
notes.trundle-combo-r: Use R immediately after starting a fight, while the enemy cannot yet escape: half its damage and armor and magic resistance steal apply at once, and the rest over its duration, so you need to stay on the target. Engage by placing W, casting R, blocking the escape route with E, and landing a Q empowered auto attack.
notes.trundle-skill-q: Q empowers your next auto attack and reduces the target's attack damage. Open with Q when trading against an enemy who deals physical damage. Do not use Q on a minion before a trade.
notes.trundle-skill-w: W creates an area that lasts for its duration, giving you a way to choose where to fight. Your attack speed, movement speed, and healing received increase only while you stand in it, so place it where you expect the fight and draw the enemy inside. Securing that ground early is much stronger than casting W after the fight begins.
