Its healing bonus also applies to heals from an allied support, so when engaging with allies, place W where they will stand.
notes.trundle-skill-e: E creates impassable terrain and pushes away enemies directly on top of the pillar. Placing it in a narrow path or beside a wall can block the passage entirely, making it strongest around river and jungle entrances. Against an enemy without a way to cross terrain, it can effectively trap them; against one who can cross, use it to draw out that ability.
notes.trundle-skill-e-gank: E also helps you respond to ganks. If your lane is pushed up and you are vulnerable, place it on the jungler's approach to delay their entry; when your jungler comes to gank, put it on the enemy's escape route. Spending E on lane trades leaves you without that response.
notes.trundle-skill-r: R deals damage based on the target’s maximum health and steals armor and magic resistance, so it gives the most value against the tankiest enemy. It weakens their frontline while making Trundle tougher; using it on an already fragile target yields fewer defensive stats.
notes.trundle-skill-passive: P heals you based on an enemy unit’s maximum health whenever it dies nearby. Each minion provides healing, so a large clashing wave can steadily restore your health, while high health jungle monsters provide even more when killed. If you are low, consider clearing the wave to heal instead of recalling immediately.
notes.trundle-laning: Trundle’s level 1 attack damage and movement speed are among the highest, making him strong in auto attack fights. When an enemy steps forward to last hit, move in on W and hit them with Q so their attack damage is reduced as they retaliate. Adding E to trades drains mana quickly, so save it for responding to ganks.
notes.trundle-laning-wave: Trundle has no area damage ability to push the lane himself, so waves naturally stack up. Work with that tendency: keeping the wave in the middle and pressuring from a distance where you can engage at any time is safer than pushing it toward the enemy tower. Push and recall only when the enemy leaves lane or retreats with low health.
notes.trundle-teamfight: Trundle has no dash, so do not walk straight into a teamfight. Place W in front of your team to set the fighting area, use E to split the enemy formation, and take down the separated side first. R weakens the frontline rather than preventing escape, so cast it on the foremost enemy once the fight is underway.
notes.trundle-phase: Trundle’s high base attack damage makes him strong from the start of lane, though his abilities alone do not deal explosive damage, so his early numbers are less striking. His strongest periods are one on one fights after he gains R at level 6 and midgame objective fights once he has core items. In the late game, his lack of area damage reduces his teamfight impact, so shift to holding one enemy in the side lane.
notes.trundle-situational-antiheal: If the enemy sustains through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to keep Grievous Wounds applied with auto attacks.
notes.vs-trundle-w: Trundle is strongest inside W, where he gains attack speed, movement speed, and increased healing received. Do not fight him there: back out, let W expire, then reengage.
notes.vs-trundle-e: E creates impassable terrain that can cut off your retreat completely in a narrow path. Fight Trundle in open ground rather than at river or jungle entrances. When the pillar appears, move sideways immediately; its surrounding slow makes escape harder the longer you wait.
notes.vs-trundle-q: Trundle's Q raises his attack damage while reducing the target's. For a champion who relies on physical damage, the few seconds immediately after being hit are the worst time to trade, so back off and reengage once the effect ends.
notes.vs-trundle-r: R deals damage based on the target’s maximum health while stealing armor and magic resistance, so champions with more health and defensive stats are especially vulnerable to it. Frontliners should not face Trundle alone. He is toughest while R is active; attack another target or create distance until it ends.
notes.vs-trundle-sustain: Trundle heals whenever an enemy unit dies nearby. A large clashing wave gives him so much sustain that poking him down and extending the lane will not work. Once you lower his health, capitalize immediately or push the lane to force a recall.
notes.vs-trundle-duel: Trundle has strong base attack damage from level one and becomes very powerful in one on one fights after getting R. Facing him alone in a side lane is a common way to lose; because his lack of area damage limits his teamfight contribution, steer the game toward five on five fights at objectives.
notes.tryndamere-combo-allin: When going all in, use W to lower the enemy’s attack damage before closing in with E. If you lead with E, they can fight back at full attack damage and turn the trade around. Once you’re close, build Fury with basic attacks; when they start to flee, W slows them as soon as they turn their back.
notes.tryndamere-combo-e-reset: Each critical strike reduces E’s cooldown, with a larger reduction when you critically strike a champion. After using E to engage, keep landing basic attacks to get it back for your escape; engaging with a low critical strike chance can leave you trapped. Check that you have enough Fury before going in.
notes.tryndamere-combo-r-escape: R can be activated even while you’re under crowd control. When death is certain, use it, then either escape with E and Flash before it expires or heal with Q and keep fighting. Plan your escape route before activating R, since surviving until it ends means little if your health is depleted.
notes.tryndamere-skill-passive: Fury drains after you’ve been out of combat for a while, so hit minions or jungle monsters just before engaging to start the fight with a chance to critically strike. With no Fury, Tryndamere is just a basic-attack champion.
notes.tryndamere-skill-q-timing: Q’s passive grants attack damage based on missing health, so healing as soon as you take damage gives up that damage. If you can survive, delay Q until you need it, but use it before your Fury drains because its healing scales with the Fury you have left.
notes.tryndamere-skill-w: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere, so time it for when a fleeing target starts to run. In a face-to-face trade, use its attack damage reduction to weaken a round of the enemy’s basic attacks rather than counting on the slow.
notes.tryndamere-skill-e-wave: E cuts through every enemy in its path. Using it through a minion wave builds Fury multiple times at once and greatly raises your critical strike chance, making a dash across the wave just before a fight the fastest way to build Fury while engaging.
notes.tryndamere-skill-r-bait: Hold R until just before you die, giving the enemy reason to commit their abilities and Flash because they think they can finish you. Surviving after that can turn the fight; activate R too early and they can simply back away until it expires.
notes.tryndamere-phase: Tryndamere’s abilities cost no resource, so he can keep using them from level 1, though his trades are weak before he has critical strike chance. Level 6 and R mark his first turning point, and from mid game, critical strike items make him nearly unbeatable one on one. Late game, if your team lacks teamfight damage, split pushing is his only way to create value.
notes.tryndamere-laning-farm: Tryndamere ranks among the best in CS and turret plates at 14 minutes: his advantages come from staying in lane and pressuring turrets rather than getting kills. With no resource cost, he can clear waves quickly using E and basic attacks, then hit the turret whenever the enemy cannot stay in lane.
notes.tryndamere-laning-trade: Against ranged opponents, accept some damage to secure CS while waiting for them to enter E range. Check river vision before closing in, since using E only to engage leaves you without an escape if a gank comes. Against melee opponents, build Fury first, then use W to lower their attack damage before going in.
notes.tryndamere-splitpush: With R available, Tryndamere can survive even when two enemies come for him in a side lane. When an objective is coming up, pushing the opposite side to draw enemy players away is often more valuable than joining the teamfight; without R, staying in the side lane can simply get him killed.
notes.tryndamere-teamfight: In teamfights, go around the side or back to target the enemy ranged carry instead of fighting the front line. Engage after the enemy uses its immobilizing crowd control on your front line, draw their focused attacks, then activate R just before dying and take out the carry during its duration.
notes.tryndamere-situational-armorpen: When enemy armor starts to blunt your basic attacks, buy Last Whisper or Lord Dominik’s Regards for armor penetration. Critical strike items lose value sharply against armor, so move the penetration purchase up after completing one core item.
notes.vs-tryndamere-r: Tryndamere cannot die while R is active, so pouring more damage into him during its duration is a waste. Stall with immobilizing crowd control or create distance instead, but remember that he can activate R even while under crowd control.
notes.vs-tryndamere-early: Deny Tryndamere last hits early to limit his Fury, which also reduces his critical strike chance and Q healing. If you see him hitting minions to build Fury, create distance before he engages.
notes.vs-tryndamere-w: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere, so walk backward while facing him when you retreat. Its attack damage reduction applies regardless of direction, so avoid a basic attack fight immediately after W hits you.
notes.vs-tryndamere-armor: Most of Tryndamere’s damage is physical and depends on critical strikes, so building armor can greatly change the duel. Thornmail directly counters his reliance on basic attacks; with no armor at all, you lose to him regardless of the item difference.
notes.vs-tryndamere-splitpush: Sending one player to stop Tryndamere in a side lane while his R is available will only cost you that player. Check his R cooldown before trying to take him down; if it’s available, trade for an objective or send enough players to stop him.
notes.vs-tryndamere-e: Each critical strike reduces E’s cooldown, so Tryndamere can use it almost continuously in a minion wave. Trying to catch him among many minions means he’ll keep slipping away; draw him into terrain without minions, or land immobilizing crowd control right after he uses E.
notes.tf-combo-ult: When roaming, use R (Destiny) to gain vision, lock in a gold card, then cast R again to move. Stun with an auto as soon as you land and follow with Q (Wild Cards); if you travel before selecting a card, your target can escape while you have nothing ready to use.
notes.tf-skill-w-cards: W (Pick a Card) cycles through blue, red, and gold in that order. Blue restores mana for staying in lane, red damages and slows nearby targets for wave clear or chases, and gold stuns to start a fight. Count the sequence to lock in the color you want more quickly.
notes.tf-skill-w-hold: Opponents can see a gold card in your hand and back away, so lock it in only when you can close the gap and use it immediately, or select it outside their vision. Holding a card throughout the laning phase wastes mana and costs you control of the wave.
notes.tf-skill-q: Q (Wild Cards) sends three cards out in a fan, but only one can hit each target. A straight cast will be caught by the front minions, so angle it around the side of the wave to reach a champion behind them.
notes.tf-skill-e: E (Stacked Deck) is a passive that increases attack speed and adds damage to every few auto-attacks. Its effect is reduced against structures, but it still helps take down turrets, making a brief window to hit one after pushing the lane worthwhile.
notes.tf-skill-r-vision: R’s mapwide vision is often more valuable than its teleport. Using it without moving can reveal the enemy jungler and mid laner to your team and create an opportunity to fight over an objective, so you need not save R just because there is nowhere good to teleport.
notes.tf-skill-r-cancel: The teleport on R’s (Destiny’s) second cast is canceled by interrupting effects. Cast it from outside enemy vision so an opponent cannot interrupt the move.
notes.tf-phase: Before level 6, Twisted Fate has some of the lowest attack damage, health, and defensive stats, making direct fights unviable. Learning R gives him mapwide reach and his first power spike; from there, push the lane and build your lead by making plays in other lanes. He remains fragile in the late game, so keep dealing damage from the back line and moving around the map.
notes.tf-laning: In lane, aim to push the wave first rather than chase kills. Clear the back-line minions with Q (Wild Cards), then use the time to roam or establish vision. While your opponent clears the pushed wave, create a numbers advantage in another lane.
notes.tf-laning-poke: Against melee opponents, repeatedly poking from beyond Q range can build an advantage. If they close the gap, a gold card stun is your only way out, so do not stand in front of them without a card ready.
notes.tf-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the very back and deal damage with Q (Wild Cards), saving a gold card to stun enemies who jump onto your allies. Interrupt those enemies instead of initiating with a stun; grouped opponents make Q easier to land, so holding your position lets the damage add up.
notes.tf-situational-cc: Prepare Quicksilver Sash against teams with a lot of crowd control that can interrupt R's teleport.
notes.tf-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing your poke damage, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-tf-card: Watch the color of the card in Twisted Fate’s hand. If he has locked in gold, stay out of auto-attack range or one hit will stun you; you can approach more safely when he holds blue or red.
notes.vs-tf-ult: After level 6, Twisted Fate disappearing from lane or pushing it quickly signals an R (Destiny) roam. When he activates R, he gains vision of the entire map, so tell your team immediately and have any lane at risk retreat under its turret.
notes.vs-tf-squishy: If you have a dash, close in right after Twisted Fate uses his gold card.
notes.vs-tf-q: Only one card from Twisted Fate’s Q (Wild Cards) can hit a single target. Stand behind minions so they catch the card first and greatly reduce his poke damage.
notes.vs-tf-cancel: Interrupting effects cancel Twisted Fate’s R (Destiny) teleport. If you see him activate R while he is in range, use crowd control to stop the move; if you can predict his landing spot, secure vision there in advance and wait.
notes.tf-combo-pick: For the basic combo, lock in a gold card with W (Pick a Card), move into auto-attack range, then stun with an auto, use Q (Wild Cards), and auto again. The locked card disappears if you do not use it within 6 seconds, so select it from a distance where you can reach auto-attack range before moving in.
notes.twitch-combo-burst: Approach from behind or the side with Q camouflage, throw W at the enemy’s feet to slow them and apply Deadly Venom, then build more stacks with basic attacks before finishing with E. E’s damage depends on the number of Deadly Venom stacks, so using it too early can ruin the combo.
notes.twitch-combo-r: Activating R does not break camouflage; your first basic attack does. Position while hidden with Q, activate R, then begin attacking along a line that lets your shots pierce enemies. You reveal yourself with the increased range already active, forcing enemies to react after you have gained a range advantage.
notes.twitch-combo-e-finish: E (Contaminate) needs no target and hits enemies in its wide range even if they enter brush or leave vision. Hold it to finish an enemy who is about to escape while you chase with basic attacks; using it midway through a trade for a little extra damage leaves it weak if Deadly Venom has too few stacks.
notes.twitch-skill-passive: Each basic attack that hits adds a stack of Deadly Venom, which deals true damage unaffected by armor and expires after a while. When an enemy champion affected by it dies, Q (Ambush) resets, letting you hide and reposition after each takedown in a teamfight. Check whether Q is available immediately after a kill.
notes.twitch-skill-q: Q (Ambush) grants camouflage and movement speed, with a larger speed boost near enemies who cannot see you. Very close enemies reveal you, so approach through brush or along a flanking route instead of coming straight in. Since Q also grants attack speed when camouflage ends, ideally use its full duration and enter the fight with that boost active.
notes.twitch-skill-w: W reaches farther than basic attacks, letting you hold enemies who are outside your attack range. Its poison cloud keeps applying Deadly Venom while they remain inside it, so throw W ahead of their path rather than at their current position. Use its slow and stacks to set up an E finish.
notes.twitch-skill-e: E (Contaminate) deals damage per Deadly Venom stack to every affected enemy nearby, making it both a finisher against one target and a way to clean up several in a teamfight. That is why maxing E first has become standard in the statistics: build stacks with basic attacks and W (Venom Cask), then use E last.
notes.twitch-skill-r: R (Spray and Pray) is valuable chiefly for its added range and piercing basic attacks. Before activating it, move sideways to line enemies up so the piercing matters. Damage drops slightly with each target pierced but has a minimum, so targets farther back still take meaningful damage.
notes.twitch-laning: Twitch is weak in basic attack trades, but E (Contaminate) remains a kill threat once Deadly Venom is stacked. His kills at 14 minutes rank near the top while his CS ranks near the bottom, so he gets ahead through kill opportunities rather than farming. Chip away at the enemy with Deadly Venom and wait for them to enter E range.
notes.twitch-laning-roam: In lane, look to use Q (Ambush) from brush or the river to get behind the enemy. Even without a kill, Twitch disappearing can force them back and give you control of the wave. Camouflage lasts long enough to reach another lane, though, so tell your teammates when you leave to keep them from misreading your position.
notes.twitch-phase: Twitch is weakest at levels 1 and 2. As E (Contaminate) levels up, its damage per Deadly Venom stack creates kill opportunities, and he peaks in the mid to late game when attack speed and critical strike come together. Win rate also rises sharply once three core items are completed, so look for early kills without overextending and dying.
notes.twitch-teamfight: Stay off the front line in teamfights: use Q to reach a flank or a position behind the enemy, activate R, and fire basic attacks through grouped enemies. Twitch has low health and armor, so a single targeted crowd control ability can end the fight for him; wait until the enemy has used their engage abilities on your frontline before revealing yourself. When someone dies and Q resets, reposition.
notes.twitch-situational-antiheal: Deadly Venom deals damage over time that enemy healing can readily offset. If healing cancels out that damage, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item.
notes.twitch-situational-qss: Consider Mercurial Scimitar against persistent crowd control that restricts movement. Twitch needs to hold his position to deal damage with R (Spray and Pray); being locked down removes his range advantage and leaves him vulnerable to being caught.
notes.vs-twitch-ward: Use a Control Ward to reveal Twitch’s camouflage, and remember that getting very close also reveals him. Avoid walking blindly through brush or narrow paths: go around or establish vision first. If Twitch disappears from lane, assume he may already be moving behind another lane and alert your teammates.
notes.vs-twitch-e: If you have taken several basic attacks, E can kill you even with around half your health left. Decide when to retreat based on how many basic attacks you have taken, rather than your remaining health. E does not target an enemy, so hiding in brush will not prevent it from hitting you. Move farther away from Twitch to avoid E.
notes.vs-twitch-poison: Armor does not reduce Deadly Venom’s true damage, and a spell shield does not stop its damage over time; it only blocks effects triggered through Deadly Venom. Even with Banshee’s Veil, limit how many basic attacks Twitch lands.
notes.vs-twitch-fragile: Twitch has low health and armor. Save targeted crowd control for the moment his camouflage ends or he positions with R active, then coordinate with your team to focus him all at once.
notes.vs-twitch-r-line: With R (Spray and Pray) active, Twitch’s basic attacks pierce enemies, hitting damage dealers behind the front line if you stand in a row. Spread sideways relative to his firing direction, and account for the extra range: distances that are normally safe may no longer be safe.
notes.vs-twitch-w: W (Venom Cask) leaves a poison cloud that slows you and adds Deadly Venom stacks. If it lands beneath you, leave immediately instead of staying to deal a little more damage. The longer you remain in it, the more stacks you gain and the easier it becomes for E (Contaminate) to finish you.
notes.udyr-combo-rotation: The basic rotation is to activate a stance, land two empowered basic attacks, then switch stances and land two more. Each stance affects your next two basic attacks, so switching before using both wastes the remaining effect. Those two attacks gain attack speed after an ability, and each hit reduces Awaken’s cooldown; treat stance changes and basic attacks as a pair.
notes.udyr-combo-awaken: To Awaken a stance, press its key again while that stance is on cooldown. Doing so immediately after activating it resets its cooldown and adds an ultimate effect. Awakening has its own cooldown and can be used only once per fight, so decide which stance to Awaken before engaging.
notes.udyr-combo-engage: For a gank, approach with E (Blazing Stampede), stun with the first basic attack, switch to Q (Wilding Claw) for two empowered attacks, then use W (Iron Mantle) to withstand damage. E stuns a target only on the first hit after you activate the stance, so switch to Q and deal damage as soon as the stun lands.
notes.udyr-skill-e: Awakened E briefly grants immunity to immobilizing and disruptive effects and lets Udyr pass through units. If you know which guaranteed crowd control the opponent has, activate it as that ability arrives to push through. Basic attacks in this stance cannot be canceled, so the attack still lands even if Udyr is knocked back or pulled.
notes.udyr-skill-w-shield: The W shield is depleted only after armor and magic resistance reduce incoming damage. Raising those stats therefore lets the same shield withstand more actual damage, making defensive items more effective on Udyr than on other champions.
notes.udyr-skill-w-timing: Activating W after taking a hit wastes the shield, so use it just before a large hit lands. If you need to endure sustained damage for a long time, Awaken W instead to gain healing over time based on maximum health.
notes.udyr-skill-q: Q (Wilding Claw) adds maximum health based damage to empowered basic attacks, making it effective against high health enemies and objectives. Its brief range increase also lets Udyr hit melee opponents slightly sooner. Use Q as your main stance in 1v1s and camp clears, alternating it with W (Iron Mantle) to clear the jungle without losing health.
notes.udyr-skill-r: R (Wingborne Storm) deals area damage over time and slows nearby enemies, making it more valuable in crowded fights; Q (Wilding Claw) is better in a 1v1. Awakened R leaves a storm that follows the last enemy Udyr basic attacked, so hit a target likely to flee before Awakening it.
notes.udyr-jungle-route: Udyr has one of the highest movement speeds among champions, and E (Blazing Stampede) makes him faster still, letting him move between camps exceptionally quickly. Take long routes through the enemy jungle and alternate lane ganks with camps to build experience and vision advantages. Switching stances sustains his health, allowing him to stay out for a long time without recalling.
notes.udyr-ganking: Udyr’s only guaranteed crowd control is the stun from E (Blazing Stampede), and he has no ranged engage. Gank only when you can get close: start from brush or behind terrain, or enter after an ally applies crowd control. Catching an enemy from behind while they push the lane is the most reliable approach; walking in from the front lets them escape with a single mobility ability.
notes.udyr-phase: Putting levels into one ability gives Udyr strong early camp clears and 1v1s. He peaks in the early and mid game, when jungle pressure and objective fights are frequent. Later, his limited range and area damage shift him from a damage dealer toward the frontline, so use objectives and control of the enemy jungle to secure your lead before then.
notes.udyr-teamfight: Engage a teamfight when Awakened E (Blazing Stampede) can carry you through the enemy crowd control that would stop your entry. If it cannot, stay beside your frontline, maintain area damage with R (Wingborne Storm), and meet enemies who engage. Once you get close, use W (Iron Mantle) to withstand damage and body block the enemy damage dealers’ path.
notes.udyr-situational-armor: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy’s physical damage is strong. Because armor increases the effective protection of the W (Iron Mantle) shield, building it first also gives Udyr a substantial durability boost.
notes.udyr-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing could turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Udyr stays close and keeps basic attacking, allowing him to maintain Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-udyr-e-stun: E (Blazing Stampede) stuns each target only on its first hit after the stance is activated and cannot stun the same target again for a while. Once you have taken the stun, use that window to counterattack or disengage. Expect the stun to be ready whenever Udyr activates E again.
notes.vs-udyr-w: Udyr is noticeably weaker after his W (Iron Mantle) shield breaks. Press the attack instead of backing away, forcing him to switch stances without giving him time to heal.
notes.vs-udyr-tracking: Udyr starts in the jungle and shows himself only when ganking. Place vision along key routes and at jungle entrances to track his path, and do not move forward in lane while he is out of sight.
notes.vs-udyr-tank: Defensive items combined with W (Iron Mantle) make Udyr very durable. Against such a build, take out the vulnerable teammates behind him first, then use your numbers advantage to kill him.
notes.vs-udyr-mobility: Udyr has one of the highest movement speeds among champions, and E (Blazing Stampede) makes him faster, so you cannot escape by simply running. Save a mobility ability or immobilizing crowd control, and apply the crowd control after Awakened E ends, since immobilizing effects do not work during it.
notes.vs-udyr-range: Udyr must get close to deal damage. As a ranged champion, your only advantage is to wear him down before he reaches you, while always keeping a way to disengage if he closes the gap.
notes.urgot-combo-basic: For basic trades, weave basic attacks into W fire. Both trigger Urgot’s leg cannons, so his damage depends on how long he keeps firing; staying close with W active is more rewarding than trading briefly and backing away.
notes.urgot-combo-legs: Urgot has a cannon on each of his six legs, each with its own cooldown. A shot gains no cannon damage if the leg facing the target is on cooldown, so circle your opponent to bring ready cannons into range. That movement makes the difference between standing still and dealing much more damage.
notes.urgot-combo-engage: Start by slowing your opponent with Q, then dash in with E to stun and throw them before using W and basic attacks. E stops at the first champion it hits and cannot cross terrain, so Q’s strong slow helps secure the hit. E always throws its target behind Urgot; to throw someone toward your allies, start E with your back to them.
notes.urgot-combo-r: Land R to slow the target, use Q, W, and basic attacks to bring them below the execution threshold, then recast R to pull them in and execute them. The slow grows stronger as the target loses health, making escape harder as you deal damage. If they remain below the threshold when R’s duration ends, it activates automatically, so there is no need to rush the recast.
notes.urgot-skill-r-fear: R executes its target in front of Urgot and fears nearby enemies at that moment, making it both a finisher and an area crowd control tool in teamfights. Pull in a target from the middle of the enemy group to fear multiple opponents; executing someone fleeing alone fears no one. Choose your R target by position, not damage.
notes.urgot-skill-w-toggle: At max rank, W becomes an indefinite toggle; until then, it has a limited duration and should be used sparingly. While active, it greatly reduces Urgot’s movement speed but increases his slow resistance, so turn it on for close fights and off when fleeing. Managing the toggle is central to playing Urgot.
notes.urgot-skill-w-mark: W prioritizes the champion most recently hit by another ability, so land Q or E on your chosen target first during a skirmish. Without a marked target, W fires at the nearest enemy or minion. Q therefore serves both as poke and as a way to aim W.
notes.urgot-skill-e: E shields Urgot as he dashes, making it useful for both engaging and surviving. It pushes through targets other than champions, allowing him to pass through minions, but cannot cross terrain. Against an opponent with a mobility ability, wait until they have used it before engaging with E; when ganked, use E’s shield and stun to escape.
notes.urgot-skill-q: Q (Corrosive Charge) has long range and slows so heavily that its target can barely move. It works for lane poke and stopping escapes, but spending it on poke can leave you without a way to set up an E (Disdain) engage. When looking for a kill, save Q to start the engage; use it to poke only when you are simply holding the lane.
notes.urgot-laning: Urgot is classified as ranged, but his very short range favors him against melee opponents and puts him at a disadvantage against true ranged champions. His level 1 health and armor are among the highest of any champion, so repeated short trades favor him. Keep up the pressure by approaching with W active and circling to fire his leg cannons.
notes.urgot-laning-wave: W automatically hits nearby minions, pushing the wave. To draw the wave toward you, turn W off and last hit only. Watch the wave and manage the toggle together, or an unwanted push can expose you to a gank.
notes.urgot-phase: Urgot is weak at levels 1–2 because Q deals little damage, but his trades improve as he levels W. His laning peaks when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. His short range makes teamfight engages harder later, so use midgame lane pressure and turrets to secure your lead.
notes.urgot-teamfight: Enter a teamfight when you can pull a target out from behind the enemy frontline with E. Ideally, damage that target with Q and W, then execute them with R. If the enemies are grouped and offer no opening, avoid forcing an engage; keep wearing down the frontline with W and look for an R finish.
notes.urgot-situational-antiheal: If an opponent’s healing can turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing your first core item. Urgot’s continuous W damage keeps Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-urgot-legs: Most of Urgot’s damage comes from his leg cannons, which deal damage based on maximum health and hurt durable champions too. Each cannon has its own cooldown, so the longer you stay near him, the more damage adds up. Stay outside his short range instead of repeatedly moving in and out.
notes.vs-urgot-w: Urgot’s movement speed drops sharply while W is active, so if he approaches with it on, walking away can take you out of firing range. His slow resistance also rises, however, making slows a poor way to keep him off you.
notes.vs-urgot-e: Urgot’s E cannot cross terrain and stops at the first champion it hits. It pushes through minions, but a frontline champion standing ahead of a damage dealer prevents E from reaching the dealer. Standing near a wall also greatly limits his engage angles.
notes.vs-urgot-q: Urgot’s Q slows so strongly that you cannot escape on foot after it hits. Decide immediately whether to use a mobility ability when you see it coming; if it has already hit, fighting back where you stand is often better than trying to flee. Q also marks you as W’s priority target, focusing its fire on you.
notes.vs-urgot-r: Once Urgot’s R hits, falling below its execution threshold triggers the pull and kills you. If marked, get completely out of Urgot’s range before your health reaches that threshold, or immediately use an option such as Zhonya’s Hourglass or Quicksilver Sash. The slow strengthens as you lose health, so waiting longer makes escape harder.
notes.vs-urgot-range: Urgot is classified as ranged, but his range is nearly melee. True ranged champions can beat him through their range, while melee champions should avoid fighting him head on in lane and either take him down with their jungler or farm for the late game. E is his only teamfight engage tool, so grouping up leaves him no opening.
notes.varus-combo-blight: For a basic trade, build Blight to its maximum stacks with basic attacks, then detonate it by hitting the target with E Hail of Arrows or Q Piercing Arrow. Blight does not detonate on its own, and using an ability before stacking it fully gives up some of the damage based on the target’s maximum health.
notes.varus-combo-ult: Open a teamfight with R Chain of Corruption, then use E and Q. A target rooted by R gains Blight stacks automatically throughout its duration, letting you detonate full stacks twice without basic attacks. Opening with R deals more total damage than saving it to finish the fight.
notes.varus-combo-q-charge: The longer Varus charges Q Piercing Arrow, the greater its range, damage, and Blight detonation effect, but he slows himself while aiming. In close combat, fire immediately instead of charging it fully; if you aim incorrectly when no one is around, cancel it to recover half the mana cost.
notes.varus-skill-passive: A kill or assist triggers P Living Vengeance, briefly increasing Varus’s attack speed, attack damage, and ability power. The bonuses are much larger on a champion takedown and can exceed the attack speed cap, making the next few seconds his strongest. Once your team gets the first kill in a teamfight, keep attacking the next target instead of retreating.
notes.varus-skill-w-cooldown: Detonating Blight on a champion or epic monster reduces the cooldowns of Varus’s basic abilities. Managing stacks well brings Q and E back noticeably faster, while using abilities only on minions slows that cycle down. The cooldown reduction also applies during objective fights, so weave basic attacks into your damage on Dragon or Baron to build stacks before using an ability.
notes.varus-skill-w-active: W Blighted Quiver’s active empowers your next Q Piercing Arrow and has a long cooldown. Save it for a Q you can reliably land, such as when an opponent is tied to the wave or has little room to dodge along a narrow path.
notes.varus-skill-e: E Hail of Arrows deals damage, slows, and leaves contaminated ground that reduces healing. Place it where a healing focused enemy wants to stand or must pass, such as in front of Dragon or Baron or at a brush entrance, to shut down their healing. Since Varus has no mobility ability, also save E to place defensively along an approaching enemy’s path.
notes.varus-skill-r: R Chain of Corruption spreads from the first champion it hits to nearby champions it has not infected. It is most effective against grouped opponents; firing it at someone isolated spends it on a single root. Because Varus has no mobility ability, decide whether to use R to start a fight or hold it to stop an assassin closing in on him.
notes.varus-laning-trade: In lane, build Blight stacks on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate them with E or Q. Letting the stacks expire leaves you with nothing, while using an ability first means there are no stacks to detonate and halves your damage. Following that order is itself a way to gain a lane advantage.
notes.varus-laning-safety: Varus has low movement speed, no mobility ability, and relatively low armor growth, so one positioning mistake can erase the advantage gained through his range. Step past the wave to aim Q only after checking both the opponent’s engage abilities and the enemy jungler’s location. Without lane priority, stay back and use your abilities only to clear the wave.
notes.varus-phase: At levels 1–2, poke and hold on with the bonus damage from W Blighted Quiver’s passive. Learning E gives you both wave clear and pressure from its ground effect; at level 6, R lets you initiate a fight yourself for the first time. Varus grows stronger with items, but he never gains a mobility ability, so his late game strength depends on positioning rather than damage alone.
notes.varus-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and begin with Q and E to disrupt the enemy formation, using R only when opponents overlap. With no way to shake off someone who closes in, step forward for basic attacks only after all opposing engage abilities have been used. A takedown makes Varus sharply stronger through his passive, so advance immediately afterward.
notes.varus-situational-antiheal: Even against healing focused opponents, antiheal items are a lower priority for Varus than for other marksmen because E Hail of Arrows already reduces healing on its contaminated ground. Choose Mortal Reminder in place of an armor penetration item only when the opposing team has several sources of healing or heals beyond E’s reach.
notes.varus-situational-cc: Buy Mercurial Scimitar earlier when the opposing team has a lot of crowd control that prevents movement. Varus has no ability to escape once caught, so a single such effect can lead directly to his death; his low movement speed also makes it hard to regain distance afterward.
notes.vs-varus-blight: When Varus has stacked Blight with basic attacks, hitting the target with an ability detonates bonus damage based on maximum health.
notes.vs-varus-r: R Chain of Corruption sends tendrils from the first champion hit, rooting everyone they reach. If an ally is rooted, keep far enough away that the tendrils cannot reach you instead of moving in to help; they disappear once you get far enough away. Spread out in teamfights so R roots only one person.
notes.vs-varus-passive: A kill or assist briefly gives Varus a large boost to attack speed and attack damage. If he gets one when an ally dies in a teamfight, stay away for those few seconds, then reengage after the boost passes.
notes.vs-varus-q-charge: Varus slows himself and stays in place while aiming Q Piercing Arrow. When you see him begin to aim, sidestep the arrow’s path and use that moment to close in. A fully charged arrow has very long range, so hiding behind minions when he starts aiming is also effective.
notes.vs-varus-mobility: Varus has no mobility ability and relatively low movement speed. Once you reach him with an engage ability or crowd control, Flash is his only way out, so you can catch him if it is down. Prepare a way past the opposing frontline to make the matchup favorable.
notes.vs-varus-e-ground: The contaminated ground left by Varus’s E Hail of Arrows reduces healing and regeneration while you stand on it. If your champion relies on healing to stay in a fight, step off the ground to recover your sustain before going back in.
notes.vayne-combo-condemn: Use Q to position yourself with a wall behind the enemy, then pin them against it with E and build W stacks with basic attacks during the stun. E pushes enemies away from where you cast it, so the wall must be behind them, not behind you. Q cannot cross walls; distinguish between using it to set up the angle and saving it to disengage.
notes.vayne-combo-w: Time trades around W: attacks and abilities both count toward its trigger when they hit the same target. Build the earlier stacks with basic attacks, then land a Q-empowered basic attack for the final hit to deal W’s maximum-health true damage and Q’s bonus damage together. Switching targets just before W triggers wastes the stacks you have built.
notes.vayne-combo-r: Activate R, move in with Q, and use its invisibility to hide your position while the enemy misses a targeted ability; then build W stacks with basic attacks. R greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, letting you use it repeatedly, so roll sideways instead of always moving in a straight line to make your reappearance harder to predict.
notes.vayne-skill-q: Q is a short roll followed by an empowered basic attack, making it both a movement tool and a damage boost. Vayne’s basic attack range is short even among ranged champions, but spending every Q to close the gap leaves you without a way to disengage. Use Q immediately after a basic attack to cancel its recovery animation and reposition without losing damage. Q cannot cross walls.
notes.vayne-skill-w: W deals true damage based on the target's maximum health. W stacks build separately on each target. W stacks disappear over time. Keep attacking one chosen target to trigger W.
notes.vayne-skill-e: E can finish a target by stunning them against a wall, and it is Vayne’s only defensive way to push away an enemy who gets close. Spending it on simple lane poke leaves you unable to respond to a gank. In open terrain, E can push the enemy out of range and end your own trade, so use it when the enemy has their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-skill-r: R increases Vayne’s attack damage, reduces Q’s cooldown, and makes her invisible when she uses Q. Takedowns extend its duration, but never beyond its original maximum. Activating R well before entering a fight wastes that time; use it once the fight has started and the enemy has spent a targeted ability so you can benefit from the extension.
notes.vayne-skill-passive: P grants movement speed only when Vayne moves toward a nearby enemy champion, with a larger bonus during R; it does not help her escape. Because she chases quickly but retreats slowly, check your retreat path before closing in.
notes.vayne-laning: Vayne’s low early health and armor and short basic attack range leave her vulnerable to longer-ranged opponents. Keep the wave near your turret and farm without forcing a push to reduce your exposure to ganks. Her CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute are among the lowest, so focus on minimizing losses during this early stretch.
notes.vayne-laning-trade: Start a trade only when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. Ideally, land enough basic attacks to trigger W once, then immediately retreat with Q; if you cannot trigger W, do not start the trade. Save E unless the enemy has their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-phase: Vayne is weakest at levels 1–2. Q (Tumble)’s cooldown drops sharply with each rank, letting her trade more often as she invests points in it; she then grows much stronger in the mid to late game as attack speed and penetration items come together. Her early game statistics are among the lowest, while the win rate for builds that complete three core items rises sharply. Avoid falling behind early and buy time to scale.
notes.vayne-teamfight: Let your allies start teamfights, then enter after the enemy has used their engage abilities and targeted crowd control. Draw fights toward narrow terrain near walls, where E can reliably stun a target. Once you enter, keep attacking one enemy to build W stacks instead of switching targets.
notes.vayne-situational-qss: If the enemy has lasting crowd control that restricts movement, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. No matter how often Q (Tumble) is available, Vayne cannot use it while immobilized, so a way to break free when caught is more valuable than another damage item.
notes.vayne-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets W’s true damage, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item. Vayne attacks one target for an extended time, allowing her to keep healing reduction active for longer.
notes.vs-vayne-wall: Vayne secures many kills through E’s wall stun, so avoid fighting her with your back to a wall. In lane, position within the minion line or toward the open river; in teamfights, face her in open areas instead of narrow passages.
notes.vs-vayne-fragile: Vayne’s early health and armor are both among the lowest, so early pressure forces her to back off. Push the lane to disrupt her farming and delay her scaling; with her early game statistics also among the lowest, do not let her get through this stage uncontested.
notes.vs-vayne-w: W deals true damage based on the target’s maximum health, so armor does not reduce it and high-health frontline champions take more damage from each trigger. Do not simply stack defensive items and keep absorbing attacks. Instead, count the hits on you: W triggers only after a set number hit the same target, and stepping out of range just before it triggers can avoid most of that damage.
notes.vs-vayne-r: While R is active, Q has a shorter cooldown and briefly makes Vayne invisible each time she uses it. Time targeted abilities for the moment she reappears. Because takedowns extend R’s duration, keep low-health allies away from her to help it end sooner.
notes.vs-vayne-late: Once Vayne has attack speed and penetration items, defensive stats alone struggle to stop her. She becomes harder to face as the game goes on, so use objectives and turrets in the early and mid game to work toward ending it.
notes.veigar-combo-basic: For a kill, trap the target with E (Event Horizon), drop W (Dark Matter) where they are trapped, then use Q (Baleful Strike) and finish with R (Primordial Burst). W takes time to land and will rarely hit on its own, so keep this order to make it land during E’s stun. Casting W first without E is the most common reason Veigar fails to deal damage.
notes.veigar-combo-e-placement: E (Event Horizon) only stuns enemies who cross its edge. If you place it under an enemy, they can move and attack freely inside it. Place it behind them to block their escape route and force them to cross the edge to leave. Against an approaching enemy, set it on their path ahead of time, rather than on yourself.
notes.veigar-combo-r: R (Primordial Burst) deals more damage based on how much health the target has lost, reaching its greatest effect when they are low. Use it at the end of a combo, after your allies have dealt damage or your W (Dark Matter) and Q (Baleful Strike) have landed. Casting it first on a full-health target gets only half the value from the same ability.
notes.veigar-skill-passive: Each ability hit on an enemy champion grants a Phenomenal Evil Power stack, and participating in a kill grants more. Hitting an opponent with Q in lane is permanent growth: farming without ever landing a spell on them costs Veigar that opportunity, while using Q whenever they enter range raises your ability power without spending gold.
notes.veigar-skill-q: Killing an enemy unit with Q grants a stack, and large minions and large monsters grant much more. Make a habit of finishing cannon minions with Q, and look to line up two low health minions for a single cast, since Q passes through only the first two units it hits.
notes.veigar-skill-w: W takes time to land, and opponents can see where it will fall, so cast it when they cannot move out of the way: during immobilizing crowd control, while trapped by E’s edge, in a narrow passage, or when minions block a sideways dodge. As you gain stacks, W’s cooldown falls enough to use it for farming too.
notes.veigar-skill-e-defense: E (Event Horizon) is Veigar’s only survival tool as well as a way to start a fight. He has no mobility ability and has the lowest level-one armor of any champion, so using E only to attack can leave him dead when an enemy engages. If the opposing team has a champion who can close in, reserve E for defense at least half the time; anticipate their approach and place it on their path.
notes.veigar-laning: Keep the wave near the middle instead of pushing it all the way out: without a mobility ability, E is Veigar’s only way out if he is ganked while pushed up. Build stacks by poking from Q range, and step forward only when you know where the enemy jungler is. Veigar relies heavily on mana and ability haste; when your mana falls below half, stop poking, farm, and wait for it to recover.
notes.veigar-laning-roam: After level 6, you can look for a kill by trapping an opponent with E, landing W and Q, then finishing with R. Veigar has no mobility ability or exceptional movement speed, so roaming out and back is slow; without a clear kill opportunity, you gain more by managing the mid wave and building stacks.
notes.veigar-phase: Veigar is weakest at levels 1–5, when he has the lowest armor, no mobility ability, and few stacks. His kill potential rises when he learns R at level 6, and his uncapped stacks make him stronger as the game goes on. Early on, aim to get through lane without losing ground rather than trying to win it.
notes.veigar-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and use E first to cut off an enemy approach or block their escape route. Land W and Q when an opponent is trapped or caught by allied crowd control, and save R for the one enemy you must kill, especially a damaged damage dealer.
notes.veigar-teamfight-terrain: If you can choose where to teamfight, choose a narrow area. Enemies can go around E in open space, but at a dragon or Baron pit entrance or on a jungle path, it can trap the whole team. Avoid open areas where opponents can approach Veigar from every side.
notes.veigar-situational-zhonya: If an assassin is targeting Veigar and closing in, move Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your core build. Veigar is fragile and needs a defensive option for an engage after E has been used.
notes.veigar-situational-void: If opponents build magic resistance, get magic penetration from Void Staff to increase R's damage.
notes.vs-veigar-w: W deals heavy damage, but its landing spot and timing are visible in advance. Move sideways when you hear it and see the ground indicator to dodge it; when trading with Veigar, keep moving instead of standing still to attack.
notes.vs-veigar-e: E stuns only when you cross its edge. If you are trapped inside, you can still move and attack, so stay within the cage until it disappears or move toward Veigar rather than rushing into the edge. Save a mobility ability or Flash for crossing the edge without being stunned.
notes.vs-veigar-r: Veigar’s R deals more damage as its target loses health, making it especially dangerous to remain in range while low. If your health falls below half, move out of R range; at full health, you can survive it without retreating out of fear.
notes.vs-veigar-passive: Veigar grows permanently stronger whenever his abilities hit, so taking needless Q poke increases his late game damage. Q passes through only the first two units it hits; standing behind minions can block many casts.
notes.vs-veigar-early: Veigar has the lowest armor and no mobility ability at levels 1–5. Keep pressuring him then to disrupt both his farming and his poke. A gank after E is used is almost guaranteed to work, so coordinate which ally will engage first to draw it out.
notes.vs-veigar-late: Veigar’s stacks have no cap, so he grows stronger as the game goes on. Late in the game, anyone without magic resistance who stands within range of his combo can be eliminated in one burst. Before starting an objective fight, check Veigar’s position and whether he has used E (Event Horizon).
notes.velkoz-combo-basic: Knock the target up with E, cast W under their feet immediately so both its initial hit and delayed explosion land during the knockup, then layer Q on top because it takes longer to arrive. That E–W–Q sequence completes the Organic Deconstruction stacks and triggers true damage.
notes.velkoz-combo-q-split: You can recast Q to choose when it splits into two beams that travel to either side of its original path. If you expect a sideways dodge, recast just before Q passes the target so the split beam catches them; against someone behind a wall or close to brush, split it in front of the wall to hit them from the side.
notes.velkoz-combo-r-setup: Build Organic Deconstruction stacks with Q or W before casting R: targets recently damaged by Organic Deconstruction take true damage from R, bypassing magic resistance, so casting it without preparation produces a very different result. The beam also builds stacks periodically while it hits, and holding it on one target long enough turns its damage into true damage midcast.
notes.velkoz-skill-passive: Vel'Koz completes Organic Deconstruction faster by landing different abilities together, so mix Q, W, and E instead of repeating the same ability. Completing the stacks deals true damage that ignores resistances. Basic attacks do not add stacks, but they extend their duration; when one more stack is needed, use an attack to buy time before finishing with an ability.
notes.velkoz-skill-q: Q is Vel'Koz's main poke and his only slow. Its long range and mana recovery make it useful for constant lane pressure, but save it when you need the slow to keep a target in place. It splits automatically at maximum range or on hit even without a recast, so letting it travel its full range can hit more enemies when they are grouped.
notes.velkoz-skill-w: W (Void Rift) holds charges, letting Vel'Koz cast it twice in a row, and each cast hits once before erupting again after a delay. That second hit makes even one cast a reliable way to build Organic Deconstruction stacks and a foundation for poke. W can also clear waves, but its mana cost is high; spending both charges on minions can cost you a chance to fight, so keep at least one available.
notes.velkoz-skill-e: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability, so avoid spending it on wave clear or simple poke. It pushes very close enemies away instead of knocking them up, making it useful for peeling off an assassin who dives in. Since E both starts combos and protects you, prioritize defense in lane while the enemy's engage ability is available.
notes.velkoz-skill-r: R is a channeled beam that follows your cursor, leaving Vel'Koz completely vulnerable while it fires. Before casting, check that the enemy has used their engage ability and cannot catch you from behind; then guide the beam slowly along the target's path instead of swinging it around. Its slow makes it easier to stay on one target, and holding the beam there without large angle changes deals more total damage.
notes.velkoz-laning: Vel'Koz support is a pure poke champion who cannot protect or buff his ADC. His job is to keep wearing down both opponents until they cannot stay in lane, repeatedly landing Q and W on the enemy ADC to complete Organic Deconstruction stacks. When an enemy's health drops, that is the signal for your ally to engage.
notes.velkoz-laning-safety: Vel'Koz has no mobility ability and ranks near the bottom in both health and armor, making the moment he steps forward for a poke angle especially dangerous. Stand behind or beside your ADC rather than behind the minions, and cast only from the edge of your range. Against an engage composition, secure vision of the river and tri-brush before pushing the lane; keep E (Tectonic Disruption) as your last safeguard.
notes.velkoz-teamfight: In teamfights, Vel'Koz fights from the back using his range. Before the fight starts, spread Organic Deconstruction stacks across several enemies with Q and W, then cast R when an ally locks them down and sweep the beam across the trapped group. Let the fight start before committing to R.
notes.velkoz-phase: At levels 1–2, limited abilities and mana make your poke rotation slow. Lane pressure grows once you have both Q and W and can complete Organic Deconstruction stacks in one rotation, while learning R at level 6 creates chances to finish enemies. As ability power builds, your true damage and late-game damage keep rising, but Vel'Koz remains fragile, so position farther back as you grow stronger.
notes.velkoz-situational-zhonya: Get Zhonya's Hourglass if the enemy has an assassin who dives in. With no mobility ability, Vel'Koz otherwise has only E's pushback to survive the engage; you need a way to weather it if you want to channel R to the end.
notes.velkoz-situational-antiheal: Against champions with strong healing, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Vel'Koz's wide-ranging abilities can hit several enemies, making it easy to spread healing reduction across the opposing team.
notes.vs-velkoz-q: Dodging the initial Q (Plasma Fission) projectile is not enough: at maximum range or when Vel'Koz recasts it, the projectile splits into two beams that travel to either side of its original path. Moving only sideways can put you in a split beam's path, so move toward Vel'Koz or slip behind the beams once they have passed.
notes.vs-velkoz-passive: Consecutive hits from Vel'Koz's abilities complete Organic Deconstruction stacks and trigger true damage that resistances cannot block, so do not keep taking his poke just because you have built magic resistance. If you have stacks on you, leave vision or retreat behind minions to let them expire.
notes.vs-velkoz-r: Vel'Koz must stand still to channel R. Crowd control or blocked vision can cut off all its remaining damage, so interrupt the beam as soon as it starts. If you cannot interrupt it, move behind a wall or past minions to break vision.
notes.vs-velkoz-e: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability, and he has no mobility ability, so bait out E and close in after it misses; he has little left to fight back with. Be ready for E to push you away instead of knocking you up if you get very close, and have a way to finish him after the pushback.
notes.vs-velkoz-position: Vel'Koz has very low health and armor and no way to escape, so getting caught can be fatal. Clear vision around the river and tri-brush to open a route from the side; that threat alone can keep him from stepping forward to poke and remove the opposing bot lane's damage.
notes.vex-combo-basic: Start a basic trade with E (Looming Darkness) to slow the enemy, follow with Q (Mistral Bolt), then land a basic attack if a mark remains. E’s area grows as it travels, making long casts easier to land; cast too close, and its narrow area may miss. Fire Q after the slow takes effect so the target is easier to predict.
notes.vex-combo-passive: When Doom is ready, your next basic ability applies fear, so the ability you use first determines who you fear. For a reliable hit, put it on long range Q or wide area E; use W only when an enemy is already close enough that it cannot miss. Clear minions while Doom is down so you do not waste it on the wave.
notes.vex-combo-ult: R has two stages: its projectile marks a target, then a recast dashes to them. If a marked champion dies soon after taking R damage, R becomes available again, so aim the first cast at someone you can finish off. Immediately after the dash lands, use E to lock down nearby enemies and W for a shield while you look for your next target.
notes.vex-skill-passive-antidash: Vex’s Doom 'n Gloom is a counter to champions with dashes: nearby enemies gain a Gloom mark whenever they dash or blink, and a basic ability used while Doom is ready interrupts a dash and applies fear. Against champions who engage, save Doom until the moment they go in.
notes.vex-skill-passive-mark: Vex’s next basic attack consumes a Gloom mark and reduces Doom’s cooldown. Against a marked enemy, weave in one basic attack before backing off; casting abilities and retreating will not trigger that cooldown reduction. Killing an enemy with E (Looming Darkness) also reduces Doom’s cooldown, so clearing a wave can help cycle the passive.
notes.vex-skill-q: Q (Mistral Bolt) gets narrower and faster as it travels. Up close, its hit area is wide, but it moves slowly enough to dodge on foot; at long range, it is fast but thin. Cast it directly in front of nearby enemies, and aim ahead of distant ones based on their movement.
notes.vex-skill-w: W (Personal Space) grants a shield and releases a close-range shockwave at the same time, so the enemy must already be close to get both effects. Save it for an engage instead of spending it early to poke: it is Vex’s only survival tool, and you should activate it as the enemy’s burst damage hits.
notes.vex-skill-e: E's slow makes the following Q and R easier to land. The farther you throw E, the larger its impact area. If you expect a trade, keep enough mana to cast the costly E at least once.
notes.vex-skill-r: The R projectile marks the first enemy champion it hits, so an overlapping frontline can cause it to mark the wrong target. Shift your angle so the projectile passes through only the backline. Once you dash in, you have no movement ability to get out, so check that W and Flash are available before committing.
notes.vex-laning: In lane, use Q to farm and poke while saving E. Poke with Q when the enemy steps forward to last-hit a minion. Use W with Doom when an enemy tries to get close.
notes.vex-laning-vs-dash: Holding Doom makes the lane easier against enemies who dash in to trade. Use a basic ability as they engage to interrupt the dash, apply fear, and counterattack. If you spend Doom on the wave, retreat behind your minions while the enemy can close the gap freely.
notes.vex-phase: At levels 1–2, Q’s long cooldown makes repeated poke slow. Once you learn E and can keep cycling Doom, you gain lane control; R at level 6 lets you roam and force engages. Vex peaks late in the game when kills reset R and let her chain engages, but her impact drops sharply if enemies group up without giving her an R angle.
notes.vex-teamfight: Never engage first as Vex in a teamfight. Your first job is to interrupt the enemy’s dash with a basic ability empowered by Doom, then use E to lock down their backline. Cast R after their formation has broken and a kill is certain; a successful R that resets can let you clean up the rest of the fight yourself.
notes.vex-situational-zhonya: Against multiple engage assassins, buy Zhonya's Hourglass before damage items to survive after going in with R.
notes.vs-vex-dash: Do not use a dash carelessly near Vex: when Doom is ready, one basic ability can interrupt the dash and apply fear. Wait while her Doom indicator is showing, then go in right after she spends Doom on the wave or on poke.
notes.vs-vex-mark: If you're marked, move out of Vex's basic attack range and wait for the mark to disappear.
notes.vs-vex-e: Vex’s E (Looming Darkness) grows wider as it travels and is narrow near her, so running straight back makes it easier to hit you. If you are already in range, move toward Vex or take a short step sideways to improve your chance of dodging it.
notes.vs-vex-r: Vex’s R projectile marks you on hit, allowing her to dash to you. Move toward your allies as soon as the mark appears so she has to dash into their midst, then look for a chance to catch her after she lands, when she has no movement ability to escape.
notes.vs-vex-reset: If an ally marked by Vex takes damage from R (Shadow Surge) and dies soon afterward, Vex gets R back. Giving her the first kill can start a chain of takedowns, so move low-health allies out of her range before starting a teamfight.
notes.vs-vex-dive: Vex has low armor and magic resistance, and her W (Personal Space) shield is her only survival tool. She is vulnerable once W is spent, so look to close in when both Doom and W are unavailable.
notes.vi-combo-gank: For a basic gank, charge Q, collide with the target to knock them back, then use an E-empowered basic attack, a basic attack, E, and another basic attack. Q stops Vi when it hits a champion, so approach from behind to knock the target toward your allied laner.
notes.vi-combo-ult: R targets and chases an enemy, so start the combo with it. After the knockup, charge E during the target’s landing, then follow with a basic attack, E, another basic attack, and Q as the knockup ends. Using Q first knocks the target away and breaks the follow-up.
notes.vi-skill-q-charge: The longer you charge Q, the more damage it deals and the farther Vi dashes, so fully charge it to catch or finish a fleeing enemy. If the charge is interrupted, Q is available again after a short wait, making a brief charge a reasonable choice when you need to act quickly.
notes.vi-skill-w: W activates only when you hit the same target repeatedly. Switching targets spreads out the stacks, so once you commit to someone, keep attacking them. Each activation reduces their armor and increases Vi’s attack speed, making extended attacks on one target more rewarding.
notes.vi-skill-e: E turns your next basic attack into a piercing area attack. If an enemy stands behind a minion or jungle monster, hitting the front unit deals full damage to the enemy behind it; use this to poke when helping a lane or to secure a last hit safely. E stores charges, so let them build up between camps.
notes.vi-skill-passive: Vi’s passive shield activates when an ability hits an enemy or structure. Before a fight, hit a nearby minion or monster with an ability and enter with the shield up to absorb part of the opening combo. Each W activation also reduces the shield’s cooldown.
notes.vi-skill-r: R chases its chosen target to the end, so Flash cannot dodge it, and Vi cannot be stopped during the cast, allowing her to ignore enemy crowd control as she goes in. It fails if the target becomes untargetable; enemies in its path are knocked aside and briefly stunned, but the chosen target does not change.
notes.vi-teamfight-engage: Do not engage with R so far ahead of your team that they cannot follow. Diving a backline damage dealer without allied support can leave you facing all five enemies alone, so walk close enough for your team to follow before using R.
notes.vi-teamfight-focus: In teamfights, pick off one key enemy damage dealer. Isolate them with R and keep attacking only that target until W activates, using Q to block their escape route or knock them toward your team. If you switch between several enemies, you may catch none of them.
notes.vi-phase: Start ganking at level 3, once you have your abilities; learning R at level 6 lets you reliably catch one target. Vi’s early damage per minute is relatively low, so clearing camps alone gives her little impact: help a lane as soon as your abilities are available to gain an advantage. Later, her role shifts toward engaging and isolating targets rather than dealing damage.
notes.vi-jungle-clear: In the jungle, clearing is faster when you keep attacking one monster until W activates. Activate your passive shield before moving to the next camp to reduce health loss, and use Q to gather scattered monsters, since it pulls enemies other than champions toward Vi on hit.
notes.vi-situational-antiheal: If the target you have committed to is hard to kill because of their sustain, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.vi-situational-cc: If the enemy team can lock you down after an R engage and prevent your escape, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. R itself cannot be interrupted; the danger comes after landing, so use the item to help survive the aftermath.
notes.vs-vi-q-charge: A fully charged Q deals much more damage, so move back or sideways when you see Vi begin charging to dodge it. Interrupting the charge lets her use Q again after a short wait, making dodging the priority.
notes.vs-vi-w: Keep fights with Vi short, then create distance instead of fighting her for long.
notes.vs-vi-r: Use forced movement abilities on Vi after she lands and the knockup ends, rather than during R.
notes.vs-vi-shield: If Vi approaches right after using an ability on a minion, wait until her shield is gone before trading damage.
notes.vs-vi-position: R targets one enemy and chases them to the end, so Flash cannot dodge it. While Vi has R available, backline damage dealers should avoid going alone into areas without vision and stay within range of their allies’ protective abilities.
notes.viego-skill-passive-possession: Viego’s passive, Sovereign's Domination, is central to his playstyle. Enemy champions who fall near him briefly leave a wraith; basic attack it to begin possession. Possessing a target heals Viego based on its maximum health and lets him use its basic abilities and items, so start a teamfight by securing one kill.
notes.viego-skill-possession-chain: While possessing a target, Viego can use his own R, Heartbreaker, once more at no cost instead of the target’s ultimate. Use the abilities gained through possession, then cast R on the next target just before possession ends to chain kills. Retreating with possession time left wastes the opportunity.
notes.viego-skill-possession-prep: If you do not know a target’s ability layout, you may hesitate as soon as you possess them. Before a fight, check which keys hold all five enemies’ basic abilities, then prioritize the wraiths of champions with dashes or shields.
notes.viego-combo-basic: In a standard fight, approach with E, Harrowed Path, stun with W, Spectral Maw, then use Q, Blade of the Ruined King. Q’s passive adds an extra attack to your first basic attack against an enemy hit by an ability, so weave in a basic attack after landing an ability to deal full damage.
notes.viego-combo-w-charge: Charging W, Spectral Maw, longer extends its stun, but Viego slows while charging and an interruption cancels it. Against a fleeing enemy, release it after a short charge to catch up; charge it fully only when you are sure it will hit.
notes.viego-combo-r-target: R, Heartbreaker, automatically strikes the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. Check whom it will target before casting, since a more wounded enemy could draw you away from the one you intended to hit. R knocks back the other enemies, which can also split their formation.
notes.viego-skill-q: Q, Blade of the Ruined King, adds damage to basic attacks based on the target’s current health, helping Viego damage high health tanks and objectives and clear the jungle or take Dragon and Baron quickly. Its thrust pierces forward, so it can also hit an enemy standing behind minions.
notes.viego-skill-e-approach: E, Harrowed Path, spreads black mist along terrain, granting Viego camouflage, movement speed and attack speed inside it. For a gank, cast it on a wall along your approach and follow the mist so the enemy spots you later. Attacking or using an ability briefly reveals you, so stay camouflaged until just before your first ability.
notes.viego-phase: Viego uses no resources, making his early jungle clear comfortable. In a small fight near an objective, securing one kill can let him turn the fight through possession. He peaks in the mid game as he builds items, but entering a late game teamfight head on first can get him killed before he creates a wraith to possess.
notes.viego-laning-gank: W, Spectral Maw, and E, Harrowed Path, are Viego’s only ways to close the gap, so solo ganks have a low success rate. Prioritize lanes where an ally has crowd control; otherwise, gank only when the enemy has pushed near your ally’s turret.
notes.viego-laning-objective: Before an objective fight, approach with E, Harrowed Path, while securing vision. Even if you lose the Smite fight, do not retreat immediately: killing one enemy can let you heal through possession and reclaim the objective.
notes.viego-teamfight: Viego should not start teamfights. Enter after the enemy has used crowd control on your allied tank and a killable target appears, then secure the first wraith. If you cannot create one on your first entry, the fight is already lost.
notes.viego-teamfight-window: Possession lasts only a short time, and its end is the most dangerous moment. Watch the remaining time and either kill your next target or retreat to safety before it runs out; if you return to Viego’s body in the middle of the enemy team, you will be caught.
notes.viego-situational-antiheal: If an enemy has strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Viego gains sustain through possession only after a kill, so failing to finish a target means possession cannot begin.
notes.vs-viego-corpse: If an ally dies near Viego, they leave a wraith where they fell, which he can basic attack to begin possession. Do not keep fighting near that spot; if possible, knock Viego away or immobilize him so he cannot reach the wraith.
notes.vs-viego-possession: During possession, Viego takes the fallen ally’s appearance and uses their basic abilities. Do not mistake him for an ally and turn your back. Keep your distance and hold out until possession ends, then counterattack as he returns to his own body.
notes.vs-viego-w: The longer Viego charges W, Spectral Maw, the longer its stun lasts, but he slows while charging and an interruption cancels it. When you see him charge, dodge to the side and, if you have crowd control, use it to interrupt him.
notes.vs-viego-r: Viego’s R, Heartbreaker, targets the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. If you are low on health and separated from your team, you become a likely target, so fall back or stay close to allies to make it harder for R to pick you out.
notes.vs-viego-fog: Black mist along terrain means Viego is camouflaged inside it. When you see it, place a Control Ward or take another route, and do not push the lane toward the mist.
notes.vs-viego-sustain: Without a kill, Viego has almost no way to heal. Do not start a small fight you cannot win; even retreating without giving him a kill keeps him from snowballing.
notes.viktor-combo-q-aa: Q empowers Viktor’s next basic attack, so using Q and backing away wastes much of its damage. Follow Q with the empowered attack, weaving in other abilities while the attack is available.
notes.viktor-combo-trade: Poke with E, then, when the enemy steps forward, place W under them to slow them before using Q and its empowered basic attack. If you use W too early, they can simply walk out.
notes.viktor-combo-ult: Place R, then use W to hold enemies in it for the full damage over time. Recast R to steer it toward their expected retreat path.
notes.viktor-skill-passive: Viktor collects fragments from minion kills to permanently augment his abilities, with siege minions granting especially many. Farming drives his growth, so always last-hit siege minions yourself.
notes.viktor-skill-augment-order: Augments cannot be undone, so choose what you need most at the time: E if lane poke and wave clear are urgent, Q if you need to withstand trades while staying close, or W if you need to hold enemies in place during teamfights.
notes.viktor-skill-q: Q deals damage and grants a shield; once augmented, it also gives movement speed. When you need to take a trade, use Q to shield yourself before going in.
notes.viktor-skill-w: W stuns only after an enemy remains in its area for a while. Place it on an escape route, in a narrow passage, or under an enemy who is already slowed or rooted; otherwise, they can walk out.
notes.viktor-skill-e: E fires in a straight line in the direction you choose. Once augmented, it triggers an additional aftershock along its path, improving both wave clear and poke, so look for an angle that catches the wave and the enemy champion in the same line.
notes.viktor-skill-r: R interrupts channels as soon as it appears. If an enemy has a channeled ultimate, save R to interrupt it instead of using it early for damage.
notes.viktor-phase-early: Viktor has among the lowest early kill participation of mid champions but among the highest damage per minute. Treat lane as a chance to build augments through E poke and farming rather than chase kills.
notes.viktor-phase-scaling: Viktor peaks in the mid to late game once he has two or three augments and core items. Augments persist through death, so even if you fall behind in lane, keep farming; time is on your side.
notes.viktor-laning-wave: Clearing a wave at once with E builds fragments quickly and creates time to roam or recall. Pushing also exposes you to ganks, so secure river vision first and keep your Q shield and W available.
notes.viktor-laning-safety: Viktor has low health and armor and no dash to escape on his own. If you do not know where the enemy jungler is, stay behind the lane’s midpoint and save W (Gravity Field) to stop a gank rather than use it for poke.
notes.viktor-teamfight: Viktor controls fights by holding enemies with W in narrow terrain and placing R over them for its full damage over time. His short range requires him to stand a step forward, but he can die immediately if engaged on, so stay just behind your frontline and focus on steering R.
notes.viktor-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against assassins who close in. Once placed, R keeps dealing damage even while Viktor is stationary, so buying time can turn a fight around.
notes.vs-viktor-augment-read: The color of Viktor’s staff light shows how many augments he has. Trades can play out differently as augments accumulate, so reassess your damage calculations when the color changes.
notes.vs-viktor-w: W stuns only if you remain in its area. Leave as soon as it appears to take only the slow and avoid the stun; do not keep trading inside it.
notes.vs-viktor-e: E travels in a straight line, so you can dodge it by stepping sideways. Viktor’s angle for clearing a wave is easy to predict; stay out of line with the wave to avoid most of his poke.
notes.vs-viktor-dive: Viktor has low health and armor and no dash to escape on his own. Once you close in, his defenses are his Q shield and W stun, so avoid W’s area as you attack him.
notes.vs-viktor-r-interrupt: R interrupts channels when it appears. If your champion has a channeled ultimate, wait until Viktor has used R before casting it.
notes.vs-viktor-distance: Viktor has more control over the battlefield at close range.
notes.vladimir-skill-passive: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into ability power and ability power into maximum health, so building health also increases Vladimir’s damage. W and E scale with health, making their area damage grow as he builds it.
notes.vladimir-skill-q-empower: After two Q casts, using a third within a short time greatly increases its damage and healing. Cast Q twice on minions, then use the empowered cast on the enemy champion; priming it just before a fight also lets you open with an empowered Q. Because Q deals damage before healing and costs no resources, it is reliable for last hits, but use it on an enemy champion when you need to heal, since it restores less health against minions.
notes.vladimir-skill-w: W briefly makes Vladimir untargetable and destroys incoming projectiles. Enemies in W's pool are slowed and have their health drained.
