Place W in the middle of the enemy team to deal damage and heal at the same time. W has a long cooldown, so avoid using it first in a trade. Use W just before enemy crowd control lands to nullify it.
notes.vladimir-skill-e: E costs health to charge and deals more damage the longer Vladimir charges it, gaining a slow past a certain point. He moves more slowly during the charge, and E fires automatically after a while, so choose your target when you begin charging. Enemy units in front can block the wave; avoid firing through a minion wave at an enemy champion.
notes.vladimir-skill-r: Enemies infected by R briefly take increased damage from all sources. After a delay, it explodes and heals Vladimir based on the number of champions hit. Because it also amplifies allied damage, cast R early in a fight and aim to catch multiple enemies when they group up or just after an ally lands area crowd control.
notes.vladimir-combo-basic: Prime Q on minions, then charge E when the enemy enters range, fire it once it gains the slow, and follow with empowered Q. The slow helps Q land before the enemy retreats out of range; using Q first gives them time to back away while E charges, causing it to miss.
notes.vladimir-combo-teamfight: Hit multiple enemies with R, charge E as you move in, land empowered Q and E, then use W when they counterattack. W can be used without interrupting E’s charge, so you can enter and emerge from the pool while charging. Coordinate your engage with your allies after casting R so their damage benefits from its amplification.
notes.vladimir-laning-early: Early in lane, last hit with Q and stay safe. Before learning W, you have no escape, so avoid standing far up the lane. Last hit waves the enemy pushes in with Q near your turret.
notes.vladimir-laning-health: Careless farming with E steadily costs health and gives the enemy an opening to engage, especially if you push a wave with it below half health. Clear waves with E when you have health to spare; when low, heal with Q first.
notes.vladimir-laning-wave: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Vladimir has very few deaths and damage per minute near the top, while his kill stats sit in the lower middle. Prioritize surviving and growing over getting lane kills. Once E can clear waves quickly, push the lane, then establish vision or join fights in other lanes.
notes.vladimir-phase: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5: W is either unavailable or on a long cooldown, leaving him little chance to escape if caught, and his abilities still deal little damage. His contribution to fights rises sharply once he learns R at level 6 and completes his first core item. Health and ability power increase each other, so his strength grows faster as he builds items; minimize losses early and look to contribute in teamfights in the mid and late game.
notes.vladimir-teamfight: In teamfights, Vladimir moves between the front and back lines while dealing area damage. He lacks guaranteed crowd control to start a fight himself, so hit as many enemies as possible with R and move in when your allies engage. Enter when W is ready and the enemy has already used targeted crowd control on your team’s initiator. Hitting several enemies increases his healing, so dive into grouped opponents instead of chasing one target.
notes.vladimir-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team also relies on healing to survive, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Vladimir’s repeated area damage can keep Grievous Wounds applied to multiple enemies.
notes.vladimir-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has a burst champion that dives onto Vladimir, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. W alone cannot cover the gaps between its cooldowns; alternating it with Zhonya’s Hourglass lets you survive two engages in one fight.
notes.vs-vladimir-early: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5, when his low defensive stats and lack of an escape make him vulnerable to lane pressure and ganks. Exploit that window to slow his growth: as time passes, his health and ability power increase each other, making him harder to face.
notes.vs-vladimir-w: Vladimir’s W breaks targeting and destroys incoming projectiles, so important crowd control can disappear if used carelessly. Draw out W with a low-cost ability early in the fight, then use your decisive ability as the pool ends. Once W is down, Vladimir has no way to escape if caught.
notes.vs-vladimir-r: While infected by Vladimir’s R, you take increased damage from all sources. Back away as soon as it lands and rejoin the fight after its effect ends. Avoid grouping inside R’s area: hitting more champions increases Vladimir’s healing.
notes.vs-vladimir-items: Items that deal damage based on maximum health are especially effective against Vladimir because building health also increases his damage. Liandry’s Torment is a magic damage option, while Blade of the Ruined King is a physical damage option. Adding Grievous Wounds makes it harder for him to survive through healing.
notes.vs-vladimir-e: Vladimir moves more slowly while charging E, and enemy units in front can block its wave. When you see the charge, keep minions between you and Vladimir or leave its range before it finishes. His reduced movement speed also gives you an opening to close the distance.
notes.volibear-combo-basic: For a basic engage, activate Q and close the gap, stun with its empowered basic attack, then use W, a basic attack, and W again. Q delivers its stun through the attack, so pressing the ability before you reach the target will not stun them; use its movement speed to get into range. Aim to land both W casts during the stun when trading.
notes.volibear-combo-w-mark: W marks its target; casting it again on that target deals much more damage and restores health. Weave a few basic attacks between casts instead of using both back to back, and save the first W for the champion if a fight is coming rather than spending it on a minion and throwing off the second cast's timing.
notes.volibear-combo-ult: For an R combo, leap in and land, stun with Q, then use W and E. Opening a turret dive with R briefly disables a turret near the landing point, while its bonus health lets you keep fighting. Because the leap is telegraphed and mobile opponents can evade it, use R when they are already immobilized or have no escape route.
notes.volibear-skill-passive: Damaging enemies with abilities or basic attacks builds passive attack speed stacks; at maximum stacks, basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. Volibear's damage depends heavily on those stacks, so build them on minions or jungle monsters just before a fight. Engaging with no stacks can produce a very different result even with the same abilities.
notes.volibear-skill-q: Q's movement speed bonus doubles only while moving toward an enemy champion, making it much less effective for escaping than for closing the gap. If you are immobilized before landing the stun, Q ends but its cooldown resets, so using it first to draw out an opponent's guaranteed crowd control carries little cost.
notes.volibear-skill-w: W provides both damage and sustain, and its short cooldown makes it central to farming and trading in lane. Because the heal scales with missing health, it restores far more after you’ve taken damage than when you’re at full health. Volibear is strongest when he’s around half health and closes in after the opponent backs away.
notes.volibear-skill-e: E is Volibear's only ranged ability, dealing damage based on maximum health and slowing enemies, so use it to poke or clear waves when you cannot close the gap. Its delayed strike is easy for moving opponents to dodge; place it over Q's stun or an ally's immobilizing effect. Volibear gains the shield only if he is inside the blast area, so even when using E to escape, place it underfoot as you move away. Its high mana cost and long cooldown also mean that using it out of habit can leave you without a shield for your next engage.
notes.volibear-skill-r: R deals damage and enables dives by briefly disabling turrets near its landing point, making the best time to use it when an opponent stays under turret for safety. Its bonus health can also help you escape, but doing so gives up its unique turret-disabling value, so save it for escapes only as a last resort.
notes.volibear-laning: Farm with W and manage your mana in lane, then trade only when Q is available. Without Q’s stun, the opponent can simply walk away while Volibear wastes mana. The best time to trade is when the enemy wave has pushed toward your turret and you can catch the opponent nearby.
notes.volibear-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, secure CS and poke with E instead of spending Q on an uncertain engage. Activate Q to close in just after they use a poke ability or step out from behind their minions. Volibear's relatively high level-one health and attack damage mean he can usually win the trade once he reaches them.
notes.volibear-teamfight: In a teamfight, wait for an ally to start the fight and for opponents to spend their abilities before using R to reach and lock down a backline damage dealer; going in first leaves you exposed to all their crowd control. Build passive stacks before entering so your attacks also damage nearby enemies. If the enemy formation is grouped together, hold R, approach with Q, and hold the frontline.
notes.volibear-phase: Volibear's relatively high level-one health and attack damage make him strong in early melee trades, though he runs out of mana quickly before learning several abilities. His first power spikes come as W gains ranks and Q comes back up, then at level 6 when he learns R. Later, defensive items and healing reduction make W's healing less reliable for survival, so use midgame dives and objectives to close out the game.
notes.volibear-situational-mr: If your lane opponent deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance early. Choose Banshee's Veil against a potentially decisive targeted ability, or Quicksilver Sash if guaranteed crowd control keeps stopping your engage.
notes.volibear-situational-antiheal: Against champions with strong healing, fit Executioner's Calling between your core items. Volibear can stay close and keep applying healing reduction through basic attacks and W.
notes.vs-volibear-q: Volibear gains much more movement speed from Q while moving toward an enemy champion than while fleeing, so running straight away while he chases with Q will usually let him catch you. Use mobility or terrain to break vision, or move toward your allies. Since the stun comes from an empowered basic attack, staying outside attack range can let Q's duration expire.
notes.vs-volibear-w: Volibear's sustain comes from W, which heals more the more health he is missing. If he is around half health and you cannot reliably finish him, back off and wait out W's cooldown instead of continuing to hit him. Healing reduction items can turn that situation around.
notes.vs-volibear-e: E's lightning strikes after a delay. When its indicator appears, step sideways out of the marked area to avoid both the damage and slow. Volibear must stand inside that area to gain the shield, which can also reveal the direction of his next engage.
notes.vs-volibear-r: Volibear's R briefly disables turrets near its landing point, so if you are low on health while R is available, retreat deeper behind your turret instead of relying on it to stop a dive. The leap is telegraphed, giving you time to use a mobility ability to leave the landing area.
notes.vs-volibear-stacks: Volibear's damage depends on his passive attack speed stacks, and at maximum stacks his basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. If he approaches while hitting minions or monsters to build stacks, avoid the fight and engage just after the stacks expire.
notes.vs-volibear-lane: As a ranged champion, poke while Volibear's Q is on cooldown. Without Q, E's slow is his only way to close the gap, so make him spend Q, then keep poking to take control of the lane.
notes.warwick-combo-gank: Start a gank by pressing W to mark a target, then use the movement speed to close in. Before level 6, head for lanes where an ally can catch the target first: Warwick can only close in with Q, land basic attacks, and follow up on allied crowd control. From level 6 onward, use R for guaranteed suppression, then follow with basic attacks, Q, and E in that order.
notes.warwick-combo-e-fear: E fears nearby enemies when its duration ends, and recasting it triggers the fear early. Recast when an enemy is about to use a mobility ability or an ally needs help landing a skillshot; if you need to withstand enemy burst damage, let E run its full duration for the damage reduction.
notes.warwick-skill-q-charge: Tap Q to leap in and bite, or hold it to move behind the target while biting and change positions. Use the held cast to move an enemy toward your allies or to escape turret range during a dive. Warwick follows the target throughout the bite, even if they try to flee.
notes.warwick-skill-q-value: Q deals damage based on the target’s maximum health and heals Warwick for the damage dealt, making it central to his sustain in both jungle clears and fights. It is also his only way to close the gap with a leap, so if you plan to gank, avoid using it up on a camp; check its cooldown before moving out.
notes.warwick-skill-w: W’s passive reveals the location of enemy champions below half health even without vision, making its detection a useful guide to your next gank target after a lane trade. Activating W marks the nearest enemy regardless of health; if it detects no target, part of its cooldown is refunded, so using it to check nearby carries little cost.
notes.warwick-skill-passive: Warwick’s passive heals him more as his health falls and is strongest when his health is very low. Retreating simply because he has reached half health gives up that advantage, but he needs something to hit to heal, so draw fights toward nearby minions or jungle monsters.
notes.warwick-phase: Warwick can gank from level 2, once he has Q and W, and reaches a power peak when he gains R at level 6. His jungle clear speed and 14 minute CS figures are among the lowest, so competing through farming yields little advantage. Scaled damage dealers beat him in late game duels, but he can still use R to take one target out of the fight.
notes.warwick-jungle-path: Plan your clear to finish near a lane with a gank opportunity. Warwick ranks high in kills at 14 minutes but low in CS, so his value comes from how often he intervenes rather than how much he farms. Choose the lane you want to gank first, then clear camps toward it instead of waiting until every camp is done to consider a gank.
notes.warwick-jungle-gank: Gank when the enemy pushes the lane and moves away from their turret. Before level 6, Warwick has no guaranteed crowd control, so an ally must land immobilizing crowd control first; if that opening is unavailable, turn toward a camp or objective on the other side instead of forcing the gank.
notes.warwick-teamfight: In teamfights, R can take a key enemy damage dealer out of the fight, but Warwick is locked in place immediately after using it. If allies cannot follow up from where they are, he will be the only one caught. Engage when the damage dealer enters your allies’ range or your allies are ready to go in with you.
notes.warwick-teamfight-dive: Activate E's damage reduction, move past the frontline, then recast E to fear the enemy backline.
notes.warwick-objective: During standoffs at Dragon or Baron, W’s passive reveals enemies as their health drops; a mark appearing is the signal to engage. Because R’s leap distance scales with movement speed, it can reach across a wall, letting Warwick find an entry angle from the far side of the objective pit.
notes.warwick-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Warwick stays close and keeps attacking, so he can maintain Grievous Wounds easily.
notes.vs-warwick-r: Warwick’s R suppresses its target, preventing them from doing anything for its duration. Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar removes the suppression immediately; without either, focus on keeping the caught ally alive. Warwick is locked in place immediately after using R, making that a good time to focus a counterattack on him.
notes.vs-warwick-w: When your health falls below half, Warwick can see your location, and his movement speed and attack speed increase.
notes.vs-warwick-e: Warwick takes much less damage while E is active and fears enemies when it ends, so unloading your burst during that window puts you at a double disadvantage. Back off and reengage after the fear triggers, but remember that he can recast E to trigger it early; do not stay close while counting down its full duration.
notes.vs-warwick-passive: Warwick heals more as his health falls, making him deceptively durable at half health; diving based on his health alone can let him refill it with a few basic attacks. Apply Grievous Wounds with Executioner’s Calling before calculating whether you can finish him off.
notes.vs-warwick-r-range: Warwick’s R (Infinite Duress) leap distance increases with his movement speed. With a movement speed buff, he can reach much farther than expected, so don’t treat a wall or an unwarded bush as a safe distance. During an objective standoff, take particular care not to leave the far side of the pit open.
notes.vs-warwick-early: Warwick has no guaranteed crowd control before level 6. Early on, gain an advantage through jungle invades and lane priority.
notes.warwick-combo-r-range: R’s leap distance scales with movement speed, so using it while W’s passive or a movement speed item or buff is active can reach an enemy from a distance they thought was safe. Cast R while running toward them, rather than from a standstill.
notes.xayah-combo-root: The key to rooting with E is to place at least three feathers first: lay down two in a line with Q, add another with a passive empowered auto attack, then recall them with E for a guaranteed root. If you rush E after landing only Q, you will deal damage but the opponent can walk away.
notes.xayah-combo-passive-weave: Xayah’s passive applies to auto attacks after she uses an ability, so weave them into trades: W, auto attack, Q, auto attack. This places far more feathers in the same amount of time, increasing E’s damage and the chance of a root.
notes.xayah-combo-ult: Xayah becomes untargetable while leaping with R and leaves a line of feathers when she lands. Use it to avoid an enemy engage or skillshot, then press E immediately to turn the dodge into a root. R → E is her strongest counterattack.
notes.xayah-skill-passive: Xayah’s passive auto attacks pierce every enemy in their path, reaching opponents behind minions; use them for most of your lane poke. Spending an empowered auto attack on a minion when you don’t need a feather leaves you with one fewer feather for a fight.
notes.xayah-skill-q: Q costs little mana and leaves two feathers in a line. Aim it along the line between Xayah and her opponent so the feathers pass through that target again when recalled with E; feathers thrown off to the side may deal damage initially but fall outside the recall path.
notes.xayah-skill-w: W increases attack speed and adds a second blade, while hitting a champion also grants movement speed. Its duration is short, so save it for moments when you can keep auto attacking instead of wasting it to push the lane. It is most efficient when you can continuously hit a stationary target, such as an objective or turret.
notes.xayah-skill-w-rakan: Nearby allied Rakan also gains W’s effect, but his movement speed increases only when Xayah actually hits a target. Activate W as Rakan engages and follow it immediately with an auto attack.
notes.xayah-skill-e: E hits enemies along each feather’s path back to Xayah, so moving sideways can change the recall angle and bring scattered feathers through one target. Later feathers deal reduced damage when they hit the same enemy, so line them up for the root rather than extra damage.
notes.xayah-skill-e-crit: E’s damage increases with critical strike chance and critical strike damage. As Xayah completes core items with those stats, each cast becomes more powerful; in the late game, E can heavily damage the enemy backline even without a root angle.
notes.xayah-skill-r: R is an escape tool before it is a damage ability, so do not use it early just to deal a little more damage. It can avoid skillshot ultimates and engage abilities, and Xayah ignores unit collision during the leap, letting her escape a surround even when cornered against a wall.
notes.xayah-phase: Xayah is weak in trades at levels 1–2 because she cannot build up feathers. Opportunities open as she levels E and its root cooldown shortens, while R gives her a survival tool at level 6. Her power peaks in the mid to late game as critical strike core items make a single E an area finishing move. At every stage, her low movement speed and lack of an escape besides R mean a positioning mistake can get her killed.
notes.xayah-laning: In lane, poke opponents through minions with Q and passive empowered auto attacks. An opponent standing over three feathers is your cue to trade; without that angle, save E for farming or disengaging. Xayah has almost no mobility, so do not stand far forward after pushing the wave deep toward the enemy turret.
notes.xayah-laning-feather-trap: Feathers remain on the ground briefly, so you can place them where a fight is likely to start. Send Q toward a brush entrance or river approach the enemy may use, and half the root requirement will already be met when they engage.
notes.xayah-teamfight: In teamfights, Xayah builds up feathers with auto attacks from the back, then uses E to root enemies as they engage. Keep E ready to stop melee champions who reach you rather than spending it before the engage begins; if several enemies are grouped together, it can root them all and turn the fight.
notes.vs-xayah-feather-count: Xayah roots a target only when at least three returning feathers hit it. Count the feathers on the ground, and if three or more lie along the line between you and Xayah, move off that line immediately.
notes.vs-xayah-move: The longer you fight Xayah from the same spot, the more feathers pile up under your feet. Keep trades short and reposition often so the feathers do not line up along their recall paths.
notes.vs-xayah-r: Don’t engage on Xayah first unless the opening is certain. If she becomes untargetable with R, your engage ability and crowd control can go to waste, leaving her with the advantage; it’s much safer to wait until you’ve confirmed her R is down.
notes.vs-xayah-mobility: Xayah has relatively low movement speed and no mobility ability besides R. Pressure her with ganks and forced engages before level 6 or while R is down.
notes.vs-xayah-e-line: When Xayah uses E, her feathers return to her in straight lines. Sidestep out of the line between the feathers and Xayah to avoid their path; moving sideways around her position is better than running straight back.
notes.xerath-combo-stun-first: For a guaranteed combo, stun with E Shocking Orb, land W Eye of Destruction in the center while the target is stunned, then use Q Arcanopulse. The central W hit and Q are guaranteed only if E connects, so if it misses, save your mana instead of continuing the combo.
notes.xerath-combo-poke: When poking without a kill opportunity, place W first, then fire Q at the slowed opponent. Leading with Q gives them time to start dodging, making it harder to land.
notes.xerath-combo-ult: Xerath cannot move during R Rite of the Arcane. Pin the opponent down with E or W before activating it, then aim the remaining shots ahead of their straight escape path. Find a safe position first or you will be caught.
notes.xerath-skill-q-charge: Q gains range as you charge it, but Xerath is slowed during the charge. Fully charge it only from a completely safe distance; if a melee opponent is close, fire after a short charge. Cancel if the shot no longer lines up: firing nothing refunds half the mana spent.
notes.xerath-skill-q-aim: Q is much easier to land when an opponent moves toward or away from you than when they move side to side. Look for the moment they step forward to last-hit a minion or retreat to a spot where they can recall.
notes.xerath-skill-w-center: W Eye of Destruction needs to hit in the center to deal its full damage and slow. Catching the opponent with only the outer edge greatly reduces its value as poke, so aim ahead of their movement and follow up with Q Arcanopulse after landing the center hit.
notes.xerath-skill-e: E stuns longer the farther its orb travels, so landing it from a distance is more rewarding. Minions can block it, so choose an angle with a clear path. As Xerath’s only means of self-defense, it is best saved to interrupt an opponent diving in.
notes.xerath-skill-r-cancel: If R ends without firing a shot, its cooldown is halved. If the opponent disappears from vision right after you activate it, end it without forcing a shot so R is available again for the next fight.
notes.xerath-phase: At levels 1–2, high mana costs limit Xerath’s poke, and he is very fragile. From level 6, R lets him pressure beyond his lane; he peaks in the mid game when he has both ability power and mana. Late in the game, opponents have ways to engage, so a single positioning mistake can get him killed instantly.
notes.xerath-laning-poke: Use your range advantage to poke with Q from behind minions, and avoid pushing the lane unnecessarily. Xerath has no movement ability and is vulnerable to ganks when his lane is pushed, so establish river vision first if you need to push.
notes.xerath-laning-mana: Excessive poke drains the mana Xerath needs for both farming and self-defense. Fire Q only when the opponent is positioned to be hit; otherwise, cancel it to recover mana. When it is safe, basic attack the opposing champion, since P Mana Surge restores more mana against champions.
notes.xerath-teamfight: Start teamfights from the very back. Once your allies engage and lock down the opponents, pour on damage with W Eye of Destruction and R Rite of the Arcane, while saving E Shocking Orb to stop assassins who get onto you. If you use all your abilities first and stand there, you will have nothing to respond with when they engage on you.
notes.xerath-teamfight-siege: Xerath is strongest during sieges and standoffs around objectives. Keep hitting opponents with Q from a safe position beyond a wall or behind a turret so they cannot settle into position; once they back off, have your team start the objective.
notes.xerath-situational-zhonya: If the opposing team has an assassin who can dive in, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. It is your only way to survive an engage during R and a safeguard if you are caught while E is unavailable.
notes.vs-xerath-close: Xerath’s range is threatening, but most champions can trade favorably once they close the gap. He has no movement ability, so move in right after he uses E and W.
notes.vs-xerath-ult: Xerath’s R Rite of the Arcane has a long cast animation, and he cannot move during it. As soon as you see the animation, start dodging or engage on his position; he cannot dodge on his own while R is active.
notes.vs-xerath-q: Xerath’s Q Arcanopulse travels through minions in a straight line, so standing behind them will not protect you. When he starts charging, change direction and move well to the side, then close the gap while the charge slows him.
notes.vs-xerath-laning: Xerath uses a great deal of mana in lane. Instead of trying to dodge every bit of poke, avoid the heavy damage and keep farming; Xerath will eventually run low on mana first. When that happens, push the lane and call your jungler.
notes.xinzhao-combo-gank: For a basic gank, close in with E Audacious Charge, activate Q Three Talon Strike, then auto attack, use W Wind Becomes Lightning, and land two more auto attacks to knock the target up on the third. Only auto attacks consume Q’s empowered attacks, so weaving in W costs nothing and adds a hit toward P Determination.
notes.xinzhao-combo-r-timing: Use R Crescent Guard to survive after engaging: activate it once you have entered the middle of the enemy team and are surrounded. It prevents damage from champions outside your spear’s range, making it especially valuable against teams with many ranged damage dealers. If you activate it just before engaging, you waste its immunity time moving in, so wait until you have closed the gap.
notes.xinzhao-skill-q: Q Three Talon Strike empowers three auto attacks, with the third knocking the target airborne. Those attacks also reduce your other abilities’ cooldowns, so keep using Q on jungle camps. When going for a kill, pace your auto attacks so the third lands as the enemy tries to Flash.
notes.xinzhao-skill-w: W Wind Becomes Lightning has a slash followed by a thrust that deals most of its damage. Its slow cast lets enemies sidestep it, so aim for a moment when the target has trouble changing direction. The thrust reveals champions and large monsters it hits, which also makes it useful for finding enemies who flee into brush.
notes.xinzhao-skill-r: R Crescent Guard deals damage based on current health, knocks enemies back, and blocks damage from champions outside your spear’s range. Its immunity is more valuable when much of the enemy team’s damage comes from marksmen and mages, while nearby melee champions can still damage you. Check where the enemy team’s damage will come from before engaging to judge R’s value.
notes.xinzhao-skill-passive: P Determination deals bonus damage and heals you on every third hit. W Wind Becomes Lightning counts toward those hits, so using it consistently during jungle clears and extended fights helps preserve your health. The healing scales with maximum health, making health items improve your sustain as well.
notes.xinzhao-phase: Xin Zhao’s dueling and ganking grow strong at level 3, once he has all three basic abilities, but his kills at 14 minutes and damage per minute are below the jungler average, so early ganks alone are not his route to snowballing. Keep clearing camps while looking for skirmishes around objectives. In the late game, he can be killed quickly when R ends, so avoid engaging alone.
notes.xinzhao-jungle-gank: The Challenge mechanic is key to successful ganks. If an enemy is pushed up in lane and an ally has crowd control, E Audacious Charge and Q Three Talon Strike can secure a guaranteed kill. If the enemy has vision in the river, land W Wind Becomes Lightning first to Challenge them, then jump in from E’s increased range instead of approaching head-on.
notes.xinzhao-jungle-counter: Xin Zhao’s base movement speed ranks among the highest of all champions, and his strong dueling makes counterjungling valuable. When you confirm the enemy jungler is clearing camps on one side, take camps on the opposite side and leave; if you meet them with your abilities ready, take the fight. Always check whether an enemy laner can join it.
notes.xinzhao-teamfight-role: In teamfights, Xin Zhao is often more valuable for clearing space in front of his carries with R Crescent Guard’s knockback than for picking off the enemy backline. Jump in just after an enemy diver reaches your carry and knock them away with R; even without a pick, this can turn the fight.
notes.xinzhao-teamfight-entry: Engage after the enemy has used its key crowd control. R Crescent Guard blocks damage only from champions outside your spear’s range, so nearby melee champions can still hurt you and crowd control can still affect you. If an enemy melee diver is still alive, relying on R alone can get you killed even while its immunity is active.
notes.xinzhao-situational-antiheal: A healing target may survive R Crescent Guard’s damage based on current health. If the target you need to kill can heal, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items.
notes.vs-xinzhao-q: Q Three Talon Strike’s third empowered auto attack knocks its target airborne. If the first two hit you, use a mobility ability or Flash to get out of range before the third. Much of Xin Zhao’s damage and crowd control hinges on that hit, so avoiding it can change the fight.
notes.vs-xinzhao-r-immunity: While R Crescent Guard is active, damage from champions outside Xin Zhao’s spear range does not affect him. A marksman must either back away or move into that range to keep dealing damage; continuing to fire from outside it is the worst choice.
notes.vs-xinzhao-r-knockback: R Crescent Guard knocks back only enemies who are not Challenged, pushing everyone except Xin Zhao’s target away and splitting the formation. If you expect him to engage, avoid standing too close together; leave enough space for the others to help if one person is knocked back.
notes.vs-xinzhao-w: W Wind Becomes Lightning is a slow skillshot whose thrust deals most of its damage. Move sideways to dodge the thrust: if it misses, you avoid becoming Challenged and deny Xin Zhao an engage from E Audacious Charge’s increased range.
notes.vs-xinzhao-r-window: Xin Zhao is very weak after R Crescent Guard ends. When he engages, create distance and wait out its immunity before counterattacking instead of committing immediately. In late game teamfights, the moment R expires is your chance to take him down.
notes.xinzhao-combo-challenge: Mark your target first: a champion hit by W Wind Becomes Lightning’s thrust becomes Challenged, extending E Audacious Charge’s range against them. Against a distant target, land W before following with E. R Crescent Guard knocks back only enemies who are not Challenged, so your mark determines who stays and who gets pushed away.
notes.xinzhao-skill-e: E Audacious Charge is a targeted dash, so escaping with it requires a minion or jungle monster in the direction you want to flee. Before choosing where to fight, check for a target behind you. E also gains range against Challenged targets, making a W Wind Becomes Lightning hit decisive for how far away you can engage.
notes.vs-xinzhao-e: E Audacious Charge is a targeted dash that cannot cross walls. Without a nearby minion or jungle monster, Xin Zhao cannot use it to escape. To break off his pursuit, move into an empty area beyond a wall; to catch him, force him somewhere with no target behind him to dash to.
notes.yasuo-combo-eq: For a basic trade, use E through a minion to dash past your opponent, then press Q during the dash. It strikes in a circle instead of thrusting forward, giving it a more forgiving hitbox; follow with a basic attack as soon as you land.
notes.yasuo-combo-tornado: After landing Q twice, your third Q becomes a tornado that knocks your opponent airborne. Press R as soon as it connects for the standard finish, or hit minions with Q to maintain your stacks while saving the tornado.
notes.yasuo-combo-e-chain: Chain E through different minions to close a large gap. When chasing, dash through minions and save E for your opponent; when retreating, use E on your opponent first so the minions remain available as an escape route.
notes.yasuo-combo-r-ally: R can also be used on enemies knocked airborne by allies.
notes.yasuo-skill-q: Q counts as a basic attack: it can critically strike and applies life steal and on-hit effects, while attack speed reduces its cooldown. Its hitbox is narrow and crowd control can interrupt it, so anticipate sideways movement before casting or use it for a circular strike during an E dash.
notes.yasuo-skill-w: W Wind Wall blocks projectiles, but turret attacks and beam abilities pass through it, and it cannot stop a projectile that arrives before the wall forms. Its cooldown is long, so save it for a grab ability or a key ranged ability.
notes.yasuo-skill-e: E dashes through a selected target, which you cannot target with E again for a short time. Identify minions positioned for a dash over a wall to give yourself an escape route, and remember that using E directly on an enemy champion during a trade leaves you unable to close the gap on them with E again for a while.
notes.yasuo-phase: At levels 1–2, Yasuo has relatively low health and stacks Q slowly, making trades unfavorable. Investing skill points in Q and learning R at level 6 opens up kill opportunities, but his early damage per minute and death statistics are poor, so focus on surviving that stretch. His real power comes in the mid to late game with two or more critical strike items.
notes.yasuo-laning: Avoid pushing the wave carelessly with Q. Minions give Yasuo routes to engage and escape with E, and clearing the wave removes both. Start a trade only when you have two Q stacks, can launch a tornado immediately, and still have your passive shield.
notes.yasuo-teamfight: Yasuo should not initiate teamfights. Before entering, work from the flank, using minions and allies to find an angle; only go in with R after allied crowd control or your own Q tornado knocks an enemy airborne. R grants armor penetration, so focus on eliminating the enemy backline afterward.
notes.yasuo-situational-antiheal: If your opponent relies on healing to sustain, buy Executioner's Calling for healing reduction. Yasuo's duels tend to run long, and continued healing can keep an opponent alive no matter how much damage you deal.
notes.yasuo-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team opens fights with crowd control that locks you down, fit Quicksilver Sash between your core items. Crowd control interrupts Yasuo's Q, so every moment spent locked down costs you damage.
notes.vs-yasuo-q-dodge: Yasuo's Q has a very narrow hitbox. When he approaches, move sideways instead of backing away: stepping out of its straight path will cause most casts to miss.
notes.vs-yasuo-tornado: After Yasuo lands Q twice in a row, his next Q becomes a tornado that knocks opponents airborne. Watch and listen for the effects that signal full stacks so you can prepare to dodge.
notes.vs-yasuo-post-tornado: Yasuo is weakest immediately after firing his tornado. His Q stacks reset, leaving him without a knock-up for a while, so engage then.
notes.vs-yasuo-shield: Yasuo's passive shield activates when he takes damage and lasts only briefly. Strip it with low-cost poke, then commit to a trade once it disappears.
notes.vs-yasuo-wall: Yasuo's W Wind Wall blocks projectiles, but turret attacks and beam abilities pass through it. If you play a projectile-based champion, reposition to attack around the wall or save your key abilities until it disappears.
notes.vs-yasuo-wave: Yasuo closes gaps by using E through minions. Keep a thin wave pushing toward your side; with fewer minions to use as stepping stones, he has fewer ways to approach.
notes.yasuo-skill-passive: Your passive shield charges through movement, so keep moving in lane to fill it. When Flow is full, damage from a champion or monster triggers the shield, which lasts only briefly; you are most vulnerable just after enemy poke removes it.
notes.yone-skill-passive: Thanks to Way of the Hunter, every second basic attack deals bonus magic damage. Yone also gains greatly increased critical strike chance, though his critical strikes deal less damage, so trading in pairs of attacks is more effective than landing one hit and backing off. Critical strike chance beyond the cap converts to attack damage, so overlapping critical strike items do not go to waste.
notes.yone-skill-q-stack: Each hit with Q (Mortal Steel) grants a stack, and at full stacks the next Q becomes a dashing whirlwind that knocks enemies up. Since stacks expire, hit a minion with Q just before a fight to prepare the whirlwind for a trade. Yone’s abilities cost no resources, so there is no need to conserve Q.
notes.yone-skill-q-basic-attack: Q (Mortal Steel) counts as a basic attack and can critically strike; its first target also receives on-hit effects and lifesteal, making it both a poke tool and an attack that applies item effects. Crowd control interrupts its cast, so do not open with whirlwind Q while the opponent has an immobilizing ability ready.
notes.yone-skill-w: W (Spirit Cleave) is chiefly a shield: it grows with each champion hit, while attack speed reduces both its cooldown and cast time. Early on, when attack speed is low, save W for the moment an opponent’s key ability comes in instead of using it in every trade.
notes.yone-skill-w-vs-tank: W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on the target’s maximum health, split between physical and magic damage. Against a frontliner who has stacked health, building only armor or only magic resistance will not fully stop it, so count W as a damage tool as well as a shield.
notes.yone-skill-e: E (Soul Unbound) is your way back after engaging. Activate it before dealing damage, since part of the damage Yone deals to champions in spirit form is dealt again when he returns to his body, and earlier damage does not count. Strong crowd control prevents that return, so do not dive with E while an opponent’s immobilizing ability is ready.
notes.yone-skill-r: R Fate Sealed teleports Yone behind the last champion in its straight-line path. Passing through a grouped team can leave him deep in enemy ranks, so an angle that crosses the whole group is usually suicidal. Check first whether R will pull enemies toward your team; if no champion is in its path, Yone simply moves forward, which can also be used to escape.
notes.yone-combo-trade: For a lane trade, stack Q (Mortal Steel) on minions, then close in and knock the opponent up with whirlwind Q before landing two basic attacks, W (Spirit Cleave), and one more basic attack. The clock starts as soon as whirlwind Q connects: plan how many attacks to land after the knockup, then back off.
notes.yone-combo-allin: For an all-in, activate E (Soul Unbound) first, engage with whirlwind Q (Mortal Steel), then use a basic attack, W (Spirit Cleave), R (Fate Sealed), and another basic attack before recasting E to return. Damage dealt before E does not count toward its damage on return, while returning immediately after activating it wastes the engage.
notes.yone-combo-r-followup: When following up on an ally’s immobilization, use R (Fate Sealed) first to pull and knock the target up, then save whirlwind Q (Mortal Steel) to knock them up again as they land. This leaves them virtually no time to use an escape or cleanse.
notes.yone-phase-early: Yone is weakest at levels 1–2: his low attack speed makes W slow, and he has no whirlwind Q yet. By the 14-minute mark, his deaths rank among the highest while his kills are low, reflecting how often overly aggressive early engages get him killed. During this period, use Q to last-hit and manage its stacks.
notes.yone-phase-spike: Yone’s power rises sharply once he gains attack speed and critical strike chance. Attack speed shortens both W’s cooldown and cast time, improving its defense and damage, while excess critical strike chance converts to attack damage, so overlapping items are not wasted. Start looking for fights proactively once your first core item is complete.
notes.yone-laning: Because Yone uses no resources, it is easy to keep using Q and push the wave unintentionally. If the lane is pushed out and E is unavailable, a gank can catch him, so when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown, farm less with Q, let the wave come toward you, and hold E. When your opponent has pushed the lane instead, look to close in with whirlwind Q and trade only then.
notes.yone-teamfight: In teamfights, disrupt the enemy backline while making it back alive. Go deep only while E Soul Unbound is active, and aim W toward a group to graze several enemies at once and increase your shield. Cast R Fate Sealed in a direction that pulls enemies toward your team; if its path would carry you through them and leave you too deep, save it.
notes.yone-situational-mercurial: Buy Quicksilver Sash earlier against a team with ways to lock Yone down. He cannot return to his body with E Soul Unbound while under strong crowd control, so a single immobilizing effect can take away his escape.
notes.yone-situational-antiheal: If an opponent’s healing could turn a duel, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Yone stays close and lands repeated basic attacks, letting him maintain Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-yone-q-stack: Yone’s engage comes from whirlwind Q Mortal Steel at full stacks. Repeated Q hits on minions signal that his whirlwind is ready; stay out of range until the stacks expire.
notes.vs-yone-cc: Strong crowd control prevents Yone from returning to his body with E (Soul Unbound), so hold your immobilizing ability until he dives in spirit form to stop his return and catch him. Crowd control can also interrupt whirlwind Q (Mortal Steel).
notes.vs-yone-w-shield: The more champions Yone hits at once with W (Spirit Cleave), the larger his shield becomes. In teamfights, spread out instead of lining up along his approach so W catches only one or two of you.
notes.vs-yone-r: R Fate Sealed teleports Yone behind the last champion in its path and pulls in every enemy it hits. Standing second from the back prevents him from getting deeper, while standing alone at the rear lets him teleport to your position. Check whether you are the farthest back before a teamfight.
notes.vs-yone-early: Yone is weakest early, before he gains attack speed, and his early deaths are noticeably high in the statistics. Pressure him at levels 1–2 to deny him health and CS, delaying the point when his items make him stronger.
notes.vs-yone-echo: Some of the damage Yone deals in spirit form is dealt again when he returns to his body. If he has hit you in spirit form and you have about half your health left, heal or move out of range before he returns to avoid that additional damage.
notes.yorick-combo-basic: For a basic trade, mark the enemy with E (Mourning Mist), close in while they are slowed, land a Q (Last Rites) empowered attack, then follow with basic attacks. Yorick needs E’s slow and movement speed boost to land Q reliably despite his short range, so do not close in if E misses.
notes.yorick-combo-ghoul: Q (Last Rites) has two uses: after consuming its empowered attack, press Q again when enough graves are nearby to open them at once and raise Mist Walkers. The empowered attack becomes available again when its cooldown ends even if you save the summon, so there is no reason to hold Q just to preserve the graves.
notes.yorick-skill-passive: Graves from P (Shepherd of Souls) form when enemies die near Yorick, and champions and large monsters always leave one when they die. Mist Walkers consume graves to rise, and only a limited number can remain active at once, so clear a wave near Yorick before a fight to prepare your forces. Without graves nearby, he starts the fight as just another melee champion.
notes.yorick-skill-q: Q (Last Rites) is an empowered attack that deals damage and heals Yorick. Its healing scales with missing health and is reduced against non-champions, so landing it on a champion during a trade is more valuable than repeatedly using it on minions to sustain in lane: you gain healing and a grave. Hitting a champion or large monster with Q leaves a grave at that spot.
notes.yorick-skill-w: W (Dark Procession) creates a wall that deals no damage. Enemies can destroy it with attacks or cross it with a movement ability, making it strongest against targets without one; against someone who still has a dash, it buys only a little time. W can also separate a jungler from a laner during a gank, so save it when you suspect the enemy jungler is nearby instead of using it on every lane trade.
notes.yorick-skill-e: E is Yorick’s main trigger for summoning Mist Walkers: when a marked enemy is near graves, the walkers keep rising and rushing at them, while Yorick and his walkers gain movement speed toward the target. The mark also reduces armor and slows, so landing E can decide a fight. Its long range makes it tempting to use for wave clear, but spending it there leaves you without the tool you need to close in for a trade or follow up on a gank.
notes.yorick-skill-r: The Maiden of the Mist summoned by R (Eulogy of the Isles) provides much of Yorick’s fighting power. Her basic attacks mark a target, and Yorick deals bonus damage based on that target’s maximum health when he hits them, so attack whoever she is attacking in teamfights. After some time, pressing R again sends her down the nearest lane to apply pressure, but Yorick’s own fighting power drops sharply. Send her only when you want to draw an enemy to a side lane for a numbers advantage; if an enemy champion can cross the map quickly and clear that pressure, keep her with you for fights.
notes.yorick-laning: Yorick’s lane phase centers on farming and turret pressure. Use Q (Last Rites) to manage your health while securing CS, and clear waves on your side of the lane to build graves instead of forcing kills. If your opponent pushes the wave and roams, attack the turret to turn their absence into an advantage.
notes.yorick-laning-trade: With virtually no mobility, Yorick should trade only when the enemy steps forward. If they walk up for a last hit, lead with E to slow them, then close in; while E is on cooldown, stay behind your minions instead. Follow this rule even more strictly against ranged opponents to avoid losing health.
notes.yorick-phase: Yorick is weak at levels 1–2 because Q (Last Rites) is his only trading tool. Learning E (Mourning Mist) lets him poke and close in, stabilizing the lane, while gaining the Maiden at level 6 boosts both his 1v1 strength and turret pressure. He peaks in the mid to late game once he has items and can take down a side lane alone, but has less impact in a standoff against five grouped enemies.
notes.yorick-teamfight: In teamfights, Yorick should raise Mist Walkers just before combat and use W (Dark Procession) to block a narrow passage, split the enemy formation, or protect allies from behind. Move in after the enemy has used its crowd control on your allies, then land E (Mourning Mist) on a key damage dealer so the Mist Walkers swarm them; do not dive deep into the backline.
notes.yorick-situational-antiheal: If an enemy champion has strong healing, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Yorick’s continuous basic attacks and Mist Walker attacks make Grievous Wounds easy to maintain.
notes.yorick-situational-armor: If your lane opponent deals mostly physical damage, buy Cloth Armor early and get Plated Steelcaps sooner. Yorick needs to stay in lane to build graves, so invest in surviving poke before buying damage.
notes.vs-yorick-wall: If W Dark Procession traps you, attack its low-health wall first: it breaks after a few hits, so there is no need to waste a movement ability in a panic. A dash or blink can get you across faster, and because Yorick’s wall does not block his allies, first look for a path toward an ally on the other side.
notes.vs-yorick-maiden: The Maiden’s basic attacks mark targets to take bonus damage based on maximum health from Yorick’s basic attacks. If she starts attacking you, create distance from Yorick first. When she is alone in a side lane, Yorick fights more like an ordinary melee champion, making that your chance to target him.
notes.vs-yorick-split: Counter Yorick’s side-lane pressure by moving across the map quickly. If your champion has global mobility or can roam fast, answer his push and then immediately rejoin your team to restore your numbers advantage. Trading his solo turret push for an objective elsewhere is worthwhile if you can secure it faster than he can take the turret.
notes.vs-yorick-e: Yorick has no mobility, so he cannot close in if E misses. Dodge the arc of its mist projectile to avoid being forced into a trade, then step forward and farm freely while E is on cooldown. As a ranged champion, repeating this pattern is enough to win the lane.
notes.yorick-combo-wall: For a guaranteed kill, place W (Dark Procession) behind the enemy to cut off their retreat, apply E (Mourning Mist) for its mark and slow, then land a Q (Last Rites) attack. Allies can pass through W, but enemies cannot, so anticipate where the opponent will retreat and place the wall ahead of time.
notes.vs-yorick-ghouls: Clear the Mist Walkers before fighting Yorick to noticeably reduce his damage. A jungler with Smite can use it to clear the Mist Walkers and the Maiden of the Mist immediately.
notes.vs-yorick-graves: A grave forms for every two enemies that die near Yorick, and those graves become his troops. Avoid starting fights where many have accumulated; keep pushing the lane so he cannot clear the wave on his side and the minions die under his turret.
notes.yunara-skill-passive-cycle: Yunara’s damage follows a cycle of basic attacks, Unleash stacks, and Q activation. Each basic attack builds Unleash, with hits on champions granting twice as much as hits on minions, so short bursts of champion harassment ready Q much faster than farming alone. Starting a fight before Unleash is full means giving up much of her damage.
notes.yunara-skill-q: Q consumes Unleash to increase attack speed and make basic attacks splash to nearby targets. Q's splash attacks can crit and apply the passive's bonus magic damage. Time Q so you have Unleash left for the fight.
notes.yunara-skill-w: W, Arc of Judgment, throws an orb that applies a heavy slow and leaves a lingering damage area. The slow fades over time, so follow up as soon as it lands; placing the area in a fleeing, low health enemy’s path can finish them off with its damage over time. Its cast time gets shorter with permanent attack speed, so early on, when the cast feels slow, use W after the enemy is already caught.
notes.yunara-skill-e: E, Kanmei's Steps, grants ghosting and movement speed rather than a dash. The speed boost is larger when approaching an enemy champion, making E better for pursuit than escape, while ghosting lets Yunara pass through minions. She gains an actual dash only during R’s transformed state, so position as though she has no dash whenever R is unavailable.
notes.yunara-skill-r: R changes the forms of her basic abilities. With R active, Q activates immediately without consuming Unleash and lasts longer. With R active, W becomes a piercing beam. With R active, E becomes a dash. Before activating R, decide whether to use it to attack or escape.
notes.yunara-combo-trade: For lane trades, build Unleash with basic attacks, activate Q, then keep attacking. Use W, Arc of Judgment, if the opponent closes in or runs away: casting it first gives them time to create distance, so use its slow to sustain a trade already underway rather than to start one.
notes.yunara-combo-ult: In a fight, activate R to turn on Q immediately, land splash basic attacks, pierce grouped enemies with Arc of Ruin (W), then adjust your angle with Untouchable Shadow (E). Do not activate Q just before R, since R activates it for free and doing so would waste Unleash.
notes.yunara-phase-early: Yunara is weakest at levels 1–2: her base attack damage and movement speed are low even among marksmen, and her Unleash cycle has not started, leaving little damage for a single trade. Farm safely and build Unleash during this window, then start trading from level 3 onward as Q’s attack speed boost grows.
notes.yunara-phase-late: R gives Yunara her first power spike at level 6, when she gains both a dash and a piercing beam and can force 2v2 fights. Her strongest point comes after she builds critical strike items: Vow of the First Lands adds magic damage to each critical strike, including those from Q’s splash attacks, sharply increasing her area damage in late game teamfights.
notes.yunara-laning-wave: Q's splash attacks deal much more damage to low health minions, so activating it quickly pushes the whole wave. Use it when you want lane priority, to keep the enemy in lane, or to set up a recall; if you are pulling the wave to invite a jungle gank, hold Q even with full Unleash.
notes.yunara-laning-poke: One basic attack against an enemy champion builds as much Unleash as two against minions. When an enemy enters range, land one or two attacks and back off to prepare for the next fight. If they engage while Unleash is empty, W is Yunara's only way to respond, so do not spend it on minions while the enemy's engage ability is available.
notes.yunara-teamfight: Yunara's low movement speed and R dependent dash make her usual teamfight role attacking several enemies with Q's splash attacks from behind her frontline. Save W to stop enemies diving your backline, and decide in advance whether to use R for area damage or escape.
notes.yunara-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team's healing becomes a problem, cut it with Mortal Reminder. Q's splash attacks apply some on-hit effects, allowing the healing reduction to reach multiple enemies at once.
notes.yunara-situational-cc: Buy Quicksilver Sash earlier if the enemy team has a lot of immobilizing crowd control. Yunara's only dash comes from R, so if she is caught without it, she has no way to dash out.
notes.vs-yunara-emanation: Yunara’s damage spikes only when her Unleash stacks are full. If she has been attacking only minions, they are likely still incomplete; if she has been harassing with basic attacks, Q may be ready soon. Trade while she is still building Unleash with Q inactive, rather than immediately after she backs away from landing a basic attack.
notes.vs-yunara-q-window: While Yunara’s Q is active, she attacks faster and her basic attacks splash onto nearby targets, so even standing near her target can hurt you. Spread out and wait through its short duration, then engage as soon as it ends.
notes.vs-yunara-w: Yunara’s W, Arc of Judgment, applies a slow that nearly stops movement, and its lingering damage can finish off low health targets. If it hits you, leave the damage area immediately; staying in it at low health can kill you without another basic attack.
notes.vs-yunara-mobility: Without R, Yunara's E only grants movement speed and ghosting; it does not dash.
notes.vs-yunara-early: Yunara is weak at levels 1–2, with low base attack damage and movement speed even among marksmen and no Unleash stacks built yet. Push the lane and trade repeatedly during this window to deny her opportunities to build Unleash with basic attacks.
notes.yuumi-skill-w-attach: When Yuumi attaches to an ally with W, units other than turrets cannot target her. Her survival depends on staying attached, so above all, avoid losing that attachment when her ally dies or Yuumi is immobilized.
notes.yuumi-skill-w-switch: Recast W to switch attached allies at any time, but if Yuumi is immobilized, she cannot reattach for a short time. In a teamfight where allies are spread out, she can be left isolated with no one to switch to, so check that the next ally is in range before attaching.
notes.yuumi-skill-w-danger: If the ally Yuumi is attached to dies, she drops at their location. Switch to another ally before an attached ally with dangerously low health dies, and when an ally dives too far in, decide in advance whether to follow them or attach to an ally who stayed back.
notes.yuumi-skill-passive: Yuumi's passive determines her Best Friend through friendship gained whenever an ally she is attached to participates in a takedown. Only while attached to her Best Friend is Q's slow always empowered and R steerable with the mouse, so choose an ally to carry early and spend most of your time attached to them to help them grow.
notes.yuumi-skill-q: Q must travel for a certain amount of time before its damage and slow are empowered, so poke from as far away as possible; firing from too close yields only the weaker effect. While attached, Yuumi can steer Q with her mouse just after firing, but it locks into a straight path as it speeds up, so decide where to turn it immediately.
notes.yuumi-skill-e: E gives the attached ally a shield, attack speed, and mana. They also gain movement speed while the shield lasts, making E useful for chases and escapes as well as trades; using it when an ally is low on mana noticeably improves their ability to stay in lane.
notes.yuumi-skill-r: While channeling R, Yuumi can still move, switch attached allies, and use E. Its waves slow enemies and heal allies, with excess healing remaining as a shield, so use it once both teams have grouped in one place rather than as soon as the fight begins.
notes.yuumi-combo-poke: For a poke combo, stay attached and land Q from long range, have your ally follow up with attacks and abilities against the slowed target, then shield them with E. While attached to her Best Friend, Q's empowered slow always applies and their follow-up hit deals bonus damage, so time Q's impact with your ally's damage.
notes.yuumi-phase: Yuumi’s level-one health and resistances are among the lowest in the game, so getting caught while unattached means death. Aim to avoid losing lane rather than win it; her strength comes in the mid to late game, once her allies have items. Her early-game stats are near the bottom across the board, while her death count is the lowest of all, and breaking that balance costs her value.
notes.yuumi-laning: Yuumi can use both Q and E while attached, so there is little reason to detach in lane. Doing so exposes her to targeted abilities; detach briefly only to establish vision or buy items, leave all CS to the ADC, and let your ally decide when to contest lane priority.
notes.yuumi-vision: Yuumi cannot move on her own while attached, making solo roams and vision control virtually impossible. Detach briefly to place a Control Ward only when your ally is in a safe position, then reattach immediately; move together with an ally into areas where vision is needed.
notes.yuumi-teamfight: Yuumi's impact in a teamfight depends on whom she attaches to. The frontline is easier to survive with but may keep her support from allies who need it, while the backline exposes her to enemy dives alongside her ally. Once the enemy has used its engage tools, the safest and most valuable choice is to attach to the carry and focus E and R on them.
notes.yuumi-situational-mikael: If the enemy has immobilizing crowd control, build Mikael's Blessing before other support items to prevent it from breaking your attachment to an ally.
notes.vs-yuumi-target: While Yuumi is attached, nothing except turrets can target her.
notes.vs-yuumi-detach: Yuumi's brief moments while detached are your only opening. Save targeted crowd control for when she detaches to place a ward or reposition: immobilizing her then prevents her from reattaching for a short time.
notes.vs-yuumi-laning: Yuumi cannot farm CS on her own and has weak lane pressure, with early-game statistics near the bottom across the board. Pressure bot lane with your jungler to build a lead during the laning phase; the longer the game goes, the more favorable it becomes for Yuumi.
notes.vs-yuumi-r: R's waves repeatedly come from a set position. Watch R's position and move aside early to dodge its waves. Keep pressuring the ally Yuumi is attached to while dodging R's waves.
notes.zaahen-combo-q: Q is a two-stage ability: use it, land two basic attacks to heal, then recast it to knock the enemy up with your next basic attack. Because the knockup rides on that attack, it disappears if the enemy leaves basic attack range; recast while you are still close enough to land it.
notes.zaahen-combo-engage: For an engage, dash past the enemy with E so its edge hits, pull them in with W, then land both stages of Q through basic attacks. Always aim E beyond the enemy: stopping on top of them misses the edge hit and greatly reduces your damage.
notes.zaahen-combo-r: R is both a finisher and a way to evade damage. Time it with an enemy burst ability or targeted ability cast: Zaahen takes reduced damage while airborne, then deals damage on landing and heals for part of that damage. The heal is most valuable when his health is low.
notes.zaahen-skill-passive-stack: Determination stacks build only when basic attacks or abilities hit enemy champions; hitting minions builds none. In lane, frequent short trades that clip your opponent help you scale. Each stack increases attack damage, and at full stacks that increase doubles.
notes.zaahen-skill-passive-revive: At full Determination, lethal damage briefly leaves Zaahen motionless before he revives with health. The revive has a very long cooldown, so you get only a few chances to use it per game: force objective fights and teamfights while it is ready, then play cautiously like an ordinary fighter after it is spent. Creating those windows of strength is central to playing Zaahen.
notes.zaahen-skill-q: Q’s healing scales with maximum health but is halved against non-champions. Healing off minions is a backup when you urgently need it; your real sustain comes from hitting enemy champions. Q also deals substantial bonus damage to monsters, so use it freely on jungle camps and objectives.
notes.zaahen-skill-w: W thrusts in a straight line and pulls enemies it hits toward Zaahen. Since the pull direction is fixed, where you stand before casting determines where the enemy ends up. Cast with allied crowd control or a turret behind you to pull them into it.
notes.zaahen-skill-e: E is Zaahen’s only mobility ability and his biggest source of damage. Only enemies caught by the edge of its cleave take increased physical damage plus magic damage based on their maximum health, so dashing directly on top of an enemy cuts your own damage. Using E to engage also leaves you without an escape; keep it available when a gank is possible.
notes.zaahen-skill-r-passive: Learning R increases Zaahen’s armor penetration immediately, even if he saves the ability. His basic attacks and physical abilities deal more damage from that point, making trades against enemies building armor noticeably stronger.
notes.zaahen-laning: Zaahen’s high health and armor let him hold his own in early trades, though his CS and kill stats rank low among top champions. His statistical path to victory is closer to building Determination through short trades and pressuring the turret than trying to end lane with a kill. He uses mana, so spending every ability on farming leaves him weaker in trades.
notes.zaahen-laning-trade: In lane, clip the enemy with the edge of E, land both stages of Q through basic attacks, then back off. Using W first pulls them toward you but leaves no way to close the gap, so save it for when they flee or need to be pulled under your turret.
notes.zaahen-phase: Zaahen’s high health and armor let him hold his own in trades from levels 1–2, and his power jumps when full Determination stacks coincide with learning R at level 6. His real peak comes while the revive is available, so judge his power windows more by his stacks and revive cooldown than by level.
notes.zaahen-teamfight: Zaahen plays the frontline in teamfights. At full Determination, engaging first carries less risk: go in with E to disrupt the enemy formation, then use W to pull a backline enemy toward your team. If the revive is on cooldown, follow your allies’ engage instead of making the same first move.
notes.zaahen-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team relies on its own healing to survive, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Zaahen stays in range and deals damage over time, letting him maintain Grievous Wounds for a long time and get more value from it.
notes.vs-zaahen-stacks: Zaahen gains attack damage from Determination stacks, which he builds by hitting enemy champions. Keep trades short and avoid even glancing hits to slow his stacking. At full stacks, his attack damage increase doubles, so do not accept a duel then.
notes.vs-zaahen-revive: At full Determination, Zaahen revives with health shortly after dying. A dive or teamfight that fails to account for this effectively starts a player down. His revive has a very long cooldown, so force it out before starting an objective fight or teamfight.
notes.vs-zaahen-e: Only the edge of E’s cleave deals the heavier damage, including magic damage based on your maximum health. Move toward the end of Zaahen’s dash and stand inside that edge; even if E hits you, it will deal much less damage.
notes.vs-zaahen-qw: Zaahen’s Q knockup comes from his next basic attack, so moving out of basic attack range makes a prepared knockup disappear. W thrusts in a straight line and pulls targets toward him; staying out of a straight line between Zaahen and his allies denies him an engage that would pull you toward them.
notes.vs-zaahen-r: While airborne during R, Zaahen takes reduced damage and heals for part of the landing damage. Save burst abilities for Zaahen until R lands. Move away from R’s landing area to reduce Zaahen’s healing. Zaahen is vulnerable to Grievous Wounds.
notes.zac-combo-engage: Start the fight by landing E (Elastic Slingshot) on the enemy backline to knock them up, then immediately use R (Let's Bounce!) to scatter their formation and give your team a favorable position for the teamfight.
notes.zac-combo-r-w: You can use W (Unstable Matter) while bouncing with R (Let's Bounce!), so keep pressing it between bounces for much of Zac’s damage. R also lets you pass through enemies; aim your path toward their backline.
notes.zac-combo-q-sling: Q (Stretching Strikes) grabs the first enemy it hits and increases the range of your next basic attack. Hit a different enemy with that attack to throw the two together and knock them up. This requires at least two enemies; against just one, use Q for the slow and keep using your basic attacks.
notes.zac-combo-q-escape: Casting Q doesn’t interrupt Zac’s movement, so throw it behind you while retreating to slow pursuers. Use it during disengages, not just to engage.
notes.zac-skill-e-charge: The longer you charge E (Elastic Slingshot), the farther Zac flies. Moving during the charge cancels it and refunds half its cooldown and cost, so if the enemy spots you and backs away, cancel instead of forcing the cast. A silence, root, stun, or knockup also interrupts the charge.
notes.zac-skill-e-range: E (Elastic Slingshot) can carry Zac into a gank from far away while barely crossing warded ground. Choose a charging spot behind a wall and out of vision before planning your route in.
notes.zac-skill-w: W (Unstable Matter) has a short cooldown and deals damage based on the target’s maximum health, so use it whenever it is ready in teamfights, including against the frontline. Its health based damage is capped against minions and jungle monsters, though, so do not rely on it as your main jungle clearing tool.
notes.zac-skill-passive-blob: Hitting an enemy with an ability drops a blob that restores health and reduces W’s cooldown when Zac picks it up. In fights, path over your blobs to sustain yourself instead of simply staying close to the enemy. Enemy champions can destroy the blobs by stepping on them, so collect them promptly.
notes.zac-skill-passive-revive: Zac’s revive passive has a very long cooldown. Dives and risky engages are viable when it is ready; while it is on cooldown, play like a regular frontline champion. Save that safety net for close fights rather than entering a fight you are certain to lose.
notes.zac-phase: Zac has relatively low kill pressure and damage early on, with low early kill and damage per minute numbers, but he also dies less often. Clear camps safely and keep up in levels until level 6, when E (Elastic Slingshot) and R (Let's Bounce!) let you force objective fights. As you build items, W’s area damage and healing from blobs steadily improve your staying power in teamfights.
notes.zac-laning-gank: For a gank, first find a spot behind a wall and out of enemy vision where you can charge E. Because it takes time to charge, aim where the enemy is about to be, rather than where they are now; the most reliable play is to fire after your laner trades damage and draws them forward.
notes.zac-teamfight-target: When engaging with E (Elastic Slingshot), land toward the enemy backline; landing on the frontline leaves Zac with very little to do. Then look for an angle to throw an enemy damage dealer toward your team with Q (Stretching Strikes), rather than toward their frontline.
notes.zac-teamfight-role: Zac’s job is to absorb damage: if enemies ignore him, his W area damage keeps adding up, and if they focus him, your damage dealers are free to act. Either way your team benefits, so after engaging, stay in the fight and keep picking up blobs to survive.
notes.zac-situational-mr: If the enemy deals heavy magic damage, build Spirit Visage early. Along with magic resistance, it increases healing from Zac’s blobs, strengthening his sustain.
notes.vs-zac-e-interrupt: Zac’s E (Elastic Slingshot) has a visible charging animation. If you see him charging behind a wall, use a silence, root, stun, or knockup to interrupt it.
notes.vs-zac-blob: Enemy champions can destroy Zac’s blobs by stepping on them. Do so during fights to deny both his healing and W cooldown reduction, or immobilize him so he cannot reach them.
notes.vs-zac-revive: Zac’s revive passive has a very long cooldown. If it is used before a teamfight, he is just an ordinary frontliner for a while, so check whether it is ready before committing to a 1v1 or an objective fight.
notes.vs-zac-revive-deny: Ignite and Smite can hit the pieces Zac splits into after going down. If you have area damage, wait until the pieces are close together, then clear them all at once.
notes.vs-zac-kite: Zac needs to stay close to deal most of his damage. After weathering his engage, create distance as you fight to avoid most of his W area damage. If your team is weak in close combat, don’t start a fight from a position where you can’t judge Zac’s engage angle.
notes.zed-combo-basic: For a basic trade, send your W shadow behind or beside the enemy, then use Q → E. When Zed and his shadow hit the same target with the same ability, he restores energy, so positioning the shadow to land its hit is part of managing that resource.
notes.zed-combo-ult: Start an R combo with full energy and all abilities off cooldown. After using R to reach the target, place your W shadow, then land Q and E with both Zed and the shadow before the mark detonates. The detonation scales with the damage Zed deals while the mark is active, so use R before the rest of the combo.
notes.zed-combo-w-safe: Before using R, place your W shadow in a safe spot behind you. Returning to it immediately after the mark detonates lets you escape from the middle of the enemy team; using it alongside the shadow left by R gives you routes both in and out.
notes.zed-skill-w-double: Press W twice quickly to move immediately to where the shadow lands. Practice the input so you can use it for an emergency escape.
notes.zed-skill-w-cost: Zed is weakest just after using W. His damage, slow, and movement all depend on the shadow, so don’t waste W on poke when the enemy jungler is out of sight.
notes.zed-skill-e-slow: E's slow only applies when a shadow lands the hit.
notes.zed-skill-q: Both Zed and his shadow throw a shuriken with Q. Place the shadow beside or behind the enemy so the two shurikens converge from different directions and both hit with one cast. They pass through targets but deal less damage beyond the first, so make the enemy champion the first target hit.
notes.zed-skill-passive: P adds damage based on maximum health when you basic attack an enemy below half health. It cannot trigger again on the same champion for a while, so weave at least one basic attack into your combo without lingering to try for a second proc.
notes.zed-phase: Zed trades well at levels 1–2 because he has high health and uses energy instead of mana. Solo kills become possible once he gets R at level 6, and he peaks in the mid game with a couple of items. His strength falls sharply late as enemies build armor and group up, so use that peak to build a lead that can end the game.
notes.zed-laning: Energy management is central to Zed’s lane. When he and his shadow hit the same target with the same ability, he restores energy, so place the shadow even when poking. Spending Q only to clear minions can leave you without the energy to trade or escape.
notes.zed-teamfight: Avoid engaging head-on in teamfights. Flank from the side or rear, focus on a single enemy damage dealer, and use R after the enemy has spent their protective abilities and crowd control on your allies. You need to survive until the mark detonates, so always keep a position you can return to with W.
notes.zed-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from killing them in one combo, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.zed-situational-mr: Choose Maw of Malmortius if the enemy's main damage is magic damage.
notes.vs-zed-w: Zed is most vulnerable just after using W because his damage, slow, and movement depend on the shadow. Move in after it disappears or after he has already swapped positions.
notes.vs-zed-e: E slows only when the shadow lands the hit. Watch its position and move outside its E range to escape without being slowed.
notes.vs-zed-r-track: After entering with R, Zed needs to stay on his target and deal damage before the mark detonates. Apply crowd control while the mark is active to interrupt his combo and reduce the detonation damage.
notes.vs-zed-late: Zed peaks in the mid game and weakens as the game goes later. Avoid giving him an early lead, then move together with your allies so he has no isolated target to kill.
notes.zed-skill-e-cdr: Each enemy champion hit by Zed’s own E reduces W’s cooldown by 3 seconds; a shadow’s E does not. If you want to use W again during a fight, position Zed to hit multiple enemies himself before pressing E.
notes.zeri-skill-q: Zeri’s real basic attack is Q. It counts as a basic attack and can critically strike; as attack speed rises, its cast time and cooldown both fall. Attack speed above the cap converts to attack damage, so none goes to waste.
notes.zeri-skill-w-wall: W spreads into a long laser when it hits terrain and critically strikes champions and monsters. Aim it at an opponent with a wall behind them, a narrow passage, or a Rift wall to deal several times more poke damage; don’t throw it into open space.
notes.zeri-skill-w-slow: W is Zeri’s only slow, so using it all to poke leaves you with no way to push an enemy away if they close in. When an enemy engage champion is still alive, first decide whether to save one use.
notes.zeri-skill-e: E is a short dash that travels much farther across terrain, so aim it over a wall when escaping. Basic attack hits and critical strikes reduce its cooldown; keep attacking during fights to get the next E back much sooner.
notes.zeri-skill-e-pierce: Using E makes your next Q pierce enemies. Against an opponent standing behind minions or several enemies lined up, use E first so the same Q deals much more damage; treating E purely as a mobility tool wastes that opportunity.
notes.zeri-skill-passive: Moving or using Q charges Zeri’s passive Spark Pack, and a fully charged basic attack deals magic damage based on the target’s maximum health. Keep moving in lane to gain a way to poke, especially against high-health opponents, who take more damage from it.
notes.zeri-skill-r: Keeping R active matters more than the moment you cast it. Each hit on an enemy champion adds a stack, raises your movement speed, and extends its duration, while Q becomes rapid fire with chain lightning. Activate R when you can keep attacking, rather than when the fight will end after one takedown.
