notes.zeri-combo-allin: To engage, slow with W, use E to close the gap and prepare a piercing Q, fire Q repeatedly, then activate R. To disengage, activate R first for movement speed, then use E to cross a wall; doing so while R is active lets you escape most pursuers.
notes.zeri-phase: Laning is a time to hold your ground and farm CS with wall-spread W and basic attacks charged by moving, rather than to seek kills yourself. Statistically, Zeri’s laning CS ranks among the highest of all marksmen, and she grows much stronger after two or three core items give her attack speed and critical strike chance.
notes.zeri-laning: Zeri’s basic attack range is short even among marksmen, so avoid standing too far forward. Keep moving to dodge poke and charge your passive while farming without falling behind, and clear waves with Q. Fire W only when you can angle it into a wall; save it otherwise.
notes.zeri-teamfight: In teamfights, keep landing Q from the side instead of facing enemies head-on. E and R make it easier to evade enemies who engage on you, and positioning beside a wall gives you both an angle to spread W and an escape route with E. Zeri has low armor and can die as soon as she is caught, so position accordingly.
notes.zeri-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Zeri wears enemies down with sustained damage, so an enemy who keeps healing can survive no matter how long she attacks.
notes.zeri-situational-qss: If the enemy team starts fights by locking Zeri down with targeted crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar between core items. She deals sustained damage while moving with E and R, so being locked down takes away both her movement speed and sustained damage.
notes.vs-zeri-range: Zeri’s basic attack range is short even among marksmen. A long-range champion can poke her without retaliation in lane, so build as large a lead as possible before she gets her core items.
notes.vs-zeri-w: Zeri’s W spreads when it hits terrain and deals much more damage. Don’t stand with your back to a wall or face her head-on in a narrow passage; in open terrain, W stops at the first target it hits.
notes.vs-zeri-e: Zeri’s E travels much farther when crossing terrain. Pushing her toward a wall gives her an escape route, so force her into open terrain away from walls when trying to catch her.
notes.vs-zeri-r: While R is active, each hit raises Zeri’s movement speed, making her impossible to catch on foot. If she activates R, give up the chase or stop her immediately with an immobilizing effect; when R is down, E is her only mobility tool.
notes.vs-zeri-squishy: Zeri’s armor is among the lowest of all champions, and she has little kill pressure in lane. Catch her before she completes her core items; afterward, her mobility makes her much harder to pick off.
notes.ziggs-combo-basic: For basic poke, place E under the enemy or along their retreat path, then follow with Q when the slow takes hold. All of Ziggs’s abilities take time to land and often miss when thrown at an unslowed target, so applying the slow first is the only way to improve your hit rate.
notes.ziggs-combo-satchel: Place W behind the enemy and detonate it to knock them toward Ziggs. Throw Q immediately after placing W, then knock the enemy into Q’s landing spot to force them somewhere they cannot dodge. To escape instead, place W between Ziggs and the enemy and detonate it to knock yourself backward.
notes.ziggs-combo-passive-turret: Short Fuse’s empowered basic attack deals much more damage to structures, and each ability cast reduces its cooldown. At a turret, use abilities on the wave to ready the passive sooner, then hit the turret with the empowered attack. Once the turret falls below W’s demolition threshold, save W to finish it instead of relying on one last basic attack.
notes.ziggs-skill-q: Q is Ziggs’s main poke and wave clear tool, with his shortest cooldown, so keep using it as mana allows. Because it takes time to land, aim where the enemy is headed rather than where they stand; the best moments are when they stop behind minions to last-hit or pause to use an ability.
notes.ziggs-skill-w: W is Ziggs’s only mobility tool: detonating it beneath you can carry you over a wall while chasing or escaping. If you need it to escape, don’t spend it on poke; Ziggs has one of the lowest movement speeds, and he is vulnerable while W is on cooldown. Save it for a turret push, too, so you can demolish a weakened turret as soon as it falls below the threshold.
notes.ziggs-skill-e: Use E to control space rather than deal damage: when the same target steps on several mines in succession, later hits deal much less damage. Place it in narrow passages, at brush entrances, on routes that lead behind your allies, or beneath you as you retreat to cut off the enemy’s approach and make them abandon the engage.
notes.ziggs-skill-r: R’s enormous range lets you affect fights in other lanes or near objectives. Its center deals full damage, so aim for the middle of a group or narrow terrain where enemies cannot escape. Supporting another lane from afar is worthwhile when an ally has already pinned the enemy down; otherwise, use R to clear a wave or pressure a turret rather than leave it unused through a long stretch of laning.
notes.ziggs-laning: In bot lane, Ziggs fills the marksman position but fights at Q range rather than trading basic attacks. Keep poking from beyond the enemy marksman’s basic attack range, and if they step forward, place E behind them to cut off their retreat. Against a support with an engage ability, stand behind your own support instead of behind the minions so you do not give them an opening.
notes.ziggs-laning-wave: One Q can clear a group of minions, letting you push the lane whenever you want. Ziggs wins by pushing lanes and destroying turrets, so keep the wave at the enemy turret to create chances to chip away at it with Short Fuse (P) empowered basic attacks. Pushing leaves you open to ganks, so check that W is available and you have vision before doing so.
notes.ziggs-teamfight: Start teamfights at the very back, behind your allies, and give up the habit of stepping forward to find an angle; W is your only way to protect yourself. Place E on the enemy’s approach before the fight begins, then cast Q repeatedly once it starts and aim R at grouped enemies.
notes.ziggs-phase: At levels 1–2, Q’s long cooldown and limited mana make repeated poke slow. Lane pressure grows as you put more ranks into Q and get a mana item, while learning R at level 6 lets you influence other lanes. Ziggs is strongest late, once he has built up ability power, but he remains fragile, so position even farther back as his damage grows.
notes.ziggs-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. Ziggs has one of the lowest movement speeds and W is his only mobility tool, so once caught, he cannot escape on foot. Having a way to survive the engage determines how much damage he can deal later in the game.
notes.ziggs-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, buy Morellonomicon after completing your first core item. Ziggs lands abilities often enough to apply healing reduction across a wide area.
notes.vs-ziggs-e: Do not step into E: once it slows you, Ziggs’s other abilities become easier to land. Go around the mined path or wait for the mines to disappear, and before engaging, identify an approach that E does not cover.
notes.vs-ziggs-cooldown: Ziggs’s abilities have fairly long cooldowns, leaving him briefly vulnerable after a full rotation. The best time to engage is immediately after he spends W on poke or wave clear; without it, he cannot escape on foot.
notes.vs-ziggs-r: R hurts most at the center of its explosion and much less at the edge. When its warning area appears, move away from the center even if you cannot leave the area entirely. Its range lets Ziggs reach fights from another lane, so avoid grouping in one spot near an objective even when he is out of sight.
notes.vs-ziggs-mobility: Ziggs has one of the lowest movement speeds, and W is his only mobility tool. If W is down or he is somewhere he cannot cross a wall, engage; a single crowd control effect is enough to finish him. If W is available, check your vision and chase route on the far side of the wall before going in.
notes.vs-ziggs-turret: Ziggs’s W instantly demolishes turrets below a certain health threshold, and turrets do not recover health on their own. Leaving a turret at middling health can let Ziggs open the lane with a single wave, so if it has taken heavy damage, keep clearing waves in that lane.
notes.zilean-combo-doublebomb: Zilean’s core combo is Q → W → Q: placing a second Time Bomb on a target already carrying one detonates the first immediately and stuns nearby enemies. Rewind cuts Q’s cooldown so you can cast it again right away. Start when the enemy is standing still or held in place; if they leave the bomb radius between casts, the combo deals no damage and lands no stun.
notes.zilean-combo-engage: Slow an enemy with E, then use Q → W → Q to stun them; Time Warp’s strong slow makes it difficult to walk out of the bomb radius. To help an ally engage, use E to speed them up before the bomb combo. Decide who needs E before casting it.
notes.zilean-skill-q-attach: Q lands at the chosen spot and attaches to the first unit that comes close, prioritizing champions and units already carrying a bomb. Even among crowded minions, it will attach to an enemy champion within its radius; if the champion is outside it, a minion may take the bomb first. Aim where the enemy is about to walk rather than where they are now.
notes.zilean-skill-w: W deals no damage on its own, but Rewind cuts E’s cooldown as well as Q’s. When escaping, speed yourself up with E and use W to get E back. If the fight may last, save a W for a second stun or another E.
notes.zilean-skill-e: E greatly slows one enemy or speeds up one ally. Use it on an enemy engager as they jump onto an ally, or on an ally trying to finish off an enemy. Keep it available for survival when the enemy jungler is missing.
notes.zilean-skill-r-timing: For R’s revive to trigger, the targeted ally must die while Chronoshift is active. Cast it too early and the enemy may switch targets; cast it too late and your ally may die first. The most reliable moment is after a key targeted enemy ability has hit an ally. They are untargetable while reviving, so time your team’s counterattack around the revival.
notes.zilean-skill-r-bluff: R can make enemies hesitate to attack the ally carrying it. Cast it early on your main damage dealer to deter an engage near an objective or in a narrow passage, even if the revive never triggers.
notes.zilean-skill-passive: P lets you give an ally stored experience to level them up, and Zilean gains the same amount. Use Time In A Bottle when it will change their level: give them their level 6 ultimate early or create a level advantage just before a fight. During lane phase, use it on a bot lane ally; from mid game onward, use it on whoever is initiating fights.
notes.zilean-laning-poke: In lane, throw a bomb ahead of time when an enemy steps forward to last-hit or stands behind minions. If they retreat, the bomb may attach to a minion and push the wave. Q costs a lot of mana, so save it for spots the enemy will struggle to leave. Stand behind or beside your allied marksman and send the bombs forward.
notes.zilean-laning-wave: A bomb attached to a minion pushes the wave, so save Q when your ally wants to keep the wave near your side. When you want to push toward the enemy turret and roam, use bombs to clear the wave, then speed up an ally with E and head to mid or the jungle.
notes.zilean-phase: Levels 1–2 are Zilean’s weakest point: without W, he has only one bomb’s damage and cannot stun. Start trading at level 3, when Rewind enables Q → W → Q. Once he learns R at level 6, he can save an ally and becomes much stronger in fights. His own damage matters less in the late game, so shift from poking to protecting allies with R and E.
notes.zilean-teamfight: In teamfights, stay back and protect your allies. When an enemy dives your backline, slow them with E and follow with a Q → W → Q stun; cast R just before your main damage dealer comes under focused attack. The bomb stun can hit several enemies in its radius, making it especially valuable when they group up in a narrow passage.
notes.zilean-situational-antiheal: Build Morellonomicon if enemy healing is strong enough to turn a fight. Area bombs can apply healing reduction to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-zilean-bomb: Zilean needs two bombs on the same target to stun. If the first attaches to you, move away so your allies are outside its explosion radius; standing next to an ally carrying a bomb can catch you in the stun too.
notes.vs-zilean-r: An ally carrying R revives where they die and cannot be targeted during the revival, so using abilities on them then is a waste. If you can keep pace with Zilean, wait for R to expire before finishing them off; otherwise, prepare to attack again immediately after they revive.
notes.vs-zilean-e: E can slow or speed up only one person at a time. Engage from multiple directions so a single cast cannot stop everyone; going in alone lets Zilean slow you and land the bomb combo.
notes.vs-zilean-early: At levels 1–2, Zilean has no W to set up a bomb stun, and his health and attack damage are among the lowest. Get close and pressure him during that window. From level 3 onward, he can use Q → W → Q, so if you gained no early advantage, switch to farming outside bomb range.
notes.vs-zilean-target: Zilean has no mobility ability and is very fragile. If R makes your allied damage dealer hard to kill, it is better to switch your target to Zilean himself; taking him out first deprives his team of both protection and speed boosts.
notes.zilean-situational-mikael: If the enemy team has enough crowd control to lock down your main damage dealer, build Mikael’s Blessing between core items. R only activates when its target is in danger of dying, while Mikael’s Blessing frees an ally the moment they are caught, so each covers a different point in the fight.
notes.zoe-combo-core: After landing E, time Q to hit when the target falls asleep, then follow with an empowered basic attack and W missiles. Time Q to arrive as the first damage when the target falls asleep. The first damage dealt to a sleeping target is doubled. Don't let a basic attack or W missile hit before Q.
notes.zoe-combo-q: After firing Q, Paddle Star!, you can redirect it once, and its damage increases with the total distance the star travels. Send it far to the side or behind you before turning it toward the target; this avoids the minion wave and maximizes damage. The window to redirect is short, so cast from a safe spot where you will not be interrupted.
notes.zoe-combo-re: Throw E first and let the bubble grow, then use R to jump in its direction and follow it far enough to land the enlarged bubble. You can also briefly cross a wall with R, throw E, and return. Either way, account for the fact that R always brings you back to where you started.
notes.zoe-skill-passive: Your first basic attack after using an ability is empowered by More Sparkles!. Early on, save it for poke or finishing off a target instead of spending it carelessly on minion last hits. Both the initial cast and the recast of Q trigger the passive, letting you get two empowered attacks from one Q.
notes.zoe-skill-e-wall: Throwing E over a wall extends its range. It is most reliable when you hide in a bush or behind a wall and cast from an angle the enemy cannot see. If the bubble hits no one, it remains where it lands as a trap, so you can place one in advance at a choke point such as in front of the first turret or at a dragon or Herald entrance to block the path.
notes.zoe-skill-e-timing: E puts its target to sleep after a short delay, giving them time to walk away. Aim for a spot where they will be held in place, such as during an ally’s crowd control or in a narrow passage. Hitting a champion greatly reduces Zoe’s ability cooldowns, bringing her next fight around much sooner.
notes.zoe-skill-w-shard: W, Spell Thief, gets shards from enemy summoner spells, active items, and certain minions. Keep count of the spells enemies use, tell your team, and collect shards that fall in lane. In teamfights, defensive or utility shards can often save allies and turn the fight around more effectively than offensive ones.
notes.zoe-skill-w-move: Using W or a summoner spell grants movement speed and sends missiles toward the last target you hit with a basic attack. A shard is therefore a movement speed tool as well as its own effect. Save it for when you need that speed, such as moving in to find an angle or escaping a gank.
notes.zoe-skill-r: R, Portal Jump, briefly moves Zoe nearby before always returning her to her starting point. She can use abilities and basic attacks during the jump but cannot walk, so use it to extend her range or gain vision over a wall. Against a delayed targeted dash, you can cast R after the dash begins, stand briefly beyond a wall, and return to leave the enemy there.
notes.zoe-laning: Zoe’s armor and magic resistance are both low, so avoid direct damage trades. In lane, use Q to last-hit and poke while looking for an angle for E, and spend your abilities only when the enemy steps forward. Q costs enough mana that spamming it can leave you unable to farm; cast it from a position where it can pass through minions and hit multiple targets.
notes.zoe-roam: After clearing the wave, move behind a river or jungle wall to find an angle for E.
notes.zoe-phase: At levels 1–2, E has a long cooldown and mana is scarce, making mistakes costly. Once you have learned E and completed an item, landing it enables a combo that can kill one enemy. Zoe keeps her burst damage into the late game, but gains little durability; when enemies have their engage abilities available, finding a position where you can survive matters more than looking for an attack angle.
notes.zoe-teamfight: Start teamfights from the very back and follow an ally’s immobilizing crowd control with E or Q instead of moving out first to look for an angle. Step forward only after confirming the enemy has used their engage abilities; until then, hold your position with E traps and movement speed from W shards.
notes.zoe-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who can engage instantly, get Zhonya's Hourglass early, since you can't escape with R.
notes.vs-zoe-q: Zoe has only a brief window to redirect Q Paddle Star! after firing it. Stun or root her as she throws it and lines up the angle; she will be unable to redirect the star, causing it to miss. Her throwing animation is your cue to use crowd control.
notes.vs-zoe-r: Zoe always returns to her starting point after using R, so aim there to counterattack. She also cannot walk while displaced.
notes.vs-zoe-e: E’s bubble puts you to sleep after a short delay. During that window, move behind a wall or an ally and out of Zoe’s range to avoid the doubled damage. Zoe is looking for one big hit as you sleep, so make sure the spot where you wake is outside her Q angle. If you have Cleanse or Quicksilver Sash, use it to remove the sleep.
notes.vs-zoe-trap: A missed E bubble remains where it lands as a trap. Against Zoe, move carefully through narrow paths without vision, bush entrances, and areas in front of objectives. Before starting an objective, use a Control Ward to reveal the surrounding area so a trap does not ruin the teamfight from the outset.
notes.vs-zoe-w: Using a summoner spell or active item near Zoe drops a shard she can use herself. When she is in sight, save spells you do not urgently need. In particular, after using Flash near her, move as though she can use that same spell to follow you.
notes.vs-zoe-dive: Zoe has some of the lowest defensive stats of any champion and no true escape. Against her, avoid fighting over angles and focus on getting within range: once you close the gap, you can stick to her and take her down. If your champion has an engage ability, use it right after Zoe uses E Sleepy Trouble Bubble.
notes.zyra-combo-basic: The basic guaranteed combo is E to root the target, W on the rooted spot, then Q. The target cannot move off the seed, so Q lands; if both E and Q hit the same seed, a Thorn Spitter and a Vine Lasher grow together. Starting with Q lets the target walk away and avoid the plant damage.
notes.zyra-combo-seed-after: Cast Q or E first, then place a W seed in its path. W has virtually no cast time, so the seed can land while Q or E is traveling, leaving the target no time to dodge it or step on it first. Plant seeds in advance only when you are sure where the target will move.
notes.zyra-combo-ult: For a teamfight combo, place seeds, grow plants with Q and E, then cast R over them. Plants inside R become enraged, have their duration refreshed, and hit harder, so casting it over plants produces a very different result from casting it on empty ground. R deals damage immediately, then knocks enemies up when the vines contract; if you save E for the knockup, you can root the target as soon as they land.
notes.zyra-skill-passive: P seeds are a resource that spawns automatically and more quickly as Zyra levels up. They stop spawning while she is hidden in a brush, so plant seeds before entering if you plan to wait there. An enemy champion who steps on a seed destroys it and briefly reveals their location.
notes.zyra-skill-w: W uses charges rather than a standard cooldown, and killing minions or monsters speeds up its recharge. Farming naturally restores charges, but keep at least one for your combo before a fight. Sitting at full charges wastes the resource, so plant seeds along your route to provide vision.
notes.zyra-skill-q: The ranged plants grown by Q keep firing, making them Zyra’s main tool for clearing waves and pressuring towers and a reason she can push faster than many supports. Q itself detonates after a delay and often misses moving enemies, so use it alone to clear minions and pair it with a root or an ally’s crowd control when targeting a champion. Because pushing costs a lot of mana, use the time it creates to set up vision or roam.
notes.zyra-skill-e: E is Zyra’s only guaranteed crowd control and starts her combo, so do not waste it on wave clear. Vine Lashers grown from seeds in E’s path are very short range melee plants and are useful only when an enemy is close. If the enemy is poking from afar, seeds placed along E will accomplish nothing; use them with Q instead.
notes.zyra-skill-r: R takes time to knock enemies up after it is cast, giving mobile targets a chance to leave its area. Starting with R alone often fails, so cast it on an enemy immobilized by an ally or one pressed against a wall or caught in a narrow passage to secure the knockup. You can also place it ahead of an advancing enemy, using the delay to block their path and discourage the engage.
notes.zyra-laning: In lane, look to trade when the enemy support steps forward to protect their ADC or place a ward: root them with E, then add a seed. Zyra has low health and resistances, leaving her little way to withstand a counterattack if E misses. While E is on cooldown, fall back and build up seeds.
notes.zyra-laning-brush: Zyra is especially strong at ambushing. Prepare seeds near brush along a passage by the river or lane, draw the enemy toward them, then lead with E the moment they enter the seeded area. Having the seeds in place saves casting time and lets the same combo deal nearly lethal damage.
notes.zyra-teamfight: In teamfights, Zyra controls an area from behind her allies. Before the fight, scatter seeds where they will stand and along the enemy's approach, then cut off the path with E and R as the enemy engages. Start at the edge of your range: if Zyra is caught first, neither her plants nor her seeds will matter.
notes.zyra-phase: Zyra is weakest at levels 1–2, when seeds spawn slowly and she has only one or two abilities. She can start trading damage from level 3, once she has learned both E and Q and built up seeds; her power peaks at level 6 when she learns R and in the mid game as she gains ability power. Later, enemies have mobility and ways to cleanse crowd control, making fights decided by a single E less likely, so secure advantages through vision and objectives before then.
notes.zyra-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, build Morellonomicon after finishing one core item to reduce it. Zyra lands many hits, including from her plants, so she can apply healing reduction easily.
notes.zyra-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, build Zhonya's Hourglass earlier. Zyra has no mobility skill and no way out once caught, so surviving the engage is essential to keeping her plants active.
notes.vs-zyra-seed: Zyra’s seeds disappear when stepped on. Their distinct color and larger size make them easy to identify, so step on any you find along your path. If Zyra casts an ability to grow a seed as you approach it, though, walking in will put you directly in her combo; when you see the ability coming, back away at the last moment, then step on the seed.
notes.vs-zyra-plants: Fully grown plants can be cleared by attacking them a set number of times, like wards, and disappear on their own over time. Rather than force a fight in an area full of plants, back off briefly and Zyra's damage will drop by half. She is weakest when there are no plants nearby.
notes.vs-zyra-position: Moving the fight makes the seeds Zyra has set up useless. Avoid fighting in an area she has occupied for a while; move to another objective and engage on fresh ground. If she has grown plants far from herself, it is safer to move in on Zyra herself.
notes.vs-zyra-e: Zyra's plays start with her E root. It travels in a straight line, and she has no mobility skill, so move sideways at the edge of its range to bait it out, then engage while it is on cooldown. Once E misses, she has virtually no way to fight back.
notes.vs-zyra-r: R knocks enemies up after a delay, when its summoned vines contract. Leave the area as soon as you see the cast indicator, saving a mobility skill for that moment if you have one. Zyra wants to cast R over groups of plants to enrage them, so avoiding fights near those groups greatly reduces its value.
notes.vs-zyra-vision: Zyra's seeds give her team vision. Assume her team can see areas where she has stayed for a while and plan your approach accordingly. Before entering a brush where you suspect an ambush, check it with a control ward or a skill.
